title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text: MOD-05 Partially addressed Very high priority Established

title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text:
Statement
An augmented estimator combining an outcome model with a sampling or transport weight model is consistent if either nuisance model is correct, given conditional exchangeability, positivity and the usual consistency conditions. The seven failures the source enumerates (unmeasured effect modifier, lack of overlap, wrong treatment or outcome version, both nuisance models wrong, wrong target moments, network inconsistency, false component bridge) are true by construction, but they are the agenda’s own list and the paper it cites asserts none of them. Campbell and Remiro-Azocar (doi:10.1017/rsm.2026.10106) do supply the augmented entropy-balancing MAIC estimator, demonstrated in simulation for binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model, and drMAIC ships doubly robust MAIC for practitioners. What is open is the layer around the estimator: no doubly robust estimator indexed by bias parameters and nested inside quantitative bias analysis exists, and network versions are absent.

title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text:
Why it is open
Double robustness is a union-model property for two measured-data nuisance models with the identification assumptions held fixed, so every threat operating through those assumptions or through data support is untouched by construction and cannot be repaired by better nuisance estimation. Packages return a single augmented point estimate with an interval that conditions on identification holding, so the residual-bias layer is never displayed to a decision maker; drMAIC ships E-values and weight trimming as separate sensitivity analyses rather than an estimator indexed by bias parameters. The estimators have also been developed for a single source and a single target rather than for the network structures HTA submissions contain, and no AIPW or TMLE network estimator was found in the implementations the auditors read.

title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Campbell & Remiro-Azocar 2026, Doubly robust augmented weighting estimators for the analysis of externally controlled single-arm trials and unanchored indirect treatment comparisons, Research Synthesis Methods (preprint arXiv:2505.00113)
Places externally controlled single-arm trials and unanchored ITCs in one causal framework and proposes an augmented entropy-balancing MAIC estimator that is doubly robust to misspecification of the weighting or outcome model. Demonstrated in simulation for binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model.


drMAIC: Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA
Released implementation of augmented doubly robust MAIC. Ships E-values and weight trimming as separate sensitivity analyses, not the bias-parameter-indexed estimator this entry asks for.

title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Nest the augmented estimators that already exist inside quantitative bias analysis, reporting the estimate as a function of bias parameters rather than as a single number, and state in every report which layer double robustness covers (measured-data outcome and transport models) and which it does not (unmeasured modifiers, positivity, treatment version, target moments, network consistency, component additivity). Extend the demonstration beyond binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model, since that is the extent of the current evidence for the augmented MAIC estimator. Combine augmented estimation with overlap diagnostics and partial identification so the residual-bias layer stays visible, and extend to network settings where nothing is implemented.

title: No doubly robust PAIC estimator is indexed by bias parameters
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Double robustness is routinely read as general robustness” The title asserts that double robustness is routinely misread, a prevalence claim neither auditor could establish, and the seven-failure list came from the entry rather than its citation.
The source said. “An augmented estimator combining an outcome model with a sampling or transport weight model is consistent under standard conditions if either nuisance model is correct, given conditional exchangeability. The report holds that the label doubly robust is routinely read as general robustness and enumerates seven distinct failures it does not protect against: an unmeasured effect modifier, lack of overlap, an incorrect treatment or outcome version, both nuisance models being wrong, wrong target moments, network inconsistency, and a false component bridge.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented a seven-item enumeration of what double robustness does not protect against as though it came from its cited paper; the literature auditor found that the paper makes no such negative claims and that its double robustness demonstration covers binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model only (doi:10.1017/rsm.2026.10106). Neither auditor could establish the prevalence claim carried by the word ‘routinely’.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): Retrieved Campbell & Remiro-Azocar, ‘Doubly robust augmented weighting estimators for the analysis of externally controlled single-arm trials and unanchored indirect treatment comparisons’, Res Synth Methods 2026 (doi 10.1017/rsm.2026.10106; preprint arXiv:2505.00113). The abstract confirms the entry’s description exactly: an entropy-balancing MAIC augmented with a conditional outcome expectation model, doubly robust to misspecification of either. Two caveats make this supported-with-caveat rather than fully supported. First, the demonstration is binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model only, so ‘doubly robust’ is evidenced for that case; the entry does not say so. Second, the seven-item enumeration of what double robustness does NOT protect against is the agenda’s own construction, not anything the cited paper asserts; the paper makes no such negative claims. Those seven items are nonetheless true by construction, since double robustness is a property of two measured-data nuisance models with identification held fixed. The ‘no reference implementation of a DR estimator indexed by bias parameters inside QBA’ claim I could not falsify; drMAIC ships E-values and weight trimming as separate sensitivity analyses, not a bias-parameter-indexed DR estimator.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Retrieved Campbell & Remiro-Azocar, ‘Doubly robust augmented weighting estimators for the analysis of externally controlled single-arm trials and unanchored indirect treatment comparisons’, Res Synth Methods 2026 (doi 10.1017/rsm.2026.10106; preprint arXiv:2505.00113). The abstract confirms the entry’s description exactly: an entropy-balancing MAIC augmented with a conditional outcome expectation model, doubly robust to misspecification of either. Two caveats make this supported-with-caveat rather than fully supported. First, the demonstration is binary outcomes with a logistic outcome model only, so ‘doubly robust’ is evidenced for that case; the entry does not say so. Second, the seven-item enumeration of what double robustness does NOT protect against is the agenda’s own construction, not anything the cited paper asserts; the paper makes no such negative claims. Those seven items are nonetheless true by construction, since double robustness is a property of two measured-data nuisance models with identification held fixed. The ‘no reference implementation of a DR estimator indexed by bias parameters inside QBA’ claim I could not falsify; drMAIC ships E-values and weight trimming as separate sensitivity analyses, not a bias-parameter-indexed DR estimator.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1-C2 state the usual double-robustness result, provided consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, and any required treatment and censoring mechanisms also hold. C3-C11 are technically correct: double robustness is a union-model property for specified measured-data nuisances and does not repair identification, support, target-definition, network-consistency, or component-additivity failures; C4 and C5 are duplicates. C12 is supported for the measured-data weighting and outcome models in the estimator’s stated scope. C13 and the word ‘routinely’ are literature and prevalence claims outside this lens. The underlying limitations are decision-critical, but they are established assumptions rather than a new technical discovery; nesting a DR estimator in QBA and extending it to networks are roadmap items. title: Ecological versus within-study effect modification
text:
Statement
Aggregate study means inform between-study associations, not individual-level treatment-by-covariate interactions, so meta-regression on study means can misattribute an ecological association to individual effect modification and then transport it to a target population. This is established rather than new: it is Berlin et al. 2002 (doi:10.1002/sim.1023), and the remedy the entry proposes, separating within-trial from across-trial information by trial-mean centering, was formalized, simulated and demonstrated by Hua et al. 2017 (doi:10.1002/sim.7171). The auditors split on ML-NMR (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579): the literature auditor read it as avoiding the ecological bias of aggregate-data network meta-regression, while GPT-5.6 Sol held that it avoids mean plug-in aggregation but that an interaction informed only by aggregate arms stays ecological unless within-study information or an identifying restriction separates the coefficients, pointing to a development implementation that fits one interaction matrix for IPD covariates and aggregate means and thereby imposes equality of the two (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9). What remains open is aggregate-only interaction identification and a formal ecological-bias sensitivity analysis over the gap between the coefficients, since an IPD-informed prior transfers information under exchangeability but does not create likelihood identification.

title: Ecological versus within-study effect modification
text:
Why it is open
In an aggregate-data study the covariate takes a single value per arm, so no within-study contrast exists to identify the individual-level interaction and the fitted coefficient is a between-study slope confounded with everything else that varies across studies. The two coefficients coincide only under an assumption the aggregate data cannot check, and because the regression is well behaved either way the substitution leaves no signature in fit statistics. Where IPD supply within-study variation the remedy is known and validated, so the residual problem is specifically the aggregate-only case, in which the identifying restriction is imposed by the model rather than tested by the data.

title: Ecological versus within-study effect modification
text:

Hua, Burke, Crowther, Ensor, Tudur Smith & Riley 2017, One-stage individual participant data meta-analysis models: estimation of treatment-covariate interactions must avoid ecological bias by separating out within-trial and across-trial information, Statistics in Medicine (PMID 27910122)

Phillippo et al. 2020, Multilevel network meta-regression for population-adjusted treatment comparisons, JRSS-A (PMID 32684669)
Integrates an individual-level model over the aggregate covariate distribution rather than plugging in means, removing the aggregation bias of standard aggregate-data meta-regression. Whether that also removes ecological bias in an aggregate-only interaction is what the two auditors disputed.

Source-code evidence cited by GPT-5.6 Sol that fitting one interaction matrix across IPD covariates and aggregate means imposes equality of the within-study and between-study interaction. cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub; an auditor confirmed it is not on CRAN and cannot be installed from there.

title: Ecological versus within-study effect modification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use the established remedy wherever IPD allow it: separate within-study and between-study coefficients by trial-mean centering, and integrate an individual-level model over the aggregate covariate distribution rather than plugging in means. The work genuinely left is the aggregate-only case: report which coefficient a transported effect relies on, and run an explicit ecological-bias sensitivity analysis over the gap between the within-study and between-study coefficients rather than assuming it is zero. IPD-informed priors on the individual-level interaction can regularize a posterior and should be reported as an assumption, not as identification.

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text: MOD-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Established

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text:
Statement
A conventional or anchored STC that fits a generalized linear or Cox model in the IPD trial and reports the treatment coefficient evaluated at the aggregate trial’s covariate means returns a conditional parameter at a mean covariate profile, which on non-collapsible scales is not the marginal effect the aggregate-data trial reports. The mismatch is real and was demonstrated by simulation in Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511), but it is no longer an open methods problem: parametric g-computation (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565, 2022) and multiple imputation marginalization (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02157-x, 2024) standardize the fitted model over the target covariate distribution, and outstandR ships both on CRAN. What is still open is the input those methods need. The target joint covariate law is rarely published, and implementations condition on reported target means and standard deviations as if they were known constants.

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text:
Why it is open
The mismatch persists in practice rather than in theory. Evaluating a fitted model at target means is numerically trivial and produces something that looks like a treatment effect, so the estimand error leaves no trace in output, diagnostics or balance tables, while the compatible route needs the target joint covariate distribution that aggregate reports rarely provide. Standardization also replaces one identification problem with two estimation problems, because the target covariate law must be modeled alongside the outcome and neither model can be validated against the aggregate data that motivated the analysis. GPT-5.6 Sol added that target-summary uncertainty is a genuine omission when the estimand indexes a superpopulation, but may properly be conditioned on when the estimand indexes the realized finite target sample.

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Remiro-Azocar, Heath & Baio 2022, Parametric G-computation for compatible indirect treatment comparisons with limited individual patient data, Research Synthesis Methods (PMID 35485582)
Standardizes a GLM or Cox outcome model over the target covariate distribution to recover a marginal effect compatible with the aggregate-data trial. This is the resolution of the estimand mismatch the entry describes, and it is the entry’s own citation.


Model-based standardization using multiple imputation, BMC Medical Research Methodology 2024 (PMID 38341552)
Supplies the multiple imputation marginalization route the entry names, with Bayesian uncertainty propagation, benchmarked by simulation for binary outcomes and a logistic model.


Methods for population adjustment with limited access to individual patient data: a review and simulation study, 2021 (PMID 34196111)
Establishes the entry’s central bias claim by simulation across 162 survival scenarios, showing that typical STC targets a conditional effect where the estimand should be marginal, and names the fix that was delivered in 2022.


outstandR: Population-Adjusted Indirect Treatment Comparison in R (described in arXiv:2601.07532)
Ships maximum-likelihood and Bayesian G-computation plus multiple imputation marginalization, so the compatible alternative is a released package rather than research-only.

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use the existing standardization implementations rather than rebuilding them, and state the conditional or marginal status and the indexing population of every reported STC quantity. The research work left is the target law: propagate uncertainty in it instead of fixing it, using a Bayesian distribution over the target law or bootstrap and influence-function expansions that include target-summary estimation, and reconstruct the joint distribution from published marginals with copulas, maximum entropy or synthetic target populations while reporting sensitivity to that reconstruction. State which estimand each uncertainty statement is for, since conditioning on the realized target sample is legitimate for a finite-population estimand.

title: Conventional STC reports a conditional effect at target means
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “A conventional or anchored simulated treatment comparison fits a generalized linear or Cox model in the IPD trial and reports the treatment coefficient evaluated at the aggregate trial’s covariate means. That quantity is a conditional parameter at a mean covariate profile; on non-collapsible scales it is not the marginal effect the aggregate-data trial reports, so the two arms of the indirect comparison are not the same estimand.”
What was wrong with it. The source framed the conditional versus marginal mismatch as an open problem. Both auditors voted it partially solved: the fix is the entry’s own citation (parametric g-computation, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565, 2022), extended by multiple imputation marginalization (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02157-x, 2024) and shipped on CRAN in outstandR, so what survives is the treatment of reported target summaries as fixed known constants.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Retrieved the cited work (Remiro-Azocar, Heath & Baio 2022, Res Synth Methods, PMID 35485582). Its abstract states verbatim: ‘Current outcome regression-based alternatives can extrapolate but target a conditional treatment effect that is incompatible in the indirect comparison. When adjusting for covariates, one must integrate or average the conditional estimate over the relevant population to recover a compatible marginal treatment effect.’ The prior_work description is accurate. The same abstract also supports the extrapolation claim (‘MAIC … cannot extrapolate beyond the observed covariate space’) and the efficiency claim (‘Parametric G-computation achieves more precise and more accurate estimates than MAIC, particularly when covariate overlap is poor’). What remains genuinely open is the sub-claim I could not verify: that implementations ignore uncertainty in the reported target summaries. Vote partially-solved, not open.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. At choxos/cpaic@9d150e9, NAMESPACE exports cstc(), R/cstc.R centers effect modifiers at target means and explicitly labels the result conditional, and R/effects.R and R/cmlnmr.R state that no marginal standardized path is returned. That establishes C1-C5, C7, and the conditional-versus-marginal core: in general m(E[X]) is not E[m(X)], and non-collapsible link-scale contrasts cannot be substituted for marginal trial contrasts. C9-C10 are resolved by g-computation and MIM. C6 is not a universal efficiency ordering; correct parametric outcome regression can outperform MAIC, but the ordering depends on the estimand, models, design, and overlap. C11 needs a sufficiently correct target-law representation only when that law must be reconstructed; empirical target IPD or special estimands need not introduce a parametric target-distribution model. C8 and C12 are prevalence claims not established by technical reasoning, and target-summary uncertainty is genuine for a superpopulation target but may properly be conditioned on when the estimand indexes the realized finite target sample. The estimand mismatch is therefore solved in method, while target-law identification, uncertainty propagation, and cpaic’s own marginal path remain open. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565: Provides explicit standardization of GLM and Cox outcome models over a target covariate distribution to obtain a compatible marginal treatment effect.. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02157-x: Provides the MIM route named in the agenda for converting conditional outcome-model predictions into target-population marginal effects..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R11:caveated(n=1)

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
Statement
When the same data select a PAIC model or bridge and ordinary conditional intervals are then reported, nominal coverage is generally not guaranteed, although the distortion can run in either direction and a prespecified or externally chosen model does not create the problem at all. Model averaging as the response is established in evidence synthesis generally (Rover, Wandel and Friede 2019; Bartos et al., arXiv:2110.01076) but has not been applied to PAIC, and predictive stacking needs a held-out unit aligned with the prediction target and dependence structure, so patient, study, and contrast level prediction are different estimands to choose between rather than an ambiguity that blocks the method. For bridges the difficulty is narrower than the source claimed: likelihood-based weights can be formed when candidate bridges imply different observed-data likelihoods or predictions, and are unavailable only for observationally equivalent identifying assumptions, which need prior elicitation or sensitivity analysis instead. No PAIC software feeds model or bridge averaging into the reported effect interval; in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, loo() is observation-level and warns that it does not validate cross-gap prediction, while prior_sensitivity() and bridge_fragility() remain diagnostics. The same failure occurs one step earlier, at the treatment partition. Whether doses, formulations, schedules, devices, class members or control conditions become one node or two is settled before any model is fitted, on clinical judgment or on a deviance comparison among candidate groupings, and the alternatives that fit almost as well are neither reported nor propagated into the interval or the ranking. Model fit cannot arbitrate that choice, because candidate partitions are not nested in a way that makes deviance comparable across different data configurations and because splitting can disconnect the network, which is a structural rather than a statistical objection. The same defect appears wherever a study’s contribution is reconstructed from an assumed nuisance parameter rather than reported: most published crossover trials give no precision estimate that respects the paired design, so a meta-analyst must impute a within-participant correlation, use first-period data only, or exclude the trial, and whichever is chosen is then conditioned on as known. Across 83 crossover trials assembled for one network, 19 (23 percent) reported a paired precision estimate and 50 (60 percent) supplied a point estimate and precision usable without further assumptions, falling to 26 (31 percent) once a washout period was also required (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0133023), so both the eligible set and the imputed correlation move the contributed weights, and no study has reported how far pooled effects or rankings shift between the resulting eligible sets.

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
Why it is open
Selection happens on the same data used for estimation, so the reported interval is conditional on a choice it does not price. The standard remedy needs a predictive unit at which the stacking weights are meaningful, and in a network the choice among patient, study, and contrast has to be made deliberately as a statement of the prediction target rather than inherited from a default. Projection predictive selection controls predictive loss and does not by itself deliver valid post-selection intervals, and robust Bayes covers only the model and prior classes actually represented, so neither is a finished answer and neither has been tried in PAIC. For bridges that are observationally equivalent no fit statistic can separate them, and the only honest input is a prior on assumption plausibility, which nobody has elicited.

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Rover, Wandel and Friede 2019, Statistics in Medicine (locator not supplied by the auditor)
heavy-tailed mixture priors for effect estimation in meta-analysis, which effectively result in a model-averaging technique robust to prior-data conflict; established for meta-analysis, not applied to population-adjusted comparisons


Bartos et al., Bayesian Model-Averaged Meta-Analysis in Medicine
Bayesian model averaging over meta-analytic models so that model uncertainty enters the reported estimate; again for meta-analysis rather than for population-adjusted or network settings


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
provides prior_sensitivity() and bridge_fragility() diagnostics and an observation-level loo() that warns it does not validate cross-gap prediction; no model or bridge averaging enters the reported effect interval


Efthimiou et al. 2016, Research Synthesis Methods (GetReal review)
States that no recipe exists for deciding whether similar-but-not-identical interventions become one node or two, that the choice is left to clinical judgment plus goodness-of-fit comparison between candidate structures, and that as included studies adopt increasingly different node definitions transitivity becomes less plausible and inconsistency or heterogeneity rises.


Welton et al. 2015, Medical Decision Making
Compares five treatment-definition models for one dataset and finds the deviance information criterion spread narrow, 168.6 to 180.5, while the resulting decision changes; resolves the choice by expert judgment and states that the approach can help determine whether grouping is reasonable only with clinical input. The closest thing to a fit-based arbitration of node granularity, and it shows fit does not arbitrate.


Mills et al. 2013, BMJ
Survey of the effects of excluding treatments from network meta-analyses, reporting node-level effect changes up to 3.64-fold and reordering of the top three treatments in half of 18 networks. Explicitly declines to question the clustering of regimens into nodes by the original analysts and names that clustering as an additional, unquantified source of variability.


Ishaq et al. 2023, European Spine Journal
Delphi consensus study built specifically to group conservative neck-pain treatments into network nodes, which records that no generally recommended procedure exists for grouping similar-enough treatments into nodes and that several different methods could therefore be followed.


Zhang et al. 2026, Frontiers in Medicine
Prespecifies three node layers, 17, 5 and 4 nodes, for a single sedation dataset and reports that the numerically best treatment in the finest layer was a sparse variant supported only by indirect evidence, with interventions at different conceptual levels risking inflated treatment hierarchies.


Ades et al. 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Reviews twenty years of network meta-analysis controversies and identifies lumping over doses and co-treatments as an avoidable source of quantitative heterogeneity, so the concern is not confined to one clinical area.


Li, Yu, Hawkins and Dickersin 2015, Design, Analysis, and Reporting of Crossover Trials for Inclusion in a Meta-Analysis, PLOS ONE 10:e0133023
Measures the exposure across 83 crossover trials eligible for one network: 19 (23 percent) report a precision estimate that accounts for the pairing, 50 (60 percent) supply a point estimate and precision usable without further assumptions, 26 (31 percent) if a washout period is also required, and 16 (19 percent) report first-period results separately, so most crossover edges in such a network rest on an assumed within-participant correlation.


Elbourne, Altman, Higgins, Curtin, Worthington and Vail 2002, Meta-analyses involving cross-over trials: methodological issues, International Journal of Epidemiology 31:140-149
The standard reference for including crossover trials in a synthesis, setting out the options of imputing a within-participant correlation, using first-period data only, or excluding the trial, and treating the imputed correlation as a fixed input rather than as an estimated quantity carrying uncertainty.


Curtin, Elbourne and Altman 2002, Meta-analysis combining parallel and cross-over clinical trials. II: Binary outcomes, Statistics in Medicine 21:2145-2159
Derives the reconstruction of a crossover trial’s contrast and standard error from reported summaries under an assumed correlation, the calculation on which the assumption is operationalized; the resulting standard error is then conditioned on as known.


Curtin 2017, Meta-analysis combining parallel and crossover trials using generalised estimating equation method, Research Synthesis Methods 8
Combines aggregated results from crossover and parallel trials through a generalized estimating equation with a marginal estimation approach and can adjust for a carryover effect; it is a fixed-effects pairwise method, states that it is limited by the level of detail crossover reports usually give, and has not been carried into a network or evaluated for what it does to rankings.

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The machinery exists outside PAIC, so the task is to port and test rather than to invent. Apply Bayesian model averaging as practiced in meta-analysis to population-adjusted networks, and state which predictive unit the stacking weights target, since that choice defines the estimand. Test whether projection predictive selection and robust Bayesian analysis over model and prior classes actually restore coverage here rather than assuming they do. For bridges, build likelihood-based weights where candidates imply different observed-data predictions, reserve elicited priors over assumption plausibility for the observationally equivalent case, and feed existing diagnostics such as bridge fragility into the reported interval instead of reporting them beside it.

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
Our study

Choosing among population-adjustment models on the same data
The question put to it. When the adjustment model is chosen from the analyzed data, does the chosen model’s interval keep its coverage, and what does averaging over candidates change?
What it found. For choices among MAIC and STC specifications the candidates are close: choosing the most precise method covered 0.938 to 0.956, like a prespecified one. Choosing the most favorable estimate shifted it by up to 0.26 on the log odds ratio scale while its interval still covered 0.927 or more, because the favored method often had a wide interval. Averaging with between-model variance over-covered (up to 0.991) because the candidates share data; that difference makes the refuting sentence fail as registered.
Results.

Registered verdict FAILS, through the averaged interval’s coverage differing from the prespecified one’s by more than 0.03.
Selection by smallest SE: coverage 0.938 to 0.956, bias as the prespecified linear STC.
Selection by most favorable estimate: bias -0.046 to -0.259, coverage 0.927 to 0.960.
Equal-weight average with added between-model variance: coverage 0.949 to 0.991, the widest intervals.

Design.

Estimand

Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target (DIA-08)

Methods compared

prespecified linear STC, prespecified MAIC on means, selection by smallest SE, selection by most favorable estimate, equal-weight model averaging

Data-generating mechanism

Re-scoring of DIA-08’s stored replicates (16 scenarios x 2000) under prespecified, precision-selected, result-selected and averaged use of four adjustment methods.

Replicates

32,000 stored replicates from DIA-08 re-scored


What this does not answer. Outcome and weighting models only; treatment partitions and bridges not studied; equal weights. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: Model and bridge selection uncertainty never enters the interval
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source said. “Results are reported from one selected model or one selected bridge as if the selection step had not happened, so the interval omits the variability that the selection itself contributes.”
What was wrong with it. The source said reporting a single selected model understates uncertainty and that likelihood-based weights for bridge selection are not available at all. The code auditor narrowed both: post-selection distortion can run in either direction and does not arise for prespecified or externally chosen models, and likelihood-based weights do exist when candidate bridges imply different observed-data likelihoods or predictions, failing only for observationally equivalent assumptions; the literature auditor added that the entry carried no prior work despite an established model-averaging literature in evidence synthesis (Rover, Wandel and Friede 2019; Bartos et al., arXiv:2110.01076), and found no projection-predictive or robust-Bayes application to PAIC.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading.

merged-in

absorbed a proposal the reading raised separately: No criterion or uncertainty propagation for treatment-node granularity 6 citation(s) added. The drafter disagreed with placing it here: Four of the five readers had this accepted as a distinct problem and only one was judged a merge, and the two objects are not the same. MIS-04 concerns selection among statistical models and bridges fitted to a fixed data configuration, whereas the node partition determines which contrasts exist, which studies are usable and whether the network is connected at all, so candidate partitions cannot be compared by deviance or by any within-model criterion and averaging over them is not defined. The merged material also carries two demands MIS-04 does not make: a criterion stating when two arms may share a node, and a diagnostic for the equality that a merge asserts. It is recorded as a merge as directed.

merged-in

absorbed a proposal the reading raised separately: Crossover-trial reconstruction uncertainty is not propagated in NMA 4 citation(s) added. The drafter disagreed with placing it here: The merge is workable but the host is arguably wrong. MIS-04 is about selection among competing models and bridges using the analyzed data, whereas an imputed within-participant correlation is a fixed nuisance input used to reconstruct one study’s precision, which is the species of defect DEC-11 already names in its title as reconstruction error and OUT-13 treats for a different data source, digitized Kaplan-Meier curves. Recommend routing the addition to MIS-04 as the reviewer decided but cross-linking DEC-11 and OUT-13, since a reader looking for crossover reconstruction will look for it under reconstruction rather than under model selection.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: Simplifying fractional polynomials in Bayesian network meta-. New citations: 10.57264/cer-2025-0126

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The entry carries no prior_work at all, which understates a mature adjacent literature. Model averaging as a response to selection uncertainty in evidence synthesis is established: Rover, Wandel & Friede (2019), Stat Med, describe ‘heavy-tailed mixture priors for effect estimation in meta-analysis, which effectively results in a model-averaging technique… robust in the sense that a potential prior-data conflict… is explicitly anticipated’; also Bartos et al., ‘Bayesian Model-Averaged Meta-Analysis in Medicine’ (arXiv 2110.01076). So ‘Reporting a single selected model understates uncertainty’ is supported but generic, not a PAIC finding. I could not retrieve any source stating the second claim, that model averaging in network settings requires choosing a valid predictive unit for stacking weights; it is defensible on general grounds about leave-one-out stacking in hierarchical data, but I found nobody writing it for NMA, so treat it as the authors’ own argument rather than a sourced one. I found no projection-predictive or robust-Bayes application to PAIC. The bridge half is the genuinely novel and correct part: candidate bridges are competing identifying assumptions rather than nested models, so likelihood-based weights do not exist and averaging would need a prior on assumption plausibility. I found no work doing that.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is too categorical. If the same data select a model and ordinary conditional intervals are reported, nominal coverage is generally not guaranteed, but distortion may be in either direction; externally chosen or prespecified models do not create this post-selection problem. C2 is correct for predictive stacking: the held-out unit and dependence structure must match the intended prediction task. It is not a requirement of every form of model averaging, and patient-, contrast-, or study-level prediction are different estimands rather than an irresolvable ambiguity. C3 is plausible as a research direction, but projection predictive selection controls predictive loss rather than automatically delivering valid post-selection intervals, and robust Bayes addresses only the model or prior classes actually represented. Likelihood-based bridge weights are not universally unavailable: they can be formed when bridge models imply different observed-data likelihoods or predictions. They cannot learn the plausibility of observationally equivalent identifying assumptions, for which prior elicitation or sensitivity analysis is appropriate. At cpaic 9d150e9, loo() is explicitly observation-level and warns that it does not validate cross-gap prediction; prior_sensitivity() and bridge_fragility() provide diagnostics, but no model or bridge averaging enters the reported effect interval. The interval problem therefore remains open, but it is decision-critical mainly after material data-adaptive selection or when conclusions are sensitive to the bridge.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text: MIS-02 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text:
Statement
For survival outcomes, censoring that depends on covariates adds a weighting or modeling layer on top of transport adjustment. Yan et al. (2025, doi:10.1002/pst.70029) built that estimator: TADA multiplies time-varying inverse-probability-of-censoring weights by method-of-moments participation weights and estimates variance by nonparametric bootstrap, evaluated in an ADEMP simulation study, so the construction is done for the unanchored survival transport case under conditionally independent censoring, positivity, and correctly specified nuisance models. What is not done is the robustness characterization, which the paper itself lists as future work: sandwich variance under heavy censoring, non-proportional-hazards censoring models, and doubly robust protection against partial misspecification of either weighting component. Sampling error in the published target moments is also not propagated, because the method of moments conditions on them, and censoring driven by unmeasured event prognosis stays unidentified without a sensitivity parameter.

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text:
Why it is open
Survival PAIC has to reweight to a target covariate distribution and correct for covariate-dependent censoring at the same time, and the estimator that does both is one paper old. Its behavior under censoring-model misspecification, heavy censoring, and non-proportional hazards is unmapped, and overlap is not examined anywhere in the source paper. The censoring mechanism is usually unverifiable from published data, and the covariates driving censoring are often not the ones reported for the target population, so the censoring model cannot be calibrated to the target. Censoring that depends on unmeasured prognosis is not identified from observed data at all, so it needs an assumption or a sensitivity parameter rather than a better model.

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Yan, Vuong, Metcalfe, Guan, Shi and Park 2025, Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data From the Target Population
TADA, a two-stage weighting framework whose final weights are the product of time-varying inverse-probability-of-censoring weights and participation weights derived by the method of moments, with nonparametric bootstrap variance and an ADEMP simulation study; it states that aggregate-data transportability methods under informative censoring remain underexplored, and it does not identify censoring driven by unmeasured event prognosis, does not propagate sampling error in the supplied target summaries, and leaves sandwich variance, non-proportional-hazards censoring models, and doubly robust extensions to future work

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The estimator exists, so the work is characterization rather than construction. Run TADA under censoring-model misspecification, weak overlap, and non-proportional hazards, and compare bootstrap variance against sandwich or stacked M-estimation under heavy censoring, which the authors name as their own next step. Add doubly robust or semiparametric versions that survive partial misspecification of either weighting component, and extend the variance to carry sampling error in the published target summaries instead of conditioning on them. Supply an explicit sensitivity parameter for censoring that depends on unmeasured prognosis.

title: No robustness theory for censoring-weighted survival transport
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “Informative censoring compounds transport weighting in survival PAIC” The title presents the compounding of censoring and transport weights as unsolved, but TADA already builds, bootstraps and evaluates that estimator.
The source said. “For survival outcomes, informative censoring adds a further weighting or modeling layer on top of transport weighting and imputation, and the combined variance has to account for the estimation of both weight systems plus the estimated target summaries. Combining target-summary calibration with censoring adjustment is recent rather than settled.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no standard variance formula covers the product of the two weight systems and treated the joint approach as recent rather than settled. Both auditors rejected the variance claim: TADA (doi:10.1002/pst.70029) already estimates variance by nonparametric bootstrap, and stacked M-estimation or sandwich influence functions can also cover product weights; the code auditor added that TADA is an operational solution under its stated assumptions rather than an untested attempt, and what genuinely goes unpropagated is the sampling error in the published target moments.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Read the full text of Yan, Vuong, Metcalfe, Guan, Shi & Park (2025) via PMC12326296. Every attribution is accurate. TADA is a ‘two-stage weighting framework named Target Aggregate Data Adjustment (TADA) that can simultaneously adjust for both censoring bias and distributional imbalances of effect modifiers… the final weights are the product of the time-varying inverse probability of censoring weights and participation weights derived using the method of moments.’ The paper itself asserts the absence the entry describes: ‘AgD-based transportability methods in the presence of informative-censoring remain underexplored.’ Two corrections to the entry’s why_open. First, TADA does propagate uncertainty across both weight systems: ‘We are estimating the variance of [the log hazard ratio] using a nonparametric bootstrap method’, so ‘no standard variance formula covers the product’ is too strong; what is not propagated is the sampling error in the published target moments, which the method of moments treats as fixed. Second, the entry’s claimed uncharacterized behaviors are confirmed by the paper’s own discussion: sandwich variance under heavy censoring, non-PH censoring models, and doubly robust or semiparametric protection against ‘partial misspecification of either weighting component’ are all listed as future work, and the word overlap does not appear anywhere in the text. codex dissented (supported-with-caveat): C1 is technically correct when censoring is conditionally independent only after adjustment for observed variables: an IPCW factor may multiply the transport weight, or the two mechanisms may be handled through outcome or joint modeling. C2 is correct: TADA combines method-of-moments participation weights with time-varying censoring weights. C3 is proportionate only as a statement about remaining scope. TADA is an operational solution under conditional independent censoring, positivity, correct nuisance-model specification, and its defined target; it is not merely an untested attempt. Arbitrary dependent censoring remains unidentified without additional assumptions or sensitivity parameters. The claim that no standard variance method covers product weights is false: stacked M-estimation, sandwich influence functions, and a bootstrap that re-estimates both nuisance systems can do so. Target-summary sampling variability additionally matters when the estimand is defined for a superpopulation rather than conditional on the supplied summaries. cpaic does not solve informative censoring: its survival likelihood uses censoring contributions but does not model the censoring process. This is high priority only where censoring is plausibly informative and consequential.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported. Read the full text of Yan, Vuong, Metcalfe, Guan, Shi & Park (2025) via PMC12326296. Every attribution is accurate. TADA is a ‘two-stage weighting framework named Target Aggregate Data Adjustment (TADA) that can simultaneously adjust for both censoring bias and distributional imbalances of effect modifiers… the final weights are the product of the time-varying inverse probability of censoring weights and participation weights derived using the method of moments.’ The paper itself asserts the absence the entry describes: ‘AgD-based transportability methods in the presence of informative-censoring remain underexplored.’ Two corrections to the entry’s why_open. First, TADA does propagate uncertainty across both weight systems: ‘We are estimating the variance of [the log hazard ratio] using a nonparametric bootstrap method’, so ‘no standard variance formula covers the product’ is too strong; what is not propagated is the sampling error in the published target moments, which the method of moments treats as fixed. Second, the entry’s claimed uncharacterized behaviors are confirmed by the paper’s own discussion: sandwich variance under heavy censoring, non-PH censoring models, and doubly robust or semiparametric protection against ‘partial misspecification of either weighting component’ are all listed as future work, and the word overlap does not appear anywhere in the text. Cites doi:10.1002/pst.70029: Delivers the joint censoring-plus-transport weighting estimator with bootstrap variance and an ADEMP simulation study, so the core construction is done for the unanchored survival transport case; the robustness characterization the entry asks for is not..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1 is technically correct when censoring is conditionally independent only after adjustment for observed variables: an IPCW factor may multiply the transport weight, or the two mechanisms may be handled through outcome or joint modeling. C2 is correct: TADA combines method-of-moments participation weights with time-varying censoring weights. C3 is proportionate only as a statement about remaining scope. TADA is an operational solution under conditional independent censoring, positivity, correct nuisance-model specification, and its defined target; it is not merely an untested attempt. Arbitrary dependent censoring remains unidentified without additional assumptions or sensitivity parameters. The claim that no standard variance method covers product weights is false: stacked M-estimation, sandwich influence functions, and a bootstrap that re-estimates both nuisance systems can do so. Target-summary sampling variability additionally matters when the estimand is defined for a superpopulation rather than conditional on the supplied summaries. cpaic does not solve informative censoring: its survival likelihood uses censoring contributions but does not model the censoring process. This is high priority only where censoring is plausibly informative and consequential. Cites doi:10.1002/pst.70029: Provides an operational survival transport estimator combining time-varying inverse-probability-of-censoring weights with target-summary participation weights and uses bootstrap variance estimation. It does not identify censoring dependent on unmeasured event prognosis or propagate target-summary sampling error automatically..

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text: IDN-20 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text:
Statement
Network meta-analysis is usually justified by joint randomizability, the claim that any patient in the network could in principle have been randomized to any of the compared treatments, but in many networks whole treatments are contraindicated for identifiable subsets of patients, so the claim is false by construction rather than merely uncertain. The trial-design literature has already stated the weaker sufficient condition: in a personalized randomized trial, where each patient is randomized only among the treatments they are eligible for, transitivity need hold only over the treatments not contraindicated for a given eligibility pattern, which is equivalent to requiring treatment effects to be common across patterns (Lee et al. 2023, doi:10.1002/sim.9663, on the design of Walker et al. 2021, doi:10.1016/S1473-3099(20)30791-X). Evidence synthesis has no corresponding statement. A pooled network estimate for a contrast is silently defined over whichever trial populations happened to admit both treatments, and there is no convention naming that sub-population, no diagnostic for how far eligibility patterns differ across the trials informing a contrast, and no way to report contrast-specific eligibility restrictions beside the estimate. Because the restriction differs by contrast, a single network-level target population statement cannot express it, so two contrasts in the same network can refer to non-overlapping sub-populations while appearing in the same league table and the same ranking. This is not covariate overlap: overlap is a support problem in covariate space that weighting or standardization can diagnose, whereas an eligibility restriction removes a treatment from a patient’s choice set entirely, so there is no covariate distribution over which the excluded contrast is even defined.

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text:
Why it is open
Eligibility restrictions are properties of the protocol rather than of measured baseline covariates, so covariate balancing and population adjustment cannot recover them, and published reports give inclusion and exclusion criteria as prose rather than as an extractable eligibility pattern. The trial-design solution works because each patient’s eligible set is observed; a synthesis of published trials observes only the union of criteria for a whole trial, so the distribution of patterns within a trial is unavailable and the sub-population a contrast refers to cannot be characterized from the record. Naming the sub-population per contrast also conflicts with the output format the field uses, since league tables and rankings presuppose one population, and a ranking over treatments whose contrasts refer to different sub-populations has no clear interpretation; adopting the honest estimand would mean changing what is reported. Adjacent machinery exists in target trial emulation, where eligibility is specified explicitly as part of the protocol, but it has not been brought to network synthesis and nobody has shown which parts survive when only trial-level criteria are observed. The problem is invisible in practice because contraindications appear as exclusion criteria that vary across trials for reasons indistinguishable from ordinary heterogeneity.

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Lee, Turner, Thwaites, Walker and White 2023, The Personalised Randomized Controlled Trial: Evaluation of a new trial design, Statistics in Medicine 42:1156-1170
States that joint randomizability and transitivity are clearly false when contraindicated treatments are not given, and supplies the weaker sufficient condition, transitivity restricted to non-contraindicated treatments within an eligibility pattern, together with analysis methods and a simulation of the resulting bias-variance trade-off.


Walker, White, Turner, Hsu et al. 2021, Personalised randomised controlled trial designs: a new paradigm to define optimal treatments for carbapenem-resistant infections, Lancet Infectious Diseases 21:e175-e181
Proposes the design in which each patient receives a personalized randomization list of the regimens they are eligible for, making the eligibility pattern an observed variable; this is the observability that a synthesis of published trials lacks.


Salanti 2012, Indirect and mixed-treatment comparison, network, or multiple-treatments meta-analysis: many names, many benefits, many concerns for the next generation evidence synthesis tool, Research Synthesis Methods 3:80-97
The statement of joint randomizability and transitivity that network meta-analysis is conventionally justified by, and the source of the phrasing that a patient could in principle be randomized to any of the alternative treatment options.


Hernan and Robins 2016, Using Big Data to Emulate a Target Trial When a Randomized Trial Is Not Available, American Journal of Epidemiology 183:758-764
Requires eligibility criteria to be specified explicitly as a protocol component of the estimand; this is the closest existing template for making the eligible population part of what an estimate is labeled with, and it has not been applied at the level of a network contrast.


Donegan, Williamson, D’Alessandro and Tudur Smith 2013, Assessing key assumptions of network meta-analysis: a review of methods, Research Synthesis Methods 4:291-323
Reviews the methods available for checking the assumptions underlying network meta-analysis; none of them examines whether the trials informing a contrast admitted comparable sets of eligible patients.

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define the contrast-specific estimand: for each contrast the target is the sub-population eligible for both treatments, and a network estimate should carry that sub-population as part of its label rather than inherit the network’s nominal population. Extract eligibility patterns as data by coding each trial’s inclusion and exclusion criteria into a structured eligibility vector over the network’s treatments, which is a coding exercise on existing publications, and report the overlap of those vectors across the trials informing each contrast as a routine diagnostic. Import the weaker sufficient condition from the personalized randomized trial literature and state its synthesis analogue explicitly, namely transitivity restricted to eligibility patterns with effects assumed common across patterns, so the assumption can be relaxed and checked where patterns are crossed. Say what a league table means when its cells refer to different sub-populations, either by restricting the table to a common eligibility pattern or by annotating each cell with the pattern it is defined over, and treat any ranking computed across patterns as uninterpretable until that is settled. Reporting eligibility in machine-readable form is the only route that would make the within-trial pattern distribution recoverable, and it has to be asked of trialists rather than solved by analysts.

title: No synthesis framework for treatment-specific eligibility patterns
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single trial-design paper, and the reviewer accepted structural treatment ineligibility as more specific than generic transitivity uncertainty, covariate overlap or an unnamed single target population, while asking that the claim of no relevant treatment-choice or target-trial literature be qualified. The identification result exists on the trial-design side; the absence of any synthesis-side statement rests on the reader’s search rather than on a source asserting it, which makes this the weaker half of the claim.

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text: IDN-18 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text:
Statement
In a randomized-withdrawal maintenance design the maintenance-phase placebo arm consists of patients who responded to the trial’s own active drug during induction and were then re-randomized off it, so its outcomes are a function of that drug’s off-treatment durability rather than of an untreated course. Anchoring two such trials on their withdrawal arms therefore violates the requirement that the common comparator be the same condition in both, and the violation is signed: the trial whose drug has the longer off-drug effect records the higher comparator response and hence the smaller active-minus-comparator contrast, so the anchored comparison penalizes durability even when on-treatment effects are identical. The magnitudes are not small; in one atopic dermatitis pair, maintenance of response at week 52 in the withdrawal arms was 56 percent against 30 percent for one endpoint and 40 percent against 14 percent for another (doi:10.1007/s13555-025-01622-9), and the risk ratios between the two withdrawal arms were reported as 1.995 and 3.724 (doi:10.1007/s13555-024-01107-1). No estimand definition states what a withdrawal-anchored contrast identifies, no sensitivity parameter indexes the residual index-treatment effect carried by the anchor arm, and no rule says when a withdrawal arm may be treated as placebo, so the dispute is settled by assertion: one side argues that the arms are demonstrably different, the other that pharmacokinetics leave no active drug at 36 weeks, and the raw between-arm difference is cited as decisive when it also contains the population imbalance that anchoring exists to absorb. Randomized-withdrawal maintenance designs are standard in atopic dermatitis, chronic pain and other chronic indications, so this is a recurring structural feature of the evidence base rather than one contested analysis, and the same argument has now run through two published exchanges over the same treatment pair.

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text:
Why it is open
The contamination is a property of the design rather than of the patients, so covariate balancing, weighting and outcome regression cannot reach it, and the quantity that would index it, the residual effect of the index treatment inside its own withdrawal arm, is never observed because no untreated control is carried through the maintenance phase. Separating that residue from ordinary between-trial population differences would require a third arm or an external reference that these designs do not supply, so the two candidate explanations for a between-trial difference in withdrawal-arm response are not identified apart. Pharmacological argument cannot settle it either, because the biasing quantity is a persisting biological effect rather than detectable drug, so an argument from half-life addresses a different quantity than the one that moves the contrast. The alternative on offer, an unanchored comparison, exchanges a signed and possibly modest bias for an unsigned and possibly large one, and nothing prices that exchange. The problem also has no owner, falling between trial design, where the withdrawal arm is a legitimate control for the trial’s own question, and evidence synthesis, where it is silently reused as a common comparator.

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Stander, Pinter, Hougeir, Guyot et al. 2025, Dupilumab versus Lebrikizumab Demonstrates Greater Likelihood of Achieving and Maintaining Improvements in Efficacy Outcomes Using a Placebo-Adjusted Indirect Treatment Comparison, Dermatology and Therapy 15:2537-2551
Runs a placebo-adjusted Bucher indirect comparison whose maintenance-phase common comparator is the two trials’ treatment-withdrawal arms, the analysis that made the design’s anchoring problem concrete.


Chovatiya, Seminario-Vidal, Gallo, Ding et al. 2025, Letter to the Editor regarding the placebo-adjusted indirect treatment comparison of dupilumab versus lebrikizumab, Dermatology and Therapy 16:1427-1431
States the direction of the bias, that using withdrawal arms as a true placebo penalizes the drug with greater off-drug durability even if on-drug effects are equal, and reports the withdrawal-arm maintenance rates (56 versus 30 percent and 40 versus 14 percent) that motivate the concern.


Stander, Pinter, Hougeir, Guyot et al. 2025, A Response to the Letter to the Editor regarding the placebo-adjusted indirect treatment comparison of dupilumab versus lebrikizumab, Dermatology and Therapy 16:1433-1437
The reply defending the withdrawal-anchored comparison; the exchange ends without any data-based adjudication because neither side has a quantity to estimate.


Rand, Ramos-Goni, Akmaz, Sole-Feu and Armario-Hita 2023, Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison of the Long-Term Efficacy Maintenance and Adverse Event Rates of Lebrikizumab versus Dupilumab in Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis, Dermatology and Therapy
The earlier analysis that took the opposite route, treating the withdrawal arms as unsuitable for anchoring and running an unanchored MAIC instead; the same design feature drives both decisions.


Bastian, Freemantle, Rossi, Shumel et al. 2024, Letter to the Editor regarding the matching-adjusted indirect comparison of lebrikizumab versus dupilumab in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, Dermatology and Therapy 14:819-821
Argues that pharmacokinetic profiles imply no active substance is detectable 36 weeks after withdrawal, so the placebo data could and should have been used for anchoring; this is the argument from drug concentration rather than from persisting effect.


Rand, Ramos-Goni, Akmaz, Sole-Feu and Armario-Hita 2024, Response to the Letter to the Editor regarding the matching-adjusted indirect comparison of lebrikizumab versus dupilumab in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, Dermatology and Therapy 14:823-827
Replies with risk ratios of 1.995 and 3.724 between the two withdrawal arms as evidence that they are not a common comparator; the comparison is naive, so it also carries the population difference that an anchored analysis is supposed to remove.


Moore, Wiffen, Eccleston, Derry and Baron 2015, Systematic review of enriched enrolment, randomised withdrawal trial designs in chronic pain, Pain 156:1382-1395
Catalogues enriched-enrolment randomized-withdrawal trials in a second therapeutic area, showing that the design and its variability in conduct and reporting are widespread rather than confined to one indication.


Bucher, Guyatt, Griffith and Walter 1997, The results of direct and indirect treatment comparisons in meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 50:683-691
The anchored comparison being applied, whose validity requires the common comparator to be the same condition in both trials; nothing in the method detects when it is not.

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define the estimand a withdrawal-anchored contrast identifies by writing the withdrawal-arm mean as an untreated maintenance outcome plus a residual index-treatment effect, so the bias of the Bucher contrast becomes an explicit function of the difference in residual effects between the two trials rather than a matter of opinion. Supply a sensitivity parameter for that difference, report the contrast across a range of it, and state the tipping point at which the conclusion changes; this is bias-parameter analysis of a familiar form and needs no new estimator. Elicit plausible ranges from relapse-time and pharmacodynamic evidence rather than from half-life, since the biasing quantity is persistence of effect and not persistence of drug. State a decision rule for the design: where the residual-effect difference cannot be bounded below the tipping point, report the anchored and unanchored analyses together rather than choosing between them. For trials still being planned, an untreated or long-washout maintenance arm, or reporting of relapse curves by induction treatment, would make the residual effect estimable and is the only route that removes the assumption instead of parameterizing it.

title: No estimand or correction for randomized-withdrawal anchors
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a published exchange of letters rather than from methodological work, and the reviewer accepted it as more specific than generic comparator-context heterogeneity while noting that a usable framework would have to distinguish pharmacologically negligible carryover from material residual durability. No methodological paper addresses withdrawal-arm anchors at all, so the evidence is applied correspondence in which the two sides reach opposite conclusions with no data-based adjudication available to either.

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text: IDN-16 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text:
Statement
When a network meta-analysis includes treatment-by-covariate interactions, the direct-indirect discrepancy is itself a function of the covariate, so the output of a consistency assessment is a set of covariate values over which the model’s estimates may be used rather than a single pass or fail. No procedure defines that set formally. In the demonstration that established the phenomenon, the region was read off a handful of integer covariate values using pointwise two-sample tests at a 10 percent level chosen to err on the side of caution, with no adjustment for testing several comparisons at several covariate values, no evaluation of power against a covariate-dependent discrepancy, and no stated rule for propagation, even though a single failure at age 1 in one comparison was taken to bring the results at that covariate value for every comparison into question (Donegan et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1257). What does not exist is an estimand for the licensed region, a selection procedure with a stated error rate over the covariate range and over the comparisons tested, and any evaluation of how often such a procedure recovers the true region. The decision consequence is direct, because the region determines which patients an interaction network meta-analysis is permitted to make recommendations for, and a region chosen by uncorrected pointwise testing will be too small where the covariate is finely sampled and too large where power is low. Only Bonferroni correction has been offered as an aid, and it has never been evaluated in this setting.

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text:
Why it is open
The quantity being selected is a set rather than a parameter, so ordinary error control does not transfer: what needs controlling is the probability that the reported region contains covariate values at which the direct and indirect evidence in fact conflict, and that criterion has not been written down. The tests are correlated in two directions at once, across covariate values within a comparison and across comparisons through the shared network structure, so a correction that treats them as independent is wrong by an amount that depends on the design matrix. Power is worst exactly where the region’s boundary sits, because the boundary is where the discrepancy crosses zero, so the covariate values that determine the answer are the ones the test can least resolve. Interaction networks are rare and usually require individual patient data, so there is very little material on which a procedure could be evaluated; the originating demonstration used one 17-site individual-patient dataset with four treatments. Nothing forces the issue, because reporting a covariate range is not required: an interaction network meta-analysis can present estimates across the whole observed covariate range without stating where consistency was assessed at all.

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Donegan, Welton, Tudur Smith, D’Alessandro and Dias 2017, Network meta-analysis including treatment by covariate interactions: Consistency can vary across covariate values, Research Synthesis Methods 8:485-495
Establishes that consistency is covariate-dependent, assesses it by visual inspection, inconsistency estimates and pointwise tests at a 10 percent level across selected covariate values, names the multiple-testing problem, and offers Bonferroni correction as an untested aid.


Donegan, Williamson, D’Alessandro and Tudur Smith 2013, Assessing key assumptions of network meta-analysis: a review of methods, Research Synthesis Methods 4:291-323
Catalogues the available methods for checking similarity, homogeneity and consistency; none of them defines a covariate region over which the network’s estimates are licensed.


Cooper, Sutton, Morris, Ades and Welton 2009, Addressing between-study heterogeneity and inconsistency in mixed treatment comparisons: Application to stroke prevention treatments in individuals with non-rheumatic atrial fibrillation, Statistics in Medicine 28:1861-1881
Sets out the network meta-regression models with treatment-by-covariate interactions in which the problem arises, including the shared-interaction and independent-interaction variants.


Potthoff 1964, On the Johnson-Neyman Technique and Some Extensions Thereof, Psychometrika 29:241-256
The existing formal machinery for exactly this shape of problem outside evidence synthesis: a region of a moderator over which a contrast is declared non-null, with simultaneous rather than pointwise error control; it has not been adapted to a network where comparisons are correlated through the design matrix.


Phillippo, Dias, Ades, Welton et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis, Medical Decision Making
Assesses residual heterogeneity and inconsistency inside a covariate-adjusted network model and relaxes the shared interaction assumption one covariate at a time; the assessment is model-level rather than a region over covariate values.


multinma R package, nma(consistency = “nodesplit”) with a regression formula
Allows a node split to be fitted inside a covariate-adjusted network model, so a covariate-indexed inconsistency estimate can be produced; it reports the estimate rather than selecting a region with a controlled error rate.

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define the estimand first: the licensed region is the set of covariate values at which the direct-indirect discrepancy is within a stated tolerance, and a procedure should be judged by the probability that the region it reports contains no value where the discrepancy exceeds that tolerance, not by pointwise p-values at selected integers. Build the selection procedure from simultaneous inference over the covariate range rather than from pointwise tests, taking the Johnson-Neyman construction and its simultaneous extensions as the template and carrying the correlation across comparisons induced by the network’s design matrix. Evaluate it against a known answer: generate networks with a covariate-dependent inconsistency of known support and report how often the recovered region admits a true conflict and how much of the true licensed region it discards, as functions of network size, covariate range and interaction magnitude. Fix the propagation rule explicitly, since a failure at one covariate value in one comparison currently invalidates all comparisons at that value by argument rather than by a stated criterion. Finally, require an interaction network meta-analysis to report the covariate range over which consistency was assessed alongside any estimate it presents.

title: Covariate-indexed consistency has no calibrated licensed region
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single methodological paper, and the reviewer accepted it as a distinct inferential problem created by testing consistency across a covariate continuum. The evidence for the gap is the originating work’s own limitations, namely a named multiplicity problem, an untested Bonferroni suggestion and a single-dataset demonstration, rather than an independent survey or a failed attempt at a solution.
