title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text: HET-19 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Tractability 4/5

title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text:
Statement
When the comparison being split appears in k multi-arm trials that contain both of its treatments, the network of indirect evidence can be parameterized in 2^k + 1 non-equivalent ways: 2^k mixtures of dropping one or the other of the two treatments trial by trial, plus a single model that drops both from every such trial. These are not relabelings of one another; they use different data and give different indirect estimates, different inconsistency p-values and different heterogeneity estimates, and the choice of which arm to retain can change the results even when every option yields an indirect estimate at all. Exploring the whole family is described as generally infeasible, and even fitting the two pure options is treated as undesirable on computational grounds, so in practice one member is chosen arbitrarily; gemtc generates the model that drops both split treatments from multi-arm trials, which is the member that retains the least evidence. No rule selects among the parameterizations, no aggregation across them has been defined, no study reports how far conclusions move over the family, and no implementation reports more than one. Because a node-splitting p-value functions in practice as a gate on whether a network meta-analysis may be reported at all, that gate rests on a modeling choice that is neither justified nor disclosed.

title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text:
Why it is open
The alternatives are not nested and do not condition on the same data, so the usual model-selection apparatus does not apply: information criteria would compare fits to different datasets, and averaging estimates that use different evidence has no agreed target. The family grows exponentially in the number of multi-arm trials carrying the split comparison, which puts exhaustive fitting out of reach for the Bayesian implementations that dominate applied use, and no cheap approximation to the spread has been derived. The global alternatives that sidestep the ambiguity, notably the design-by-treatment interaction model, answer a different question, testing the network rather than localizing a conflict to a comparison, so they do not remove the demand for a per-comparison split. And nobody has measured the spread, so there is no evidence that the problem is large; measuring it is the missing first step rather than a preliminary to a fix that already exists.

title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




van Valkenhoef, Dias, Ades and Welton 2015, Research Synthesis Methods
Proves an unambiguous decision rule for which comparisons to split and shows model generation is trivial for those comparisons, while stating that the parameterization ambiguity survives: the family has 2^k + 1 members, exploring it is generally infeasible, one member is chosen arbitrarily in practice, and gemtc generates the option that includes neither split treatment from multi-arm trials.


Dias, Welton, Caldwell and Ades 2010, Statistics in Medicine
The original node-splitting method for checking consistency in mixed treatment comparisons, in which only the two pure arm-dropping options are considered and the mixtures are not raised.


Dias, Welton, Sutton, Caldwell, Lu and Ades 2013, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD 4)
The applied protocol for assessing inconsistency in networks of interventions, which is what turns a node-splitting p-value into a gate on reporting and therefore what makes the parameterization choice decision-relevant.


van Valkenhoef, Lu, de Brock, Hillege, Ades and Welton 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Automates model generation for network meta-analysis and establishes that basic-parameter choice is arbitrary for consistency models but not for inconsistency models, which is the asymmetry that creates the node-splitting ambiguity.


Higgins, Jackson, Barrett, Lu, Ades and White 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
The design-by-treatment interaction model, a global inconsistency test that handles multi-arm trials without an arm-dropping choice; it avoids the ambiguity but does not localize inconsistency to a comparison.


White, Barrett, Jackson and Higgins 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Estimates the design-by-treatment interaction model by multivariate meta-regression, the frequentist implementation of the global alternative that applied reviewers run alongside node splitting.


Tu 2016, Value in Health
Recasts node splitting as a generalized linear mixed model, an estimation route fast enough that fitting several members of the family becomes practical rather than prohibitive.


Veroniki, Vasiliadis, Higgins and Salanti 2013, International Journal of Epidemiology
Evaluates inconsistency across published networks with several methods and shows detection depends on the method chosen, establishing that inconsistency conclusions are already known to be fragile to analytic choices.


gemtc: Network Meta-Analysis Using Bayesian Methods, CRAN
The implementation in which the parameterization is fixed: node-splitting models are generated by dropping both split treatments from multi-arm trials, so an applied user cannot see the alternatives without writing their own model.

title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Measure the spread before proposing a rule: on a database of published networks, enumerate the family wherever k is small enough to fit exhaustively and sample the mixtures where it is not, then report the range of the inconsistency p-value, the indirect estimate and the heterogeneity estimate across the family, together with how often the gate decision at conventional thresholds changes. If the spread is material, define the target explicitly rather than by default, either a single defensible member such as the mixture that maximizes the evidence retained in the indirect network, which is computable from the graph before any model is fitted, or a summary across the family under a stated weighting. Report the spread rather than a point in any case, since a p-value that moves across the family is itself the finding a reader needs. The enabling software step is to let implementations expose the choice: the dominant package fixes one member, so nothing else can be reported until the pure and mixed options are generated and summarized together.

title: Node splitting reports one arbitrary member of a family of multi-arm parameterizations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it because the arm representation chosen for multi-arm trials can change the indirect evidence and hence the local inconsistency result. The evidence is a single paper, but it is the definitive treatment of node-splitting model generation, it enumerates the family and states that the choice is made arbitrarily, and no later work reports how far conclusions move across it.

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text: HET-17 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text:
Statement
A sequential monitoring boundary for a cumulative or living network meta-analysis is a function of the statistical information accumulated so far against a maximum information target, and both quantities depend directly on the between-study heterogeneity variance. In the early updates that decide when a boundary is first crossed, that variance is estimated from a handful of trials and is unstable, so re-estimating it at every update makes the boundary itself a noisy random object, while fixing it at an external value makes the stopping decision partly an artifact of an imported constant. The leading empirical evaluation of living network meta-analysis took the second route across 49 comparisons from 44 networks, imputing the heterogeneity variance at the median of the empirical Cochrane predictive distributions, 0.049, for the primary analysis and re-estimating it only in sensitivity analysis, and it named the appropriate handling of heterogeneity in a sequential meta-analysis as an outstanding methodological priority. No method establishes how heterogeneity should enter a sequential network boundary, how the stopping decision inherits heterogeneity uncertainty, or what type I error is actually realized under either convention. The question compounds in a network relative to a pairwise sequential analysis, because a single network-wide variance sets the information clock for every comparison at once and indirect evidence contributes through the same parameter.

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text:
Why it is open
The two available answers fail in opposite directions and nothing arbitrates between them: a plug-in estimate makes maximum information a random variable that the alpha-spending calculus treats as fixed, while an imported constant fixes it at a value the accumulating data may contradict, and both choices are made before the boundary has any data to be judged against. Sequential methods for random-effects meta-analysis exist in the pairwise case, including a treatment that carries uncertainty in the heterogeneity parameter and the trial sequential analysis convention of inflating required information by a heterogeneity or diversity factor, but neither has been carried into a network where one variance serves many comparisons and where information arrives along indirect paths the analyst never planned. Establishing the realized error rate requires simulating the entire update process including the arrival order of trials, so the evaluation is expensive and its answer depends on arrival assumptions that are themselves unvalidated. Living reviews are run as a service commitment rather than as a methods project, so their operators need software now and adopt whatever convention the available package implements.

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis, Furukawa, Cipriani, Tricco, Straus, Siontis, Egger and Salanti 2018, BMJ
Compares living network with living pairwise meta-analysis across 49 comparisons from 44 networks using alpha-spending monitoring boundaries, imputes the heterogeneity variance at the empirical median of 0.049 for the primary analysis, and states that the most appropriate approach to dealing with heterogeneity in a sequential meta-analysis is an outstanding priority.


Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis, Egger and Salanti 2018, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
Adapts alpha-spending sequential monitoring to continuously updated network meta-analysis, defining the statistical information and maximum information used to construct the boundaries; the method whose heterogeneity handling is unresolved.


Higgins, Whitehead and Simmonds 2011, Statistics in Medicine
Develops sequential methods for random-effects meta-analysis, including treatments that acknowledge the heterogeneity parameter is estimated rather than known; the pairwise precursor that has not been extended to a network.


Wetterslev, Thorlund, Brok and Gluud 2009, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Defines required information size in trial sequential analysis inflated by a measure of between-trial variation, the established pairwise convention for letting heterogeneity enter an information target.


Simmonds, Salanti, McKenzie and Elliott 2017, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Reviews statistical methods for updating meta-analyses in living systematic reviews, including repeated testing and its error control, without settling how heterogeneity should be handled across updates.


Turner, Jackson, Wei, Thompson and Higgins 2015, Statistics in Medicine
The empirical predictive distributions whose median supplied the imported heterogeneity value used in the living network evaluation; the source of the constant whose influence on the stopping decision has not been measured.


Salanti, Nikolakopoulou, Sutton, Reichenbach, Trelle, Naci and Egger 2018, Trials
Plans a future randomized trial from a network of past trials using the same information accounting, so it shares the dependence on the heterogeneity assumption and shows the decision consequences reach study design as well as reporting.

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Simulate the update process rather than argue about it: generate networks with known heterogeneity, add trials in realistic arrival orders, and compare three rules, re-estimating at every update, fixing at an empirical median, and carrying a prior on the variance and spending alpha against the posterior predictive information, on realized type I error, power and expected time to boundary crossing. Derive a boundary that treats heterogeneity as uncertain rather than known, for example by defining maximum information through the posterior predictive precision so the boundary widens while the variance is poorly determined and tightens as it becomes identified. Report a heterogeneity-adjusted repeated confidence interval alongside any boundary crossing, so a stopping claim can be inspected for its dependence on the assumed variance rather than presented as a binary. Then ship the surviving rule in the software that living reviews actually run, because the convention in force today is whichever one the package defaults to.

title: Heterogeneity has no principled place in a sequential or living NMA boundary
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it because heterogeneity affects both information accumulation and the stopping boundary, and its uncertainty is most consequential early in a living network. The direct evidence is a single paper, but it is the field’s main empirical evaluation of living network meta-analysis, it had to sidestep the problem by imputation, and it names the gap as a priority.

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text: HET-15 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text:
Statement
Networks increasingly turn on comparator nodes that are mixtures rather than treatments: best available therapy, standard of care, conventional care, physician’s choice, best supportive care. Trials normally report the composition of that mixture, and it varies widely across them; in a polycythemia vera feasibility assessment the hydroxyurea share of best available therapy ran from 25% to 97% across six studies, with the remainder differing in interferon, anagrelide, pipobroman, immunomodulators and no active treatment. Current practice collapses each such node to a single vertex, which voids the protection the anchored design is supposed to give, because the anchor is a different intervention in each trial; population adjustment cannot repair it either, since the difference lies in the comparator regimen rather than in patient characteristics. The reported composition is usable information, and what is missing is a model that represents the node as a mixture over its constituent treatments with the reported proportions entering as data, a diagnostic that quantifies how far the target contrast moves over the observed composition spread, and a rule stating when the spread is large enough that the node must be split or the synthesis abandoned. Without those three, the only available responses are to assume the mixture away or to declare the network infeasible, which is what the polycythemia vera assessment did despite being able to construct a connected network. Pragmatic control arms are becoming more common, so the number of networks that hinge on such a node is growing.

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text:
Why it is open
Component and additive network models decompose an intervention that every patient in the arm received, whereas a composite comparator is a distribution over patients within a single arm, so the arm-level effect is a weighted average of constituent effects with weights that differ by study; the constituent effects are identified only insofar as those constituents also appear elsewhere in the network as nodes of their own. Where the mixture contains something that appears nowhere else, or where composition is confounded with calendar era or geography, the decomposition is not identified from the network at all and only bounds are available. The reported proportions describe treatment received rather than randomized allocation, so a mixture model built on them combines a randomized contrast with an observational one, a modeling decision that no existing method has had to price. Extraction is a further obstacle: composition appears in baseline tables in idiosyncratic formats, sometimes only for the most frequent components, and there is no reporting item that requires it, so the data that would drive the model are not collected systematically even though they are printed in the source publications.

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Walden, Hummel, Kopiec, Maliszewska and Naslazi 2025, Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research
Tabulates the composition of the best-available-therapy arm in each polycythemia vera trial, showing hydroxyurea shares from 25% to 97%, and concludes that the shared comparator does not represent a consistent treatment context, so the network was judged infeasible despite being connected.


Welton, Caldwell, Adamopoulos and Vedhara 2009, American Journal of Epidemiology
Introduces mixed treatment comparison models for complex interventions in which the effect of a multi-component intervention is built from component effects; the additive machinery a mixture node model would adapt.


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
Develops frequentist component network meta-analysis for multicomponent interventions with additive and interaction models, implemented in netmeta; supplies the estimation route but assumes every patient in an arm receives the stated combination.


Petropoulou, Efthimiou, Rucker, Schwarzer, Furukawa, Pompoli, Koek, Del Giovane, Rodondi and Mavridis 2021, PLoS ONE
Reviews the available methods for handling intervention components in meta-analysis, which establishes that none of them represents a node as a within-arm mixture with study-reported proportions.


Del Giovane, Vacchi, Mavridis, Filippini and Salanti 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Builds network meta-analysis models that account for variability in treatment definitions, applied to dose, which is the closest existing treatment of a node that is not a single well-defined intervention.


Owen, Tincello and Keith 2015, Value in Health
A three-level hierarchical network model with dose-related constraints, showing how a node label can be given internal structure rather than being treated as atomic.


Caldwell and Welton 2016, Evidence-Based Mental Health
Sets out the lumping and splitting choices for synthesizing complex interventions, which frames the node-granularity decision that a composition-based splitting rule would replace with a quantitative criterion.


Cipriani, Higgins, Geddes and Salanti 2013, Annals of Internal Medicine
States the conceptual requirements for defining network nodes and for transitivity across a common comparator, the assumptions a heterogeneous composite node violates in a way that is measurable from reported data.

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write the arm-level model explicitly: let the linear predictor of a composite arm be the study-reported-weight average over its constituent treatment effects, so the arm contributes information about constituents rather than about an ill-defined average, and derive the rank condition under which the constituent effects are identified from the rest of the network. Where that condition fails, report the target contrast as a range over the observed composition spread rather than as a point, so the synthesis produces bounds instead of nothing. Build the diagnostic alongside it: for the observed spread, report the implied variation in the anchor effect and hence in every contrast routed through the node, and calibrate a splitting threshold on simulated networks where the truth is known. Make the composition table a reporting item, since the proportion of patients receiving each constituent in each composite arm is already printed in trial publications and is the one input the model needs.

title: Composite comparator nodes are collapsed rather than modeled as reported mixtures
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it as a specific transitivity failure driven by observed within-node treatment mixtures rather than by generic clinical heterogeneity. The direct evidence is a single feasibility assessment, which is a weak base for prevalence claims, but it documents the composition spread quantitatively and the abandonment it caused, and the surrounding component-model literature confirms that no existing method takes reported proportions as data.

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text: HET-13 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text:
Statement
Models for network meta-analysis with random inconsistency effects, and the design-by-treatment interaction model behind them, estimate an inconsistency variance that the likelihood barely identifies in typical networks, because it is informed only by the small number of independent loops. Empirically derived predictive distributions exist for the between-study heterogeneity variance, built from 14,886 Cochrane meta-analyses and published for 80 settings indexed by outcome and comparison type, but no analogous corpus-derived distribution exists for the inconsistency variance. Analysts therefore use either vague priors that leave the parameter unidentified or a heterogeneity prior rescaled by a factor chosen by hand, a derivation its own authors call somewhat speculative because it assumes the amount of prior information about heterogeneity matches that about inconsistency. The sensitivity is not hypothetical: on a topical antibiotics network estimating six parameters from sixteen comparisons, setting the inconsistency prior mean equal to the heterogeneity prior mean gives posterior means of 0.22 for heterogeneity and 0.35 for inconsistency, while setting it to one tenth gives 0.37 and 0.06, and the prior’s 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of 0.03 and 1.20 essentially reproduce the posterior interval. Because the inconsistency variance is what a Bayesian analysis uses to judge whether a network is coherent enough to pool, a prior-driven estimate makes the coherence judgment prior-driven. The missing object is concrete: a database-derived predictive distribution for the inconsistency variance, indexed the same way as the heterogeneity distributions, together with an empirical estimate of the ratio of the two variances.

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text:
Why it is open
The heterogeneity corpus could be assembled from pairwise meta-analyses, of which the Cochrane database holds tens of thousands; an inconsistency variance exists only in networks containing loops, and the standard sampling frames of published networks are two orders of magnitude smaller, with the reference database describing 186 networks. Within each network the parameter is informed by a handful of independent loops, so every corpus entry is a noisy draw and a predictive distribution built by pooling point estimates would inherit that noise as if it were signal; a hierarchical extraction model is required and none has been specified. No indexing scheme has been agreed either, since the analogues of outcome type and comparison type for inconsistency would have to involve loop count and design structure, which vary far more across networks than outcome type does. Beyond the technical obstacles, nobody has attempted it: the proposal was left as future work by the same group that identified the need, and the random-inconsistency models it would serve remain rare in applied practice, so no user community is pressing for the prior.

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Law, Jackson, Turner, Rhodes and Viechtbauer 2016, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Fits the random-inconsistency-effects model with empirically based lognormal priors on both variances, derives the inconsistency prior by rescaling the heterogeneity prior mean, calls that derivation speculative, demonstrates the prior sensitivity across scaling factors of one, one half and one tenth, and names corpus-derived predictive distributions for the inconsistency variance as possible future work.


Jackson, Barrett, Rice, White and Higgins 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Defines the design-by-treatment interaction model with random inconsistency effects, which introduces the inconsistency variance as a single parameter describing the extent of inconsistency across the network.


Higgins, Jackson, Barrett, Lu, Ades and White 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Develops the design-by-treatment interaction framework for multi-arm studies, the modeling setting in which a global inconsistency parameter is defined and needs a prior.


Turner, Davey, Clarke, Thompson and Higgins 2012, International Journal of Epidemiology
The corpus method that would be imitated: predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity derived from 14,886 Cochrane meta-analyses and indexed by outcome and comparison type.


Turner, Jackson, Wei, Thompson and Higgins 2015, Statistics in Medicine
Supplies the 80 published heterogeneity predictive distributions that current inconsistency priors are rescaled from, and sets the format any inconsistency-variance corpus would follow.


Nikolakopoulou, Chaimani, Veroniki, Vasiliadis, Schmid and Salanti 2014, PLoS ONE
Describes a database of 186 published networks with their size and connectivity characteristics; the kind of sampling frame a corpus-building exercise would use, and evidence of how small that frame is compared with the pairwise corpus.


Veroniki, Vasiliadis, Higgins and Salanti 2013, International Journal of Epidemiology
Evaluates inconsistency empirically across published networks using several methods and shows that detection depends on the method used; the closest existing empirical anchor for how much inconsistency is present in practice.


Song, Xiong, Parekh-Bhurke et al. 2011, BMJ
Meta-epidemiological study of disagreement between direct and indirect comparisons across many independent triangles, giving a second empirical source on the typical magnitude of inconsistency that a predictive distribution would have to reproduce.


Veroniki, Mavridis, Higgins and Salanti 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Simulation study of which loop characteristics affect detection and estimation of inconsistency, which is what any corpus-building design would have to condition on when deciding how to index the distributions.


Jackson, Veroniki, Law, Tricco and Baker 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
Supplies classical Paule-Mandel, DerSimonian-Laird and REML estimators for the same two variances, which is the fast frequentist route a large-scale corpus refit would use instead of MCMC.

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Refit an existing database of published networks with a random-inconsistency model under matched weakly informative priors on both variances, using the classical estimators where MCMC is too slow, and publish the resulting predictive distribution for the inconsistency variance together with the distribution of its ratio to the heterogeneity variance, indexed in the same outcome-type and comparison-type scheme as the published heterogeneity distributions. Make the extraction hierarchical so that each network’s estimation uncertainty enters the predictive distribution rather than being discarded, since a naive histogram of point estimates from loops-poor networks would overstate the spread. Validate by leave-one-network-out prediction: does a prior derived this way beat both a vague prior and the current hand-scaled prior at predicting the held-out network’s design-level effects. Report explicitly whether the empirical ratio supports the one-half default that current practice assumes, since that single number is doing most of the work in every published application of these models.

title: No corpus-derived prior distributions exist for the NMA inconsistency variance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it because the corpus-building task is concrete and distinct from generic prior-sensitivity concerns. The direct evidence is a single paper, but that paper both demonstrates the prior dominance numerically and names the missing corpus as future work, and no such corpus has appeared since.

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text: HET-11 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text:
Statement
Trial publications report a treatment effect for the whole randomized population and separately within the levels of each of several covariates, so a single patient contributes to the overall row and to one row per covariate split. Methods that exploit those reports to adjust for effect modification, network meta-interpolation in particular, enter the subgroup contrasts into a multivariable regression as independent observations, which reuses the same patients across rows and understates the variance of the resulting balanced estimate. No published method supplies the within-study covariance matrix that overlapping marginal subgroups induce, and no correction, bound or robust alternative has been derived or evaluated for the intervals that follow. The dependence is a different object from the shared-arm covariance of a multi-arm trial and from the covariance induced by a shared weighting step: it arises in a two-arm trial with a single weight set as soon as two covariate splits are reported, because the two splits partition the same patients. It is also distinct from unreported target moments, since here the inputs are present and the problem is that they are correlated. The practical consequence is a narrower interval for a population-adjusted comparison presented to a decision maker as calibrated.

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text:
Why it is open
The covariance is a function of quantities the publication does not print, namely the joint distribution of the covariates that define the splits and the outcome covariance within cells of that joint distribution, so it cannot be computed from the reported margins alone. Bounds are available in principle, since the overlap between two marginal splits of the same patients is constrained by Frechet-type inequalities on the compatible joint tables, but nobody has derived them for this setting or shown how much wider the resulting intervals become. Robust variance estimation was built for exactly this shape of dependence and needs no covariance matrix, but it was calibrated for many independent studies contributing clustered estimates, whereas a population-adjusted comparison has a handful of studies, which is the regime in which the small-sample corrections for those estimators are themselves approximations. Methods that consume marginal subgroups are recent and used mainly in submissions rather than in the methods literature, so the independence assumption has been raised as a caution by a second group rather than tested, and the response to that caution is to avoid marginal subgroup data or relax assumptions one covariate at a time, which indicates that no correction is available.

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler and Ishak 2026, Anchors Away: Navigating Unanchored Indirect Comparisons with Multilevel Unanchored Meta-Regression (ML-UMR), preprint
Proposes multilevel unanchored meta-regression for disconnected evidence and names the problem: network meta-interpolation treats marginal subgroups as independent in a multivariable regression, which may underestimate uncertainty by effectively double-counting patients across overlapping subgroups, with the same caution applying to incorporating marginal subgroup data within the new method; supplies the caution and no correction.


Harari, Soltanifar, Cappelleri, Verhoek, Ouwens, Daly and Heeg 2023, Research Synthesis Methods
Network meta-interpolation, which adjusts for effect modification using subgroup analyses reported in aggregate publications together with their standard errors; the method whose independence assumption across overlapping subgroup rows is at issue.


Hedges, Tipton and Johnson 2010, Research Synthesis Methods
Robust variance estimation for meta-regression with dependent effect size estimates; the assumption-light route that yields valid standard errors without knowing the covariance, and the natural off-the-shelf fallback here.


Tipton 2015, Psychological Methods
Small-sample corrections for robust variance estimation in meta-regression; identifies the number of independent studies as the binding constraint, which is exactly what a population-adjusted comparison lacks.


Pustejovsky and Tipton 2022, Prevention Science
Expands the range of working models for robust variance estimation, giving the menu of dependence structures a correction for overlapping subgroups could be specified within.


Riley 2009, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
Quantifies the consequences of ignoring within-study correlation in multivariate meta-analysis; the closest measured analogue of the error made by treating correlated rows from one trial as independent.


Wei and Higgins 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Methods for estimating within-study covariances in multivariate meta-analysis when they are not reported; the template for deriving the missing covariance from quantities publications do print.


Phillippo et al. 2020, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
Multilevel network meta-regression, which sidesteps the problem where individual patient data exist by modeling at the individual level and integrating over the aggregate covariate distribution; it does not solve it for the aggregate-only comparator whose subgroup rows are the only covariate information available.

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Derive the covariance in the case that can be done exactly first: for a two-arm trial reporting an overall effect and two marginal splits, write the covariance of the reported contrasts as a function of the cell counts of the joint covariate distribution, then establish what is identified when only the margins are reported and give sharp bounds over the compatible joint tables. Feed those bounds into network meta-interpolation as an interval-valued weight matrix, so that the reported uncertainty covers the worst compatible dependence rather than assuming none. Quantify the current error with a simulation in which the joint distribution is known: fit the method under the independence assumption and under the true covariance, and report the ratio of interval widths and the realized coverage across realistic numbers of covariates and split proportions, since the magnitude of the problem is not currently known. Benchmark robust variance estimation with a small-sample correction against the derived covariance on the same simulations as the immediate fallback, and test borrowing the joint covariate distribution from a trial that does have individual patient data as a calibrated approximation for the trials that do not.

title: No covariance correction for overlapping reported subgroups
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted overlapping marginal subgroup reports as a within-study dependence structure distinct from shared-arm and shared-weighting covariance, affecting both regression weighting and interval calibration. The base is a single preprint, which identifies the independent-row treatment and its double-counting consequence while offering no correction, so the entry rests on a stated caution rather than on a measured error.

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text: HET-09 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text:
Statement
Multivariate network meta-analysis with random inconsistency effects carries two covariance matrices over the outcomes, one for between-study heterogeneity and one for inconsistency, and each has an explicit identification requirement: two or more studies of the same design must supply data on every pair of outcomes to identify the heterogeneity covariance, and two or more studies of different designs must do so to identify the inconsistency covariance. Published networks rarely satisfy either condition, because replication within and between designs is scarce and outcome reporting is incomplete. The workaround in use restores identifiability by data surgery: multi-arm trials are split into separate two-arm trials with the control arm halved, which manufactures the between-design replication the model requires out of studies that do not supply it, and it is adopted as an acknowledged pragmatic decision rather than defended. The stated fallbacks are to fit a lower-dimensional model or to assume consistency, both of which answer a different question from the one asked. What does not exist is a structured covariance family, a shrinkage prior or a regularized estimator that keeps the inconsistency covariance estimable at the replication levels real networks have, together with evidence on how much such a restriction moves the treatment effects it exists to protect.

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text:
Why it is open
The identification conditions are properties of the design matrix rather than of the estimator, so no care in fitting recovers a covariance the network never observed; the only routes are to impose structure, to borrow strength across outcomes, or to accept partial identification. Imposing structure is not free, because restricting the covariance to a compound-symmetric or factor-analytic form changes the borrowing of strength between outcomes, which is the entire reason multivariate synthesis is used, and nobody has measured that trade. The Bayesian route has the tools, since correlation-matrix priors are standard, but with two or three studies per design the posterior for the inconsistency covariance is the prior, and no work reports how far the treatment effects move as that prior is varied. Trial splitting is convenient and leaves no trace in the output, which removes the pressure to solve the problem properly: the fitted model reports an inconsistency variance, and nothing in the report says it was made estimable by counting one control arm twice.

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Jackson, Bujkiewicz, Law, Riley and White 2018, Biometrics
Matrix-based method of moments for multivariate network meta-analysis with multiple outcomes and random inconsistency effects; states the identification conditions verbatim, meets them in the worked example by splitting three interferon-beta trials into separate two-arm trials with halved control arms as an explicitly pragmatic decision, and offers only lower dimension or the consistent model as alternatives.


Jackson, White and Riley 2013, Biometrical Journal
Matrix-based method of moments for the multivariate random effects model in meta-analysis and meta-regression; the estimator the network version generalizes, where the same replication requirements first appear without the design dimension.


Jackson, Law, Barrett, Turner, Higgins, Salanti and White 2016, Statistics in Medicine
Extends DerSimonian and Laird estimation to network meta-analysis with random inconsistency effects; the univariate model whose multivariate generalization creates the covariance that cannot be identified.


Riley 2009, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
Quantifies what ignoring within-study correlation does to multivariate meta-analysis estimates and intervals; establishes that the covariance structure is not a nuisance detail whose misspecification can be assumed harmless.


Riley, Thompson and Abrams 2008, Biostatistics
Alternative bivariate random-effects model for when the within-study correlations are unknown, replacing separate within- and between-study correlations with a single overall correlation; the closest existing precedent for restructuring a covariance to restore estimability, at the bivariate rather than the network level.


Wei and Higgins 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Methods for estimating within-study covariances in multivariate meta-analysis when they are not reported; supplies the template for deriving a covariance from reported quantities instead of requiring the design to identify it.


Achana, Cooper, Bujkiewicz, Hubbard, Kendrick and Jones 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Bayesian network synthesis of multiple outcome measures with explicit borrowing of information across outcomes; the hierarchical route through which a shrinkage prior on an inconsistency covariance would be built, applied to the heterogeneity side.


Bujkiewicz, Thompson, Sutton, Cooper, Harrison and Symmons 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Bayesian multivariate meta-analysis of mixed outcomes with the covariance structure specified through priors rather than estimated freely; shows the prior-based regularization exists as a technique while leaving the inconsistency covariance untouched.


Efthimiou, Mavridis, Cipriani, Leucht, Bagos and Salanti 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Models multiple correlated outcomes within a network of interventions using odds ratios; the applied multivariate network model whose covariance requirements this identification problem constrains.


Lewandowski, Kurowicka and Joe 2009, Journal of Multivariate Analysis
Vine-based prior for random correlation matrices, the standard regularizing prior available for a covariance of this shape; developed outside evidence synthesis and never evaluated for keeping a network inconsistency covariance estimable.


Nikolakopoulou, Chaimani, Veroniki, Vasiliadis, Schmid and Salanti 2014, PLOS ONE
Characterizes 186 published networks by size, topology and replication; supplies the empirical distribution of designs against which any claimed estimator has to be tested and against which the identification conditions can be scored.

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Characterize the failure before proposing a fix: using the published database of network topologies, compute for each real network how many designs would supply the replication required for a two-outcome and a three-outcome inconsistency covariance, so that the fraction of the literature in which the unstructured model is identified becomes a measured number. Then compare candidate restrictions on the same simulated networks, namely a scalar inconsistency variance shared across outcomes, a compound-symmetric or factor-analytic covariance, and a hierarchical prior shrinking the inconsistency covariance toward zero, scoring each on bias and coverage of the treatment effects and on how often it correctly detects true inconsistency. Include trial splitting as a comparator so its cost is measured rather than assumed, since it is the current default and the direction of the bias it introduces is unknown. Report the prior sensitivity of the Bayesian versions explicitly, and where nothing is identified, say so and fall back to the consistent model with a stated bound rather than to a model that reports an inconsistency variance it did not estimate.

title: Multivariate NMA inconsistency covariance is unidentifiable in sparse networks
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted that the quoted identification conditions support the concern and that no existing catalog entry addresses multivariate inconsistency estimability, while cautioning that the wording must not claim regularized or prior-based approaches are wholly nonexistent; it is worded accordingly, naming the prior and structured-covariance tools that exist and have not been applied here. The evidence is a single paper, which is also the paper that states the conditions and adopts the splitting workaround.

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text: HET-07 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text:
Statement
Fractional polynomial, piecewise exponential and parametric survival network models carry several treatment-effect parameters per contrast: a scale contrast plus one or more time-varying shape contrasts, and the shape contrasts are what allow the hazard ratio to change over follow-up. A between-study covariance across the whole parameter vector was specified when fractional polynomial network synthesis was introduced, as an unstructured multivariate normal assumed constant across all treatment comparisons, and spline formulations likewise place a random effect on the full coefficient vector. Practice has not followed the specification: a current survival network application places a random effect on the scale coefficient alone, stating that the methodology for including all heterogeneity parameters still needs development, and offers piecewise exponential models in fixed-effect form only. Nothing establishes which of the parameters a realistic network can identify heterogeneity for, what covariance structure they should share, whether the assumption that the covariance is common across comparisons survives contact with data, or what it costs to place the random effect on the wrong subset. The consequence is specific rather than generic: constraining the shape contrasts to be common across studies imposes a single time profile of the treatment effect on the entire network, which is the assumption these models were adopted in order to relax, and it does so silently because the fitted model still reports a heterogeneity parameter.

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text:
Why it is open
An unstructured covariance over a scale contrast and one or two shape contrasts carries three to six free parameters, and survival networks routinely hold fewer than ten studies, so the full specification is at best weakly identified and its posterior is governed by the covariance prior. The shape contrasts are also the least well determined parts of each study’s own fit, since they depend on the tail of follow-up where events are scarce and where reconstructed patient data are least reliable, so a between-study variance for them is estimated on top of large and unequal within-study uncertainty. Any structured alternative must keep the covariance positive semidefinite while sharing information across comparisons, and there is no accepted family for doing so over a parameter vector whose elements are not exchangeable, because a scale contrast and a shape contrast mean different things and should not be shrunk toward a common variance. Model comparison cannot arbitrate, since deviance-based criteria have little power to distinguish covariance structures at these sample sizes. And the restriction is currently made inside software defaults rather than in an analysis plan, so it is not reported as an assumption at all.

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Shao, Zhao, Shi, Rui and Tang 2025, Research Synthesis Methods (NMAsurv)
Survival network meta-analysis application covering fractional polynomial, piecewise exponential, parametric and Cox models, which models a heterogeneity parameter for the scale coefficient only because the methodology for including all heterogeneity parameters still needs further development, and which offers piecewise exponential models in fixed-effect form only.


Jansen 2011, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Introduces fractional polynomial network meta-analysis with a multi-dimensional treatment effect and specifies a full between-study covariance matrix over the fractional polynomial parameters, with variances for each parameter and correlations between them, assumed constant across all treatment comparisons; the specification exists, its identifiability at realistic network sizes does not.


Ouwens, Philips and Jansen 2010, Research Synthesis Methods
Network meta-analysis of parametric survival curves, where each contrast again carries several parameters and the between-study structure over them is a modeling choice rather than a settled convention.


Jansen and Cope 2012, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Adds covariates to the multi-dimensional survival contrast so that systematic differences across comparisons are explained rather than absorbed into a random effect; the meta-regression alternative to enlarging the heterogeneity structure.


Heinecke, Tallarita and De Iorio 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Bayesian splines versus fractional polynomials in network meta-analysis, decomposing the whole coefficient vector into a study-specific random effect and an arm deviation from the reference treatment; demonstrates that a full-vector random effect is implementable.


Cope, Chan and Jansen 2020, Research Synthesis Methods
Multivariate network meta-analysis of survival function parameters, treating the parameter vector jointly; the closest existing treatment of the covariance across survival parameters, approached from the correlation side rather than the identifiability side.


Wiksten, Hawkins, Piepho and Gsteiger 2020, Value in Health
Efficient strategies for building and selecting non-proportional-hazards network models; supplies the model-building workflow into which a heterogeneity-structure decision would have to be inserted, and does not itself resolve which parameters may carry heterogeneity.


Freeman and Carpenter 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
One-step Bayesian individual-patient-data network synthesis of time-to-event data with Royston-Parmar models, in which the between-study structure over the spline coefficients is again chosen rather than derived.


Phillippo, Dias, Ades and Welton 2024, preprint
Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods with applications to survival analysis; carries the same multi-parameter contrast into the population-adjusted setting and therefore inherits the same unresolved heterogeneity structure.

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Establish identifiability before proposing structure: derive, for fractional polynomial and piecewise exponential contrasts, how many studies and how many events per study are needed before a two-parameter or three-parameter between-study covariance is estimable rather than prior-driven, and publish that as a table an analyst can look up. Then compare candidate structures on the same networks, namely a scale-only random effect, a diagonal covariance across scale and shape, an unstructured covariance, and a hierarchical structure that shrinks the shape variances toward zero while leaving the scale variance free, scoring them on bias in the time-varying hazard ratio, coverage of survival differences and of restricted mean survival, and on extrapolated survival where the shape contrasts dominate. Simulate the misplacement directly by generating data with heterogeneity in the shape contrasts and fitting the scale-only model, so the cost of the current default becomes a number rather than a concern. Make the heterogeneity structure an explicit argument in survival network software rather than a fixed internal choice, and require an analysis plan to name it.

title: Heterogeneity structure is undefined for multi-parameter survival NMA
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it as a concrete modeling problem specific to multi-parameter time-varying survival contrasts rather than a restatement of the shared-scalar-heterogeneity entry. It is partially addressed because a full between-study covariance across the parameter vector was specified when fractional polynomial network synthesis was introduced and full-vector random effects are implemented for spline formulations; what is open is which parameters a real network identifies, what structure they should share, and what restricting to the scale coefficient costs, with the evidence for the restriction being a single current implementation.

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text: HET-05 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text:
Statement
Network meta-analysis is fitted almost universally with additive random effects, in which the variance of an observed contrast is the within-study variance plus a between-study variance. The multiplicative alternative instead inflates the within-study variance by a factor, so the total variance is phi times sigma squared rather than sigma squared plus tau squared; additive therefore treats within- and between-study variation as independent, while multiplicative treats between-study variation as proportional to within-study variation. Both are available for networks: a structural equation formulation fits a network with a common inflation factor or with contrast-specific inflation factors, and a penalized-likelihood network model for rare events uses a multiplicative overdispersion term precisely because an additive heterogeneity parameter is unworkable there. What does not exist is any comparison of the two in a network on the criteria that matter, namely coverage, interval width, treatment rankings and inconsistency assessment, under the conditions networks actually present: few studies per contrast, contrasts informed only indirectly, multi-arm trials, and heterogeneity that differs by comparison. In pairwise meta-analysis the comparison has been made twice, and both times the multiplicative model produced systematically narrower intervals, so the choice is not neutral. In a network it also propagates, because the variance parameterization enters the consistency equations and therefore reaches every indirectly informed contrast, so a convention adopted for one comparison changes estimates for comparisons in which no study was ever run.

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text:
Why it is open
Nobody has run the comparison, and the reasons it is unattractive are ordinary rather than deep: it is a simulation study whose deliverable is a table of coverages, it requires fitting the multiplicative model in a network estimator that mainstream applied packages do not expose, and it yields no new method to name. The two parameterizations also give similar point estimates, which makes the difference easy to dismiss as second order even though it lands on interval width, which is what a decision reads. Model comparison statistics cannot settle it from data at realistic network sizes, since the two models carry the same number of variance parameters and differ in a shape assumption that few studies per contrast cannot resolve, so the choice has to be defended on operating characteristics rather than on fit. And because the additive model is the default in every mainstream network package, it is the multiplicative option that an analyst must justify, so the burden of evidence has never been placed on the default.

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Tu and Wu 2017, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Fits network meta-analysis as a structural equation model, including the unrestricted weighted least squares form of the multiplicative model with a common or contrast-specific inflation factor, sets out that additive treats within- and between-study heterogeneity as independent while multiplicative treats them as related, and states that comparison of their performance in networks has not been done.


Stanley and Doucouliagos 2015, Statistics in Medicine
Develops the unrestricted weighted least squares multiplicative estimator for meta-analysis as an alternative to both fixed and additive random effects.


Stanley and Doucouliagos 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
Extends the multiplicative weighted least squares approach to meta-regression, which is the form a network model with covariates would need.


Mawdsley, Higgins, Sutton and Abrams 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
Empirical comparison of additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models across pairwise meta-analyses, reporting broadly concordant point estimates with narrower intervals under the multiplicative model; this is the study that has never been repeated for networks.


Evrenoglou, White, Afach, Mavridis and Chaimani 2022, Statistics in Medicine
Penalized-likelihood network model for rare events that accounts for heterogeneity through a multiplicative overdispersion term in a two-stage approach, because an additive heterogeneity parameter is not available in that model; demonstrates multiplicative heterogeneity already operating inside a network estimator.


Jackson, Law, Stijnen, Viechtbauer and White 2018, Statistics in Medicine
Compares seven random-effects models for the summary odds ratio in pairwise meta-analysis on bias, coverage and interval width; the template for the comparison this entry asks for, executed one level below the network.

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Run the comparison as a preregistered network simulation: vary the number of studies per contrast from two upward, the proportion of contrasts informed only indirectly, the presence of three-arm and four-arm studies, and heterogeneity that is constant across the network versus contrast-specific, and generate data under both an additive and a multiplicative truth so that each model is scored when it is right and when it is wrong. Report coverage and width for contrast intervals, the stability of rank probabilities and SUCRA, and the size of the design-by-treatment inconsistency test under each parameterization, since the error term of that test is exactly what the parameterization changes. Add an empirical arm over a database of published networks, refitting each under both models and recording how often the conclusion for the decision-relevant contrast changes; that frequency is what a guideline would need in order to recommend either as a default. Expose the multiplicative option in a mainstream network package so the answer is actionable rather than a paper, and state the network size above which each parameterization should be preferred.

title: Additive and multiplicative heterogeneity models have not been compared in NMA
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted that the network consequences cannot be read off the pairwise results, because the parameterization propagates through the consistency equations into indirectly informed contrasts and into rankings. The evidence is a single methods paper’s stated research need; what makes the gap conspicuous rather than speculative is that the pairwise version of the same comparison has been published twice and the multiplicative model has already been fitted inside a network estimator.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Statement
Network models in current software default to a single between-study heterogeneity variance shared across the whole network, adopted for estimability rather than for plausibility: multinma’s tau is one network-wide scalar, as is the common tau recorded by cMLNMR in cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN. The structured alternatives are not open research. Thorlund et al. 2013 (pmid:23311298) state the problem and build and compare four replacements for the homogeneous-variance assumption, empirically derived heterogeneity priors exist for 80 settings (Turner et al. 2015, doi:10.1002/sim.6381) and weakly informative ones for the very-few-studies case (Rover et al. 2021, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475), and class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes ship in multinma via class_sd since 0.8.0 (Perren et al. 2025, doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887), although that is a within-class treatment standard deviation rather than tau. What has not been done is establishing how large a network must be before the competing variance structures are distinguishable, and no structure indexes heterogeneity by target population; nor is the direction of the error fixed, since a shared variance can overstate uncertainty in a sparse stratum as readily as understate it, depending on which strata are more heterogeneous.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Why it is open
Networks rarely contain enough studies per class or component to estimate separate variances, so a separate-variance model is often only nominally identified and its posterior is driven by the prior rather than by the data. Model comparison statistics have little power to distinguish competing variance structures at realistic network sizes, and no one has established the size at which they become distinguishable, so the default is neither tested nor visibly violated. Component-specific variances need further assumptions about the covariance among component deviations, and any structured alternative must keep the random-effects covariance positive semidefinite, which is why the existing proposals have not displaced the default in software. Population-indexed heterogeneity has no implementation at all: the software parameter is a single network-wide scalar, so the question of whether tau should differ by target population cannot currently be asked.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Thorlund, Thabane and Mills, 2013, Modelling heterogeneity variances in multiple treatment comparison meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology 13:2
States the entry’s problem (the homogeneous variance assumption is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates, so credible intervals may lose nominal coverage and rank probabilities may be distorted) and builds and compares four alternatives: exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, and two informative variance-prior schemes.


Turner et al., 2015, Predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity and simple methods for their application in Bayesian meta-analysis
Derives empirically based predictive distributions for heterogeneity in 80 settings defined by outcome and comparison type, usable directly as heterogeneity priors; this is the robust-prior component the source lists as needed.


Rover et al., 2021, On weakly informative prior distributions for the heterogeneity parameter in Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis
Guidance on heterogeneity priors when very few studies contribute, which is the sparse-stratum case the entry names.


Perren, Pedder, Welton and Phillippo, 2026, Network Meta-Analysis with Class Effects: A Practical Guide and Model Selection Algorithm
Class-specific variance components with sharing of the standard deviation across groups of classes when a class has too few treatments to estimate its own, implemented in multinma as class_sd since 0.8.0, plus a model selection algorithm; note this is a within-class treatment standard deviation, not the between-study heterogeneity variance.


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
cMLNMR records a single common tau and offers half-normal and half-Student-t priors for it, with no class-specific or component-specific heterogeneity structure; the source-code auditor used this to confirm that the software default persists.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The modeling work is largely done, so the useful contributions are evaluation and porting rather than invention. Run the distinguishability simulation the field lacks: how many studies per class or component are needed before exchangeable, consistency-constrained and separate-variance structures can be told apart, so a default can be defended or abandoned on the basis of network size rather than convention. Carry the existing structures and the empirically derived heterogeneity priors into population-adjusted network models, where the heterogeneity parameter is still a single scalar, and report prior sensitivity rather than claiming any prior is universally robust. The genuinely new case is heterogeneity indexed by target population, which none of the existing work addresses.

title: Single shared heterogeneity variance across classes and populations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Network models default to one common between-study heterogeneity variance even when the network spans treatment classes, components, and populations for which a shared value is implausible. The default is adopted for estimability rather than for plausibility.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented structured heterogeneity models and robust heterogeneity priors as work still to be developed; the literature auditor found them published and evaluated years ago (Thorlund et al. 2013, pmid:23311298; Turner et al. 2015, doi:10.1002/sim.6381; Rover et al. 2021, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475; class-specific variances in multinma since 0.8.0, doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887), so the residual gap is adoption plus the population-indexed case. The two auditors split on whether the entry is open or partly solved, and the code auditor added that ‘often unrealistic’ is an unsupported prevalence claim and that a shared variance does not automatically understate uncertainty where a new treatment sits; the entry is published at the weaker claim.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): Retrieved Thorlund, Thabane & Mills (2013), BMC Med Res Methodol 13:2, which is the entry’s problem and much of its proposed direction, already executed. Verbatim: ‘Random-effects MTCs have commonly modeled heterogeneity under the assumption that the between-trial variance for all involved treatment comparisons are equal… The homogeneous variance assumption, however, is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates. Consequently 95% credible intervals may not retain nominal coverage, and treatment rank probabilities may become distorted.’ They build and compare four alternatives (exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, two informative variance-prior schemes) and conclude ‘All four approaches should be viable candidates for replacing or supplementing the conventional homogeneous variance MTC model.’ The ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ claim is likewise delivered rather than open: Turner et al. (2015) empirical predictive distributions for tau, Rover et al. (2021) weakly informative heterogeneity priors, Lilienthal et al. (2024) empirical HTA priors. Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes are implemented in multinma 0.8.0+ via class_sd, though that is the within-class treatment SD, not between-study tau; multinma’s tau remains a single network-wide scalar, so the software-default half stands. Genuinely open: population-indexed heterogeneity, and the distinguishability simulation (Thorlund used two illustrative datasets).
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Perren, Pedder, Welton and Phillippo, 2025, Network Meta-Analysis with Class Effects: A Practical Guide and Model Selection Algorithm’ -> ‘Perren, Pedder, Welton and Phillippo, 2026, Network Meta-Analysis with Class Effects: A Practical Guide and Model Selection Algorithm’ 10.1177/0272989X251389887 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2025 online and 2026 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Retrieved Thorlund, Thabane & Mills (2013), BMC Med Res Methodol 13:2, which is the entry’s problem and much of its proposed direction, already executed. Verbatim: ‘Random-effects MTCs have commonly modeled heterogeneity under the assumption that the between-trial variance for all involved treatment comparisons are equal… The homogeneous variance assumption, however, is unrealistic and can severely bias variance estimates. Consequently 95% credible intervals may not retain nominal coverage, and treatment rank probabilities may become distorted.’ They build and compare four alternatives (exchangeable variances, consistency-constrained variances, two informative variance-prior schemes) and conclude ‘All four approaches should be viable candidates for replacing or supplementing the conventional homogeneous variance MTC model.’ The ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ claim is likewise delivered rather than open: Turner et al. (2015) empirical predictive distributions for tau, Rover et al. (2021) weakly informative heterogeneity priors, Lilienthal et al. (2024) empirical HTA priors. Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes are implemented in multinma 0.8.0+ via class_sd, though that is the within-class treatment SD, not between-study tau; multinma’s tau remains a single network-wide scalar, so the software-default half stands. Genuinely open: population-indexed heterogeneity, and the distinguishability simulation (Thorlund used two illustrative datasets). Cites pmid:23311298: Already states the problem and supplies four evaluated alternatives to a single shared heterogeneity variance.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.6381: Supplies empirically derived heterogeneity priors for 80 settings, the ‘robust priors for sparse strata’ the entry lists as needed.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1475: Guidance on robust heterogeneity priors when very few studies contribute, the sparse-stratum case the entry names.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887: Class-specific variance components with sharing across sparse classes, implemented in multinma (class_sd argument, since 0.8.0), plus a model-selection algorithm..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 is technically plausible but context-dependent; the word often is an unsupported prevalence claim. A common heterogeneity variance can be implausible across distinct classes or populations, but it can either understate or overstate uncertainty depending on which strata are more heterogeneous. Understatement near a new treatment is not automatic. C2 is a valid modeling direction only if the resulting random-effects covariance is positive semidefinite and the network supplies enough replication. Component-specific variances also require assumptions about covariance among component deviations. In sparse strata, separate variances may be practically unidentified and dominated by priors. C3 is too categorical: proper regularization, hierarchical pooling, and prior-sensitivity analysis are advisable, but there is no universally robust prior that is always required. At cpaic 9d150e9, cMLNMR explicitly records a single common tau. It offers half-normal and half-Student-t priors but no class-specific or component-specific heterogeneity structure, so the core package limitation remains open. This is a potentially material sensitivity issue, not automatically a high-severity defect in every network.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:literature
