title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text: HET-01 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Statement
Cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy and care pathway are properties of the trial rather than of the patient, so baseline covariate balancing in MAIC or STC cannot remove them, and a standard PAIC output does not separate residual protocol difference from residual patient-mix imbalance. Known design features are not beyond the reach of every estimator: they can enter study-level meta-regression, estimand or measurement models, and bias models, provided the network supplies enough cross-study variation to identify them. What stays nonidentifiable is the latent part and the split between design difference and patient mix. The bias-adjustment machinery the source proposes as new is mature: elicited, design-stratified priors for internal and external bias were published in Turner et al. 2009 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x), and threshold analysis quantifies how much study-level bias would have to be present to change a network’s recommendation (Phillippo et al. 2018, doi:10.1111/rssa.12341); neither has been ported to the population-adjusted setting.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Why it is open
The offending quantities have no patient-level distribution, so a weight that equalizes age and biomarker status leaves an imaging schedule or a rescue-therapy rule untouched, and separating the latent part of a design difference from residual patient-mix imbalance is not identified without further information or assumptions. Where a design feature is recorded and varies across enough studies it can be modeled, but PAIC networks are usually too small for that variation to exist, and these features are written up as narrative study characteristics rather than as variables. Adherence is a further complication because it is post-randomization: balancing baseline predictors can equalize it incidentally, while adjusting for it directly can change the estimand. Once baselines are balanced the analysis looks comparable, which makes the residue easy to overlook, and how much it matters is not established, since severity turns on whether the difference changes the estimand or the treatment as implemented.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Turner, Spiegelhalter, Smith and Thompson, 2009, Bias modelling in evidence synthesis, JRSS-A 172:21-47
Constructs prior distributions from elicited opinion to represent internal bias (lack of rigour) and external bias (lack of relevance) in each study and performs a bias-adjusted meta-analysis; this is the hierarchical bias model with design-stratified priors that the source lists as a new direction.


Phillippo et al., 2018, Sensitivity of treatment recommendations to bias in network meta-analysis
Threshold analysis: quantifies how much study-level bias would have to be present before a network’s treatment recommendation changes, giving existing machinery for the design-feature direction the source proposes.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing bias-adjustment apparatus rather than build it. Turner et al.’s elicited, design-stratified bias priors and Phillippo et al.’s threshold analysis are both defined for aggregate-data meta-analysis and NMA; what is missing is their combination with a weighting or standardization step and with an explicit target population. Design-feature meta-regression stays a reasonable route where the network holds enough studies to identify a study-level coefficient, and that replication, not the modeling, is the binding constraint. Negative-control endpoints are worth trying as a residual-heterogeneity signal, but there is no use of them in this field to build on, and a negative control can at best flag residual incompatibility; it cannot attribute that incompatibility to patient mix rather than to trial design.

title: Design and conduct differences survive baseline covariate balancing
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy and care pathway are properties of the trial, not the patient, so baseline covariate balancing cannot remove them and standard PAIC output does not distinguish them from residual patient-mix imbalance. Bayesian bias-adjustment models with elicited, design-stratified priors exist and are well developed for meta-analysis and NMA (Turner et al. 2009), but have not been ported to the population-adjusted setting.
The source said. “Population adjustment balances baseline patient covariates, but cross-trial differences in endpoint definition, follow-up schedule, adherence, rescue therapy, and care pathway are properties of the trial rather than of the patient and remain once balancing is complete. Nothing in a standard PAIC output distinguishes residual patient-mix imbalance from residual protocol difference.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented hierarchical bias models with design-stratified priors as an emerging response and cited nothing; the literature auditor found them a seventeen-year-old evidence-synthesis literature, so the entry is now sourced to Turner et al. 2009 (doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x) and Phillippo et al. 2018 (doi:10.1111/rssa.12341) and the gap is their absence from PAIC, not from the literature. The same auditor could verify neither the claim that reviews find these sources under-handled in ITC and PAIC work nor any literature at all on negative-control endpoints in this field, and the code auditor struck the source’s assertion that these features cannot enter the estimator even when known.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

closure-upheld

27 findings from the reading assert this problem is open; the closure was re-examined and stands Put to an independent reviewer with the closing auditors’ reasoning, the work they relied on, and the new findings in view together. The new findings repeatedly establish the closure’s conceded residual: baseline-only MAIC and STC cannot adjust trial-level protocol, measurement, delivery, or care-pathway differences. They do not contradict Turner et al.’s established bias-adjustment framework or Phillippo et al.’s threshold-analysis machinery, and several findings explicitly acknowledge that alternative modeling requires additional information or assumptions. Empirical demonstrations that these differences matter, including the 2026 imaging-schedule finding, strengthen the residual but do not make the already-mature bias-model direction newly open. The closure correctly distinguishes an unresolved PAIC-specific identification and implementation problem from the overstated claim that the relevant bias machinery is new or absent. (reviewer confidence: high)

Flagged for reopening

29 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. Retrieved Turner, Spiegelhalter, Smith & Thompson (2009), JRSS-A 172:21-47: ‘We present simple methods of allowing for differences in rigour (or lack of internal bias) and relevance (or lack of external bias) in evidence synthesis… Using elicited opinion, we construct prior distributions to represent the biases in each study and perform a bias-adjusted meta-analysis.’ Hierarchical bias models with design-stratified elicited priors are therefore a 17-year-old, mature evidence-synthesis literature, extended by Phillippo et al. (2018) threshold analysis and by the 2025 RoB NMA tool. Presenting them as an emerging idea is the overstatement. The core identification problem is genuinely open: design and conduct features have no patient-level distribution, so no weighting or standardization estimator can separate residual protocol difference from residual patient-mix imbalance; this is structurally untestable, so no paper can solve it. Two sub-claims fail verification. I found no review asserting that design and conduct heterogeneity is specifically under-handled in ITC/PAIC; the reviews I retrieved (Phillippo 2019 NICE TAs, Freitag 2023, van Beekhuizen 2025 EUnetHTA) concern covariate/effect-modifier selection and overall ITC suitability. And I found no literature at all on negative-control endpoints in ITC/PAIC, so that absence claim is unverifiable. Cites doi:10.1111/j.1467-985X.2008.00547.x: Supplies the real reference for the entry’s unsourced ‘Bayesian hierarchical bias models and design-stratified bias priors’ direction. It already exists for evidence synthesis; the gap is its absence from PAIC, not its absence from the literature.. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12341: Existing quantitative machinery for asking how much study-level bias would have to be present to change a network’s treatment recommendation; a real prior-art anchor for the ‘design-feature’ direction..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The core limitation is real, but several claims exceed it. C2 and C4 are correct for baseline-only MAIC and STC: patient reweighting cannot change endpoint definitions, follow-up, rescue rules, care delivery, or latent study-level features. C3 is generally but not logically true because balancing complete baseline predictors could incidentally balance adherence; adherence itself is postrandomization, and direct adjustment may change the estimand or introduce bias. The statement that known design features cannot enter an estimator is false: they can enter study-level meta-regression, measurement or estimand models, and bias models when replication and identifying assumptions permit. Negative controls can signal residual incompatibility only under valid negative-control assumptions and cannot by themselves attribute it to patient mix versus trial design. C5 through C7 are prevalence or current-use claims with no cited source and are unverifiable in this offline technical audit. C8 is plausible but limited by study-level confounding and sparse replication. Very high severity is justified when the differences change the estimand or treatment implementation, not automatically for every conduct difference.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text: EVB-14 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text:
Statement
In a network with closed loops, comparison-specific reporting bias and design or loop inconsistency both surface as disagreement between what different evidence paths say about the same contrast, and no fitted model separates them. The two literatures rest on incompatible structure: network selection and small-study models assume the selection process is exchangeable across the network and take the direction of bias as an input, while design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting models assign free per-design deviations and take the reported effects at face value. There is no estimator carrying both, no identifiability result stating what is estimable when both are present, and no study reporting whether a routine inconsistency test keeps its size and power under reporting bias or whether a bias adjustment is distorted by genuine inconsistency. The problem has a worked instance: adjusting a network of 12 antidepressants for reporting bias, where 74 trials existed in the US Food and Drug Administration database and only 51 were published, moved the pairwise effect sizes, the probabilities of being best and the rankings, and corrected the placebo-relative effects toward the full-data answer for some drugs but not others. Fitting the two models in sequence is not equivalent to fitting them jointly, because a discrepancy absorbed by whichever is fitted first is no longer available to the other. An analyst facing a loop conflict therefore has two explanations with opposite remedies, down-weighting the small studies or refusing to pool the loop, and nothing to choose between them.

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text:
Why it is open
The two mechanisms compete for the same residual variation, so identifying both at once requires either an external anchor on the selection process or a restriction on the inconsistency structure, and the network data supply neither. Reporting-bias models are already fragile in sparse networks, since a selection or small-study component estimated from a handful of trials per comparison is weakly identified and driven by its prior and by the assumed weight function; adding free per-design inconsistency terms removes what identification remained. In the head-to-head part of a network the direction of bias is an assumption rather than an estimate, and plausible directions such as sponsorship bias and novelty bias can contradict one another around a single loop, which has no analogue in pairwise meta-analysis and no accepted resolution. Validation is also awkward, because the natural gold standard is a regulator’s complete trial inventory, which exists for a small number of drug classes, so operating characteristics have to come from simulations that nobody has run.

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Trinquart, Chatellier and Ravaud 2012, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Builds two Bayesian network reporting-bias adjustments, a meta-regression of effect size on standard error and a selection model weighting up trials with low publication propensity, applies them to 12 antidepressants against the FDA record, and names the collision: disentangling the sources of bias on direct and indirect evidence is difficult when reporting bias and inconsistency are twisted together or when assumed bias directions conflict on a loop.


Mavridis, Sutton, Cipriani and Salanti 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Fully Bayesian Copas selection model extended to network meta-analysis; supplies the selection-model branch that would have to be carried inside any joint model.


Mavridis, Welton, Sutton and Salanti 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Selection model for publication bias fitted in a full network rather than comparison by comparison; the most developed reporting-bias machinery available for networks, with the consistency assumption left unmodeled.


Chaimani and Salanti 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Comparison-adjusted funnel plot, the routine small-study-effects diagnostic for networks; descriptive, with no inconsistency term and no way to attribute an asymmetry to selection rather than to a loop conflict.


Higgins, Jackson, Barrett, Lu, Ades and White 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
The design-by-treatment interaction model, the standard global inconsistency framework, in which reported effects are taken at face value and no bias-generating process appears in the likelihood.


Dias, Welton, Caldwell and Ades 2010, Statistics in Medicine
Node splitting, the local direct-versus-indirect check whose output is exactly the discrepancy that reporting bias and inconsistency both produce.


Jackson, Barrett, Rice, White and Higgins 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Design-by-treatment interaction model with random rather than fixed inconsistency effects; shows the inconsistency side is already parameterized as a variance component, which is what a joint model would have to keep separate from a selection component.


Rucker, Carpenter and Schwarzer 2011, Biometrical Journal
Limit meta-analysis and related small-study-effect adjustments for pairwise meta-analysis; the pairwise ancestor of the small-study branch, developed where there are no loops and therefore no competing explanation.


Page, Sterne, Boutron et al. 2023, BMJ (ROB-ME)
Structured judgement of risk of bias due to missing evidence in a meta-analysis; the qualitative response to the same threat, which records a concern rather than separating it from inconsistency in a fitted model.

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write one network likelihood carrying a selection or small-study component and design-by-treatment inconsistency terms at the same time, and do the identifiability analysis before the simulation: state which parameters are estimable from network data alone, which require an external anchor such as a regulatory trial inventory or a registry-derived publication probability, and which are only bounded. Then run the cross-contamination study in both directions, reporting the size and power of the standard inconsistency test under reporting bias of known magnitude and the bias of the standard reporting-bias adjustment under loop inconsistency of known magnitude; that pair of curves is the missing operating-characteristic evidence and it needs no new theory. Use the drug classes for which a regulator’s complete trial set is available as the empirical anchor, refitting the joint model on published-only data and scoring it against the full-data answer. Where the two mechanisms cannot be separated, report the discrepancy as a partially identified region spanning both explanations rather than assigning it in full to whichever model happened to be fitted.

title: Reporting bias and inconsistency cannot be disentangled in NMA
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted the identification collision as distinct from a standalone reporting-bias adjustment and from a standalone inconsistency test. The primary evidence is a single paper’s stated limitation, which is a narrow base, although it is the paper that builds the network bias adjustment and therefore reaches the wall from inside; a sweep of every catalog entry mentioning publication bias, reporting bias, small-study effects or funnel plots found none that models the two mechanisms together.

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text: EVB-12 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text:
Statement
When the decision to run a new trial is taken because an existing network showed a promising but non-significant contrast, and that trial is later pooled back into the same network, the network estimate for that contrast is conditioned on the very result that triggered the trial. The cost is measured rather than conjectured: type I error for the targeted contrast rises from the nominal 5 percent to between 23.8 and 38.5 percent under ordinary network analysis, and to between 29.1 and 47.3 percent under alpha-spending sequential analysis, across new-trial sizes from 50 to 200 and in both an indirect-only and a direct-comparison setting. No estimator, weighting scheme or selective-inference correction recovers valid inference for such a contrast, and the alpha-spending boundaries imported from trial sequential analysis make the inflation worse rather than better under the strongest triggering rule. The only remedy currently on offer is to refuse to pool the triggered trial, which discards the precision gain that network-informed trial planning exists to deliver. Nothing in current trial reporting records whether a comparison was chosen from a prior synthesis, so a network cannot identify which of its own studies were triggered even if a correction existed.

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text:
Why it is open
The correction needs the selection event to be written down, and the triggering rule is almost never stated: investigators and sponsors respond to a promising synthesis informally, so there is no threshold, no test statistic and no decision function to condition on. Even where the rule is explicit, conditioning changes the estimator that everything downstream depends on, so a corrected contrast is no longer the same quantity as the uncorrected contrasts elsewhere in the network, and nothing says how a decision model should combine the two. The problem also cannot be avoided by intent, because living and continuously updated network meta-analyses absorb every relevant trial regardless of why it was run, so a policy of excluding triggered trials is not implementable at scale. And the machinery currently used to control repeated testing in updated networks was designed for a different multiplicity, namely repeated looks at accumulating evidence, and it makes this inflation larger rather than smaller.

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ye et al. 2023, Frontiers in Pharmacology
Simulates the type I error of a network estimate for a contrast whose new trial was triggered by a promising prior network result, under both network analysis and alpha-spending sequential analysis, and states that methods for analyzing triggered and independently motivated trials together remain to be developed.


Salanti et al. 2018, Trials
Conditional trial design: sizes and configures a new trial against an existing network while minimizing required sample size; the practice that creates the dependence this problem is about.


Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis and Salanti 2016, Statistics in Medicine
Plans future studies from the precision of network meta-analysis results, making the prior network an explicit input to the decision to run a trial.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2018, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
Continuously updated network meta-analysis with statistical monitoring, importing alpha-spending boundaries from trial sequential analysis into repeated network updating; the machinery shown to worsen the inflation under a strong triggering rule.


Brok et al. 2008, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Establishes the multiplicity created by repeated meta-analytic testing and the trial sequential analysis response; the origin of the boundaries used in updated networks.


Crequit et al. 2016, BMC Medicine
Documents how quickly a synthesis goes out of date and argues for living cumulative synthesis; the reason a policy of excluding triggered trials is not implementable at scale.


Berk et al. 2013, Annals of Statistics
Valid post-selection inference: guarantees that hold simultaneously over all possible selections, the conservative route requiring no knowledge of the selection rule.


Lee et al. 2016, Annals of Statistics
Exact post-selection inference by conditioning on a polyhedral selection event; the construction closest to what a stated triggering threshold on a network contrast would need.


Bauer and Kohne 1994, Biometrics
Combination tests for adaptive interim analyses, showing how a second stage chosen in response to first-stage data can be combined with the first while preserving the overall error rate whatever the adaptation rule.


Whitehead 1986, Biometrika
Bias of maximum likelihood estimation following a sequential stopping rule, with a correction; the single-trial analogue of estimating a contrast whose data existence depended on an earlier result.

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Treat the triggering rule as a selection event and condition on it: where the rule can be stated, for instance run a trial when the network contrast exceeds a threshold, the conditional distribution of the pooled estimate given that event is computable under the normal network likelihood, so a selection-adjusted interval follows by the same construction used for exact post-selection inference after the lasso. Where the rule is unavailable, use a combination test instead: treat the pre-trigger network and the new trial as two stages and combine their evidence with a prespecified combination function, which is valid whatever generated the second stage, at a known cost in efficiency. Compare the two across the triggering rules that occur in practice, calibrating against the published simulation and reporting type I error, power and estimator bias for each. Fix the reporting gap in the same pass, since no correction can be applied to a network that cannot tell which of its studies were triggered: a trial record should state whether its comparison was chosen from a prior synthesis, and a living review should date-stamp the network state that preceded each new inclusion. Revisit the alpha-spending boundaries currently imported into updated network meta-analysis, which were designed for repeated looks at accumulating evidence and were shown to increase rather than reduce the inflation under the strongest triggering rule.

title: No selective-inference correction for outcome-triggered new trials pooled into NMA
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single simulation study that quantifies the inflation and states that methods for jointly analyzing triggered and independently motivated trials remain to be developed, and the reviewer accepted it as distinct from evidence-set selection, model selection and ordinary next-study design because the existence and target of the new data depend on prior network results. Resting on one paper, the error rates are simulated under stated triggering rules and how often real trials are triggered this way is undocumented.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis and Salanti 2015, Statistics in Medicine’ -> ‘Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis and Salanti 2016, Statistics in Medicine’ 10.1002/sim.6608 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2015 online and 2016 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text: EVB-10 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text:
Statement
Network meta-analysis models assume every included trial contributes a randomized contrast between concurrently randomized arms followed from a common time zero. Re-randomization, randomized withdrawal, enrichment, response-adaptive allocation and dose titration break that assumption: their published contrasts are conditional on an interim response, on a run-in or on an adaptive allocation rule, and the arms the network needs were in part never randomized. No general framework states, for a given non-parallel design, which target contrast the trial identifies, which assumptions convert it to a parallel-design contrast, and how the conversion uncertainty enters the network likelihood; practice is a bespoke arithmetic reconstruction per trial, or more often silent use of the conditional subgroup as though it were the trial. The consequences are first order rather than second order. In the one worked example available, treating the re-randomized responder subgroup as the trial gave a placebo maintenance response of 31.2 percent against 15.5 percent after reconstruction and roughly halved the odds ratios against placebo, and a published network meta-analysis had already made that error. The canonical guidance does not close the gap: the Cochrane Handbook chapter on variants of randomized trials covers cluster, cross-over, stepped-wedge and factorial designs and says nothing about randomized-withdrawal, responder-enriched or re-randomization designs.

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text:
Why it is open
The reconstructions rest on assumptions no data can check: that a responder-to-non-responder efficacy ratio observed at one dose transports to another, that all protocol-mandated switchers would have dropped out, and, where an external prior fills a missing arm, that its arbitrary down-weighting is the right one; none of that uncertainty is separated from sampling uncertainty in the reported interval. The designs are also not one family with one fix, because an interim-response gate, an adaptive allocation rule and a titration schedule each destroy a different piece of the parallel-design structure, so a general framework must enumerate them rather than generalize over them, and the enumeration has not been written. The problem grows rather than shrinks: established class efficacy makes long placebo-controlled maintenance periods hard to justify, so more of the pivotal evidence entering networks comes from designs of this kind. The obvious conservative remedy is not obviously safe either, since work on trials stopped early for benefit concludes that excluding them from a synthesis underestimates effects and overestimates information while including them is close to unbiased, so exclusion of non-standard designs cannot be adopted as a default without its own analysis.

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Druyts et al. 2014, Clinical Epidemiology
Names the challenge of incorporating alternative-design trials into network meta-analyses and indirect comparisons, and supplies the worked reconstruction of a re-randomized maintenance trial that shows how far the naive analysis is off.


Varu et al. 2019, Current Medical Research and Opinion
Treatment sequence network meta-analysis case study; a bespoke per-trial reconstruction presented as novel and explicitly unvalidated, with no simulation and no benchmark.


Higgins, Eldridge and Li, Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, chapter 23
The canonical guidance on including variants of randomized trials; covers cluster-randomized, cross-over, stepped-wedge and multi-arm or factorial designs, and does not address randomized-withdrawal, responder-enriched or re-randomization designs.


Elbourne et al. 2002, International Journal of Epidemiology
The template for successfully bringing one non-parallel design into meta-analysis, with the correlation structure and unit-of-analysis issues of cross-over trials handled explicitly rather than by conversion.


FDA 2019, Enrichment Strategies for Clinical Trials to Support Approval of Human Drugs and Biological Products
Regulatory guidance defining prognostic and predictive enrichment and randomized-withdrawal designs; establishes which population an enriched trial’s result belongs to, the fact a synthesis has to respect.


Barberio et al. 2025, Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics
Runs design-stratified networks, separately for re-randomizing and treat-through maintenance trials, and reports different rankings in each; the conservative alternative to conversion, at the cost of two answers to one question.


Marschner and Schou 2022, Clinical Trials
Analyzes adaptive platform trials using a network approach, showing that some non-parallel randomization structures can be represented inside a network rather than converted into a parallel-design contrast.


Schou and Marschner 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Investigates bias in meta-analysis from trials stopped early and finds that excluding them underestimates effects and overestimates information while including them is close to unbiased; the counterweight to a default of dropping non-standard designs.


Marschner, Askie and Schou 2020, Research Synthesis Methods
Recommends sensitivity analyses for the impact of early stopping on a systematic review; a worked example of treating a design feature as a sensitivity dimension rather than an exclusion criterion.


Pallmann et al. 2018, BMC Medicine
Catalogues adaptive designs and their reporting requirements, supplying the enumeration of design features that a synthesis framework would have to work through.


Efthimiou et al. 2017, Statistics in Medicine
Combines randomized and non-randomized evidence in a network with explicit bias and down-weighting parameters; the closest existing template for admitting evidence of a different structure without pretending it has the same status.


Dias et al. 2013, Medical Decision Making
The generalized linear modeling framework on which network likelihoods are built, which takes concurrently randomized arms and a common time zero as given.

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Enumerate before generalizing: build a catalogue of non-parallel randomized designs and, for each, write the target contrast the trial identifies in potential-outcome terms, the assumptions mapping it to a parallel-design contrast, and whether those assumptions are checkable from what gets published. Represent the conversion as a model rather than as arithmetic, so its uncertainty is a parameter with a prior or a sensitivity range that enters the network likelihood alongside sampling error instead of disappearing into a point estimate. Where the conversion is not identified, make the design-stratified network the primary analysis and the converted network a sensitivity analysis, following the applied practice that already runs separate re-randomized and treat-through syntheses. Extend the network representation used for adaptive platform trials, which handles non-concurrent randomization without converting it away, to see how far interim-response gates and titration schedules can be modeled as extra nodes and time strata rather than reconstructed. Simulate networks mixing design families against known truth and report bias, coverage and rank reversals for naive pooling, stratification and conversion, since no benchmark exists for any of the three.

title: No general NMA framework for non-parallel randomized trial designs
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single 2014 paper that names the challenge and supplies the worked reconstruction, and the reviewer accepted it as an identification problem not reducible to endpoint, population or treatment-switching heterogeneity. An independent search supports the absence: the conversion technique appears only in the methods sections of applied network meta-analyses without derivation or validation, and the Cochrane Handbook chapter on design variants does not cover these designs at all.

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text: EVB-08 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Tractability 4/5

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text:
Statement
The comparison-adjusted funnel plot is the applied default for detecting small-study effects in a network, and it requires the analyst to prespecify an ordering of comparisons encoding the direction in which small studies are expected to be biased, typically newer drug versus older drug or active versus placebo. Where no such ordering can be justified, which is common outside that case, the plot cannot be drawn and no assumption-light substitute is available; reviewers then judge reporting bias from the completeness of their literature search, which speaks to retrieval rather than to selective publication. Six Cochrane reviews sharing one prespecified protocol each record that no meaningful order of comparisons could be found, so the plot was not produced and search completeness was substituted for the assessment. Selection models for a full network meta-analysis do exist in the methods literature, but they are not in the applied toolchain those reviews used and they require an assumed selection function or direction, so they relocate the assumption rather than removing it. What is missing is a diagnostic whose null does not depend on an assumed direction of bias: a statistic, or a bound on how much small-study effects can move a given network estimate, that is invariant to how the comparisons are labeled.

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text:
Why it is open
Small-study effects are detectable only as an association between a study’s precision and its effect, and in a network the effects sit on different comparisons, so they must be projected onto a common axis before any association can be read; the prespecified ordering is that projection, and estimating it from the data would assume the thing being tested. A direction-free alternative has to give up resolution: a statistic invariant to relabeling can indicate that asymmetry exists somewhere in the network without saying which contrast it distorts, and the contrast is what a review needs. The selection-model route is identified only through its parametric selection function, whose sensitivity parameters are precisely the judgment the reviewers said they could not make. A separate and equally binding constraint is operational: these assessments are made by review authors inside review software that offers no such method, so a diagnostic requiring a bespoke Bayesian selection model will not be run whatever its properties.

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chaimani and Salanti 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Introduces the comparison-adjusted funnel plot for networks and states the requirement that comparisons be ordered by a prespecified expectation about the direction of small-study effects.


Chaimani et al. 2013, PLoS ONE
Provides the Stata implementation that made the comparison-adjusted funnel plot the applied default, including the user-supplied ordering as a required input.


Mavridis et al. 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Extends the Copas selection model to network meta-analysis in a fully Bayesian formulation, adjusting network estimates for publication bias given an assumed selection mechanism.


Mavridis et al. 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Selection model for a full network meta-analysis in which the probability of publication depends on the study’s p-value; the closest thing to a network-level statistical adjustment, still requiring an assumed selection function.


Trinquart, Chatellier and Ravaud 2012, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Applies reporting-bias adjustment to a network of antidepressant trials, showing how much a network’s conclusions can move once selective publication is modeled.


Copas and Shi 2000, Biostatistics
The pairwise selection-model sensitivity analysis that the network extensions generalize, with the selection parameter varied over a range rather than estimated.


Rucker et al. 2011, Biostatistics
Limit meta-analysis, which adjusts a pairwise effect for small-study effects by extrapolating to infinite precision without positing a publication mechanism; the assumption-light pairwise method that has no network form requiring no ordering.


Egger et al. 1997, BMJ
The regression test for funnel-plot asymmetry that the comparison-adjusted plot generalizes, and the source of the precision-versus-effect framing.


Chiocchia et al. 2021, BMC Medicine
ROB-MEN gives per-comparison risk-of-bias judgments for missing evidence in a network without requiring an ordering, but it is a structured judgment framework rather than a statistical diagnostic, and it does not apply to disconnected interventions.


Page et al. 2021, Research Synthesis Methods
Review of methods for investigating publication and other reporting biases in meta-analyses, setting out what is available and how weak the evidence for each method’s operating characteristics is.

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the direction-free statistic first: a relabeling-invariant measure of the association between precision and effect across a whole network, calibrated by simulation so that its size and power are known under a null of no small-study effects and under alternatives differing in how many comparisons are affected and how strongly. Pair it with a bound rather than a test: for a selection function whose strength is swept across a range, report how far each network estimate can move, attributing the movement through the contribution matrix to the comparisons that actually supply the contrast. Establish the operating characteristics of the comparison-adjusted funnel plot under a misspecified ordering, which is what a reviewer risks by choosing one anyway; nothing currently says whether a wrong order is worse than no plot at all. Ship whatever survives in the packages reviewers already use, with a default that runs without a user-supplied ordering, since a diagnostic that has to be commissioned separately will not be run. Use the six reviews sharing one protocol as the benchmark case, where the same recorded failure and the same fallback to search completeness give a clean comparison for anything new.

title: Network small-study-effects diagnostics lack an assumption-light default
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a family of Cochrane reviews sharing a protocol, all of which record that no ordering of comparisons could be justified, and the reviewer accepted it on the grounds that existing selection models do not supply an assumption-light applied default. The evidence is applied rather than methodological, so it documents that the diagnostic is unavailable in practice rather than proving that no direction-free statistic could be constructed.

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text: EVB-06 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text:
Statement
Meta-analysis and network meta-analysis likelihoods treat every study as an independent sample, and that assumption fails whenever real-world evidence enters the network: several eligible publications frequently analyze the same registry, claims database or electronic health record source, produced by different investigators with different study years, populations and analytic choices, so their reported treatment effects share an unknown fraction of the same patients. The same failure arises between real-world studies and trials whose participants also appear in a national treatment database, between salami-sliced multicenter reports, and between single-arm studies sharing a historical control. Double counting overstates the precision of the affected contrasts and can move point estimates: removing overlapping-population studies from one public health synthesis moved a pooled adjusted risk ratio from 1.63 (1.39 to 1.92) to 1.50 (1.24 to 1.83) with increased heterogeneity, and in another review overlap was so pervasive that no meta-analysis could be run at all. The two responses in use are both unsatisfactory. Selecting one pivotal publication per database discards evidence and makes the estimate depend on a discretionary rule, which changed statistical conclusions for three of six comparisons in one sparse multiple sclerosis network; including all publications requires a between-publication correlation that cannot be estimated from published summaries and was therefore fixed at assumed moderate values that neither reproduced the single-publication point estimates nor widened the intervals beyond the base case. The one estimator that models the dependence directly takes the number of overlapping observations as an input, which is exactly what published reports do not give. What is missing is an overlap-aware synthesis model identifiable from what publications actually report, a defensible bound on the dependence when it cannot be counted, and comparative evidence on which of the ad hoc inclusion rules is least harmful.

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text:
Why it is open
The overlap fraction is a property of the underlying patient records, which the analyst does not hold, so the correlation between two published effect estimates from one database is not a function of the reported summaries; it is unidentified rather than merely hard to estimate. Matching, weighting and trimming inside the source studies mean the number of patients actually contributing to each published estimate is unknown, so even the magnitude of the precision error cannot be bounded by comparing sample sizes. A three-level model with a database random effect does not repair it, because that model assumes sampling errors are conditionally independent given the database effect, which is precisely what shared patients violate. Robust variance estimation handles clustered effect estimates with unknown within-cluster correlation, but it has never been evaluated for participant overlap in a network, where the dependence links specific contrasts across studies rather than effect sizes within one. The remedy that would identify the quantity is organizational rather than statistical, requiring either record-level data sharing or a convention obliging authors to report enough provenance to bound the overlap, and no synthesis reporting standard asks for it.

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Betts et al. 2023, Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research
case study in multiple sclerosis handling related real-world publications in a network meta-analysis; states that estimating a specific correlation between any two related publications is impossible, specifies assumed moderate correlations instead, and shows that neither the assumed-correlation route nor the single-publication selection route is satisfactory


Hussein et al. 2022, BMC Public Health
catalogs the mechanisms by which the same participants enter a synthesis twice, quantifies the effect in case studies, and states that current practices only mitigate it and that methodological and guideline development is needed


Lin and Sullivan 2009, American Journal of Human Genetics
gives a closed-form correction for meta-analysis of association studies with overlapping subjects; the correction requires the number of overlapping subjects as an input, which published clinical reports do not supply


Hedges, Tipton and Johnson 2010, Research Synthesis Methods
robust variance estimation for dependent effect estimates with unknown within-cluster correlation; a candidate route that has not been evaluated for participant overlap across studies in a network

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Parameterize the dependence by the overlap fraction between two publications and derive how the network variance and the point estimate move as a function of it, so a sensitivity analysis becomes a one-parameter curve on an interpretable axis rather than an assumed correlation. Then derive worst-case bounds over the overlap sets consistent with what the publications report, namely the data source, accrual window, extraction date, eligibility criteria and arm sizes, so an analyst can publish an interval valid for every overlap compatible with the evidence. Evaluate the inclusion rules currently in use, keep the largest, keep the peer-reviewed, keep one per database, include everything, against record-level truth in a database where the individual records are available and the true overlap can be computed, across overlap sizes and network topologies. Add the minimum provenance fields to reporting standards for real-world evidence in synthesis, since overlap cannot be bounded at all without them.

title: No usable correction for overlapping participant populations across studies
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Two independent readers proposed it, one from a methods commentary on double counting in public health synthesis and one from an applied network that had to assume correlations it could not estimate, and the reviewer accepted both, noting that assumed-correlation sensitivity analyses supply neither an identification strategy, nor a defensible bound, nor a principled inclusion and weighting rule.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text: EVB-04 Partially addressed Very high priority Speculative

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Statement
Methods for choosing the next data collection by expected decision value exist and are mature: conditional trial design sizes and configures a new trial against an existing network to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value (Salanti et al. 2018, doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2; Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014, pmid:25225031), and expected value of sample information has practical tutorials and worked prioritization examples (doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292; doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-092158). Neither has been applied to deciding which individual patient dataset to acquire for a population-adjusted comparison, nor to sizing and allocating a bridging trial that would connect two disconnected subnetworks. Whether acquisition in ITC practice is in fact opportunistic is undocumented: no auditor found a survey of it.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Why it is open
The general machinery is decision-theoretic and only produces an answer once the decision, utility, costs, access probability, model uncertainty and target population are specified; for a population-adjusted comparison none of these is currently packaged as an input to acquisition. The value of an additional IPD study depends on the target population, the bridge in use and the decision threshold, and no published formulation ties those to a request for a specific dataset. For disconnected networks the harder version, choosing which bridge treatment to run and how to allocate sample across the gap, was not found by any auditor. What is open is the ITC-specific operational formulation and its robustness, not the existence of a principled criterion.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Salanti et al. 2018, Trials
Four-step framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial that updates an existing network while minimizing required sample size, allowing the new trial to omit some interventions and still contribute direct and indirect evidence.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014, Biometrical Journal
Derives conditional power of a network meta-analysis to inform the design of future trials; earliest of the conditional trial design papers and establishes that sample size can be computed conditional on the existing network.


Heath et al. 2022, Medical Decision Making
Practical guidance and recommendations for four model-based methods of computing expected value of sample information efficiently; shows the machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature and tutorialized.


Glynn et al. 2025, BMJ Open (DiaDeM)
Worked example of value-of-information analysis used to prioritize which data to collect, showing the acquisition-as-decision-object framing is present in the wider literature.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing value-of-information and conditional trial design machinery to the ITC setting rather than build new criteria: specify the decision, utility, costs, access probability and target population, then rank candidate IPD acquisitions by expected decision value. Extend conditional trial design from adding a trial to a connected network to the disconnected case, where the objects of choice are the bridge treatment, the sample size and the allocation across the gap. Establishing whether current acquisition is opportunistic requires a survey of practice, which no auditor could find, so that claim should be tested before it is used to justify the programme.

title: No decision-value method chooses which IPD or bridging trial to get
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides. Reopened by the full-text reading: 3 findings from 3 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from unverifiable to partially-addressed.
The source titled this. “Data acquisition is opportunistic rather than decision-driven” The title asserts that acquisition is opportunistic, which the audit recorded as undocumented since no survey of ITC practice was found.
The source said. “Decisions about which individual patient dataset to obtain, or which bridging trial to run, are made opportunistically rather than by any principled criterion linking the acquisition to the decision it would improve.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no formal object exists to quantify what a dataset would contribute and listed bridging-trial design as a research direction; conditional trial design for networks has been published since 2014 (pmid:25225031; doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2) and EVSI tooling is mature (doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292), as the literature auditor documented and GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed on decision-theoretic grounds. Grok agreed the ITC-specific application is absent but read the entry as supported, so the disagreement here is over framing rather than over what exists.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): Claim 3 is the weak point. Salanti et al. 2018 Trials present a four-step conditional trial design framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial updating an existing network while minimizing required sample size, explicitly allowing the new trial to omit some interventions while still contributing direct and indirect evidence. Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014 Biometrical Journal derive conditional power of an NMA to inform future trial design; Nikolakopoulou 2019 Trials surveys methodologists on it; Siontis 2022 F1000Research applies conditional sample size calculation. Designing the next trial from an existing network is an established literature, not a proposed research direction. What I could not find in any retrieved source is the specific case the entry names: sizing and allocating a bridging trial across the gap between disconnected subnetworks. Claim 2 is similarly half-built: EVSI machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature (Heath 2022 MDM, Vervaart 2023/2024 MDM, Glynn 2025 BMJ Open), but I found no application to choosing which IPD to acquire for an ITC. Claim 1 concerns current practice and I found no survey of it; Clayton 2017 Trials reports only 6% of trialists using VOI, which is adjacent but a different population.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Corrected

statement: corrected a factual claim Salanti et al. 2018 minimizes sample size for a target conditional power or precision. The words ‘net benefit’ and ‘utility’ do not appear in it. The entry’s other citation, Heath et al. 2022 on expected value of sample information, is decision-value and is correctly described. Previously: “Methods for choosing the next data collection by expected decision value exist and are mature: conditional trial design sizes and configures a new trial against an existing network (Salanti et al. 2018, doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2; Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014, pmid:25225031), and expected value of sample information has practical tutorials and worked prioritization examples (doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292; doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-092158). Neither has been applied to deciding which individual patient dataset to acquire for a population-adjusted comparison, nor to sizing and allocating a bridgi”

Verdict changed

unverifiable -> partially-addressed 3 surviving findings from: Connecting a disconnected trial network with a new trial: op; Continuously updated network meta-analysis and statistical m; OP22 Using Threshold Analysis To Guide Searches For Addition. New citations: 10.1017/s0266462322000812, 10.1177/0962280216659896, 10.1186/s12874-023-01896-7 Previously: “Methods for choosing the next data collection by expected decision value exist and are mature: conditional trial design sizes and configures a new trial against an existing network to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision rather than by expected decision value to reach a target power or precision ra”

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Claim 3 is the weak point. Salanti et al. 2018 Trials present a four-step conditional trial design framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial updating an existing network while minimizing required sample size, explicitly allowing the new trial to omit some interventions while still contributing direct and indirect evidence. Nikolakopoulou et al. 2014 Biometrical Journal derive conditional power of an NMA to inform future trial design; Nikolakopoulou 2019 Trials surveys methodologists on it; Siontis 2022 F1000Research applies conditional sample size calculation. Designing the next trial from an existing network is an established literature, not a proposed research direction. What I could not find in any retrieved source is the specific case the entry names: sizing and allocating a bridging trial across the gap between disconnected subnetworks. Claim 2 is similarly half-built: EVSI machinery for deciding what data to collect is mature (Heath 2022 MDM, Vervaart 2023/2024 MDM, Glynn 2025 BMJ Open), but I found no application to choosing which IPD to acquire for an ITC. Claim 1 concerns current practice and I found no survey of it; Clayton 2017 Trials reports only 6% of trialists using VOI, which is adjacent but a different population. Cites doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2: Directly contradicts the framing of claim 3 as a proposed direction: optimal design of the next trial given an existing network is published methodology with worked examples.. Cites pmid:25225031: Earliest of the conditional-trial-design papers; establishes that sample size for a future trial can be computed conditional on the existing network.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X211026292: Confirms claim 2’s machinery exists and is tutorialized; the ITC-specific application of choosing which IPD to acquire is what remains unbuilt.. Cites doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-092158: Recent worked example of VOI used to prioritise which data to collect, showing the acquisition-as-decision-object framing is not absent from the literature generally..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 and C3 are technically valid research directions: expected-utility or value-of-information criteria can rank candidate IPD acquisitions, and optimal-design criteria can choose bridge treatments, sample size, and allocation. The central empirical claim C1, that current decisions are generally opportunistic, is unsupported here. The literal statement that no formal object exists is false because decision theory already supplies such objects once the decision, utility, costs, predictive model, access probability, and relevant uncertainties are specified. What remains open is an ITC-specific operational formulation and its robustness, not the existence of a principled criterion. This is generally a roadmap and resource-allocation issue rather than a universal threat to identification or decision-grade validity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Search assumed VOI and optimal design had already made IPD acquisition decision-driven. General value-of-information methods for HTA research prioritization and study design are mature (ISPOR VOI task force reports; Jackson et al. reviews of VOI in policy models; EVPI/EVPPI/EVSI tooling). That infrastructure means C2 is a defensible direction rather than science fiction. However, no retrieved 2020–2026 paper or software release implements a standard, decision-linked criterion for which IPD dataset to request for PAIC/ITC, or optimal sample allocation of a bridging trial across a gap between disconnected subnetworks, as a routine acquisition object. Dose-response and other NMA extensions discuss reconnecting disconnected networks when common agents exist; that is model-based reconnection, not VOI-guided bridge-trial design. No CRAN/GitHub signal for multinma/maicplus/netmeta/outstandR closed this acquisition gap. C1 (opportunistic access in practice) remains descriptive and unfalsified by a competing formal acquisition framework. Queries: VOI/EVSI IPD meta-analysis; VOI network meta research prioritization; optimal bridge trial disconnected NMA; active IPD acquisition strategy. Vote open with moderate-low confidence because VOI is adjacent and may be applied without being published as ITC-specific method.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

section: How the evidence falls in time
text:
How the evidence falls in time
7 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2016 to 2023. The most recent paper to touch this reports progress on it, and every paper calling it open is older.
It is also being closed in pieces: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.
Does the later work answer the earlier work? Put to an independent reviewer with the older and newer claims side by side, it judged that the later work answers a component of it, leaving a named part (high confidence). The 2023 disconnected-network paper gives a substantive, network-dependent rule for selecting the treatment pair in a new bridging trial. It fixes equal allocation and does not formulate acquisition or trial design by decision value, costs, or utility, so it resolves only one component of the earlier gap. What remains: Choosing which IPD to acquire; decision-value or cost-based selection and sample allocation for a bridging trial; and evidence on whether such methods are used in practice.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text: EVB-02 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Statement
Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can materially change an indirect comparison by changing which studies, populations and contrasts are represented, and this is demonstrated rather than hypothetical: a multiverse of 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone reported a Janus effect (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3), and a multiverse over all possible antidepressant networks found 172 of 231 pairwise comparisons showing opposite effects between the 1st and 99th percentiles (Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848). What remains open is that multiverse reporting is not required or routinely performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible. Selection changes how relevant the assembled evidence is to an externally defined target population; it does not by itself define the target estimand. The same discretion operates on the boundary of the network and not only on which studies pass eligibility. Admitting a non-focal treatment can connect the network, sharpen the focal contrasts and stabilize the heterogeneity estimate while importing populations whose effect-modifier distributions threaten transitivity, and because a rank is defined relative to the treatments in the network, scope is part of the estimand rather than a nuisance choice. No criterion prices that trade-off in a common currency, the search and extraction cost of extension falls on the reviewer rather than on the decision maker, and only 40 percent of 365 published drug network meta-analyses reported any objective criterion for which drugs or classes were admitted. Ranking output is affected more sharply than effect estimates, because SUCRA and P-score are functionals of the whole admitted node set, so admitting regimens that no decision-maker can choose shifts every other treatment’s position in the hierarchy. Nothing in current reporting requires the node-admission rule to be stated, requires the hierarchy to be recomputed over a decision-relevant set of available and viable regimens, or reports any measure of how far a treatment’s rank depends on inadmissible nodes.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Why it is open
The evidence set is assembled by the party that reports the result, and every downstream analysis conditions on the assembled network, so no covariate adjustment recovers the comparisons that were excluded. The tools to expose this now exist and their published applications show inclusion choices can flip the direction of an estimate, but nothing obliges a sponsor submission to report one, and the demonstrations to date sit in the general synthesis literature rather than in HTA practice. An undefined multiverse over all defensible networks also reintroduces analyst discretion and multiplicity, so the missing piece is a transparent rule for what counts as defensible rather than the technique itself.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Vinatier et al. 2024, BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine
Multiverse analysis covering all possible network meta-analyses over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step.


Palpacuer et al. 2019, BMC Medicine
Enumerates 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene versus naltrexone by varying eligibility criteria and analytic model, showing that inclusion decisions alone can reverse the direction of the comparison.


Guelimi et al. 2025, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Quantifies how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change network meta-analysis conclusions in psoriasis; shows sensitivity over alternative networks is operational.


Tonin et al. 2018, PLOS ONE
Maps 365 drug network meta-analyses and finds that fewer than half, 146 or 40 percent, reported objective criteria for selecting the drugs or classes included, while 87 or 23.8 percent gave explicitly non-objective reasons such as most commonly used drugs, with no improvement over the period studied. Supplies the base rate for undisclosed node-admission rules.


Batson et al. 2016, PLOS ONE
Extends an atrial fibrillation network from 4 trials to 19 trials and 15 treatments solely to make covariate and baseline-risk models fittable, finds no interaction signal, and states that there is an unmet practical need to know how far to extend a network in the search for indirect evidence in health technology assessment.


Caldwell et al. 2015, Value in Health
Supplies the precision half of the scope decision and concludes that reviewers should include only those additional non-focal treatments compared with at least two focal treatments. Names value-of-information analysis as the tool for the cost and bias halves without applying it, and leaves the bias consequence of extension as an important question to address.


Caldwell 2014, Systematic Reviews
Overview of conducting systematic reviews with network meta-analysis, which records that network size has been called an unsolved issue in network meta-analysis and an area of developing interest, and reduces practice to prespecifying a population, intervention, comparator and outcome plus an extension strategy.


Babul et al. 2026, Cureus
Editorial examining how dose and regimen nodes were admitted into three alopecia areata evidence syntheses of oral JAK inhibitors. In a network of placebo against 22 active interventions, only six corresponded to approved drugs at approved doses, ritlecitinib entered at five regimens although one is approved, and deuruxolitinib 12 mg twice daily, never approved and placed under an FDA clinical hold in May 2023 for unfavorable benefit-risk, was reported in the abstract as the most efficacious intervention for both the primary and the aspirational endpoint. Its remedy is procedural: prespecify exclusion of doses never advanced to pivotal trials or analyze them only in prespecified sensitivity analyses, and report approval status and regulatory actions alongside pooled estimates.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The multiverse machinery exists and the work is to require and discipline it rather than to invent it: specify transparent rules for which alternative evidence sets are defensible, then report the estimate across them as a matter of course. Protocol-first feasibility assessment that fixes eligibility before results are known addresses the outcome-aware part of the problem that a multiverse cannot, since a multiverse run after the fact still starts from a chosen frame. Applying target-trial emulation to the construction of the evidence set rather than to a single analysis remains unevidenced; the literature auditor could not verify any published instance and Grok also left it open.

title: Evidence-set assembly can favor the sponsor before modeling begins
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Multiverse analysis over the assembled evidence set has been demonstrated for indirect comparisons and for network meta-analysis and shows that inclusion decisions can flip the direction of the estimate; what remains open is that it is not routinely required or performed in sponsor submissions, and there is no accepted criterion for which alternative networks count as defensible.
The source said. “Eligibility and comparator decisions taken while assembling the evidence base can induce a favorable network or a favorable target population before any modeling begins, and only one of the defensible networks is ever shown.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented multiverse analysis over defensible networks as an emerging direction and said alternative networks are never reported; the literature auditor found two published multiverses of exactly that object (Palpacuer et al. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3; Vinatier et al. 2024, doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848), with a third for inclusion criteria in psoriasis (Guelimi et al. 2025, doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02558-6). GPT-5.6 Sol separately rejected the conflation of the population represented by the selected studies with an externally defined target population, and struck the universal claims that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are never shown.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): The claim that eligibility and comparator choices can favor a network or target population before modeling, and that only one defensible network is typically shown, remains faithful for HTA/ITC practice. Recent work does, however, implement the multiverse response for treatment/network assembly in evidence synthesis, so the problem is not open as if no method existed. Vinatier et al. (2024) ran a multiverse covering all possible NMAs on different treatment combinations in antidepressants and showed large vibration of effects, especially for indirect comparisons. Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading.

46 findings from the reading assert this problem is open; the closure was re-examined and stands Put to an independent reviewer with the closing auditors’ reasoning, the work they relied on, and the new findings in view together. The new findings repeatedly document that evidence-set and comparator choices can change results, sometimes in sponsor-authored analyses, but that mechanism was already conceded by the closure. The closure also expressly retained the practical residual that multiverse reporting is not routinely required and that no accepted rule defines defensible alternative networks. The 2026 Pompe analyses are strong applied examples, but they show adoption and governance gaps rather than contradicting Palpacuer or Vinatier’s demonstrations that the sensitivity method exists. None establishes that the cited methods fail to apply or that a principled defensibility criterion has since displaced the closure’s factual basis. (reviewer confidence: high)

53 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I retrieved two published multiverse analyses of exactly the object this entry proposes as future work, both in indirect comparison settings. Palpacuer 2019 BMC Medicine enumerated 9216 indirect comparison meta-analyses of nalmefene vs naltrexone by varying eligibility (condition, abstinence, sex, comorbidity, psychological support, dose, duration, outcome, publication status, risk of bias) and analytic model, and reported a ‘Janus effect’. Vinatier 2024 BMJ EBM ran the multiverse over network composition itself: all possible NMAs over treatment combinations across 522 antidepressant trials and 116,477 patients. Claim 1 and claim 2 are therefore not merely plausible but empirically demonstrated. Claim 4, however, is written as if multiverse analysis over defensible networks were a promising future direction (‘Emerging’ maturity); it has been executed at scale and published in general medical journals. The why_open sentence ‘Defensible alternative networks usually exist and are never reported’ is contradicted by these two papers. Claim 3 (target-trial emulation applied to evidence-set construction) I could not verify; the only candidate I found was in an obscure venue I will not cite. Cites doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848: Executes the entry’s proposed direction: a multiverse over all defensible network compositions, quantifying how far conclusions move with the assembly step.. Cites doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3: Demonstrates claims 1 and 2 for an indirect comparison specifically, varying eligibility criteria that define both the network and the target population..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Evidence-set selection can materially change network connectivity, available contrasts, precision, and conclusions, so C1 and the underlying robustness problem are valid. C2 conflates the population represented by the selected studies with the externally defined target population; study selection changes evidential relevance to a target but should not itself define the target estimand. Target-trial principles can help prespecify eligibility and estimand attributes, but calling evidence-set assembly target-trial emulation does not recover excluded information or identify selection effects. C4 is a reasonable sensitivity strategy if defensible networks are specified by transparent rules, although an undefined multiverse of all defensible networks invites further researcher discretion and multiplicity. The assertions that every inclusion decision is outcome-aware and that alternatives are usually or never reported are unsupported universal claims. This can be critical when eligibility was selected after results were known, but it is not automatically a modeling failure in every ITC.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

Guelimi et al. (2025) quantified how inclusion criteria and other methodological choices change NMA conclusions in psoriasis and explicitly contrasted their design with prior all-possible-networks work. These papers substantiate C1/C4 as live, demonstrated issues and give a usable multiverse template. They do not solve sponsor-side selective assembly, protocol-first eligibility fixed before knowing results, or target-trial emulation applied to the evidence set itself (C3); those remain open. RoB-NMA (2025) and PRISMA-NMA update work improve transparency of synthesis bias but do not replace multiverse reporting of defensible networks.
