title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text: DIS-21 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text:
Statement
When single-arm or aggregate studies are matched on reported baseline summaries to manufacture an edge that randomization did not supply, the analyst must set a maximum admissible dissimilarity, and nothing ties that cutoff to the bias it induces in the bridged contrast. The one empirical anchor available points the other way: arms of the same randomized trial differ by an average distance of 0.01, range 0.00 to 0.03, on a clinician-weighted covariate index, roughly an order of magnitude tighter than the threshold of 0.1 used in practice, and only one of eight admitted matches in a multiple myeloma network would have survived a randomized-trial-comparable cutoff (Schmitz et al. 2018, doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7). The cutoff also decides which cross-gap comparisons exist at all, since 8 of 56 candidate pairings fell below it and 5 of those connected the two subnetworks, so one number silently fixes both the point estimate and the reported comparison set. What the choice can cost is visible where an external check exists: on one contrast the matched analysis returned a hazard ratio of 1.15 (0.77 to 1.74) against 0.73 (0.52 to 1.03) and 0.60 (0.35 to 1.01) from individual-patient analyses, putting the bridged estimate on the opposite side of the null with the widest interval. A loose threshold matches studies that are not comparable while a tight one leaves the network disconnected or admits so few matches that uncertainty is understated, and nothing trades the two off. The distance metric, its covariate weights, its normalization and the threshold are all analyst choices with no standard, and a released implementation now exposes them as ordinary function arguments.

title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text:
Why it is open
Calibrating a cutoff against bias requires knowing the bridged contrast for candidate pairs at each level of dissimilarity, which is exactly what a disconnection removes; the calibration can only be borrowed from settings where the answer is known, and no such reference collection has been assembled. The index itself is not standard, since covariate choice, weighting and normalization vary by application, so a threshold calibrated on one index does not transfer to another. The two failure modes are not commensurable, one biasing the point estimate and the other understating uncertainty while shrinking the reported comparison set, and no loss function has been written that trades them against each other. Individual-level matching solved the analogous problem with caliper widths calibrated by simulation against mean squared error, but the study-level version has more covariates, no individual data, and a distance defined on reported summaries rather than on an estimated propensity score, so the existing result does not port.

title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Schmitz et al. 2018, BMC Medical Research Methodology
builds the matching bridge with a clinician-weighted covariate distance, states that no guidance exists on how similar is similar enough, adopts 0.1, then measures within-randomized-trial distances an order of magnitude smaller and reports the resulting sensitivity of between-network rankings to which matches are admitted


Thom et al. 2022, Medical Decision Making
extends aggregate-level matching to whole disconnected trials using Euclidean covariate distance and quantifies its bias and coverage by simulation, supplying the bias scale against which a threshold would have to be calibrated


Rucker et al. 2021, Biometrical Journal
compares component network meta-analysis against the matching bridge on the same disconnected network, the only head-to-head evidence on what admitting a manufactured edge buys relative to an alternative bridge


Austin 2011, Pharmaceutical Statistics
derives optimal caliper widths for propensity-score matching by simulation against mean squared error, the individual-level template for the calibration that study-level matching lacks


Austin 2009, Statistics in Medicine
sets out standardized differences as balance diagnostics and the conventional 0.1 rule of thumb, which is a balance convention rather than a calibration against bias and has no study-level analogue


closeloop 0.1.0 (CRAN, 2024)
implements the distance-based admission of single-arm observational studies into a network, leaving covariate set, weights and cutoff to the user with no default calibration, so the uncalibrated choice is now a routine software argument

title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Calibrate on networks where the answer is known: take connected networks with covariate reporting, delete edges to create artificial gaps, admit matches over a grid of thresholds, and report bias, interval coverage and decision reversal in the bridged contrast as a function of dissimilarity, separately for each index definition. Publish the resulting curve rather than a single number, so an analyst can read the expected bias at the threshold being proposed and see how many comparisons survive it. Standardize the index first, since a calibrated threshold means nothing without a fixed covariate set, weighting rule and normalization; the distribution of within-randomized-trial distances is the natural unit, so express thresholds as multiples of it. Report the whole admissible match space as a sensitivity analysis rather than one admitted set, and state the comparison set as a function of the threshold so that comparisons existing only at loose cutoffs are visibly conditional on it.

title: Match acceptance thresholds are uncalibrated against bridge bias
text:
Our study

A matched bridge’s admission threshold sets its bias: at the threshold used in practice the bridged contrast was biased by twice the true effect
The question put to it. How do the bias of a matched bridge across a disconnected network and the existence of the bridged comparison depend on the admission threshold, expressed in multiples of the distance between arms of one randomized trial?
What it found. No. With trial populations shifted across the gap, the bridged contrast (truth -0.2) was biased by -0.03 at the within-trial arm distance, where the bridge existed in only 8% of replicates, -0.13 at three times it and -0.44 at ten times it, near the threshold used in practice, where it always existed and its interval never covered. An index omitting the most prognostic covariate was biased by -0.25 even at the tightest threshold. Pooling pairs that reuse arms made intervals undercover even without bias (0.76 at ten units with good overlap).
Results.

Bias moved by 0.19 to 0.39 across thresholds at which the bridge existed at least a fifth of the time (poor overlap).
Probability the bridge exists at the within-trial distance: 46% (good overlap) and 8% (poor), all covariates in the index.
Study-level baseline heterogeneity (SD 0.1) lowered coverage at every threshold, since no covariate distance sees it.

Design.

Estimand

Cross-gap mean difference A versus B through a matched C-D bridge

Methods compared

matched bridge at thresholds of 1 to 20 within-trial distance units, two covariate indices

Data-generating mechanism

Two disconnected subnetworks of six trials; cross-gap control arms matched on covariate means at thresholds of 1 to 20 within-trial units; good or poor overlap, an index with or without the most prognostic covariate, study-level heterogeneity absent or present. 8 cells, 2000 replicates each.

Replicates

2000 per cell, 8 cells, 8 thresholds on the same data


What this does not answer. Monte Carlo networks only, no real-network deletions; one distance with two covariate sets; no component network meta-analysis bridge; admitted pairs pooled as independent. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted the admission cutoff as an estimand-defining decision rather than an overlap diagnostic or a covariate-selection question, noting that the reported within-trial distances show the threshold is consequential while providing no calibration from threshold to bias. The basis is a single applied network, which measured the within-randomized-trial distance distribution, found its own threshold an order of magnitude looser, and reported no way to trade the two failure modes.

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text: DIS-19 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text:
Statement
Population-adjustment methods split cleanly by connectivity: multilevel network meta-regression and network meta-analysis require a connected randomized network, while unanchored MAIC, STC and multilevel unanchored meta-regression assume fully disjoint evidence and buy identification with cross-treatment structural assumptions such as the shared prognostic factor assumption. Health technology assessment evidence bases routinely contain both at once, a connected set of randomized comparisons plus one or more single-arm studies for the new therapy. No published population-adjusted model places both in one likelihood, and no theory states how the randomized part should constrain the unanchored part: whether connected evidence partially identifies the prognostic coefficients the single-arm evidence needs, how far it can relax the shared prognostic factor assumption, and what identified set for the target contrast survives. Weaker versions of the architecture exist. Aggregate-data bridges hold connected and disconnected evidence in separate likelihood blocks with separate heterogeneity variances, which protects the randomized part but deliberately prevents it from informing the bridge (Thom et al. 2022, doi:10.1177/0272989X221097081); an arm-based Bayesian network meta-analysis borrows variance rather than mean information from single-arm trials through a commensurate prior (Wang et al. 2021, doi:10.1214/21-aoas1469); and an unmerged multinma branch adds baseline synthesis with mixed individual and aggregate data and single-arm handling. None of them adjusts for covariate imbalance across the two kinds of evidence, and none labels which reported contrasts rest on randomization and which on structural assumption.

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text:
Why it is open
The two halves are identified by different arguments, so combining them requires deciding how far a randomized contrast is allowed to discipline an assumption-identified one, and the single-arm part is nonidentified in exactly the directions the randomized part cannot see, which means no data-driven answer exists. A joint likelihood also forces a shared parameterization of study effects: unanchored models typically need a common intercept because study effects are not separable from treatment effects there, which conflicts with the study-specific baselines that make the randomized part safe. There is no reporting convention for a mixed analysis, so even a correct model would produce a table whose rows mean different things under one heading. The problem is recent, named as future work by the authors of the newest unanchored method, and the components that exist were built separately in the aggregate-data and population-adjusted literatures with no reason to meet.

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler and Ishak 2026, Anchors Away: Navigating Unanchored Indirect Comparisons with Multilevel Unanchored Meta-Regression (arXiv:2606.20341)
extends multilevel network meta-regression to fully disconnected single-arm evidence with an explicit assumption ledger, and names partially connected networks as the second priority for future work, stating that connected evidence can help identify relative effects and separate them from study-level differences while disconnected single-arm evidence enters through explicit assumptions about baseline risk, prognostic factors and effect modifiers


Thom et al. 2022, Medical Decision Making
keeps connected evidence, disconnected trials and single-arm studies in separate likelihood blocks with separate heterogeneity variances, showing that the connected part can be protected from the bridge, and measures the price: bias for disconnected treatments an order of magnitude larger than for connected ones


Wang et al. 2021, Annals of Applied Statistics
places randomized and single-arm trials in one arm-based Bayesian network meta-analysis using a commensurate prior that borrows variance rather than mean information, an explicit choice of how much the single-arm evidence is allowed to move the answer


Phillippo et al. 2020, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
gives the connected-network population-adjusted likelihood, modeling individual data conditionally and integrating the model over each aggregate study’s covariate distribution, which is the framework a partially connected model would extend


Phillippo et al. 2018, Medical Decision Making
sets out the anchored and unanchored split that the connectivity boundary follows, and describes the unanchored assumptions as much stronger and widely regarded as infeasible, which is why mixing the two kinds of identification needs labeling rather than averaging


multinma pull request #68
adds fixed and random baseline connections, baseline synthesis and mixed individual, aggregate and single-arm handling to a population-adjusted package, the closest existing implementation; open rather than merged as recorded in DIS-10


Beliveau et al. 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
fits random baseline treatment effects across disconnected components and validates by disconnecting connected networks, the deletion design a partially connected model should be scored on

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Derive the identification result first: for a network with a randomized core and one or more single-arm studies, state which functionals of the outcome model are identified by randomization, which require the shared prognostic factor assumption, and which are identified only up to a bias parameter, then give the identified set for the target contrast as a function of that parameter. Build the joint likelihood inside the multilevel network meta-regression framework, letting the randomized studies estimate the prognostic coefficients the single-arm study needs while allowing a study-specific deviation with a declared prior, and report how much the connected evidence actually narrows the unanchored contrast. Evaluate by deletion on connected networks: convert randomized arms into single-arm evidence, refit the mixed model, and score the recovered contrast against the connected analysis across degrees of overlap and modifier imbalance. Require every reported contrast to carry a provenance label, randomization-identified, transport-identified or prior-identified, because a single likelihood is exactly what makes the distinction invisible in the output.

title: No population-adjusted likelihood mixes a randomized core with single-arm evidence
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed it from the discussion of a single preprint, and the reviewer accepted a unified partially connected likelihood with clearly labeled contributions as a distinct target from choosing a bridge for a wholly disconnected network. It is partially-addressed rather than open because separate likelihood blocks, commensurate-prior borrowing from single-arm trials and an unmerged baseline-synthesis branch each supply part of the architecture; what is missing is the population-adjusted joint likelihood, the theory of how the randomized core constrains the unanchored part, and provenance labeling of the result.

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text: DIS-17 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text:
Statement
Multivariate network meta-analysis can connect a treatment that is disconnected, or entirely unstudied, on one outcome by borrowing its position in the network for a different correlated outcome. The information crossing that gap is carried by a restriction on the treatment-by-outcome effect surface, typically the additive form in which a treatment’s effect on an outcome is a treatment term plus an outcome term with a single shared deviation variance, so a treatment’s profile across outcomes is assumed to differ from the average profile only by noise of that one variance. Nothing in the observed data distinguishes a small fitted deviation variance from genuine cross-outcome constancy for the specific unobserved treatment-outcome cell, and the fitted variance is a network-wide scalar that cannot be interrogated cell by cell. The construction is decision-changing in use: in a network of 143 overactive bladder trials and 115 interventions where only 51 studies reported all three outcomes, sacral nerve stimulation, never measured for urgency in any trial, was estimated as the best treatment for urgency with a 95 percent credible interval of -10.11 to -6.78 episodes, displacing the univariate recommendation, and a class layer raised its precision on that outcome by roughly 28 percent (Owen et al. 2020, doi:10.1186/s12874-020-01025-8). The restriction is strongest exactly where it is most used, since for an active-versus-active contrast the outcome term cancels and the contrast is carried entirely by the treatment terms and the shared variance, and residual deviance was not computable in that parameterization, so no fit statistic was reported for any model. Cross-outcome borrowing does not appear in the standard enumeration of bridge families for disconnected evidence, has no named sensitivity parameter and no partial-identification bound, and no diagnostic reports how much of a given cell’s estimate is borrowed rather than observed.

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text:
Why it is open
The quantity the restriction supplies is an unobserved treatment-outcome cell, so no in-sample check can bear on it: fit is computed over the cells that were reported, and every candidate restriction agreeing on those cells is indistinguishable there. Multivariate synthesis was developed to gain precision on outcomes that are partially reported, where borrowed information supplements observed data, and the identification-by-borrowing use arrived as a by-product without its own assumption ledger. Within-study correlations, which govern how much strength is borrowed, are usually imported as fixed constants from an external individual-level dataset, so the borrowing rate is itself an assumption whose uncertainty is not propagated. And because the output is an ordinary posterior with an ordinary credible interval, nothing in a report signals that a particular number was manufactured by the restriction rather than measured.

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Owen et al. 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology
adds a class-exchangeability layer to arm-level multivariate network meta-analysis, uses the additive treatment-plus-outcome restriction to reach all 115 interventions on all three outcomes, and reports a decision reversal driven by a treatment with no data on the outcome, while conceding the restriction is strong for active-versus-active contrasts and that model fit could not be assessed


Achana et al. 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
introduces the arm-level multivariate network meta-analysis with borrowing across outcomes and the additive restriction later used as a bridge, developed for prediction of unreported outcomes rather than for identification of unstudied ones


Efthimiou et al. 2015, Biostatistics
gives the joint synthesis of multiple correlated outcomes across a network of interventions, the model class in which the treatment-by-outcome restriction lives


Riley et al. 2017, BMJ
sets out the rationale and concepts of multivariate and network meta-analysis, including the dependence of any borrowing on within-study correlations that are rarely reported


Jackson et al. 2017, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
gives the borrowing-of-strength statistic, the nearest available quantification of how much of an estimate’s precision comes from evidence other than the direct data, but as a study-weight summary rather than a cell-level provenance measure


Copas et al. 2018, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C
characterizes when secondary outcomes actually contribute information to a primary outcome in multivariate meta-analysis, which is the analytic route by which a cell-level borrowing diagnostic could be derived


Kirkham et al. 2012, Statistics in Medicine
uses multivariate meta-analysis explicitly to recover outcomes suppressed by reporting bias, the same borrowing mechanism operating as an identifying device, and evaluates it against known reported values

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Name the bridge and write its ledger row: the identifying restriction is exchangeability of a treatment’s deviation from the additive treatment-plus-outcome surface, and the natural sensitivity parameter is a cell-specific shift added to that surface for the unobserved cell, reported as the shift at which the recommendation changes. Compute a cell-level borrowing diagnostic, for example the share of the posterior precision for a treatment-outcome cell attributable to other outcomes, so that a fully borrowed cell is labeled as such in the output rather than printed like any other. Validate by deletion: mask observed treatment-outcome cells in networks that report them, refit under the restriction, and report prediction error and interval coverage against the withheld estimates, indexed by outcome pair and by the strength of the between-study correlation. Propagate the uncertainty in imported within-study correlations rather than fixing them, since the borrowing rate that carries the gap is a function of those correlations.

title: Cross-outcome borrowing is a bridge with no diagnostic
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted cross-outcome borrowing as a bridge family distinct from class, component, baseline and external-control bridges, while noting that the blanket claim that no sensitivity analysis exists is broader than the quoted evidence establishes. The basis is a single applied methods paper, whose own discussion concedes the restriction is strong for active-versus-active contrasts and that no fit statistic was computable in its parameterization.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Statement
Decision-linked threshold analysis is not missing. Caldwell et al. 2016 proposed threshold analysis for network meta-analysis and computed it numerically, and Caldwell et al. 2016 proposed threshold analysis for network meta-analysis and computed it numerically, and Phillippo et al. 2018 derive bias-adjustment thresholds algebraically algebraically giving the smallest changes to the data that change a treatment decision in fixed and random-effects NMA, released as the CRAN package nmathresh, and the cpaic development package maps uniform box-bounded component main-effect drift to any scalar link-scale decision threshold, which for a one-dimensional monotone economic model can already represent a reimbursement tipping point. Two extensions are genuinely absent: perturbing a cross-gap bridge parameter in a disconnected network rather than an observed data point, and propagating a multidimensional cross-gap identified set through costs, QALYs, survival extrapolation, and competing decisions to incremental net benefit. cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub and is not installable from CRAN, so its part of this capability is not available to a general user.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Why it is open
The existing threshold machinery perturbs observed evidence in a connected network, so it has no notion of a bridge parameter carrying a gap, and the fragility calculation that does perturb a bridge is limited to a uniform box bound on component main effects and to a scalar threshold on the link scale. Mapping a drift set into a reimbursement decision needs the economic model as well as the synthesis model, so it crosses the boundary between synthesis software and decision-analytic software and neither side currently owns the interface. Until that interface exists, a bound on the effect scale cannot be translated into a statement about whether the recommendation is robust, except in the special case where net benefit is monotone in a single contrast.

title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the interface rather than the primitive: extend decision-invariant threshold analysis so the perturbed quantity is a bridge parameter in a disconnected network, and extend the existing per-component fragility calculation from a scalar link-scale threshold to a full net-benefit boundary. Propagate multidimensional identified sets through the health-economic model and report the smallest cross-gap assumption violation that flips the reimbursement decision, alongside superiority and noninferiority thresholds. title: Cross-gap bridge bounds are not propagated to net benefit
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Decision-invariant threshold analysis (Phillippo et al. 2018, R package nmathresh) already reports the smallest change to observed evidence that flips a treatment recommendation in a connected NMA, but it has not been extended to perturbations of a cross-gap bridge parameter in a disconnected network, nor propagated through a cost-effectiveness model to a net-benefit or reimbursement threshold.
The source titled this. “Cross-gap bounds are not linked to decision thresholds” The title says bounds are not linked to decision thresholds, but decision-invariant threshold analysis is on CRAN and component-drift fragility already maps to a decision threshold.
The source said. “The research opportunity flagged by the report is to connect partial-identification bounds for cross-gap contrasts to decision thresholds and net benefit, producing the smallest assumption violation that changes reimbursement.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no current method reports the smallest cross-gap assumption violation that would change a reimbursement decision and that bounds are not linked to decision thresholds; both auditors judged this too strong. The literature auditor cited doi:10.1111/rssa.12341 and the nmathresh package, and GPT-5.6 Sol found that cpaic’s bridge_fragility() already computes the smallest per-component drift that moves the contrast to a user-supplied decision threshold. What survives is the net-benefit and reimbursement propagation, not an absence of all decision-linking machinery.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

corrected who is credited with threshold analysis Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1111/rssa.12341) state in their own text that ‘Threshold analysis has previously been proposed by Caldwell et al. (2016)’ and that their contribution avoids the limitations of that approach. Caldwell et al. 2016 is now cited as the origin; the later work remains cited for the algebraic procedure. Previously: “Decision-linked threshold analysis is not missing. Phillippo et al. 2018 derive bias-adjustment thresholds giving the smallest changes to the data that change a treatment decision in fixed and random-effects NMA, released as the CRAN package nmathresh, and the cpaic development package maps uniform box-bounded component main-effect drift to any scalar link-scale decision threshold, which for a one-dimensional monotone economic model can already represent a reimbursement tipping point. Two extensions are genuinely absent: perturbing a cross-gap bridge parameter in a disconnected network rather”

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Claim 1, that no current method reports the smallest assumption violation that would change a decision, is contradicted as written. Phillippo, Dias, Ades, Didelez and Welton (JRSS-A 2018) derive decision-invariant bias-adjustment thresholds that give exactly ‘the smallest changes to the data that result in a change of treatment decision’, for individual studies or aggregate contrasts, in fixed and random-effects NMA, with an accompanying R package; nmathresh is on CRAN and its stated purpose is ‘the calculation and presentation of decision-invariant bias adjustment thresholds and intervals for Network Meta-Analysis’. What is genuinely missing is the two extensions the entry actually needs: the perturbed quantity being a bridge parameter in a disconnected network rather than an observed data point, and the decision being net benefit at a cost-effectiveness threshold rather than the treatment recommendation from the synthesis. Stated that way the problem is real and well posed. Stated as ‘no current method’, it will be read as unfamiliarity with a well-known Bristol method by the same group whose software the catalog audits elsewhere. Cites 10.1111/rssa.12341: Provides the decision-linked smallest-violation quantity the entry claims does not exist, for connected NMA. Cites cran:nmathresh: Released implementation of decision-invariant thresholds, showing this is available software rather than a research direction.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is too absolute. At the requested cpaic snapshot, the exported bridge_fragility() function computes d* = |D - tau| / sum|m_c| per posterior draw for box-bounded cross-subnetwork component drift and accepts any finite scalar link-scale decision threshold. Mathematically, the drift set produces the interval [D - d sum|m_c|, D + d sum|m_c|], so this is exactly the smallest violation whose bound reaches tau. For a one-dimensional monotone economic model whose net-benefit boundary can be translated into tau, it can already represent a reimbursement tipping point. C2 is therefore false regarding decision thresholds, although it remains true regarding general net benefit: cpaic does not propagate multidimensional identified sets through costs, QALYs, survival extrapolation, or competing decisions. The remaining work is an economic-model interface, not an absence of all decision-linking machinery. Very-high severity is conditional on the reimbursement decision actually being bridge-sensitive. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: bridge_fragility() implements the exact tipping violation for uniform per-component main-effect drift relative to a user-supplied scalar decision threshold; it does not implement general net-benefit propagation..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text: DIS-13 Confirmed open Very high priority Speculative Tractability 2/5

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Statement
Using several imperfect bridges at once is a reasonable response to bridge-choice uncertainty, but the aggregation rule is the problem: if candidate bridges induce the same observed-data distribution within the components and differ only across the unobserved gap, the data cannot update weights for cross-gap correctness. Weights can still be estimated against an observed predictive objective; that objective simply need not track cross-gap accuracy. Two of the listed constructions are established rather than novel: a mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states is the robust meta-analytic-predictive prior of Schmidli et al. 2014, and ensembling over a bridge’s admissible configurations was done in a real disconnected network by Schmitz et al. 2018, who propagated uncertainty by analyzing the space of possible matches. What has not been done is averaging across distinct bridge families in a disconnected network, where the weights are unidentified.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Why it is open
Ensemble weights are learned from fit inside the connected components while the quantity at stake is a functional of the extrapolation across the gap, and nothing in the data-generating structure forces the two to agree, so a bridge that fits the observed subnetworks best can extrapolate worst. Model averaging cannot bear on any assumption every member shares, so an ensemble whose families all assume, say, population exchangeability inherits that assumption intact while looking like a hedge. Averaging across families is also incoherent when the members target different estimands, and none of these constructions has been developed or validated for a disconnected network; the catalog’s own portfolio rates the direction at tractability 2 of 5 because validation is difficult.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes

establishes the two- and three-component mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states, so that construction is validated prior art rather than a new direction


Schmitz et al. 2018
ensembles over the admissible configurations of a single bridge in a genuinely disconnected network by analyzing the space of possible matches

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing constructions rather than inventing them: robust mixture priors and match-space ensembling already work within a bridge, and the open step is extending them across families with weights that are declared rather than estimated, or with bridge-specific bias parameters shrunk toward zero. Score any proposal on synthetic bridge-deletion experiments, where a connected network is thinned so the cross-gap answer is known, since that is the only setting where ensemble weights can be checked against extrapolation accuracy. Never treat model averaging as validation: pair it with structural sensitivity analysis over the assumptions the members share, and report intersection or union bounds so disagreement between bridges is visible rather than absorbed into a single interval.

title: Bridge-ensemble weights cannot be learned for cross-gap accuracy
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Multi-bridge ensembles need weights that cannot be learned” The title says the weights cannot be learned at all, but the audit noted weights can be estimated against an observed predictive objective that simply need not track cross-gap accuracy.
The source said. “A novel direction is to use several imperfect bridges simultaneously without pretending any one is certainly valid, via Bayesian model averaging over bridge families, stacking on leave-one-study or synthetic bridge-deletion prediction, robust Bayes with neighborhoods around each bridge, intersection or union bounds, a mixture prior spanning commensurate to noncommensurate states, or bridge-specific bias parameters shrunk toward zero. Predictive performance within observed subnetworks may not identify which bridge extrapolates correctly across the gap, so the aggregation rule itself is not identified.”
What was wrong with it. The source described mixture priors, robust Bayes, and bridge ensembles as undeveloped; the literature auditor identified doi:10.1111/biom.12242 and doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7 as existing validated constructions, so the novelty claim narrows to averaging across distinct bridge families. GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the claim that averaging narrows intervals relative to any single model, which is false in general because a mixture variance contains both within-model and between-model components, and noted that a single model can include an explicit bridge-discrepancy term, so selecting one model does not always understate uncertainty.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The central claim, that ensemble weights learned inside connected components need not identify which bridge extrapolates across a gap, is correct and I found nothing that solves it. But two of the listed constructions are presented as novel when they are established methods in adjacent literatures, and the entry should say so. A ‘mixture prior containing commensurate, partially commensurate, and noncommensurate states’ is the robust meta-analytic-predictive prior of Schmidli et al. 2014, a validated construction with a large downstream literature on external and historical controls; robust Bayes over neighbourhoods likewise. Ensembling over a bridge’s admissible configurations has already been done in a real disconnected network: Schmitz et al. 2018 propagate uncertainty by analysing the space of possible matches. So the accurate framing is not that these constructions are undeveloped, but that they have never been developed for averaging across distinct bridge families in a disconnected network, where the weights are unidentified. Claim 5 is self-referential to the source report and unauditable. Cites 10.1111/biom.12242: Shows the proposed commensurate-to-noncommensurate mixture prior is an established validated construction, not a new direction. Cites 10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7: Prior instance of ensembling over admissible bridge configurations in a genuinely disconnected network.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C6 captures the real problem when candidate bridges are observationally equivalent on the observed subnetworks and differ only in their cross-gap extrapolations. Otherwise, ensemble weights can be learned for an observed-data predictive objective, although that objective need not track cross-gap accuracy. C1 is not universal because a single model can explicitly include bridge discrepancy or conservative bounds. The claim that averaging narrows intervals relative to any single model is mathematically false in general: mixture variance contains both within-model and between-model components and may increase or decrease interval width relative to particular members. C3-C4 are coherent constructions, but they do not solve the relevance of the weighting objective. C2 is a literature-status claim outside this audit, while C5 is confirmed only as a self-description of the local report.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text: DIS-11 Partially addressed Very high priority Established

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Statement
Predictive criteria computed on observed within-subnetwork units compare models but cannot establish the correctness of an unobserved cross-gap extrapolation, and leave-one-out cross-validation will still return a winner when every candidate shares a false bridge assumption. The qualifier matters: predictive checks can falsify observable restrictions, and validation using external cross-gap evidence or synthetic deletion of a link from a connected network does have leverage. Population comparison is a useful screening diagnostic for bridges that require population exchangeability, but it is computed over reported covariates while the bridge requires exchangeability with respect to every variable creating cross-study outcome differences, so it cannot rule out unmeasured prognostic or design differences; it is not logically required for component, class, or mechanistic bridges. Both checks are shipping alongside disconnected-network fits: multinma pull request #68 lists LOO-PSIS cross-validation and compare_populations() under testing.

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Why it is open
Predictive scores measure fit to observed data while the bridge governs an extrapolation to a contrast that is unobserved by construction, so an ordinary within-subnetwork leave-one-out score has no leverage on it, and a ranking reads as validation to a user who does not check what was held out. The prediction unit is usually left implicit in software output, so reported criteria may not answer a consistent question across models, and grouped validation at the study or subnetwork level, which would come closer to the cross-gap question, is unimplemented in the tools the auditors inspected. A favorable similarity table over reported covariates is easy to produce and looks like evidence, so it is presented as justification even for bridges whose assumption is not about population overlap at all.

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Declare the prediction unit explicitly (participant, arm, study, or subnetwork), implement leave-one-study and leave-one-subnetwork validation matched to the cross-gap question, and keep ordinary predictive criteria labeled as model comparison. Where a connected network can be thinned into a disconnected one, use synthetic bridge deletion as the validation with actual leverage, and use external cross-gap evidence where any exists. Present population comparison as a screening step for bridges that assume population exchangeability, paired with sensitivity analysis for unmeasured prognostic and design differences, negative-control or falsification checks, and a stated bridge assumption, rather than as evidence the bridge holds.

title: Predictive criteria and population comparison cannot validate a bridge
text:
Our study

A predictive winner among models that share a false bridge
The question put to it. When candidate models share a bridge assumption across a disconnected network, does a predictive criterion computed on observed trials rank them by their cross-gap error?
What it found. No. Candidate models that share the bridge had identical cross-gap bias (0 to 0.5 across scenarios), and the leave-one-trial-out winner was set by within-subnetwork structure: meta-regression won when a trial covariate changed the contrast, the common-effect model when not, with the same distribution at every bridge error. A predictive criterion on observed trials cannot rank models by an error they share.
Results.

Refuting sentence fails: winner distribution independent of the bridge error (chi-square p 0.68 and 0.44).
Cross-gap bias -0.007 to 0.499, identical across candidates.

Design.

Estimand

Cross-gap contrast C versus A

Methods compared

leave-one-trial-out log predictive density over three candidate models sharing an exchangeable-baseline bridge

Data-generating mechanism

Two disconnected subnetworks linked by exchangeable baselines with a design nuisance of varying size; three candidate models sharing the bridge ranked by leave-one-trial-out predictive density. 6 cells, 1000 replicates each.

Replicates

1000 per scenario, 6,000 in total


What this does not answer. Frequentist predictive densities rather than LOO-PSIS on ML-NMR; no grouped leave-subnetwork-out or synthetic deletion; population comparison not simulated. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “The two checks routinely offered as validation of a disconnected analysis do not test the bridge. Predictive model-comparison criteria rank models without validating the bridge, and leave-one-out cross-validation can select the best predictor among a set of wrong bridge models; comparing the populations of the subnetworks is necessary but cannot rule out unmeasured prognostic or design differences.”
What was wrong with it. The source said predictive criteria never validate the bridge and that population comparison is necessary but not sufficient. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed both: the first holds when the prediction unit contains no bridge-relevant observation, and the second applies only to bridges that assume population exchangeability. Sol also found the cpaic development package already declares its observation-level LOO prediction unit and warns that it does not validate cross-gap prediction for a new study, a held-out treatment contrast, or a held-out subnetwork, so the reporting gap is partial; the literature auditor noted the prediction-unit argument is standard Bayesian cross-validation reasoning rather than a citation-backed NMA finding.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): prior_work is empty and I found no paper asserting these propositions for disconnected networks, so on the support axis this is partly unverifiable; but the claims are individually defensible and one is corroborated by an unexpected source. The multinma disconnected-networks pull request lists exactly the two checks the entry criticizes, LOO-PSIS cross-validation and compare_populations(), under ‘testing’, which is direct evidence that predictive criteria and population comparison are being offered as validation of a bridge in the leading implementation. The claim that measured similarity cannot rule out unmeasured prognostic or design differences is the same logic Phillippo et al. 2018 use to call unanchored comparisons ‘widely regarded as infeasible’. The prediction-unit claim is standard Bayesian cross-validation reasoning rather than a documented NMA finding; I could not source it to an NMA-specific paper, so it should be presented as an argument, not a citation-backed result. codex dissented (overstated): C1 and C3-C5 are correct. C2 requires the condition that the prediction unit contains no bridge-relevant observation: predictive checks may falsify observable restrictions, and validation using external cross-gap evidence or synthetic deletion from a connected network can have leverage, even though ordinary within-subnetwork LOO cannot establish the missing extrapolation. C6 is not universally necessary; population comparison is relevant to bridges requiring population exchangeability, but not logically required for every component, class, or mechanistic bridge. cpaic already makes the observation-level prediction unit explicit and warns that it does not validate the gap, while grouped validation remains unimplemented.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty and I found no paper asserting these propositions for disconnected networks, so on the support axis this is partly unverifiable; but the claims are individually defensible and one is corroborated by an unexpected source. The multinma disconnected-networks pull request lists exactly the two checks the entry criticizes, LOO-PSIS cross-validation and compare_populations(), under ‘testing’, which is direct evidence that predictive criteria and population comparison are being offered as validation of a bridge in the leading implementation. The claim that measured similarity cannot rule out unmeasured prognostic or design differences is the same logic Phillippo et al. 2018 use to call unanchored comparisons ‘widely regarded as infeasible’. The prediction-unit claim is standard Bayesian cross-validation reasoning rather than a documented NMA finding; I could not source it to an NMA-specific paper, so it should be presented as an argument, not a citation-backed result. title: Structured elicitation is not applied to the cross-gap contrast
text:
Statement
When the likelihood does not identify a cross-gap contrast, an explicitly justified prior can supply external identifying information under the Bayesian model, though it does not create likelihood identification; Goring et al. 2016 already describe inserting a distribution for the unknown treatment effect as the recommended approach for disconnected networks. Structured elicitation is likewise codified rather than missing: the NIHR reference protocol of Bojke, Soares and Claxton covers expert selection, level of elicitation, fitting, and pooling, and the STEER resources operationalize it for health care decision making. Software defaults are modeling conventions that may dominate a flat likelihood direction; calling a hidden default prior undocumented expert judgment overstates it, since a default need not represent anyone’s elicited belief. What is not standard is applying either apparatus to the cross-gap quantity itself, and reporting prior-only alongside posterior estimates so a reader can see how much of the answer is prior.

title: Structured elicitation is not applied to the cross-gap contrast
text:
Why it is open
In a weakly identified disconnected model the prior determines the flat direction of the likelihood, so the number a reader sees can be mostly prior, and without a prior-only estimate beside the posterior there is no way to tell how much. The elicitation protocols that exist were built for health-economic parameters rather than for cross-gap treatment contrasts, which are harder to phrase in clinically interpretable terms and harder to check against an expert’s experience. Prior-data conflict diagnostics are also ill-posed for a parameter with no likelihood contribution across the gap, since there is nothing for the prior to conflict with.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Statement
Real-world or historical controls can bridge a disconnected gap, but doing so replaces randomization-only identification with cross-design exchangeability, transportability, consistency, and positivity assumptions. If residual design bias is left unmodeled, reported intervals omit an important source of uncertainty; the false precision follows from that omission rather than arising automatically. Most of the design-bias layer the source proposed is already built: Hussein et al. 2023 nest studies within designs with an additional, optionally class-specific bias parameter for observational studies and report that uncertainty around effect estimates increased once design differences were modeled; Schmitz et al. 2018 bridged two disconnected myeloma networks with single-arm observational data and propagated bridge uncertainty by analyzing the space of possible matches; a 2022 rheumatoid arthritis study bridged first- and second-line networks using registry data with target-trial emulation; and robust mixture priors for down-weighting external information have been standard since Schmidli et al. 2014. What remains is calibration: where no overlapping randomized and observational contrasts, validation data, negative controls, or external calibration inform the bias, treatment effect and residual design bias are not separately identified.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Why it is open
The external control supplies the missing arm, so any difference between the observational source and the randomized trials that still affects the outcome after adjustment loads directly onto the cross-gap contrast. A synthesis likelihood that treats the external control as another randomized arm shrinks the interval while leaving that residual bias unmodeled. Where no design overlaps both evidence types and no validation or negative-control data exist, the treatment effect and the residual design bias are not separately identified, and there is no accepted way to elicit or calibrate the bias parameter that the published hierarchical models require as an input.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use the published design-bias machinery rather than rebuilding it: fit hierarchical models with design-level bias parameters, use robust mixture priors to down-weight external evidence and react to prior-data conflict, and keep the randomized and observational likelihoods separate. Direct new work at the calibration problem that remains: elicitation protocols and empirical calibration evidence for how large residual design bias is in a given disease area and era, and estimation of it wherever overlapping randomized and observational contrasts, validation samples, or negative controls exist. Report the sensitivity of the cross-gap contrast to that bias parameter alongside the point estimate, since separating likelihoods or emulating a target trial does not by itself remove residual bias.

title: External-control bridges become cross-design causal synthesis
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Real-world or historical controls can create a bridge across a disconnected gap, but doing so converts the problem into one of cross-design causal synthesis. Combining randomized and nonrandomized evidence without an explicit design-bias layer often produces false precision.”
What was wrong with it. The source listed the design-bias layer, robust priors, cross-design estimators, and target-trial emulation as directions to build; the literature auditor found each already published, at doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01925-5, doi:10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7, doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2022.06.011, and doi:10.1111/biom.12242. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed two overstatements: only residual differences affecting the outcome after valid adjustment load onto the contrast, not all confounding, selection, and measurement differences, and design bias is not invariably unidentified, since overlapping randomized and observational comparisons, validation samples, negative controls, or external calibration can inform it.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty and the entry’s proposed direction is largely already published. Hussein et al. 2023 (BMC Med Res Methodol) build exactly the design-bias layer the entry asks for: hierarchical NMA models nesting studies within designs with an additional bias parameter for observational studies, optionally class-specific, and they report that uncertainty around effect estimates increased once design differences were modelled, which is the entry’s false-precision claim demonstrated. Schmitz et al. 2018 bridged two genuinely disconnected myeloma networks with single-arm observational studies and propagated bridge uncertainty by analysing the space of possible matches. Bujkiewicz et al. 2022 bridged disconnected first- and second-line networks using registry data with target-trial emulation, which the entry lists as a future direction. Robust mixture priors for down-weighting external information are standard since Schmidli et al. 2014. What genuinely remains open is calibration and elicitation of design-bias parameters, which are not identified from the data. The entry overstates novelty by presenting existing methods as directions. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01925-5: Implements the explicit design-bias layer the entry proposes, and shows the widened uncertainty relative to naive pooling. Cites 10.1186/s12874-018-0509-7: External-control bridging of a real disconnected network with explicit propagation of bridge-choice uncertainty. Cites 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2022.06.011: Target-trial emulation as a bridge is already implemented, not merely a proposal. Cites 10.1111/biom.12242: The robust/down-weighting prior for external controls the entry proposes is an established, validated construction.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is correct: once an external or historical control carries the missing comparison, identification rests on cross-design exchangeability, transportability, consistency, and positivity rather than randomization alone. C2 is directionally correct but its frequency word often is empirical, and false precision is conditional rather than automatic. The problem occurs when nominal uncertainty conditions on an unjustified no-residual-bias assumption. The why-open text overstates that all design differences load onto the contrast; only residual differences affecting the outcome after valid adjustment do so. Design bias is not invariably unidentified or necessarily elicited. It may be estimated or partially informed by overlapping randomized and observational comparisons, validation samples, negative controls, or external calibration. Without such information, however, treatment effect and residual design bias are not separately identified. The strategies in C3 are useful conditional tools, but separating likelihoods, down-weighting, or target-trial emulation alone does not remove residual bias. The residual identification problem remains open and decision-critical when the external control materially carries the comparison.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text: DIS-05 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Statement
Hierarchical class models group treatments into classes and borrow strength across them, and can stabilize sparse or disconnected evidence where a network is disconnected at the treatment level but connected at the class level, as Perren et al. 2026 state in their practical guide and four-step model-selection algorithm. Class definitions are contestable and can hide genuine between-treatment heterogeneity. Observed class members can inform and sometimes challenge the hierarchy: Perren et al. assess it by comparing model fit statistics and between-study and between-treatment standard deviations, and advise looking for alternative methods when the class assumption is not supported. What cannot be validated is extrapolation of that learned relationship to a treatment whose cross-gap effect has no independent randomized identification. The same vulnerability appears in ordinary connected networks, where a hierarchical or class-structured model shrinks contrasts that are already identified: the declared partition sets how far each contrast is pulled toward the pooled mean, and the separate decision of which treatments are admitted to the network at all silently changes the amount of borrowing, so a review-scope decision becomes an estimation decision. What is missing there is not only a diagnostic but a sensitivity convention reporting how conclusions vary over plausible partitions, and a validated elicitation protocol; the elicitation device on offer is two informal yes-or-no questions.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Why it is open
The class mean and variance supply the cross-gap information, so a treatment on the far side of the gap is assigned an effect largely by its class membership rather than by evidence about it. The class partition is an analyst input, several plausible partitions are compatible with the same fit statistics, and a class variance driven small imposes similarity the data never demonstrated, with the resulting shrinkage read as precision. Model selection that optimizes fit inside the observed evidence does not test whether borrowing extrapolates to a held-out treatment, and leave-one-treatment-out validation works only when the held-out effect remains independently identifiable after deletion, which is exactly what fails across a gap.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Perren et al. 2026
publishes a practical class-effects guide and four-step model-selection algorithm, states that class effect models can estimate relative effects in networks disconnected at the treatment level but connected at the class level, and documents the implementation of class effects in multinma


Efthimiou and White 2020, Research Synthesis Methods
Proposes Bayesian network models that shrink treatment effects toward a common mean or toward class means as a remedy for multiplicity, and concedes the grouping problem in the same paper: the decision of which treatments to include in the network, and how to group them in the class models, matters more than in standard network meta-analysis; including an older less efficacious drug can make estimates about newer drugs more conservative; exchangeability may be false where drugs act through different biological pathways; and exchangeability is hard to convey to clinicians, for which the offered device is two informal yes-or-no questions rather than a validated elicitation protocol.


Owen, Tincello and Keith 2015, Value in Health
A three-level hierarchical network model in which treatments are grouped and dose-related constraints imposed; an example of a partition declared a priori on clinical grounds and never scored against an alternative partition.


Del Giovane, Vacchi, Mavridis, Filippini and Salanti 2013, Statistics in Medicine
Network models that account for variability in treatment definitions, applied to dose; demonstrates directly that how treatments are grouped into nodes and classes changes the estimates, which is the effect a sensitivity convention would have to display.


Caldwell and Welton 2016, Evidence-Based Mental Health
Sets out lumping and splitting choices for synthesizing complex interventions, the informal practice that a partition sensitivity standard would replace with a reported range.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Let clinically prespecified classes constrain the candidate structures and use transparent algorithmic comparison and sensitivity analysis to choose among them, rather than treating either alone as sufficient. Extend the assessment step in Perren et al. toward held-out validation wherever a treatment can be deleted from a connected part of a network and its effect still identified, since that is the only setting in which class borrowing can be scored against something it did not see. Use structured heterogeneity with class-specific variance components, robust priors, and multivariate random effects so similarity is estimated rather than imposed, and report how much of the target contrast the class bridge contributed through shrinkage.

title: Class-effect bridges extrapolate to treatments with no randomized link
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Class-effect bridges rest on untestable class exchangeability” The title calls class exchangeability untestable, but the audit found observed class members can inform and challenge the hierarchy through fit and variance comparisons.
The source said. “Hierarchical class models group treatments into classes, borrow strength across them, and can stabilize sparse or disconnected evidence under exchangeability within classes and a correctly specified class variance; a practical class-effects guide with a model-selection algorithm was published in 2026. Class definitions are contestable, may hide genuine heterogeneity, and class exchangeability cannot be tested from the disconnected data.”
What was wrong with it. The source said class exchangeability cannot be tested from the disconnected data; GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed this to the extrapolation, since with several observed treatments per class the data can inform class means, between-treatment variance, outliers, and the relative fit of candidate hierarchies, and since class variance is normally estimated with uncertainty rather than fixed at a supposedly correct value. The literature auditor confirmed doi:10.1177/0272989X251389887 and noted that leave-one-treatment-out validation, class-outlier probability, and the preference for clinical over algorithmic class definition are the catalog’s own proposals rather than findings of that paper; class effects also already ship in multinma 0.8.0.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading.

merged-in

absorbed a proposal the reading raised separately: No validation or sensitivity standard for exchangeability partitions in hierarchical NMA 4 citation(s) added. The drafter disagreed with placing it here: The merge is defensible, since analyst-defined classes set the borrowing structure in both settings and the subjectivity of class definition is the same vulnerability. One correction should travel with it. DIS-05 is framed around extrapolation across a disconnection, and its why-open turns on leave-one-treatment-out validation working only when the held-out effect stays independently identifiable after deletion, which fails across a gap. In a connected network that validation is available, so the connected case is strictly more tractable than DIS-05 currently implies, and absorbing this proposal without saying so would import DIS-05’s pessimism into a setting where held-out scoring of a partition is the obvious first experiment.

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Efthimiou and White 2019, Research Synthesis Methods’ -> ‘Efthimiou and White 2020, Research Synthesis Methods’ 10.1002/jrsm.1377 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2019 online and 2020 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I read the Perren et al. 2026 open-access text. The citation is accurate: it is a practical guide with a four-step model-selection algorithm, and it does claim disconnected-network utility: ‘In some cases, class effect models can also facilitate the estimation of relative effects in evidence networks that are disconnected at the treatment level, as long as they are connected at the class level.’ Two caveats. First, the entry’s claim that class exchangeability ‘cannot be tested from the disconnected evidence itself’ is the entry’s own inference, not Perren’s; Perren instead offers assessment by comparing model fit statistics and between-study/between-treatment standard deviations, and warns that ‘if the network is disconnected at the treatment level but a class model assumption is not supported, we may need to look for alternative methods’. Second, the paper does not prescribe algorithmic versus clinical class definition, so claim 9 is the entry’s recommendation, not a finding. Neither leave-one-treatment-out validation nor a class-outlier probability appears in Perren. Class effects shipped in multinma 0.8.0, which the entry does not note. Cites 10.1177/0272989X251389887: Confirms the citation and supplies the disconnected-network caveat the entry paraphrases; also documents implementation of class effects in multinma.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2, C4, C6, and C7 are broadly correct: hierarchical class models borrow through a distributional similarity assumption, and poorly justified classes can hide genuine treatment heterogeneity. C3 is too absolute. With several observed treatments per class, the data can inform class means, between-treatment variance, outliers, and relative fit of candidate hierarchies. What remains untestable is extrapolation of that learned relationship to the particular treatment or cross-gap contrast lacking independent identification. C5 is imprecise because class variance may be estimated with uncertainty rather than fixed at a supposedly correct value. C8 works only when the held-out treatment effect remains independently identifiable after deletion; otherwise the validation target is unavailable. C9 is overly categorical: clinical prespecification should constrain the candidate structures, but transparent algorithmic comparison and sensitivity analysis can supplement it. C1 is a publication-attribution claim outside this lens. The residual transport problem remains open and important when class borrowing determines the decision.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Statement
Arm-based baseline-synthesis, reference-prediction, and aggregate-level matching models link disconnected subnetworks through a baseline-outcome structure, allowing disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies to be included. An observed control-arm risk depends on prognosis, endpoint definition, follow-up, ascertainment, care context, and calendar time, so it is not intrinsically exchangeable across designs or components. Thom et al. 2022 measured what this costs: disconnected-treatment bias ran from -0.16 to 0.392 for aggregate-level matching and from -0.102 to 0.40 for reference prediction, with coverage of 0.30 to 0.82 and 0.64 to 0.94 respectively, and they recommend reference prediction on coverage grounds. Beliveau et al. 2017 is not the cautionary result the source made it: across the two disconnected datasets it examined it found the use of random baseline treatment effects appropriate, while warning that the normality and exchangeability assumptions could be inappropriate in datasets it did not observe.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Why it is open
Where a single baseline parameter both carries the cross-gap bridge and absorbs study-level nuisance variation, nothing inside a disconnected graph separates the two roles, so a difference in endpoint definition can be absorbed as a difference in prognosis and propagated into the relative effect. Observed baseline heterogeneity and design associations can be examined, but no such check reaches the cross-gap counterfactual, which is exactly what the bridge supplies, and regression to the mean and measurement error in the baseline term add distortion invisible in the fitted output. Thom et al. 2022 show the residual bias and undercoverage are material rather than theoretical, and better relative coverage for reference prediction in one simulation program is a conditional preference under stated assumptions, not evidence that disconnected networks are solved.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chandler and Ishak 2026, Anchors Away (arXiv:2606.20341v1)
states that in fully disconnected single-arm evidence treatment effects are not separately identifiable from study, population and design effects without additional structural assumptions, so unanchored comparisons typically require a common conditional baseline risk across study populations; it calls that assumption highly restrictive and unlikely to be plausible in most applications, and recommends fixed study effects with hierarchical pooling as a sensitivity analysis


Beliveau et al. 2017
asks how dangerous random baseline treatment effects are in disconnected networks and finds their use appropriate for the two datasets considered, with an explicit caveat about datasets it did not observe


Thom et al. 2022
extends baseline-effect and aggregate-level matching to disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies, and quantifies the residual bias and undercoverage of both by simulation

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use separate baseline distributions for connected, disconnected, and single-arm evidence, and use commensurate rather than fully exchangeable baseline priors so the bridge is down-weighted when source and target baselines conflict. Condition reference prediction on design covariates where the relevant covariates are measured, overlap, and can be modeled correctly, since the improvement depends on those conditions rather than being automatic, and calibrate with negative controls that detect design-driven baseline differences. Report an explicit posterior decomposition of how much the baseline bridge moves each treatment contrast, and treat reference prediction as a conditional method rather than a solution to disconnection.

title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Our study

A baseline-risk bridge across a disconnected network
The question put to it. When disconnected subnetworks are linked through exchangeable baseline risks, does study-level design nuisance pass into the cross-gap contrast, and can design covariates separate it from prognosis?
What it found. A baseline-risk bridge transports whatever makes the subnetworks’ baselines differ. When a design nuisance (such as an endpoint definition) coincided with the subnetwork it passed one for one into the cross-gap contrast (bias 0.2 to 0.7) and no adjustment was possible. When a quarter of trials used the other definition, adjusting for it removed the nuisance but not prognostic drift between subnetworks (bias 0.19 to 0.20).
Results.

Refuting sentence fails: without crossover, adjustment possible in 0% of analyses and bridge bias 0.207 to 0.712.
With 25% crossover and no drift, adjusted bias within 0.003.
With prognostic drift 0.2, adjusted bias 0.191 to 0.204.

Design.

Estimand

Cross-gap contrast C versus A on the log odds scale

Methods compared

exchangeable-baseline bridge, bridge adjusted for a design covariate

Data-generating mechanism

Two subnetworks with prognostic drift, a design nuisance on the baseline and a design covariate overlapping the gap or not; exchangeable-baseline bridge with and without design adjustment. 24 cells, 2000 replicates each.

Replicates

2000 per scenario, 48,000 in total


What this does not answer. Study-level summaries, no Bayesian arm-based model or commensurate prior, one design covariate. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.
