title: Baseline risk is not a neutral anchor for disconnected evidence
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. Auditors judged the problem open, and the source attributed it to the wrong work. Chandler and Ishak, Anchors Away (arXiv:2606.20341v1, appendix A.7), supplies the formal support the closure said was absent: in disconnected single-arm evidence, study-level effects are not separately identifiable from treatment effects, so a common conditional baseline risk is an identifying constraint and not a neutral anchor. The same paper calls that assumption highly restrictive and recommends fixed study effects with hierarchical pooling, which is this entry’s own proposed direction, so the problem is real but its strong form is overstated.
The source said. “Arm-based baseline-synthesis, reference-prediction, and aggregate-level matching models link disconnected subnetworks through a baseline-outcome structure, allowing disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies to be included. Baseline risk is not a universal bridge: it mixes prognosis with outcome definition, ascertainment, follow-up, supportive care, and calendar time, and simulations show cross-disconnected estimates can still be materially biased.”
What was wrong with it. The source’s gloss on Beliveau et al. 2017, its severity line, and the associated claim all inverted the paper’s finding; the literature auditor quoted doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256 saying that for the two datasets considered the use of random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks was appropriate. GPT-5.6 Sol added that not every implementation forces one baseline parameter to carry both nuisance variation and the whole bridge, and that observed baseline heterogeneity and its association with design features can be partly assessed, so the untestability narrows to the missing cross-gap counterfactual.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

verdict-corrected

not-supported -> overstated The adjudication rule let a misattributed citation set the published verdict to not-supported, though every auditor on this entry voted the problem open. A misattribution is a fault in the provenance, not in the claim. The rule is corrected in build/adjudicate.mjs and the verdict re-derived from this entry’s own audit record. Auditors judged the problem open, and the source attributed it to the wrong work. Chandler and Ishak, Anchors Away (arXiv:2606.20341v1, appendix A.7), supplies the formal support the closure said was absent: in disconnected single-arm evidence, study-level effects are not separately identifiable from treatment effects, so a common conditional baseline risk is an identifying constraint and not a neutral anchor. The same paper calls that assumption highly restrictive and recommends fixed study effects with hierarchical pooling, which is this entry’s own proposed direction, so the problem is real but its strong form is overstated.

Corrected

severity: removed a line that inverted the cited finding The correction_note already recorded that the source’s gloss on Beliveau et al. 2017, its severity line and its associated claim all inverted the paper’s finding, and that the auditor quoted doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256 saying the use of random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks was appropriate for the two datasets considered. The correction had reached the statement but not this field. claims_to_check keeps the inverted wording deliberately, since it records the claim as the source made it, which is what was checked. Previously: “random baseline treatment effects can be dangerous in disconnected networks”

Flagged for reopening

14 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

open / misattributed. I read the Beliveau et al. 2017 abstract in full. The title is a question and the paper’s answer is largely reassuring, not cautionary: ‘For the 2 datasets considered, we found that the use of random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks was appropriate.’ The entry’s prior_work gloss (‘shows random baseline treatment effects can be dangerous’), the severity line, and claim 1 all invert the paper’s finding. The authors do add a hedge about other datasets, which is the defensible version. This is the kind of error the people who wrote the paper will notice immediately. Everything attributed to Thom et al. 2022 checks out exactly: disconnected-treatment bias -0.16 to 0.392 (ALM) and -0.102 to 0.40 (reference prediction), coverage 0.30-0.82 versus 0.64-0.94, and ‘Reference prediction has greater coverage and may be recommended overall.’ The substantive problem (baseline risk mixes prognosis with ascertainment and design era) remains open; only the attribution needs fixing.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The technical core of C2-C9 and C13 is sound. An observed control-arm risk depends on prognosis, endpoint definition, follow-up, ascertainment, care context, and calendar time, so it is not intrinsically exchangeable across designs or components. A baseline bridge requires an appropriate arm-level outcome model plus explicit exchangeability or regression assumptions, and aggregate relationships do not identify individual-level transportability. The report nevertheless overgeneralizes. Not every implementation makes one baseline parameter carry both nuisance variation and the entire bridge; separate distributions, design covariates, measurement-error models, and partial pooling are possible. Observed baseline heterogeneity and design associations can be assessed, although such checks cannot validate the missing cross-gap counterfactual. Conditioning on design covariates is helpful only with measured relevant covariates, overlap, and a correctly specified model. C14-C15 are universal current-method absence claims, while C1 and C10-C12 are paper-attribution claims; none is established by the permitted technical and source-code lens. The issue is high priority only when baseline structure materially carries the decision contrast.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R6:counter-quote-uncontested

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text: DIS-01 Confirmed open Very high priority Established

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Statement
In a connected network the relative effect between two treatments is identified through a path of randomized contrasts; when no such path exists the cross-subnetwork contrast lies outside the row space of the design and is absent from the randomized likelihood, so no amount of additional within-component data supplies it. Any finite estimate of that contrast comes from structure the analyst imposes: a proper prior, an equality restriction, a component or class model, external evidence, or a bridging trial. Goring et al. 2016 describe the setting and the standard fix of inserting a distribution for the unknown contrast, and Pedder et al. 2021 state that comparisons between disconnected treatments are not possible without strong assumptions. Unanchored MAIC and STC sit in this class; their requirement is conditional exchangeability of absolute potential outcomes across studies together with positivity, consistency, and correct outcome modeling, which Phillippo et al. 2018 describe as much stronger assumptions widely regarded as infeasible.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Why it is open
The missing quantity is a structural property of the evidence graph rather than a sampling limitation: the cross-component contrast lies in a null direction of the design, so within-component precision can grow without ever touching it. Removing the anchor removes the structure that made cross-trial differences cancel, so the analysis must reconstruct an absolute-outcome comparison from studies never designed to be compared. Once any linking structure is added, Bayesian and frequentist software returns a finite estimate with an interval that reads to a decision maker exactly like an identified result, and posterior connectedness is not likelihood identification. Reporting guidance for population-adjusted comparisons now exists (Ishak et al. 2025), so this is not a total absence of standards, but that framework is scoped to population adjustment and does not require a disconnected-network result to name the structure that supplied the cross-gap contrast.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Precede every disconnected-network result with an explicit statement that the randomized evidence identifies effects only within each connected component and that the cross-component comparison is identified only after imposing the stated bridge assumptions. Report the linking structure as part of the estimand definition rather than as a modeling footnote, and extend the existing population-adjustment reporting framework so it covers which parameter carries a disconnected gap. Drop the goal of a single algorithm combining five named linking devices: that combination is unbuilt only because nobody has proposed it, and the useful work is making whichever bridge is used auditable.

title: Cross-gap contrasts are absent from the randomized likelihood
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “In a connected network the relative effect between two treatments is identified through a path of randomized contrasts; when no such path exists the cross-subnetwork contrast is not merely imprecise but absent from the randomized likelihood. Any finite estimate of that contrast is supplied entirely by structure the analyst imposes, which is why unanchored MAIC and STC and other disconnected-network methods inherit strong no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions.”
What was wrong with it. The source asserted the identification claim without attribution; the literature auditor supplied the canonical sources, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1204 (Goring et al. 2016), doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315 (Pedder et al. 2021), and doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740 (Phillippo et al. 2018), so the claim is now sourced. GPT-5.6 Sol replaced the loose no-unmeasured-confounding wording with the assumption unanchored comparisons actually require, and neither auditor could establish the entry’s further claims that disconnected aggregate-data methods are still niche or that no algorithm combines five named linking devices, so both are dropped.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, so I retrieved the canonical sources myself. Goring et al. 2016 (Res Synth Methods) frames disconnected networks exactly as the entry does and states the standard fix is to insert a distribution for the unknown contrast. Pedder et al. 2021 states outright that comparisons between disconnected treatments are not possible without strong assumptions. Phillippo et al. 2018 supplies the unanchored-MAIC/STC claim verbatim. The structural non-identification claim is correct and cannot be solved by any paper, so open is right. Caveats: two claims are absence claims I cannot verify by finding nothing, namely that disconnected aggregate-data methods are ‘still niche in practice’ and that ‘no network-connecting algorithm currently combines’ five named devices. The second is trivially true only because nobody has proposed that particular five-way combination; it should not be read as a research gap of consequence. The entry should cite Goring 2016, which is the reference a disconnected-networks reader will expect first. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1204: Sources the unsourced identification claims and is the canonical missing citation for this entry. Cites 10.1177/0272989X17725740: Sources the claim that unanchored MAIC and STC inherit much stronger (no-unmeasured-confounding style) assumptions. Cites 10.1177/0272989X20983315: Sources the claim that a cross-gap contrast requires structure beyond the randomized evidence.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C2-C6 are correct for a standard contrast-based NMA after fixing a common estimand and the usual consistency and transport assumptions. With an edge-incidence design, a disconnected graph has component-specific shift directions that leave the randomized likelihood unchanged; a cross-component contrast is outside the design row space. Additional within-component data cannot remove that null direction. A proper prior, equality restriction, component or class model, external evidence, or bridging trial can produce a finite estimate, but posterior connectedness is not likelihood identification. C7 is directionally correct, although the precise requirement for unanchored MAIC or STC is conditional exchangeability of absolute potential outcomes across studies, together with positivity, consistency, and correct modeling, rather than generic treatment-confounding language. C8-C9 and C1 are practice, universal-absence, or sourcing claims that cannot be established under this technical-only audit. Identification disclosure is decision-critical; the proposed five-way algorithm is a roadmap item.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text: DIA-25 Partially addressed High priority Established Tractability 5/5

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text:
Statement
At least four published measures of how much a study contributes to a network meta-analysis estimate return materially different numbers for the same network: hat-matrix off-diagonals, the flow-based proportion contribution matrix, percentage weights from a Fisher-information decomposition, and variance-reduction importance. The differences are structural rather than estimation error. Importance is a variance ratio conditional on the rest of the network, so it equals 1 for every study that is an essential link and can equal 1 for several studies at once, whereas flow-based contributions divide a fixed 100 percent among studies; where three studies form the only path between two treatments the first returns 1 for each and the second one third for each. In the thrombolytics network the sole trial containing one treatment has importance 1 for the contrast involving that treatment against a 67.13 percent Fisher-information contribution, and percentage contributions summing to 100 percent may not exist for network meta-analysis at all (Rucker et al. 2020, doi:10.1186/s12874-020-01075-y). One of these measures, the proportion contribution matrix, is the weighting with which CINeMA aggregates study-level risk of bias into a per-comparison confidence rating, and netmeta now ships two different contribution constructions side by side. No study establishes which definition is appropriate for that use, and none reports how many confidence ratings change when one definition is substituted for another.

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text:
Why it is open
The measures answer different mathematical questions, so no calculation adjudicates between them; picking one is a decision about what contribution should mean when it is used as a weight for a certainty judgment, and that decision has never been posed as a research question. What has been resolved is a different ambiguity: the random-walk construction gives closed-form proportion contributions without the path-selection arbitrariness of the original algorithm, and the path-weight framework then shows that the underlying linear system generally admits infinitely many solutions, of which shortest-path and random-walk are two. Because a substitution changes a rating rather than an estimate, nothing in the analysis looks wrong when the wrong definition is used, and the downstream object has no ground truth against which a definition could be validated. Running the comparison needs a corpus of networks with study-level risk-of-bias judgments attached, which exists inside CINeMA projects but has not been assembled for this purpose.

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Rucker et al. 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology
defines the importance of a study for a contrast as the relative loss of precision when the study is dropped, implements it as netmeta::netimpact(), shows importances systematically exceed Fisher-information percentage contributions, and argues that a breakdown of indirect evidence into percentage contributions summing to 100 may not exist


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, F1000Research
defines the flow-based proportion contribution matrix by decomposing evidence flow into paths and streams; this is the measure CINeMA uses to propagate study-level risk of bias


Riley et al. 2018, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
derives percentage study weights for multi-parameter models including network meta-analysis from a decomposition of the Fisher information, giving a third and numerically different answer


Jackson et al. 2017, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
gives the borrowing-of-strength statistic, quantifying how much of an estimate’s precision comes from evidence other than the direct comparison, a fourth quantity often read as contribution


Konig et al. 2013, Statistics in Medicine
builds the evidence flow network from the hat matrix and defines the direct evidence proportion, mean path length and minimal parallelism, the hat-matrix family from which the later measures diverge


Davies et al. 2022, Statistics in Medicine
derives closed-form proportion contributions from a random walk on the evidence flow network, removing the path-selection ambiguity of the original algorithm; implemented in netmeta alongside the earlier definition


Rucker et al. 2024, Statistics in Medicine
formulates path contributions as a linear system on the path-design matrix, shows shortest-path and random-walk are two special solutions minimizing the sum of absolute path contributions, and shows the general solution set is infinite


Papakonstantinou et al. 2020, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
applies the flow-based contributions across a large sample of published networks, establishing how much of the field’s evidence is indirect and how routinely the measure is now used


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
CINeMA, which converts study-level risk of bias into a per-comparison confidence rating using contributions as weights, making the choice of definition consequential for a published judgment

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Run the substitution study: take a corpus of published networks with study-level risk-of-bias judgments, compute each candidate contribution measure, propagate each into a CINeMA-style within-study-bias rating, and report how many comparison-level ratings change and in which direction. This is feasible now, since netmeta implements the flow-based and random-walk contributions and netimpact() implements importance, so the experiment is a loop over existing datasets. Then settle the normative question: state what property a measure must have to be a legitimate weight for aggregating study-level bias, for example that a study whose removal leaves the estimate and its variance unchanged receives zero weight, and check which measures satisfy it. Where no measure dominates, report the rating under each definition, or report the range, rather than presenting one rating as the rating.

title: Rival study-contribution definitions feed the same certainty rating
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed it from a single methods paper, and the reviewer accepted that the measures answer different mathematical questions and that the choice becomes consequential once it feeds a CINeMA risk-of-bias judgment. It is partially-addressed rather than open because the path-selection ambiguity within the flow-based family has since been resolved analytically and the admissible solution space characterized; what has not been done is any evaluation of which definition is appropriate for risk-of-bias propagation, or any sensitivity analysis of confidence ratings to the choice.

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text: DIA-23 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Tractability 5/5

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text:
Statement
In a network meta-analysis the contrast of interest is usually a functional parameter, assembled from basic parameters through the consistency equation, so correlated bias in two basic parameters can subtract out and leave the reported contrast looking nearly unbiased. Nothing in the simulation literature requires bias, coverage and interval width to be reported for the full set of basic parameters alongside the target contrast, and no performance measure quantifies how much of the reported number depends on cancellation. The effect is documented rather than hypothetical: in simulated triangle networks of a new treatment, an old treatment and placebo analyzed by one-stage and two-stage pattern-mixture models for missing outcome data, both placebo-referenced basic parameters were substantially underestimated by both approaches while the new-versus-old contrast carried a bias of about 0.03 for the two-stage approach (Spineli et al. 2021, doi:10.1186/s12874-020-01205-6). Cancellation is method-dependent, so a head-to-head ranking built on the functional parameter alone can invert relative to a ranking on the whole parameter vector. The problem grows with the network, because the number of estimable contrasts greatly exceeds the number of basic parameters and any single reported comparison is one of many possible cancellation paths, while treatment rankings, absolute-outcome predictions and economic models consume the contrasts that were never scored. ADEMP indexes performance by estimator and by estimand and says nothing about linear dependence among the estimands produced by one fit.

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text:
Why it is open
The omission is structural rather than an oversight: a simulation reports the quantity whose estimator is being recommended, and in evidence synthesis that is one contrast, even though the model that produced it estimated the whole network. Scoring every contrast forces a decision about what truth is for parameters the data-generating mechanism defines only implicitly, and the split between basic and functional parameters is a modeling convention rather than a property of the data, so a reporting requirement has to be stated over contrasts rather than over a favored parameter set. No agreed summary of cancellation exists, so an author who wanted to report it would have to invent the measure, and no journal or reporting item set asks for one. Nothing corrects the record afterward, because a functional parameter that is unbiased through cancellation looks identical to one that is unbiased because the model is right.

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Spineli et al. 2021, BMC Medical Research Methodology
documents the failure directly: in a simulated triangle network both placebo-referenced basic parameters were substantially underestimated by one-stage and two-stage pattern-mixture network meta-analysis while the target contrast showed small bias, and warns that presenting only the functional parameters of interest may be misleading when the bias cancels through the consistency equation


Morris et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
ADEMP, the reference framework for planning and reporting simulation studies; performance measures are indexed by estimator and estimand and no item addresses dependence among several estimands estimated from the same fit


Lu and Ades 2004, Statistics in Medicine
introduces the basic-versus-functional parameter distinction and the consistency equations that make functional parameters linear combinations of basic ones, which is the mechanism through which bias cancels


White et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
compares arm-based and contrast-based parameterizations, showing that which parameters count as basic is a modeling choice, so any reporting rule must be phrased over the set of contrasts rather than over one parameterization


Karahalios et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
empirically investigates where contrast-synthesis and arm-synthesis models diverge across networks, giving the applied scale of the parameterization dependence a reporting requirement has to survive

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Change the reporting unit: require simulation studies of network methods to report bias, empirical standard error, coverage and interval width for every estimable contrast, or for a declared basis together with the target, and to publish the full matrix rather than a single row. Add an explicit cancellation measure, for example the ratio of the bias in the target contrast to the norm of the bias vector over a declared basis, so a reader can see whether an apparently unbiased contrast rests on offsetting errors. Existing simulation code can supply this at no extra computational cost, since the parameters are already estimated on every replicate; what changes is what is stored and printed. Score rankings and absolute predictions too, since those functionals depend on the contrasts that go unreported, and file the requirement as an evidence-synthesis extension item to ADEMP so that reviewers have something to ask for.

title: No convention requires network simulations to score basic parameters
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted it as a real simulation-reporting failure, distinct from generic performance-measure inventories, after a registry search returned no entry mentioning basic parameters, functional parameters or the consistency equation. The evidence is a single study that observed the cancellation in its own results and warned about it, which is a weaker basis than a demonstrated pattern across the simulation literature.

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text: DIA-21 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Tractability 3/5

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text:
Statement
Percentage-contribution matrices attribute each network meta-analysis or network meta-regression result to individual studies, and they are load-bearing: they drive CINeMA’s per-comparison confidence judgments, feed ROB-MEN’s risk-of-bias labels, and serve as provenance for indirect contrasts. Competing constructions disagree both numerically and in their properties. The evidence-flow family built on the hat matrix, which is what standard software ships, is not invariant to transformation of the data, so rescaling the data changes the contribution matrix; the multi-parameter study-weight construction derived from a decomposition of Fisher’s information is invariant. On real networks the two disagree by up to 15.29 percentage points on one dataset and 18.64 on another, against trial contributions that themselves range from 0 to 49.86 percent, so the disagreement is a large fraction of the quantity being reported. A third position holds that unique percentage contributions may not exist for network meta-analysis at all: defining a study’s importance as the relative loss of precision when it is omitted gives uniquely defined values that do not sum to one and therefore cannot be read as percentages. There is no agreed list of properties a contribution measure must satisfy, no criterion tying the choice of measure to the use it is put to, and no evaluation of how far a published per-comparison credibility judgment would move under an alternative definition.

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text:
Why it is open
The requirements conflict rather than merely being unstated: additivity to one and invariance under reparameterization cannot both hold for a general multi-parameter model, and the path decomposition that makes evidence flow interpretable is defined on a particular parameterization of the hat matrix. Contributions are not an estimand with a truth to recover, so no simulation can adjudicate between definitions; the choice has to be settled by first stating what question a contribution answers, which is a definitional exercise nobody has taken on. Within the flow family the answer is not even unique, because the decomposition of flow into paths is non-unique in networks with multiple loops and depends on the enumeration algorithm chosen. The disagreement is invisible downstream because the consumer is a qualitative label: no published CINeMA or ROB-MEN report shows how its judgment would change under an alternative contribution definition, so nothing in practice creates pressure to resolve it. The transformation-invariant alternative also does not yet cover the models that would need it, having not been extended to network meta-regression with exchangeable or common interactions, or to Bayesian models where an informative prior itself contributes.

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Donegan et al. 2018, Research Synthesis Methods
Derives the contribution each trial and covariate value makes to each network meta-regression quantity, for fixed and random effects, frequentist and Bayesian, and independent, exchangeable or common interactions, with graphical displays; benchmarks against the study-weight method and reports absolute differences of 0 to 15.29 percentage points on a malaria network and 0 to 18.64 on a fluoride network, and concedes that its own contributions, unlike the alternative, change when the data are rescaled.


Riley et al. 2018, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
Percentage study weights for multi-parameter meta-analysis models by decomposing Fisher’s information matrix into study-specific contributions; transformation-invariant and applicable to meta-regression, network meta-analysis and one-stage individual participant data models.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, F1000Research
The proportion contribution matrix based on paths, flows and streams of evidence; the construction shipped in netmeta and used by CINeMA to weight study-level judgments.


Rucker et al. 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Defines a study’s importance as the reduction in the variance of a network estimate when that study is added, equivalently the relative loss of precision when it is omitted; the values are uniquely defined but do not sum to one, and the paper questions whether unique percentage contributions can be obtained for network meta-analysis at all.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLoS Medicine
CINeMA, whose within-study bias and indirectness domains weight study-level judgments by contribution, so that the choice of contribution definition is consequential for a published confidence rating.

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Start with an axiom list rather than another estimator: state candidate properties (invariance to rescaling and to link reparameterization, non-negativity, summation to one, behavior under multi-arm trials and random effects, and behavior when a study is essential to connectivity) and prove which are jointly attainable, since most of the value lies in the impossibility results. Tie each surviving measure to a use: provenance reporting needs additivity so a reader can say where an estimate came from, influence assessment needs the leave-one-out interpretation, and any scheme that weights bias judgments needs invariance to the scale the analysis happens to be run on. Quantify the stakes empirically by recomputing published CINeMA and ROB-MEN labels under each contribution definition across a database of networks and reporting how often the label changes; all three constructions are already implemented, so this is re-analysis rather than development. Extend the transformation-invariant construction to network meta-regression with exchangeable and common interactions and to Bayesian models with informative priors, which its own authors named as the missing coverage.

title: Competing contribution measures disagree and none is agreed correct
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single methods paper whose own comparison supplies both the numerical disagreement and the transformation-invariance criticism, and the reviewer accepted that criteria for selecting or validating a contribution construction are a genuine methodological gap rather than a software issue. The audit adds a third construction that questions whether unique percentage contributions exist at all, which strengthens rather than weakens the case.

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text: DIA-19 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text:
Statement
Outlier and influence diagnostics for network meta-analysis are proposed, implemented and illustrated, but none has a null reference distribution, a reported false-positive rate, or a power curve against a planted outlier of stated magnitude. The forward search for networks monitors standardized residuals, a network Cook’s statistic, the COVRATIO of variance-covariance determinants, the heterogeneity variance, Q_total, Q_het, Q_inc and direct-versus-indirect z-values across a data-chosen nested sequence of subsets, and outliers are read off plots as sharp changes; simulation envelopes are named as the fix and not built, because each envelope would need hundreds of complete searches per analysis, and the available non-simulation asymptotic theory is derived for the linear regression model rather than for the graph-theoretic network model with back-calculated multi-arm weights and an estimated heterogeneity variance. The leave-one-trial-out family, comparison-specific studentized residuals, COVRATIO, the heterogeneity-covariance change measure and a mean-shift likelihood ratio test, has never been scored as a classifier in any simulation; its evidence is one antihypertensive network that happened to contain a trial already retracted for data falsification. Those measures are computed for every trial-by-contrast cell, 28 comparisons across 26 trials in the illustrating example, with no family-wise or false-discovery calibration, so the nominal 5 percent threshold is not the realized error rate of the screening procedure. The stakes are visible in that same example: excluding the flagged trials moved the heterogeneity standard deviation from 0.099 to 0.009, carried two comparisons across significance, reversed a ranking and removed two inconsistent edges. A screen used routinely as a sensitivity analysis therefore manufactures apparent precision, and the decision to exclude a trial carries no stated error control.

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text:
Why it is open
The null is genuinely hard rather than merely unimplemented. In the forward search the monitored statistics are computed on a nested sequence of subsets that the data themselves choose, so their joint null behavior is not that of the corresponding one-shot statistics, and the search is additionally sensitive to the random starting subset, which can move a study from the final iteration into the initial one. The network model adds what the existing regression theory does not cover: an estimated between-study variance, correlated multi-arm contributions and weights back-calculated from the graph, so scaled forward residuals derived for linear regression do not transfer. Simulation envelopes are the honest fallback and are computationally prohibitive at analysis time, since one envelope requires hundreds of complete searches for the network in hand. Calibrating the leave-one-out family is much easier and has simply not been done: those measures were introduced with an illustration rather than a simulation study, and their multiplicity was acknowledged in a single sentence and set aside on the informal ground that the frequencies of detected trials exceeded the range of random error. Any calibration also has to settle what an outlier is in a network, because a trial can be extreme with respect to its own comparison, with respect to the consistency equations, or with respect to the heterogeneity estimate, and those are three different null hypotheses.

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2021, Statistics in Medicine
Extends the forward search algorithm to network meta-analysis, monitoring residuals, fit measures and test statistics along the search and identifying outliers by sharp changes in the plots. Names simulation envelopes as the reference bands that would be needed under a no-outlier null and does not construct them, and states that the same problem applies to backward deletion methods.


NMAoutlier R package
Released implementation of the forward search and its monitored statistics for network meta-analysis, so the screen is routinely available to applied analysts while its operating characteristics are not.


Noma et al. 2020, Research Synthesis Methods
Introduces four leave-one-trial-out outlier and influence measures for the contrast-based network model with missing-outcome-aware degrees of freedom, and illustrates them on a network of antihypertensive drugs where omitting the flagged trials changed the comparative estimates and the drug ranking. Runs no simulation, and acknowledges the multiplicity across the evaluated comparisons in one sentence before setting it aside.


Viechtbauer and Cheung 2010, Research Synthesis Methods
Extends standard regression outlier and influence diagnostics to fixed- and random-effects meta-analysis, the pairwise ancestor of the network measures. Presented as diagnostics with conventional cutoffs rather than as tests with known size and power, so the calibration gap is inherited rather than introduced.

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Take the leave-one-out family first, because each measure is a one-shot statistic per cell and its null is directly simulable: generate networks under a correctly specified model across topologies, heterogeneity levels and multi-arm structures, report the per-cell and network-wide false-positive rate of each measure at its proposed cutoff, and report power against planted outliers of stated magnitude so the four measures can be ranked by discrimination. Treat the trial-by-contrast cells as an explicit testing family and calibrate a false-discovery-rate rule over them using the network covariance matrix, then report the realized rate rather than the nominal one. For the forward search, derive or approximate the null band for the monitored statistics under the network model with estimated heterogeneity and correlated multi-arm contributions; if that fails, publish precomputed envelopes indexed by network size, topology and heterogeneity so an analyst does not have to run hundreds of searches. Score every candidate on the use the screen is actually put to: the rate at which a correctly specified network produces an exclusion, and the change in the reported treatment conclusion caused by acting on the flag.

title: NMA outlier and influence screens have no calibrated null
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Two independent readers proposed this from the two methods papers that define the screens, and the reviewer accepted both, holding that data-adaptive search paths invalidate one-shot reference distributions and that trial-level screening creates a multiple-testing decision problem. The claim rests on the primary sources themselves: one names simulation envelopes as the missing reference band and does not build them, the other acknowledges multiplicity in a sentence and runs no simulation at all.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text: DIA-17 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Statement
No study masks selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset down to aggregate data and scores PAIC estimates against the full-IPD target-standardized analysis, and PAIC validation concentrates on relative effects rather than on the absolute arm-level predictions a transport model actually makes; the closest multi-IPD study, Phillippo et al. 2022 (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), validates through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency and modifier relaxation, with no held-out trial and no predicted-versus-observed arm check. Real-data benchmarking against randomized evidence does exist as one-off case studies, which the source does not acknowledge: Signorovitch et al. 2023 (doi:10.1080/09546634.2023.2169574) compares previously published guselkumab MAIC estimates against the subsequently completed ECLIPSE and IXORA-R head-to-head trials. The benchmark is a prespecified reference analysis carrying its own uncertainty rather than known truth, and it must match the estimand: a marginal PAIC estimate needs a marginal target-standardized comparator while conditional STC or conditional ML-NMR output needs a conditional one, a distinction that is material on non-collapsible scales.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Why it is open
Both designs require multi-trial IPD, which sits with sponsors and consortia rather than with methodologists, and data-sharing agreements rarely permit the repeated re-analysis a validation study needs. Population-shift validation additionally requires an identified absolute-risk transport model, compatible outcome definitions and follow-up, adequate overlap and preferably a shared arm for calibration, a rarer configuration than it appears. Masked-IPD validation is uniquely capable of embarrassing a method, so incentives run against it and the real-data checks that exist are sponsor-authored one-offs rather than standing benchmarks with reusable protocols.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Signorovitch et al. 2023, Matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC) results confirmed by head-to-head trials: a case study in psoriasis
Benchmarks published MAIC estimates against subsequently completed head-to-head randomized trials on PASI 90 risk differences; a real-data check with a known answer, though a single sponsor-authored case study rather than a standing benchmark.


Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis
The closest existing multi-IPD validation of population adjustment; validates through residual heterogeneity and inconsistency checks and shared-modifier relaxation, with no held-out trial and no predicted-versus-observed absolute arm outcome check.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Cited by GPT-5.6 Sol to show the estimand distinction that determines the correct benchmark: cstc() returns a conditional effect at the target covariate values while cmaic() returns a marginal weighted effect in the target population.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Establish standing IPD-masking benchmarks on shared multi-trial datasets with a fixed protocol: mask selected trials to aggregate data, run the comparator method set, and report discrepancy from a prespecified full-IPD analysis of the same estimand, marginal for marginal methods and conditional for conditional ones, with uncertainty in both estimates carried through, alongside decision agreement. Where trial pairs with IPD from distinct populations and a shared arm exist, transport in both directions and compare uncertainty-aware predicted arm outcomes with observed ones, treating a failed arm-level prediction as evidence against the transport model. Report arm-level calibration as a routine validation output rather than relative-effect agreement alone.

title: Held-out IPD is not used to benchmark transport against truth
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The two real-data designs with an unambiguous benchmark are not standard practice: IPD masking, in which selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset are reduced to aggregate data and the PAIC estimate is compared with the full-IPD target-standardized analysis it is supposed to approximate; and population-shift validation, in which transport between IPD populations is checked by comparing predicted with observed absolute arm outcomes as well as contrasts.”
What was wrong with it. The source called masked IPD the one design with an unambiguous benchmark and did not mention that MAIC estimates have already been checked against subsequent head-to-head trials (Signorovitch et al. 2023, doi:10.1080/09546634.2023.2169574). GPT-5.6 Sol added that a full-IPD benchmark is a prespecified reference analysis with its own sampling uncertainty and must be marginal or conditional to match the estimand of the method being scored.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is sound only if ‘known target’ means a prespecified reference analysis, not known causal truth. A full-IPD estimate remains finite-sample uncertain and may depend on its outcome and transport models. C3 must be estimand-specific. Marginal target standardization is the appropriate comparator for a marginal PAIC estimand, but conditional STC or cML-NMR output requires a corresponding conditional benchmark. This distinction is material on non-collapsible scales. The cpaic source confirms that cstc() is conditional and cmaic() is marginal, while cML-NMR’s current effect path is conditional rather than marginally standardized. C4 requires more than two IPD populations: absolute arm prediction needs an identified baseline-risk model, compatible outcomes and follow-up, positivity, and cross-trial transportability of absolute risks; a shared arm can provide calibration. Observed arm outcomes are noisy benchmarks and should be compared using uncertainty-aware predictions. C6 is correct because common baseline-risk errors can cancel in a contrast. C2 and C5 are literature-practice assertions outside this audit. The validation agenda remains valuable, but its benchmark is neither universal nor unambiguous.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict left unchanged

verdict left unchanged Later work reports progress, but on the chronology review the second reviewer judged it ‘different-question’ at high confidence: The later study uses leave-one-registry-out validation of patient-level prediction models and compares predictions with observed outcomes. That is useful external-validation methodology, but it neither creates the aggregate-data information constraint nor evaluates population-adjusted indirect-comparison transport estimators.

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Phillippo et al. 2022, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis’ -> ‘Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis’ 10.1177/0272989X221117162 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2022 online and 2023 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I found no study that masks selected trials of a multi-trial IPD dataset down to aggregate data and scores PAIC estimates against the full-IPD target-standardized analysis, so the core claim holds. Two caveats. First, real-data benchmarking of PAIC against randomized evidence does exist and the entry does not acknowledge it: Signorovitch et al. 2023 compared previously published guselkumab MAIC estimates against the subsequently completed ECLIPSE and IXORA-R head-to-head trials on PASI 90 risk differences (14.4% in ECLIPSE vs 9.4% in the MAIC at week 48; 0.0% vs 0.7% at week 24). That is a one-off sponsor-authored case study, not a standing benchmark, which is consistent with the entry’s ‘not standard practice’ framing. Second, the population-shift design is not entirely unexercised: Phillippo et al. 2022 fit ML-NMR to a plaque psoriasis network with IPD from several trials and produce absolute target-population predictions, but explicitly do not hold out a trial or compare predicted with observed absolute arm outcomes, which confirms the entry’s arm-level calibration claim. Cites 10.1080/09546634.2023.2169574: A real-data benchmark of PAIC against randomized evidence with a known answer, which the entry does not acknowledge; it is a single sponsor-authored case study rather than the standing masked-IPD benchmark the entry calls for.. Cites 10.1177/0272989X221117162: The closest existing multi-IPD validation of population adjustment; confirms the entry’s claim by validating only via residual heterogeneity/inconsistency and shared-modifier relaxation, with no held-out trial and no predicted-vs-observed absolute arm outcome check..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is sound only if ‘known target’ means a prespecified reference analysis, not known causal truth. A full-IPD estimate remains finite-sample uncertain and may depend on its outcome and transport models. C3 must be estimand-specific. Marginal target standardization is the appropriate comparator for a marginal PAIC estimand, but conditional STC or cML-NMR output requires a corresponding conditional benchmark. This distinction is material on non-collapsible scales. The cpaic source confirms that cstc() is conditional and cmaic() is marginal, while cML-NMR’s current effect path is conditional rather than marginally standardized. C4 requires more than two IPD populations: absolute arm prediction needs an identified baseline-risk model, compatible outcomes and follow-up, positivity, and cross-trial transportability of absolute risks; a shared arm can provide calibration. Observed arm outcomes are noisy benchmarks and should be compared using uncertainty-aware predictions. C6 is correct because common baseline-risk errors can cancel in a contrast. C2 and C5 are literature-practice assertions outside this audit. The validation agenda remains valuable, but its benchmark is neither universal nor unambiguous.

section: How the evidence falls in time
text:
How the evidence falls in time
2 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2019 to 2022. The most recent paper to touch this reports progress on it, and every paper calling it open is older.
Does the later work answer the earlier work? Put to an independent reviewer with the older and newer claims side by side, it judged that the later work is about a different question and leaves the earlier gap untouched (high confidence). The later study uses leave-one-registry-out validation of patient-level prediction models and compares predictions with observed outcomes. That is useful external-validation methodology, but it neither creates the aggregate-data information constraint nor evaluates population-adjusted indirect-comparison transport estimators. What remains: A PAIC-specific benchmark that masks trials from multi-trial IPD to aggregate summaries and compares PAIC estimates with an estimand-matched full-IPD target-standardized reference remains unperformed.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text: DIA-15 Overstated High priority Emerging

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Statement
Two of the five measures the entry calls unreported already exist. Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected when it truly holds, rising from 3.5 percent to 18.8 percent with increasing heterogeneity, plus correct-model selection rates, which is false-synergy selection under another name; Mao et al. 2025 (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w) gives a variance-based leave-one-out contribution measure for component networks; and cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package not on CRAN, exports fitted-analysis bridge fragility and edge influence diagnostics. What is reported nowhere is bias under deliberately corrupted component coding, rank reversal as a performance measure, and sensitivity calibration, meaning whether a sensitivity interval covers the truth at the true drift. Two framings also need adjusting: false-synergy selection is a conventional null selection rate (type I error, family-wise error or false discovery), and component-effect error is meaningful only for identified parameters, so rank-deficient designs must score estimable row-space contrasts rather than arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Why it is open
Coding a treatment into components is a human data-preparation step, so its error propagates in ways only a simulation with deliberately corrupted coding can quantify, and no such simulation is standard. Sensitivity calibration is repeated-sampling coverage evaluated under a specified true drift rather than under the reference model, so it cannot be read off any currently reported quantity and has to be reported separately from nominal coverage. Rank reversal is an error only relative to a fixed target population and decision estimand, since a genuine population-dependent reversal is not a failure, and that conditioning is exactly what current reporting omits.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected when it holds and the rate at which the wrong interaction model is selected, which is the false-synergy selection probability the entry says is unreported.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis
Provides a quantified bridge-contribution and fragility measure for component networks based on variance inflation when each direct comparison is removed.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Implements a fitted-analysis tipping-point measure for cross-subnetwork main-effect drift, explicitly excluding interaction drift, and per-edge influence weights that can identify an adjusted IPD edge contributing nothing to the requested contrast. It does not provide false-selection rates, coding-error operating characteristics, or standardized Monte Carlo calibration.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Bring the measures that already exist into routine use rather than reinventing them: report the additivity-rejection and interaction-selection error rates computed in component simulation studies, and the leave-one-out contribution measure, as standard outputs for component and disconnected-network methods. Add the three that do not exist: robustness under an explicitly specified component-miscoding mechanism, ranking or decision loss for a fixed target estimand, and repeated-sampling coverage under a specified true sensitivity violation reported alongside reference-model coverage. Score error on estimable row-space contrasts and predictions, and extend the existing fitted-analysis fragility and influence diagnostics to interaction drift and to methods beyond the single package that implements them.

title: Coding-error bias, rank reversal and drift calibration go unscored
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Bias under component coding error, rank reversal, and sensitivity calibration at the true drift are not reported performance measures in component and disconnected-network simulation studies; false-synergy selection and bridge contribution have already been operationalized, as model-selection error rates and as variance-based leave-one-out contribution respectively.
The source titled this. “False synergy, coding error, and bridge fragility are never scored” The title says false synergy and bridge fragility are never scored, but the audit found both already operationalized as model-selection error rates and leave-one-out contribution.
The source said. “Component and network simulations do not report the performance measures that would expose their characteristic failures: component-effect and component-interaction error, bridge contribution and fragility, rank reversal, the probability of selecting a false synergy, bias under component coding error, and sensitivity calibration, meaning whether a sensitivity interval covers the truth at the true drift.”
What was wrong with it. The source said false-synergy selection probability and bridge contribution and fragility are not reported; the literature auditor found both already operationalized, as additivity-rejection and model-selection error rates (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) and as a variance-based leave-one-out contribution algorithm (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w), and GPT-5.6 Sol found bridge_fragility() and edge_influence() implemented in cpaic at commit 9d150e9. Three of the five measures survive as genuinely unreported.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Two of the five claims are contradicted by papers I read. False-synergy selection IS reported: Petropoulou et al. 2023 report, for scenarios where additivity truly holds, ‘The percentage of networks rejecting the additivity assumption increases from 3.5% to 18.8% with increasing [heterogeneity]’, and give correct-model selection rates (69.3% and 65.2% for no and low heterogeneity, under 50% for moderate). Rejecting additivity when additivity holds is precisely the probability of concluding a synergy exists when it does not. Bridge contribution and fragility are also quantified: Mao et al. 2025 give a variance-based leave-one-out contribution algorithm for CNMA that measures how excluding each direct comparison inflates component-effect variance and flags comparisons whose removal destroys identifiability. The remaining three claims survive: I found no reporting of bias under deliberately corrupted component coding, no rank-reversal performance measure in this literature, and nothing on sensitivity calibration at the true drift. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Reports the rate at which additivity is wrongly rejected and the rate at which the wrong interaction model is selected, i.e. the false-synergy selection probability.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w: Provides a quantified bridge-contribution/fragility measure for component networks based on variance inflation on removal of each direct comparison..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 and C2 are uncited literature-absence assertions and are outside this technical audit. The methodological framing is nevertheless too broad. False-synergy selection probability is a conventional null selection rate, type I error, family-wise error rate, or false discovery measure. Raw component-effect or interaction error is meaningful only for identified parameters; in rank-deficient designs, simulations must score estimable row-space contrasts or predictions rather than arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients. Rank reversal is an error only relative to a fixed target population and decision estimand; a true population-dependent reversal is not a failure. C5 is repeated-sampling coverage evaluated under a specified true drift, not a fundamentally different probability concept from coverage, although it should be reported separately from reference-model coverage. At 9d150e9, cpaic already exports bridge_fragility() and edge_influence(), partly addressing C4 at the fitted-analysis level. They do not provide false-selection rates, coding-error operating characteristics, or standardized Monte Carlo calibration. The asserted High severity is justified only when interaction selection, ranking, or a cross-gap decision is actually part of the analysis. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Implements a fitted-analysis tipping-point measure for cross-subnetwork main-effect drift, while explicitly excluding interaction drift.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9: Implements per-edge influence weights for a requested contrast and can identify an adjusted IPD edge that contributes nothing to that contrast..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text: DIA-13 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Statement
Quantitative bias analysis for unanchored PAIC has not been evaluated over a design crossing bias mechanisms with the primary data-generating factors. The leading recent method paper, Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates plus deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed marginal means of unmeasured confounders, and runs no simulation study of the proposed method, relying instead on prior results for standard unanchored STC and on a case study. The cells that would be decisive are the ones nobody runs: the truth outside the elicited range, cancelling biases, a misspecified bias model, non-confounding biases acting jointly with omitted-variable bias, and correlated sensitivity parameters. A complete Cartesian factorial is not mathematically required; the scenario set should be chosen by estimand, plausible mechanisms and the interactions that could change the conclusion.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Why it is open
QBA papers typically demonstrate a single bias mechanism in a single scenario to show that a correction works, which cannot reveal how the correction behaves when several biases act at once or when the bias model itself is wrong. Crossing bias mechanisms with the primary factors multiplies the design size, so authors avoid it unless a shared simulation platform exists. The scientifically decisive cells, where the truth lies outside the elicited range, where biases cancel, or where the bias model is misspecified, are precisely the cells a proponent has no incentive to run.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates with deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed means of unmeasured confounders, demonstrated on a case study with no simulation study of the proposed method; the state of practice the entry describes.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build a QBA simulation design that crosses bias count, bias type, measurement status of the unmeasured variable, dependence structure, elicitation correctness and bias-model correctness with the primary population and outcome factors, selecting cells by which interactions could change the decision rather than by exhaustive crossing. Include cells where the truth lies outside the elicited range, where multiple biases cancel, and where selection, index-date, outcome-misclassification and censoring bias act jointly with omitted-variable bias. Treat correlated sensitivity parameters as a factor wherever the QBA is probabilistic or its joint sensitivity set is dependence-sensitive.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Our study

Do bias mechanisms in an unanchored MAIC combine additively?
The question put to it. When an omitted confounder, comparator outcome misclassification and covariate measurement error act together on an unanchored MAIC, is their joint bias the sum of their separate biases, and does a one-at-a-time analysis bound it?
What it found. No. An omitted confounder and misclassification of the comparator’s outcome interacted by up to 0.16 on the log odds ratio scale: with both at their largest the joint bias was about half the sum of the separate biases, and with the confounder reversed the joint bias had the opposite sign to that sum. Measurement error in a matched covariate combined nearly additively with either. The joint bias exceeded the largest single-mechanism bias in 22 of 36 combinations, so one-at-a-time analyses neither add up to nor bound it.
Results.

Refuting sentence fails: median interaction 30% of the summed separate biases where two or three mechanisms acted.
Confounder by misclassification: interaction up to 0.163; other pairs at most 0.005.
Joint bias beyond the largest single-mechanism bias in 22 of 36 combinations; mechanisms partly cancelled in 16.

Design.

Estimand

Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target (unanchored)

Methods compared

unanchored MAIC limit under combinations of three bias mechanisms

Data-generating mechanism

Population-level numerical study: exact bias of the MAIC limit over 45 combinations of three mechanisms, with interaction terms by inclusion-exclusion.

Replicates

Population-level calculation, 45 combinations, exact quadrature


What this does not answer. Population-level only; no bias-analysis procedure, false reassurance or tipping sets; three mechanisms; selection and correlated parameters not varied. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: QBA bias mechanisms are not crossed with the primary factors
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Quantitative bias analysis for unanchored PAIC has never been evaluated over a factorial design crossing the primary data-generating mechanisms with explicit bias mechanisms: one, two or five omitted variables of varying type; U measured in source IPD but unreported in target AgD versus unmeasured in both; prognostic-only, treatment-modifying, component-modifying and time-varying U; varying source-target imbalance and U-X dependence; correct versus misspecified target prevalence, outcome association and interaction; true sensitivity parameters inside versus outside the elicited range; deterministic versus probabilistic QBA; independent versus correlated sensitivity parameters; selection, index-date, outcome-misclassification and censoring bias separately and jointly; component drift; reinforcing versus cancelling biases; correct versus misspecified bias models; and target-population versus comparator-trial-population QBA.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors judged the claim open, and the literature auditor sourced the state of practice to Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13), which conducts no simulation of its proposed method. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed the prescription: no complete Cartesian factorial is mathematically required, and correlated sensitivity parameters matter for probabilistic QBA or dependence-sensitive joint sensitivity sets rather than for a deterministic analysis whose joint support is held fixed.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I retrieved the leading recent QBA-for-unanchored-PAIC paper, Ren, Ren, Welton & Strong 2025 in Research Synthesis Methods, which proposes NORTA-based simulation of unreported comparator covariates plus deterministic sensitivity analysis over assumed marginal means of unmeasured confounders. No simulation study was conducted for the proposed method; the authors instead lean on prior simulation properties of standard unanchored STC and demonstrate on a case study. A companion strand, flexible QBA for subject-level ITC under proportional-hazards violation, is likewise method development with case-study demonstration. That is direct positive evidence for the entry’s claim that QBA in this setting varies one mechanism at a time at most and has never been crossed factorially with the primary data-generating factors. The decisive cells named by the entry (truth outside the elicited range, cancelling biases, misspecified bias model, joint non-confounding biases, correlated sensitivity parameters) appear nowhere in what I retrieved.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The proposed stress tests are technically well motivated. C2 tests elicitation failure rather than merely correction under oracle inputs; C3 correctly separates reinforcing from canceling biases; C4 distinguishes partial measurement, where source associations can be estimated, from complete nonmeasurement; C5 separates mechanisms with different identifying assumptions; and C6 distinguishes estimands defined in different target populations. C7 applies specifically to probabilistic QBA or dependence-sensitive joint sensitivity sets: correlation can materially change the distribution of combined bias, but it need not change a deterministic analysis whose joint support is held fixed. A complete Cartesian factorial is not mathematically required for every QBA method; scenarios should be chosen according to the estimand, plausible mechanisms, and interactions that could alter conclusions. The assertion about how existing studies vary factors is a literature-coverage claim and was not assessed. This is primarily a method-validation roadmap rather than a uniformly critical omission in each applied analysis.

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=1)
