title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Statement
Estimability in component networks is neither unstudied nor unimplemented: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) implements a screen for inestimable interactions and reports inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in both simulation and a real Cochrane network, Rucker et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/bimj.201800167) formalizes the design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, Mao et al. 2025 (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w) identifies comparisons whose removal destroys component identifiability, and cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, implements target-dependent augmented row-space screening that labels contrasts exact, first-order or not identified and suppresses nonidentified estimates. What does not exist is a canonical published scenario library spanning the five estimability classes with target-dependent estimability, and the identification-focused performance measures: true and false estimability classification rates, false finite-estimate rate, smallest singular value of the design or information matrix, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and target mass outside source support. The design claim also needs precision: a contrast is structurally estimable when its contrast vector lies in the row space of the relevant design, and rank and nullity counts alone give dimensions rather than saying which contrasts qualify.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Why it is open
Estimability in component models is a property of a design matrix crossed with a target covariate value, not of data volume, so it cannot be discovered by running more replicates and has to be constructed deliberately. The dangerous cases are the ones that produce output: a proper prior yields a finite posterior for a direction the likelihood does not inform, and a first-order rank-based screen can pass while the nonlinear aggregate-data likelihood remains weakly identified. Bias, coverage and RMSE can reveal poor behavior for particular truths but cannot certify structural identification or say whether a method should have abstained, so nothing in the standard performance set penalizes software that silently reports prior-driven answers, and without a scenario library there is nothing to test screens against.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Implements an algorithm to identify inestimable interactions and reports inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in simulation and in a real Cochrane network, where eleven combinations of two interventions yield only ten estimable two-way interactions.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis
Identifies which direct comparisons are essential for component identifiability and defines behavior when their removal makes a component unidentifiable.


Rucker et al. 2020, Network meta-analysis of multicomponent interventions
Formalizes the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component combination matrix, the structure the entry’s rank and nullity claim refers to.


Graphical evaluation of evidence structure within a component network meta-analysis, 2023
Addresses evidence structure and component identifiability in component network meta-analysis. The literature auditor could not retrieve the full text and relied on title and venue only, so no claim is made about its exact content.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Implements target-dependent augmented row-space estimability classification with exact, first-order and not-identified labels, suppresses nonidentified contrasts rather than reporting finite posterior summaries, and refits under tighter and looser priors as an identification diagnostic. It does not supply the five-class scenario library or the identification performance measures.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build the canonical scenario library with known ground truth over the five estimability classes, including cases where estimability changes with the target covariate value and where a first-order screen passes while the nonlinear likelihood stays weakly identified, and validate the screens that already exist, in component network meta-analysis and in cpaic, against it rather than writing new ones. Add identification measures to the standard performance set: true and false estimability classification rates, false finite-estimate rate, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and target mass outside source support. Report the smallest singular value only with the weighting and parameter scaling made explicit, since it is not scale-free, and score error on estimable row-space contrasts and predictions rather than on arbitrary generalized-inverse coefficients.

title: No scenario library or performance measures for estimability failure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Estimability failure is neither simulated nor measured” The title says estimability failure is neither simulated nor measured, but published screens report inestimable cross-subnetwork contrasts in simulation and in a real network.
The source said. “No published library of simulation scenarios spans component-network estimability (rank and nullity of the treatment-by-component matrix X = BC, contrasts inside versus outside its row space, subnetwork-unique and duplicated components, coding errors, higher-order and antagonistic interactions, and the five estimability classes), and performance measurement stops at bias, coverage and RMSE with no measures for identification. True and false estimability classification, the false finite-estimate rate for non-estimable contrasts, the smallest singular value of the design or information matrix, prior-only versus likelihood-informed posterior contraction, and the proportion of target mass outside source support are not reported.”
What was wrong with it. The source framed estimability failure as neither simulated nor measured; the literature auditor found published estimability screens and reported inestimable contrasts in component network meta-analysis (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9, doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w), and GPT-5.6 Sol found target-dependent row-space screening and prior-sensitivity refits already implemented in cpaic at commit 9d150e9, a GitHub development package that is not on CRAN. The scenario library and the identification performance measures remain missing.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): Structural estimability is genuinely critical, and C2, C3, C6, C9, and C12 are technically defensible. C4 is sloppy: scalar rank and nullity give dimensions, but the orientation of the row or null space determines which particular contrasts are estimable. C1 is true only for a functional lying wholly in a likelihood-null direction; a generally non-estimable contrast can contain a data-informed row-space projection plus a prior-determined null-space projection. C7 is also too absolute: bias, RMSE, and coverage can reveal poor behavior for selected simulation truths, but they cannot certify structural identification or whether a method should abstain. A smallest singular value is informative only after specifying weighting and parameter scaling, and prior-to-posterior contraction is a useful diagnostic rather than a proof of identification. At cpaic 9d150e9, the blanket title is already stale: the package implements target-dependent augmented row-space screening, labels results as exact, first-order screen, or not identified, suppresses nonidentified estimates, provides prior-sensitivity refits, and tests several structural scenarios. It does not yet provide the proposed canonical five-class simulation library or the full performance-measure suite. Literature-existence claims C5 and C8 were not adjudicated.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

normalized a citation year: ‘Rucker et al. 2019, Network meta-analysis of multicomponent interventions’ -> ‘Rucker et al. 2020, Network meta-analysis of multicomponent interventions’ 10.1002/bimj.201800167 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2019 online and 2020 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

Estimability in component networks is neither unstudied nor unimplemented: the paper states ‘we describe an algorithm to identify inestimable interactions in the supplement as only estimable interactions should be considered in interaction CNMA models’, and in the Cochrane application reports ‘The network has eleven combinations of two interventions, however, only ten 2-way interactions are estimable’, with specific cross-subnetwork contrasts reported as inestimable in the simulated and applied disconnected networks. Rucker et al. 2019 gives the B and C design matrices whose product defines the CNMA design, so the rank/nullity claim is correct and already formalized. Mao et al. 2025 adds explicit redistribution rules for the case where removing a comparison renders a component unidentifiable. What genuinely remains open is a canonical, published scenario library spanning the five estimability classes with target-dependent estimability, and the identification-focused performance measures (false finite-estimate rate, smallest singular value, prior-only versus likelihood-informed contraction, target mass outside support), none of which I found reported anywhere. Cites 10.1186/s12874-025-02619-w: Identifies which direct comparisons are essential for component identifiability and defines behavior when their removal makes a component unidentifiable.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.201800167: Formalizes the CNMA design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component combination matrix, which is the structure the entry’s rank/nullity claim refers to.. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1623: Addresses evidence structure and component identifiability in CNMA. I could not retrieve the full text (paywalled), so I rely on title and venue only and make no claim about its exact content..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. Structural estimability is genuinely critical, and C2, C3, C6, C9, and C12 are technically defensible. C4 is sloppy: scalar rank and nullity give dimensions, but the orientation of the row or null space determines which particular contrasts are estimable. C1 is true only for a functional lying wholly in a likelihood-null direction; a generally non-estimable contrast can contain a data-informed row-space projection plus a prior-determined null-space projection. C7 is also too absolute: bias, RMSE, and coverage can reveal poor behavior for selected simulation truths, but they cannot certify structural identification or whether a method should abstain. A smallest singular value is informative only after specifying weighting and parameter scaling, and prior-to-posterior contraction is a useful diagnostic rather than a proof of identification. At cpaic 9d150e9, the blanket title is already stale: the package implements target-dependent augmented row-space screening, labels results as exact, first-order screen, or not identified, suppresses nonidentified estimates, provides prior-sensitivity refits, and tests several structural scenarios. It does not yet provide the proposed canonical five-class simulation library or the full performance-measure suite. Literature-existence claims C5 and C8 were not adjudicated. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: R/estimability.R and tests/testthat/test-estimability.R implement and exercise augmented row-space classification, including rank-deficient decision contrasts, covariate-support restrictions, and target-dependent estimability. Nonidentified effects are suppressed rather than reported as finite posterior summaries.. text:
Statement
Published PAIC simulations score survival on the hazard ratio: Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 on the log hazard ratio, Liu et al. 2025 on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, Hatswell et al. 2020 on mean error of the effect measure, and none reports time-indexed survival-probability error, RMST bias, integrated Brier score or extrapolation error. Under delayed, waning or crossing effects a hazard-ratio bias summary can be small while the survival curves the economic model consumes are badly wrong. Cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate processes, proportional-odds violations for ordinal outcomes and jointly generated efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes are absent from this simulation literature. The tooling is no longer the obstacle: ML-NMR has been extended to general individual-level likelihoods with flexible M-spline baseline hazards (arxiv:2401.12640), so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable even though simulations do not score on them.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Why it is open
PAIC theory is cleanest for collapsible linear-scale outcomes, so simulation practice has concentrated where the theory is tidy while HTA submissions are dominated by survival endpoints with non-proportional hazards. Generating crossing hazards, cure fractions or competing risks with a known target-population marginal estimand requires deriving that estimand analytically or by large-sample Monte Carlo, which is more work than a Gaussian scenario and is routinely skipped. Correlated multi-outcome generation is needed to evaluate net benefit and other nonlinear decision functionals, yet simulations generate one outcome at a time.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods: synthesis of individual and aggregate data with applications to survival analysis, 2024
Extends population-adjusted synthesis to arbitrary individual-level likelihoods with flexible M-spline baseline hazards and survival applications, so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable. Retrieved at abstract level.


Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021, Methods for population adjustment with limited access to individual patient data: A review and simulation study
Scores survival performance on the log hazard ratio, one of the studies the literature auditor cites as evidence of hazard-ratio-only survival scoring.


Liu et al. 2025, Is the Use of Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Always Superior to Naive Indirect Comparison on Survival Outcomes? A Simulation Study
Scores survival performance on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, with no absolute-scale or time-indexed measures.


Hatswell et al. 2020, The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison: Results of a Simulation Study
Scores on mean error and mean absolute error of the effect measure, again with no survival-probability, RMST or extrapolation measures.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend simulation generators to the missing outcome families with explicitly derived target-population marginal estimands (survival probability, RMST, cumulative incidence, cure fraction, event burden), using the general-likelihood ML-NMR machinery that already computes absolute-scale target-population quantities, so that bias is computed against the quantity the decision uses. Score survival PAIC on time-indexed survival-probability error and RMST bias by default, and add the remaining measures where they apply rather than universally: integrated Brier score where survival predictions and censoring handling are defined, extrapolation error where the pipeline extrapolates beyond observed follow-up, recurrent-event calibration where event burden is the estimand. Generate efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes jointly where the decision functional is nonlinear or joint uncertainty matters.

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Our study

Competing risks: a correct hazard ratio, a wrong cumulative incidence
The question put to it. When population adjustment transports a time-to-event outcome with a competing cause, does a correctly transported cause-specific hazard ratio give the right cumulative incidence in the target, and what repairs it?
What it found. For competing risks, population adjustment transports the cause-specific hazard ratio (unbiased in every scenario) but not the cumulative incidence a decision model uses: when the target’s competing hazard differed from the source’s beyond the measured covariate, A’s absolute incidence at 2 years was biased by up to 0.20 (true value 0.25) with coverage near zero. The between-arm difference was affected less. Recalibrating the competing hazard to the target’s reported competing-event proportion removed the bias. The registered rule (bias beyond 0.05 wherever the competing hazard differed) was met in 20 of 24 method-scenarios; the exceptions were at half the competing hazard, with bias 0.041 to 0.049.
Results.

Cause-1 log hazard ratio: bias within 3 MCSE in 16 of 16 scenarios, at most 0.013.
A’s cumulative incidence from MAIC or STC: bias 0.13 to 0.20 with coverage at most 0.03 at four times the competing hazard; -0.04 to -0.06 at half; registered verdict NOT CONFIRMED (20 of 24 method-scenarios beyond 0.05).
A-minus-C difference: bias at most 0.049.
Recalibrated competing hazard: bias at most 0.004; coverage 0.851 to 0.943 for the absolute incidence and 0.943 to 0.972 for the difference.

Design.

Estimand

Target cumulative incidence of the event of interest at 2 years under A, and its A-minus-C difference; cause-1 log hazard ratio

Methods compared

MAIC, cause-specific STC, cause-specific STC with the competing hazard recalibrated to target data

Data-generating mechanism

Anchored transport with exponential cause-specific hazards, the target’s competing hazard differing from the source’s beyond the measured covariate; 16 cells crossing that difference, effect modification and overlap; MAIC, cause-specific STC and STC with the competing hazard recalibrated to the target’s reported competing-event proportion. 1000 replicates per cell.

Replicates

1000 per scenario, 16,000 in total


What this does not answer. Only the competing-risks family; cure fractions, recurrent events, ordinal and joint net-benefit outcomes not run. Exponential hazards, one covariate, no ML-NMR. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument · Code and data: studies/DIA-09-outcome-families-beyond-the-hazard-ratio · Protocol: registered before the run

title: Narrow outcome families and hazard-ratio-only survival scoring
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The simulation evidence base does not span the outcome families decision problems involve (rare and very rare binary events, overdispersed, zero-inflated and exposure-dependent counts, ordinal outcomes violating proportional odds, delayed, waning and crossing hazards, non-Weibull mixtures, cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate disease, and correlated efficacy, safety, quality-of-life and cost outcomes), and survival performance is scored by hazard-ratio bias rather than by the quantities decisions use.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors judged the problem open, and the correction is a caveat the source did not acknowledge: the literature auditor notes that survival PAIC methodology has moved, with ML-NMR extended to general likelihoods and flexible baseline hazards (arxiv:2401.12640), so the gap is in what simulations score rather than in what methods can produce. GPT-5.6 Sol also narrowed the proposed measures, since integrated Brier score, extrapolation error, joint outcome generation and recurrent-event calibration apply to specific pipelines and estimands rather than universally.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The survival-scoring claim is broadly right in the PAIC simulation literature I retrieved: Remiro-Azocar 2021 scores on the log hazard ratio, Liu et al. 2025 on marginal log hazard ratios from Cox models, Hatswell 2020 on mean error/mean absolute error of the effect measure. None reports time-indexed survival-probability error, integrated Brier score, RMST bias or extrapolation error. The caveat is that survival PAIC methodology has moved: ML-NMR has been extended to general likelihoods with M-spline baseline hazards and survival applications, and unanchored STC has been implemented with parametric and Royston-Parmar models explicitly to handle non-proportional hazards and extrapolation, so the tooling for absolute-scale survival quantities exists even though simulations do not score on them. I found no PAIC simulation work at all on cure fractions, competing risks, recurrent events, multistate processes, ordinal proportional-odds violation, or jointly generated efficacy/safety/QoL/cost outcomes, so those parts of the claim stand. Cites arXiv:2401.12640: Extends population-adjusted synthesis to arbitrary individual-level likelihoods with flexible (M-spline) baseline hazards and survival applications, so absolute-scale target-population survival quantities are computable even though simulations still score on the hazard ratio. Retrieved at abstract/summary level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The technical core is sound. Under non-proportional hazards, bias against a single constant hazard ratio does not characterize errors in survival probabilities, RMST, cumulative incidence, or downstream economic quantities. Delayed, waning, and crossing effects can have materially different decision consequences and merit distinguishable scenarios. Rare events and proportional-odds violations are also genuine factors. The proposed measures are not all universal requirements: integrated Brier score is a predictive-distribution score requiring defined survival predictions and censoring handling, not a generic measure of causal contrast estimation; joint outcome generation is essential for joint uncertainty and nonlinear decision functionals but not for every marginal-effect evaluation; extrapolation error belongs only to pipelines that extrapolate; and recurrent-event calibration is relevant only when recurrent burden is an estimand. The claims about which outcome families and measures appear in published studies are literature-coverage claims and were not adjudicated. Very high priority is proportionate for methods making survival decision claims, while the full outcome catalogue is a broader roadmap.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Statement
PAIC simulations are built on two-trial or three-treatment templates with no topology factor and index information by participants per arm, so their results cannot be extrapolated to the networks that submissions actually contain. A topology scenario generator does already exist in the wider network meta-analysis literature: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) publishes a procedure with R code that builds families of connected and disconnected topologies from a seed network, but it has not been wired to PAIC estimators. Two of the entry’s design prescriptions need narrowing: information for binary and survival outcomes depends on events plus non-events, allocation, baseline risk, risk sets, censoring and timing rather than on events per contrast alone, and post-weighting effective sample size is a method-dependent output that can be a calibration target but cannot be crossed as an independent data-generating factor.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Why it is open
The one-IPD-trial, one-AgD-trial template has no topology at all, and topology acts through the design matrix, its row space and the contrast-specific information matrix to determine which contrasts are identified and where information flows, so an estimator that behaves well on a single indirect comparison can fail on a loop-rich or hub-and-spoke network with articulation edges. Two networks with identical total sample size can differ entirely in the estimability of the decision contrast depending on where the IPD sit. Building larger networks and keeping track of information per contrast requires a generator wired to PAIC estimators, and the one generator that exists was written for component model selection instead.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Provides a reusable procedure and R code for generating families of distinct network topologies, connected and disconnected with differing subnetwork composition, from a seed network; the topology scenario generator the source says no platform provides, though it is not wired to PAIC estimators.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the published topology generator to drive PAIC and component-PAIC estimators rather than writing a new one, and report performance conditional on topology rather than averaged over it, treating articulation edges and articulation treatments as explicit fragility factors because they control the fragility of indirect paths. Index information with outcome-appropriate measures (events and non-events, allocation and baseline risk for binary outcomes; event counts, risk sets, censoring and timing for survival) and calibrate scenarios to a target ESS range instead of crossing achieved ESS as an input. Treat integration points as a numerical-convergence check for models that require numerical integration, and prior informativeness as a Bayesian sensitivity factor, rather than as mandatory factors in every design.

title: Scenario grids omit network topology and information placement
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 9 findings from 9 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed.
The source said. “Simulation designs are built on the two-trial anchored template and index information by participants per arm, so they span neither the topologies HTA networks actually have (3 to 20 treatments, varying trial density, two-arm versus multi-arm trials, connected, weakly connected and disconnected graphs, 2 to 4 subnetworks, star, chain, loop-rich and hub-and-spoke shapes, articulation edges and treatments, unequal allocation, classes and doses) nor the quantities that actually carry information (events per contrast, studies per component, post-weighting ESS, IPD study placement, AgD precision, integration points and prior informativeness).”
What was wrong with it. The source said no shared platform provides a topology scenario generator; the literature auditor found one already published with code in the component network meta-analysis literature (Petropoulou et al. 2023, doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9), which is simply not connected to PAIC estimators. GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the information index for binary and survival outcomes and the treatment of post-weighting ESS as a crossable design factor.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): Topology and information placement matter through the design matrix, its row space, and the contrast-specific information matrix, so C4, C5, and C7 are sound. Articulation edges and treatments are reasonable fragility factors, but the specific treatment counts and two-to-four-subnetwork grid are not universal requirements. C6 is too strong: binary-outcome information depends on both events and non-events, allocation, and baseline risk; survival information depends on event counts plus risk sets, censoring, timing, and allocation. Post-weighting ESS is endogenous and method-specific, so it cannot generally be crossed as an independent data-generating factor, although scenarios can be calibrated to target an ESS range. Integration points are a numerical-convergence factor only for models requiring numerical integration, and prior informativeness is relevant when Bayesian robustness is an aim, not a mandatory factor in every simulation. Field-wide claims that particular grids or articulation effects have never been evaluated are unsupported here.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Corrected

an auditor opinion cites a simulation that does not exist; the opinion text is left as recorded The rationale cited a Kiefer, Sturtz and Bender simulation with no year or DOI. The Kiefer, Sturtz and Bender paper in the corpus (doi:10.3238/arztebl.2015.0803) contains no simulation; it is a narrative review producing an appraisal checklist. The citation is unresolvable as written and has been withdrawn from the rationale.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 9 surviving findings from: A scoping review of indirect comparison methods and applicat; Bias in identification of the best treatment in a Bayesian n; Characteristics of a loop of evidence that affect detection ; Characteristics of networks of interventions: a description ; Extending DerSimonian and Laird’s methodology to perform net; Model selection for component network meta-analysis in conne; Network meta-analysis in psychology and educational sciences; The attractiveness of network meta-analysis: a comprehensive; When does the use of individual patient data in network meta. New citations: 10.1002/sim.6752, 10.1186/1471-2288-14-106, 10.1186/s12874-016-0146-y, 10.1186/s12874-020-01198-2, 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9, 10.1371/journal.pone.0086754, 10.2147/clep.s69660, 10.3758/s13428-022-01905-5

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The gap is real for PAIC specifically: the retrieved PAIC simulations (Phillippo 2020, Remiro-Azocar 2021, Hatswell 2020, Liu 2025, Serret-Larmande 2025) are all built on two-trial or three-treatment templates with no topology factor and index information by participants. But the entry’s framing ignores that the broader NMA simulation literature already varies topology deliberately: Kiefer, Sturtz & Bender’s simulation spans networks with several interventions and inconsistency structures, degree-irregularity work simulates multiple network geometries and scores rank-probability bias, and Petropoulou et al. 2023 build an explicit generator that constructs many distinct connected and disconnected topologies from one seed network under a retain-all-interventions constraint. So a scenario generator over topology exists, just not one wired to PAIC estimators. Most remaining sub-claims (‘a comprehensive program must vary…’, ‘ESS should be a controlled design factor’) are normative design assertions rather than checkable facts, and the integration-points and prior-informativeness claims I could not verify. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Provides a reusable algorithm and R code for generating families of distinct network topologies (connected, and disconnected with differing subnetwork composition) from a seed network, i.e. the topology scenario generator the entry says no platform provides..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Topology and information placement matter through the design matrix, its row space, and the contrast-specific information matrix, so C4, C5, and C7 are sound. Articulation edges and treatments are reasonable fragility factors, but the specific treatment counts and two-to-four-subnetwork grid are not universal requirements. C6 is too strong: binary-outcome information depends on both events and non-events, allocation, and baseline risk; survival information depends on event counts plus risk sets, censoring, timing, and allocation. Post-weighting ESS is endogenous and method-specific, so it cannot generally be crossed as an independent data-generating factor, although scenarios can be calibrated to target an ESS range. Integration points are a numerical-convergence factor only for models requiring numerical integration, and prior informativeness is relevant when Bayesian robustness is an aim, not a mandatory factor in every simulation. Field-wide claims that particular grids or articulation effects have never been evaluated are unsupported here.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text: DIA-05 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Statement
No shared platform runs the field’s methods on common data-generating mechanisms with published scenarios, seeds, code and ground truth, so nothing accumulates across papers and the ranking of methods under assumption failure cannot be read off the literature. The oracle claim does not survive scrutiny: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) defines truth as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate, and the general-likelihood ML-NMR work (arxiv:2401.12640) includes full-IPD reference comparisons. A single full-IPD oracle also cannot separate information loss from method failure, because it changes data granularity, covariate availability and model specification at the same time; that decomposition needs nested arms that vary one feature at a time. The proposed 28-family minimum comparator set is a design proposal rather than a derived requirement, and several of its categories overlap.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Why it is open
Data-generating mechanisms, estimands and performance measures differ between papers, so published rankings do not compose and each new comparison starts over. Average-case simulation under correct specification rewards efficiency in a regime applied HTA data are rarely in, and building adversarial mechanisms that break one’s own method runs against the incentives of a methods paper. A shared benchmark needs shared code, shared scenarios and a maintainer, which is infrastructure work with no conventional publication reward.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Anchored population-adjustment simulation of ML-NMR, MAIC and STC named as a foundational benchmark in the source; the locator was missing and was recovered by the literature auditor. Defines the estimand as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate.


Hatswell et al. 2020, The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison: Results of a Simulation Study
Unanchored misspecification simulation named as a foundational benchmark in the source; the locator was missing and was recovered by the literature auditor. Varies the simulation setup to violate implicit and explicit MAIC assumptions.


Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods: synthesis of individual and aggregate data with applications to survival analysis, 2024
Contains simulated comparisons against a full-IPD analysis, that is an oracle-style reference arm, weakening the claim that PAIC simulations commonly omit one. Retrieved at abstract level.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build a public benchmark that prespecifies estimands, combines benign and adversarial scenarios, verifies implementations against known analytic results, and publishes scenarios, seeds, code and ground truth so that results accumulate. Choose the comparator set by applicability to each scenario rather than by a fixed family count, and where information loss is the question use nested paired arms that change one feature at a time (data granularity, covariate availability, model specification) instead of a single full-IPD oracle. Score on bias, coverage, ESS collapse, decision error and runtime, and report excess error against the appropriate nested reference rather than raw bias alone.

title: No shared benchmark platform with common scenarios, seeds and truth
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “No neutral adversarial benchmark, comparator set, or oracle arm” The title says no oracle arm exists, but the audit found a gold-standard full-IPD reference already defined and used, and rejected the 28-family comparator set as a derived requirement.
The source said. “No shared simulation platform compares the field’s methods on common data-generating mechanisms; published comparisons are pairwise contests run by method authors under benign conditions, against a handful of chosen comparators, and almost never include an oracle analysis that uses full IPD, the true bias variables and correct models. Consequently neither the ranking of methods under assumption failure nor the separation of information loss from method failure can be read off the literature.”
What was wrong with it. The source said PAIC simulations almost never include an oracle and that a minimum comparator set contains 28 method families; the literature auditor found the gold-standard full-IPD reference already explicit in Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) and full-IPD comparisons in arxiv:2401.12640, and GPT-5.6 Sol found no argument establishing 28 as a minimum, noting that exponential-tilting MAIC and entropy balancing can be dual formulations of the same calibration problem and that trimming is a tuning choice. The entry’s two prior_work items carried no locators; the literature auditor identified them as Phillippo et al. 2020 and Hatswell et al. 2020 (doi:10.1016/j.jval.2020.02.008), which are now cited.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Citation fidelity: the two prior_work entries carry no DOI, but they map cleanly onto real papers whose descriptions match. ‘Phillippo and colleagues, anchored population-adjustment simulation’ is Phillippo, Dias, Ades & Welton 2020 (Stat Med 39:4885-4911), which is exactly an anchored population-adjustment simulation of ML-NMR, MAIC and STC. ‘Hatswell and colleagues, unanchored misspecification simulation’ is Hatswell, Freemantle & Baio 2020 (Value Health 23:751-759), ‘The Effects of Model Misspecification in Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison’. Both are accurately characterized; supplying the locators would make them non-decorative. I found no public neutral adversarial benchmark platform for PAIC; outstandR is a unified software interface, not a benchmark with shared scenarios and published ground truth. The oracle claim is too strong: Phillippo 2020 explicitly defines truth as what a gold-standard correctly specified IPD network meta-regression would estimate, and full-IPD reference arms are actually run in ML-NMR and IPD-NMA simulation work. The ‘28 method families’ figure is a design proposal, not a checkable fact. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Confirms the ‘Phillippo and colleagues’ prior_work description and supplies the missing locator; also shows the gold-standard IPD network meta-regression concept is explicit in the anchored benchmark literature.. Cites 10.1016/j.jval.2020.02.008: Confirms the ‘Hatswell and colleagues’ prior_work description and supplies the missing locator.. Cites arXiv:2401.12640: Contains simulated comparisons against a full-IPD analysis, i.e. an oracle-style reference arm, weakening ‘PAIC simulation studies commonly omit an oracle comparator’. Retrieved at abstract/summary level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C6 is correct, C7 is a sound design principle, and C11 correctly counts ten grouped scenario families. The remainder is inflated. No mathematical or decision-theoretic argument establishes 28 families as a minimum, and several categories overlap. Conventional exponential-tilting MAIC and entropy balancing can be dual formulations of the same calibration problem when they use identical moments and base weights; trimming is a tuning intervention rather than necessarily a separate method family. A single full-IPD oracle cannot separate information loss from method failure because it simultaneously changes data granularity, available covariates, and model specification. That decomposition requires nested paired arms that change one feature at a time. Simulation truth itself can be the relevant reference, so an estimated oracle need not appear in every scenario. Claims about the absence of public benchmarks, author behavior, and routine oracle omission are literature claims unsupported here. A shared adversarial benchmark would be useful infrastructure, but not a decision-grade requirement in the asserted form.

Decision path

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
Statement
Apart from isolated work relating low effective sample size to error, PAIC diagnostics have not been evaluated as classifiers of realized error with reported discrimination and calibration. Two exceptions exist: a simulation reported at ISPOR Europe 2024 (abstract MSR65) found bias in unanchored MAIC once absolute ESS fell below roughly 30 to 35, and Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511) reports that the robust sandwich variance estimator underestimates variability where effective sample sizes are small. Cross-validation is also still reported at a hierarchical level that does not match the prediction task; in cpaic at commit 9d150e9, PSIS-LOO is observation-level and documented as incapable of validating cross-gap prediction, and grouped study-level leave-one-out is not implemented.

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
Why it is open
Diagnostics are computed from the same data and model that produced the estimate, which does not logically prevent them from predicting error but does mean the predictive value has to be demonstrated rather than assumed. Sensitivity, specificity and calibration are not intrinsic properties of a diagnostic; they are defined only relative to a specified distribution of scenarios and a prespecified threshold for material error, so establishing them requires a simulation program with an agreed scenario set, which the field has not built. Patient-level cross-validation measures within-study accuracy dominated by information the target task does not have, while the decision quantity is a prediction for a new population or study, and importance-sampling diagnostics behave differently at each hierarchical level and are rarely reported per level.

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Specify a scenario distribution and a material-error threshold first, then score each diagnostic as a predictor of realized error against known truth and report its discrimination and calibration, taking the published ESS-to-bias findings as the starting calibration point rather than the endpoint. Separate descriptive from error-predictive diagnostics in reporting guidance and retain only the latter as evidence. Aggregate log-likelihood contributions at the deployment-relevant unit by adding grouped study-level, comparison-level and subnetwork-level leave-one-out to the observation-level PSIS-LOO that implementations currently provide, and report the diagnostics separately by level.

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
Our study

Effective sample size tracks the error an analysis got by chance better than the error it got from adjusting on the wrong covariates
The question put to it. Every population adjustment arrives with a panel of numbers beside it: effective sample size, the same figure as a percentage, the largest weight, standardized differences before and after adjustment, a distance between populations. A committee reads them as evidence about whether to believe the estimate, and a widely quoted rule says to worry below an effective sample size of about 30 to 35. Scored as classifiers of realized error, with discrimination and calibration, against known truth and under a declared distribution of analyses, what are they worth?
What it found. At the level at which a diagnostic is actually read, one analysis at a time, effective sample size tracks the error a study got by chance far better than the error it got from adjusting on the wrong covariates: AUROC 0.847 against the outcome-noise component and 0.813 against chance covariate imbalance between the source arms, both of which are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, against 0.653 for the transport component that adjustment exists to remove. At the quoted cutoff of 35 it catches between a quarter and a third of material errors in every misspecification stratum, 0.309 where an effect modifier is omitted and the omission is diagnosable in principle, at specificity 0.926. No evaluated fixed cutoff met the registered requirement of sensitivity 0.80 at specificity 0.50 in every stratum. Three of the panel’s members are provably one statistic, since ESS/n = 1/(1+CV^2(w)) exactly and area under the ROC curve is invariant to monotone transformation; a fourth, the post-weighting balance on matched moments, is zero at the solution of the calibration equations and among converged analyses cannot discriminate anything. On a decision-curve basis every rule in the panel is beaten by scrutinizing every analysis, up to an action threshold of 0.3.
Results.

Prespecified verdict: the panel does not classify realized error at the thresholds in use. No rule reached sensitivity 0.80 with specificity 0.50 in every misspecification stratum. ESS below 35 reaches sensitivity 0.251 to 0.326 across strata at specificity 0.909 to 0.926.
The mechanism, registered before the run and holding at the level of a single analysis: effective sample size discriminates the outcome-noise component at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component at 0.653, a gap of 0.194, and the arm-imbalance component at 0.813. The two it reads well are the two that are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, which is what the panel is built from.
Peer review changed this claim and the paper’s title. Scored against SYSTEMATIC transport bias with the design cell as the unit, rather than against the realized transport component of one replicate, effective sample size reaches 0.808 rather than 0.653. That analysis does not rescue the panel either: the statistic that is identically zero reaches 0.708 on it, because 128 cells is a small sample in which the bias and every diagnostic move along the same overlap axis. Both levels are reported and the title now claims only the replicate-level result.
The panel is smaller than it looks, by algebra rather than by simulation. ESS, ESS as a percentage and the coefficient of variation of the weights had identical areas under the ROC curve to 0.0e+00 within a fixed source size. The matched-moment balance statistic never exceeded 1.4e-14 and its apparent AUROC of 0.550 is discrimination of floating-point residual, not of balance.
Silence is where the damage is. Across the 88 cells the ESS rule never fires in, the material-error rate runs from 0.045 to 0.835. The registered version of this claim, a spread across the cells it does fire in, was not met (0.150 against a prespecified 0.30) because those cells are all bad. A first draft called the silent-cell span a stronger version of the registered claim; peer review established that both spans are variation in predictive value, which moves with prevalence and case mix, so neither is a test of whether a threshold transports. That promotion is withdrawn and the leave-one-factor-level-out calibration is the evidence on transportability.
Decision-curve analysis: at action thresholds up to 0.3, flagging every analysis beats every rule in the panel. From 0.4 upwards three distinct statistics beat both alternatives, relative effective sample size, pre-weighting imbalance and Mahalanobis distance; the absolute cutoff that gets quoted is not among them at any threshold examined.
The same statistics work when they measure the actual gap. Pre-weighting imbalance predicts the unadjusted comparison’s transport error at AUROC 0.891, against 0.655 for the same statistic applied to MAIC. These diagnostics are informative about the problem and uninformative about the solution: weighting sets to zero the very quantity they measure.
Our proposal, converting residual imbalance on a measured but unadjusted covariate into the units of the estimand with the source-estimated interaction, reaches 0.937 against the transport component over the diagnosable set where effective sample size as a percentage reaches 0.851. That gain of 0.086 misses the 0.10 we registered and is reported as a miss. Inside the omitted-modifier stratum alone the plain balance check on unmatched covariates beats it, 0.946 against 0.938, because there the covariate is always a modifier and converting imbalance into effect units only adds estimation noise. The conversion earns its keep exactly when the analyst does not know whether the unmatched covariate matters.
An adversarial critique of the design before the run found two arithmetic errors in the protocol: the dispersion factor was not the pure variance instrument it was described as wherever the cross-moment channel was on, and the target trial’s variance was understated by a factor of two to three. Both were confirmed numerically and corrected before any result was seen.
Round one of review found the load-bearing claim of the paper wrong, and all three reviewers found it independently. The arm-imbalance component uses no outcome at all, and the noise component’s variance is exactly sigma^2 (1/ESS_A + 1/ESS_C), so a weight statistic is its natural summary rather than merely correlated with it. Round one also found that the calibration split was perfectly confounded with the dispersion factor, because cells are enumerated with that factor varying fastest; leave-one-factor-level-out replaced it and the previous claim that overlap statistics calibrate worse than weight statistics was withdrawn as an artifact.

Design.

Estimand

Transported A versus C mean difference in the target superpopulation; the anchored A versus B contrast as a secondary reference

Methods compared

MAIC matching means and standard deviations, MAIC matching means only, STC with a heteroskedasticity-consistent variance, no adjustment

Data-generating mechanism

An anchored indirect comparison with a continuous outcome and an identity link, chosen so that the realized error of a linear estimator splits exactly into arm imbalance, transport error and outcome noise, so each diagnostic can be scored against each component separately: two of the three are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, which is what the panel is built from, and the third is what adjustment exists to remove. 128 cells crossing an omitted effect modifier, a cross-moment modifier that no baseline table could reveal, overlap, source size, how correlated the omitted modifier is with the adjustment set, and a target dispersion ratio that destroys effective sample size while adding no bias where the modifier structure is correct. 4000 replicates per cell, four estimators. Primary results are reported within misspecification strata rather than over a mixture, so no investigator-chosen frequency enters the headline.

Replicates

4000 per cell, 512,000 datasets and 2,048,000 estimates


What this does not answer. The second half of DIA-03 is untouched: no PSIS-LOO is computed at any hierarchical level and grouped study-level leave-one-out is no more implemented here than in the packages, so the mismatch between the level at which cross-validation is reported and the level at which the prediction is made remains open. DIA-06 is answered only in part; two estimator families and no adjustment are compared on identical replicates, but ML-NMR, NMI, doubly robust estimators and flexible learners are absent. The outcome is continuous with an identity link, which is what buys the exact error decomposition and is also the largest restriction: nothing here transfers to non-collapsible effect measures or time-to-event outcomes, where part of the error is a collapsibility artifact rather than an adjustment failure. Covariates are normal, comparisons are anchored, conditional constancy holds, and target moments are exact. The deployment weights are a declared judgment and nothing in this program measured them, which is why the primary results are within strata.
Peer review. 2 rounds, two independent reviewers. The reports, the point-by-point responses and the editorial decision are published in full: read the review.

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
What this project measured
Study studies/DIA-03-diagnostics-as-classifiers, run and decided against a rule registered before the run. 128 cells, 4000 replicates each, four estimators, ten diagnostic rules.
Conclusion: the panel does not classify realized error at the thresholds in use. Material error, meaning the transported effect wrong by more than 0.20, occurs on 0.479 of fitted MAIC replicates under the deployment weights, so the target is close to a coin flip and a useful diagnostic has room to be informative.
Operating points are reported within misspecification strata, so no assumed mixture of misspecification frequencies enters the headline. In the well-specified stratum the rules divide into two useless families: high specificity with little sensitivity (ess 0.326/0.923, max_w 0.350/0.919, bias_hat 0.099/0.962), or high sensitivity bought with false alarms (smd_pre 0.822/0.408, ess_pct 0.742/0.623). The matched standardized difference, smd_matched, fires on no replicate at all (sensitivity 0.000, specificity 1.000): after matching it is zero by construction and carries no information about error. The pattern is essentially unchanged when a modifier is omitted.

title: PAIC diagnostics are not evaluated as classifiers of realized error
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Apart from isolated work relating low effective sample size to bias, PAIC diagnostics have not been evaluated as classifiers of realized error with reported discrimination and calibration, and cross-validation for PAIC is not routinely performed at the hierarchical level matching the prediction task.
The source titled this. “PAIC diagnostics are never scored on whether they predict error” The title says diagnostics are never scored on predicting error, but the audit found two exceptions relating low effective sample size to bias and to variance underestimation.
The source said. “Whether the diagnostics used in PAIC (ESS, balance, overlap, influence, fit statistics) actually predict the error of the resulting estimate, or only describe the fitted model, has never been quantified. Relatedly, cross-validation is reported at a hierarchical level that often does not match the prediction the analysis is making, so a good statistic can accompany a failed transport.”
What was wrong with it. The source said predictive validity has never been quantified; the literature auditor found an ISPOR Europe 2024 simulation abstract identifying an ESS threshold below which bias appears, and Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511) tying small ESS to sandwich-variance underestimation. Neither treats a diagnostic as a classifier with discrimination and calibration against known truth, so the narrowed claim stands.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. The blanket ‘has never been quantified’ fails for at least one diagnostic. An ISPOR Europe 2024 / Value in Health simulation abstract (MSR65, ‘Can Low Effective Sample Size in Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons (MAICs) Lead to Bias?’) simulated unanchored MAICs of time-to-event and binary outcomes across sample size, event rate and overlap and reported bias when absolute ESS fell below roughly 30-35, irrespective of whether the low ESS came from small n or poor overlap. That is a diagnostic evaluated against realized error with a threshold. Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 similarly ties a diagnostic to a performance failure, reporting that the robust sandwich variance estimator underestimates variability where ESS is small. Neither treats a diagnostic as a classifier with discrimination and calibration against known truth, and I found nothing on hierarchical-level-matched cross-validation or per-level PSIS reporting for PAIC, so the substantive gap stands. I read only abstract-level material for the ISPOR item, hence the low confidence. Cites https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(24)05162-3/fulltext: Quantifies, in simulation with known truth, whether a standard PAIC diagnostic (ESS) predicts bias, identifying an approximate ESS threshold below which bias appears. Conference abstract; I retrieved title and venue plus a summary of findings, not the full text.. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1511: Links a diagnostic quantity (small ESS) to a documented inferential failure (sandwich variance underestimation), i.e. a diagnostic with demonstrated predictive content for one error mode..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2, C4, and C5 are technically correct: descriptive fit is not automatically error-predictive, and patient-level versus study-level validation target different deployments. But computing a diagnostic from fitted data does not logically prevent it from predicting error. Sensitivity, specificity, ROC curves, and calibration are defined only relative to a specified distribution of scenarios and a prespecified material-error threshold; they are not intrinsic properties of a diagnostic. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, PSIS-LOO is explicitly observation-level and documented as incapable of validating cross-gap prediction, while grouped study-level LOO is not implemented. The field-wide claims that predictive validity has “never” been quantified are unsourced. A systematic evaluation remains an open research task, but the report overstates what follows from same-data computation.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC
text:
Statement
Balance, support, fit and inconsistency diagnostics can falsify limited observable restrictions, but none of them can establish the absence of unmeasured effect modification or cross-study noncomparability, which is the part of the identifying assumption the analysis depends on. Residual heterogeneity and inconsistency checks, and covariate-by-covariate relaxation of the shared effect modifier assumption, are already available and are used inside ML-NMR target-population projections (Phillippo et al. 2022, doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), and a proof-of-concept falsification test built on partitioning a single arm’s IPD exists for measured-covariate sufficiency (Yi and Jiang 2025, doi:10.57264/cer-2024-0235). What has not been developed for PAIC is falsification of transport itself through held-out IPD or leave-one-study-out prediction.

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC
text:
Why it is open
Balance diagnostics are functions of measured covariates and fit statistics are functions of observed outcomes, so both speak to the measured, within-network part of the model and are silent on unmeasured effect modification and cross-study comparability. Under the classical two-trial configuration only one trial supplies IPD, so there is no second source from which observable implications of the transport assumption could be built. Held-out-study and deleted-edge designs do exist in disconnected NMA (Beliveau et al. 2017, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256), but a failed reconstruction is not uniquely attributable to transport failure, so such procedures test a joint prediction procedure rather than the identifying assumption on its own.

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis
Integrates residual heterogeneity and unrelated-mean-effects inconsistency checks with ML-NMR target-population projection and relaxes the shared effect modifier assumption one covariate at a time; contradicts the claim that residual inconsistency checks are not integrated with target-population projections.


Yi and Jiang 2025, A process to validate prognostic factors for unanchored matching-adjusted indirect comparison of single-arm trials in oncology: a proof-of-concept study
Splits a single arm into two risk-stratified groups with an imposed hazard ratio and tests whether reweighting on the candidate covariate set drives it back to one; a falsification-style test of measured-covariate sufficiency built on an IPD partition.


Jiang et al. 2025, A critical assessment of matching-adjusted indirect comparisons in relation to target populations
States that the shared effect modifier assumption is statistically untestable under the classical two-trial scenario; supplies the published attribution the source lacked.


Beliveau et al. 2017, Network meta-analysis of disconnected networks: How dangerous are random baseline treatment effects?
Disconnects real connected networks in multiple ways and scores the reconstructed cross-gap comparisons against the connected-network analysis, showing that synthetic bridge deletion is an established design rather than a new proposal.

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the falsification designs that already exist rather than build new machinery: generalize the single-arm IPD-partition test to multi-covariate and anchored settings, and carry the leave-one-study-out and edge-deletion designs already used in disconnected NMA into PAIC where IPD sit on both sides of the deleted edge. State for each check what it can and cannot rule out, since rejection implicates the joint model rather than transport alone and acceptance cannot validate a genuinely missing gap. Where negative-control outcomes or falsification endpoints are available, add them as a second observable implication rather than as a substitute for the transport check.

title: No diagnostic can falsify unmeasured effect modification in PAIC
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No falsification test exists for the unmeasured-covariate component of PAIC identifying assumptions. Residual heterogeneity/inconsistency checks and shared-effect-modifier relaxation are available and are used within ML-NMR target-population projections, but they interrogate the measured, within-network part of the model; held-out-IPD and leave-one-study-out falsification of transport has not been developed for PAIC.
The source titled this. “Reported diagnostics cannot falsify the assumptions they rest on” The title says reported diagnostics cannot falsify the assumptions at all, but the audit found balance, fit and inconsistency checks do falsify limited observable restrictions.
The source said. “Covariate balance and model fit can look excellent in a population-adjusted comparison even under severe residual confounding, so the diagnostics that are routinely reported carry no evidential content for the assumption the analysis actually depends on. No formal falsification test of PAIC identifying assumptions, built on held-out IPD or aggregate-data partitions, currently exists.”
What was wrong with it. The source said routine diagnostics carry no evidential content and that residual inconsistency checks are not integrated with target-population projections; the literature auditor found them integrated in Phillippo et al. 2022 (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162) and found a proof-of-concept IPD-partition falsification test in Yi and Jiang 2025 (doi:10.57264/cer-2024-0235). The core claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced to Jiang et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10), which states that under the classical two-trial scenario the shared effect modifier assumption is statistically untestable.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Phillippo et al. 2022, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis’ -> ‘Phillippo et al. 2023, Validating the Assumptions of Population Adjustment: Application of Multilevel Network Meta-regression to a Network of Treatments for Plaque Psoriasis’ 10.1177/0272989X221117162 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2022 online and 2023 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

closure-upheld

10 findings from the reading assert this problem is open; the closure was re-examined and stands Put to an independent reviewer with the closing auditors’ reasoning, the work they relied on, and the new findings in view together. The new findings repeatedly establish the boundary already preserved in the closure: observed-data diagnostics can test limited observable implications but cannot establish the absence of unmeasured effect modification or noncomparability. Phillippo et al. 2022 is the closure’s central counterexample and explicitly acknowledges the external-target limitation, so it supports rather than contradicts the residual. Yi and Jiang 2025 is likewise already conceded as a within-source measured-covariate check. Practice examples of overinterpreted null diagnostics and evidence of low power do not create a held-out-IPD or leave-one-study-out falsification procedure for PAIC transport. (reviewer confidence: high)

Flagged for reopening

10 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. Retrieved Phillippo et al. 2022 (Med Decis Making, psoriasis ML-NMR), which does exactly what the entry says is not done: it fits UME ML-NMR to test residual inconsistency and RE ML-NMR to test residual heterogeneity AFTER population adjustment, inside a framework that projects to arbitrary target populations, and relaxes the shared-effect-modifier assumption one covariate at a time. So ‘residual inconsistency checks are not currently integrated with target-population projections’ is false. I also retrieved Yi & Jiang 2025, a proof-of-concept falsification procedure for unanchored MAIC built on partitioning a single arm’s IPD, inducing a known hazard imbalance and asking whether reweighting on candidate covariates removes it. The core claim survives: nothing I found tests the unmeasured-confounding/conditional-constancy assumption itself, and Jiang et al. 2025 assert its untestability outright. Synthetic bridge deletion is already used in disconnected NMA (Beliveau 2017), so that sub-claim is not novel. Cites 10.1177/0272989X221117162: Integrates residual heterogeneity and residual inconsistency (UME) checks with ML-NMR target-population projection, and relaxes the shared effect modifier assumption covariate-by-covariate. Contradicts the claim that residual inconsistency checks are not integrated with target-population projections.. Cites 10.57264/cer-2024-0235: Proposes a formal falsification-style test built on an IPD partition: split a single arm into two risk-stratified groups with a known imposed hazard ratio, then test whether reweighting on the candidate covariate set drives it back to 1. Partially contradicts ‘no formal falsification test built on held-out IPD partitions currently exists’; it is a proof-of-concept covering measured-covariate sufficiency only.. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.10: Supplies a real published assertion of untestability for the shared effect modifier assumption, converting the unsourced core claim into a sourced one..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C5 and a limited form of C6 are correct: excellent measured balance or within-source fit can coexist with severe bias and cannot establish absence of unmeasured effect modification or cross-study constancy. However, “no evidential content” is false because balance, support, fit, and inconsistency checks can falsify observable necessary conditions. Synthetic bridge deletion and leave-one-study-out emulation test a joint prediction procedure only when the held-out unit is independent, relevant, and prespecified; failure is not uniquely attributable to transport, and success cannot validate a genuinely missing gap. The field-wide absence claims in C2 and C4 are unsourced and cannot be established within this audit. The identification limitation remains open, but the proposed procedures are not universal falsification tests of PAIC assumptions.

Decision path

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text: DEC-33 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text:
Statement
Expected value of perfect information, expected value of sample information and expected net benefit of sampling are computed conditional on one chosen evidence-synthesis structure: splitting, lumping, a multi-level model, an informative prior, a mixture prior, a commensurate prior or a power prior, equivalently one choice of how much strength to borrow across populations, treatments, outcomes or study designs. That choice changes the research decision and not only the effect estimate. In a severe sepsis case study extending 17 adult trials with 11 pediatric trials, odds ratio estimates ranged from 0.55 to 0.90 across sharing methods, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios from about 16,000 to 52,000 pounds per quality-adjusted life year, the probability of cost-effectiveness moved from 0.80 to 0.10, and the optimal design moved from a trial of 1,940 patients per arm to no trial at all, while each individual analysis reported a definite optimal sample size. No method propagates uncertainty over the structural choice into research-prioritization output, so the recommended trial and its sample size are reported as though the borrowing model were known. Model averaging exists as a response for effect estimates but has not been carried into value-of-information or expected-net-benefit-of-sampling output, and the general decision-model literature on structural uncertainty has never been instantiated on synthesis structures. The specific obstacle is that these structures differ mainly in what they extrapolate, so averaging weights cannot be learned from the observed data.

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text:
Why it is open
Structures that share more information differ in parameters no study measures directly, so the likelihood cannot rank them; any weight over structures is a prior judgment, and a value-of-information figure computed under a weighted mixture absorbs that judgment into a single number that does not display it. The computation compounds: value of information is already a nested expectation, and expected value of sample information requires the data-generating and refitting step to be repeated, so ranging over candidate structures multiplies an expensive calculation by their number. Model fit does not help either, because poor fit under a sharing model may signal a conflict between evidence sources that is itself informative rather than a reason to discard the model, so selection on fit is not defensible here. The honest output may not be a single number: when structures disagree on whether to run a trial, a set of research decisions with the assumption supporting each is more informative than an averaged expectation, but funders and reimbursement processes ask for one recommendation and no reporting convention exists for the set. The parameters that index intermediate sharing are not stably interpretable either; the power-prior discount behaves non-monotonically under random effects and can impose more sharing than lumping, so there is no ordered scale along which to integrate.

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Nikolaidis et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Implements splitting, lumping, multi-level, informative-prior, mixture-prior, commensurate-prior and power-prior models on one health technology assessment case study with cost-effectiveness and value-of-information output, introduces three metrics for the realized strength of sharing, and reports that the choice of method is a key determinant of the value of further research, including whether a trial is worth running at all.


Nikolaidis et al. 2021, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Classifies 89 information-sharing methods into functional, exchangeability-based, prior-based and multivariate relationships with the assumptions each imposes; the candidate set any averaging or robustness analysis would have to range over.


Jackson et al. 2019, Journal of the American Statistical Association
EVPPI and EVSI for Bayesian evidence-synthesis models fitted by MCMC, comparing candidate data sources and trading expected benefit against cost to choose a sample size; every quantity conditional on one synthesis model.


Strong, Oakley and Brennan 2014, Medical Decision Making
Nonparametric regression estimator of multiparameter partial EVPI from a probabilistic sensitivity analysis sample; the computational route that would have to be repeated for each candidate structure.


Jackson et al. 2011, Medical Decision Making
General framework for addressing structural uncertainty in decision models, including model averaging and discrepancy formulations; never instantiated on evidence-synthesis or borrowing structures.


Bojke et al. 2009, Value in Health
Review and application of methods for characterizing structural uncertainty in decision-analytic models, including parameterizing the structural choice so that it can be integrated over rather than selected.

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The first tractable step is a robustness report rather than an average: compute the full value-of-information output under every candidate sharing structure and publish the resulting set of research recommendations together with the realized-sharing metrics that place each structure on a scale, so a funder can see whether the recommendation to run a trial survives the structural choice. Where averaging is wanted, parameterize the structural choice as a continuous discount rather than a discrete list, elicit a distribution over it, integrate the value-of-information calculation over that distribution, and report the result explicitly as conditional on an elicited prior with sensitivity to it. Nested Monte Carlo cost can be held down with the existing regression-based EVPPI and EVSI estimators refitted per structure, so the obstacle is bookkeeping rather than new theory. Score the whole thing by what a decision-maker loses through conditioning on one structure: simulate an evidence base, take the trial each structure recommends, and report the realized net benefit of each research decision under the others.

title: Value-of-information output is conditional on the chosen synthesis structure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single case study, and the reviewer accepted that structural synthesis uncertainty can change the value of future information and therefore the recommended study design, distinct from acquiring individual patient data and from interval coverage after model selection. The demonstration covers one clinical problem, so the typical magnitude elsewhere is unestablished, though the argument does not depend on it.
