title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text: DEC-31 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text:
Statement
Evaluating a personalized treatment strategy against a network of trials requires restricting to strategy-congruent participants, those whose received treatment matches what the strategy would have recommended. That subset is a function of the strategy’s decision thresholds, so as the thresholds move the retained network changes: arms drop out, the reference arm can vanish, retained studies can become single-arm, and the network can disconnect. Where it disconnects the strategy’s net benefit is not estimable and the affected threshold region is simply blank on the decision curve; in the published multiple sclerosis application the uncomputable region was the lower threshold range the consulting neurologists considered clinically relevant. The available fallback, admitting single-arm studies to the synthesis, reintroduces exactly the non-randomized comparison the congruent-subset construction exists to avoid. The construction is also information-hungry: the congruent data set there held 652 of roughly 2,000 randomized participants, and the discarded non-congruent randomized arms carry information about the same relative effects that nothing currently uses. Missing are an estimator of strategy net benefit that survives disconnection of the congruent subnetwork, a principled way to use the discarded arms, and a support diagnostic reporting which parts of the threshold space are unsupported rather than leaving them empty. The failure is general to any decision-analytic evaluation of a treatment-selection rule against a network of trials, not specific to one clinical application.

title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text:
Why it is open
The disconnection is induced by the object under evaluation, so unlike an ordinary disconnected network it cannot be repaired once: the support gap moves as the decision thresholds move, and any bridge would have to be indexed by the threshold. Restricting to congruent participants conditions on a function of the treatment actually received, so the retained comparison is randomized only if the recommendation is independent of arm assignment; nobody has stated the conditions under which a congruent-subset contrast recovers the strategy’s causal net benefit, and the existing formulation reads arm event rates from a pooled control rate multiplied by network estimates rather than from a randomized contrast inside the congruent set. Using the discarded non-congruent arms requires a model relating congruent and non-congruent populations, which is the effect-modification assumption the decision curve is meant to interrogate, so the obvious fix is circular unless that model is identified elsewhere. Decision curve analysis over a network is a new construction used by a handful of groups, so the failure mode has attracted no attention beyond the analysis that ran into it. Reporting conventions conceal it as well: a decision curve that stops short of a threshold range reads as a design choice rather than as an estimability failure.

title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chalkou et al. 2023, Medical Decision Making
Extends decision curve analysis from a single randomized trial to a network, defining the congruent data set and the net benefit of a model-based strategy against treat-all and treat-none alternatives; records that for some threshold combinations the congruent set holds only single-arm studies so net benefit is not estimable, that omitting them discards potentially relevant information, and names both as needing further research.


Vickers and Elkin 2006, Medical Decision Making
Original decision curve analysis: net benefit as a function of the threshold probability, defined for a single dataset and two options.


Chalkou et al. 2021, Statistics in Medicine
The two-stage prediction model whose recommendations the network decision curve evaluates: a prognostic baseline risk score used as the single effect modifier in a network meta-regression.


Beliveau et al. 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
Random baseline treatment effects as a bridge for disconnected networks, validated by deliberately disconnecting two published networks and scoring the reconstructed comparisons; the standard response to disconnection, developed for networks that arrive disconnected rather than for a subnetwork that disconnects as a function of the rule being evaluated.


Hamza et al. 2026, Value in Health
Carries risk-specific network meta-regression effects into a cost-effectiveness model, reporting incremental cost-effectiveness ratios and net monetary benefit across the baseline risk distribution without conditioning on treatment congruence; an alternative route to a personalized decision that avoids the subsetting but does not evaluate a rule’s clinical usefulness.

title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write the estimand down first: the net benefit of a strategy is a contrast of expected outcomes under the strategy and under fixed alternatives in a named population, and it is a function of the whole network rather than of the congruent subset alone. Estimated that way, by predicting each participant’s outcome under the recommended treatment from the fitted network model instead of subsetting to those who happened to receive it, the disconnection problem is replaced by an explicit extrapolation whose assumptions can be stated and stress-tested. Compare that estimator against the congruent-subset estimator on a simulated network with known truth, scored on net-benefit bias and on how much of the threshold space each can cover. Where subsetting is retained, ship a support diagnostic that plots, over the threshold grid, whether the congruent subnetwork is connected, how many arms and participants survive, and where the reference arm is lost, so an empty region of a decision curve is labeled rather than silent. Report the congruent sample size alongside every net benefit, since the current construction discards most of the randomized evidence.

title: Evaluating a treatment strategy can disconnect the network it is evaluated on
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single application paper whose own authors hit the failure and named it as needing research, and the reviewer accepted it as a specific failure induced by the congruent-treatment restriction rather than an ordinary disconnected-network problem. The evidence is one paper and no second group has reported the same failure, which makes this a weaker base than most entries here.

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text: DEC-29 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text:
Statement
Rank probabilities, the probability of being ranked best and SUCRA are computed from the joint posterior of relative effects, so a treatment estimated imprecisely carries more posterior mass in both tails of its rank distribution and is systematically over-ranked at the extremes and under-ranked in the middle. Simulation shows the distortion tracks how information is distributed over the graph rather than efficacy: with degree irregularity defined as the normalized variance of weighted node degree, the probability of being ranked best is overestimated for the least-studied treatment and underestimated for the most-studied one, total rank-probability bias grows with irregularity, and bias in the relative effects themselves shows no such relationship. SUCRA is only accidentally protected; its bias is roughly ten times smaller and is unaffected by irregularity when all treatments are equally effective, because the rank-2 and rank-3 biases cancel the rank-1 and rank-4 biases, and that cancellation fails once true effects differ. What does not exist is any estimator, correction or reporting convention separating a top rank earned by efficacy from a top rank earned by a thin evidence base: no precision-standardized ranking metric, no bias correction for the rank-probability vector, and no diagnostic reporting how much of a treatment’s rank is attributable to its own posterior width. Work since then quantifies or reframes hierarchy uncertainty rather than removing the dependence, and the one structural remedy on offer is to plan future trials that reduce irregularity, which cannot repair a network that already exists. The consequence is visible in appraisal practice, where some reviews decline to report any hierarchy at all, citing sensitivity of ranking methods to network composition and the absence of an established standard for which method to use.

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text:
Why it is open
The bias belongs to the estimator rather than to the fit: a rank probability is a functional of an ordering, and unequal marginal variances change the distribution of orderings even when every posterior mean is identical, so no improvement in estimation removes it. Any correction must decide what to hold fixed, and standardizing each treatment’s posterior to a common precision changes the question the hierarchy answers; since different ranking metrics already answer different hierarchy questions, a corrected rank probability needs an agreed target before it can be defined at all. The distortion is a property of the whole network rather than of one contrast, so it cannot be absorbed into a per-comparison adjustment, and the feature that indexes it, the irregularity of the graph, is a property of the evidence base that no analysis choice can alter. Guidance has responded by asking authors to report the full set of rank probabilities rather than the probability of being best alone, which does not remove a bias that afflicts all of them, and the leading credibility framework explicitly defers appraisal of a treatment hierarchy to future work.

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Davies and Galla 2021, Research Synthesis Methods
Defines normalized degree irregularity and shows by simulation across five four-treatment geometries that disparity in the number of trials per treatment produces a systematic bias in estimated rank probabilities that grows with irregularity, while bias in the relative effects does not; offers no correction, only guidance on choosing which trial to add next.


Salanti, Ades and Ioannidis 2011, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Introduces SUCRA and the rank-probability presentation that is now the standard ranking output of Bayesian network meta-analysis.


Rucker and Schwarzer 2015, BMC Medical Research Methodology
P-score, the frequentist analogue of SUCRA computed without resampling; inherits the same dependence on how precisely each treatment’s effect is estimated.


Trinquart et al. 2016, Annals of Internal Medicine
Reanalysis of published network meta-analyses showing that treatment rankings carry substantial uncertainty which the conventional presentation hides.


Salanti et al. 2022, American Journal of Epidemiology
Introduces the treatment hierarchy question and shows that ranking metrics encompass estimation uncertainty in different ways and so produce different hierarchies; makes the target explicit but corrects no metric.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2021, Research Synthesis Methods
PreTA, the probability that a treatment is preferable to a fictional treatment of average performance, obtained by deviation-from-means parameterization; agreement with existing metrics across 232 networks is found to depend on the precision with which relative effects are estimated.


Wigle et al. 2025, Statistics in Medicine
Precision of Treatment Hierarchy, a single metric linking the variance of SUCRA values, the variance of mean ranks and the average variance of individual rank distributions, which quantifies certainty in a hierarchy as a whole and can be restricted to subsets such as the top three; it grades the hierarchy rather than correcting per-treatment rank bias.


Evrenoglou et al. 2026, Research Synthesis Methods
Converts network estimates into pairwise preferences using a smallest worthwhile difference and fits a probabilistic ranking model assigning each treatment a latent ability, implemented in the R package mtrank, so that small differences stop driving the hierarchy; agreement with existing metrics across 153 networks again depends on the precision of the estimates.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLoS Medicine
CINeMA rates confidence in each relative effect and states that assessment of confidence in a treatment hierarchy is left to future work.


Janke et al. 2020, BMJ
Network meta-analysis of biological medicines in rheumatoid arthritis that reports no treatment ranking, citing the sensitivity of ranking methods to network composition and the absence of an established standard.

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text:
Probable solution or research direction
State the target first, because the correction depends on it: a rank-probability vector that would be obtained if every treatment were estimated with equal precision is one candidate, and the probability that a treatment’s effect exceeds a clinically relevant threshold is another that is already precision-honest. Then derive the correction analytically, since under a multivariate normal posterior the mapping from unequal marginal variances to the rank distribution is explicit, so a first-order bias expression in those variances can be written down and validated against the published simulation design. Report a per-treatment decomposition beside any hierarchy, separating the part of a SUCRA value attributable to the estimated effect from the part attributable to posterior width, and pair it with the existing hierarchy-level certainty metric so a reader sees both the global and the per-treatment components. Make degree irregularity a routinely reported feature of a network, since it is cheap to compute and predicts both the precision of the estimates and the size of the rank bias.

title: Ranking metrics reward imprecision and no correction exists
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed this from a single simulation study, and the reviewer accepted that a precision-driven distortion of estimated rank probabilities is different from uncertainty in the relative effects. It is not recorded as confirmed-open because a line of work now quantifies hierarchy certainty and reframes the hierarchy question; what remains absent is any correction indexed to how information is distributed across the network.

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text: DEC-27 Confirmed open High priority Established Tractability 4/5

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text:
Statement
When the direct, indirect and network estimates of the same contrast disagree and carry different certainty ratings, no convention states which one a decision should use. GRADE directs the reader to the estimate from the highest-certainty evidence, which can be the indirect estimate and can therefore require acting on a quantity no network model outputs as its answer; other authorities hold that having committed to a network analysis one should always use the network estimate. The two rules can recommend differently from the same fitted model: in a worked pediatric antidepressant example the direct estimate for fluoxetine versus placebo was a standardized mean difference of -0.26 rated very low certainty, the indirect estimate -1.41 rated moderate, and the network estimate -0.51 rated very low, so following GRADE the clinician acts on an effect more than twice the size of the network estimate and more than five times the size of the direct one. Nothing establishes which selection rule has the better decision properties, because no simulation or empirical study scores them against realized error or decision error. The GRADE rule is also applied with no account of how selecting on estimated certainty distorts the reported interval, which is a selection problem rather than a reporting one.

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text:
Why it is open
Detecting the divergence is solved and deciding what to do about it is not: node splitting, inconsistency models and the meta-epidemiological literature all measure disagreement between direct and indirect evidence, and none of them prescribes an action. The three estimates are not independent, since the network estimate is a weighted combination of the other two, so selecting whichever carries the best rating is selecting on a statistic correlated with the quantity being chosen, and the interval reported afterwards is not the interval of the selection procedure. Certainty ratings are ordinal categories rather than probabilities, so no arithmetic converts moderate versus very low into weights, and any rule that uses them is a convention rather than a derivation. The alternative to selecting is modeling, through an inconsistency-allowing or bias-adjusted synthesis that returns one estimate with the disagreement priced into its width, but that changes what is reported rather than answering the question the panel asked, and no guidance names it as the resolution.

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Al Khalifah et al. 2018, Network meta-analysis: users’ guide for pediatricians, BMC Pediatrics
Poses the question directly, records the conflict between the GRADE highest-certainty rule and the position that committing to a network commits one to the network estimate, and resolves the worked fluoxetine example on the indirect estimate (-1.41, moderate certainty) rather than the network estimate (-0.51, very low).


Puhan et al. 2014, A GRADE Working Group approach for rating the quality of treatment effect estimates from network meta-analysis, BMJ
Sets out the rating approach and the rule of taking the higher-certainty of the direct and indirect estimates, which is the selection rule in dispute.


Izcovich et al. 2023, A guide and pragmatic considerations for applying GRADE to network meta-analysis, BMJ
Current practical guidance for applying the rating framework, which keeps the certainty-based selection without evaluating its decision properties.


Dias et al. 2010, Checking consistency in mixed treatment comparison meta-analysis, Statistics in Medicine
Gives node splitting, the standard device for detecting the disagreement that triggers the choice; it says nothing about what to report once disagreement is found.


van Valkenhoef et al. 2015, Automated generation of node-splitting models for assessment of inconsistency in network meta-analysis, Research Synthesis Methods
Automates node splitting so that the direct, indirect and network estimates of each contrast are routinely produced, which is what makes the selection problem a routine one.


Veroniki et al. 2013, Evaluation of inconsistency in networks of interventions, International Journal of Epidemiology
Compares methods for evaluating inconsistency, establishing that detection is mature while the downstream decision is unaddressed.


Song et al. 2011, Inconsistency between direct and indirect comparisons of competing interventions: meta-epidemiological study, BMJ
Measures empirically how often direct and indirect estimates disagree, which fixes how frequently the selection question arises in practice.


Dias et al. 2013, Evidence Synthesis for Decision Making 4: Inconsistency in Networks of Evidence Based on Randomized Controlled Trials, Medical Decision Making
Sets out the modeling alternative in which inconsistency is represented within the synthesis rather than resolved by choosing among estimates.


Chaudhry et al. 2015, Network Meta-analysis: Users’ Guide for Surgeons, Part II: Certainty, Clinical Orthopaedics and Related Research
Presents the same certainty-based reading to a second clinical audience, showing the rule is taught rather than debated at the point of use.


Phillippo et al. 2019, Threshold Analysis as an Alternative to GRADE for Assessing Confidence in Guideline Recommendations Based on Network Meta-analyses, Annals of Internal Medicine
Offers the nearest decision-level alternative, reporting how far the evidence could change before the recommendation changes rather than selecting among competing estimates.

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Score the rules rather than argue them: simulate networks with known truth and known inconsistency, apply the GRADE highest-certainty rule, the always-network rule and a bias-adjusted synthesis, and report realized error and decision error for each; nothing in that comparison requires machinery that does not already exist. Quantify the selection effect separately, since where a rule picks the estimate with the best rating the reported interval is conditional on that selection, so its coverage has to be derived or simulated rather than assumed. Where the disagreement is large, test whether an inconsistency-allowing or bias-adjusted model that returns a single estimate with the disagreement priced into its width outperforms any selection rule, which would replace the choice with a model. Where a selection rule is retained, require it to be prespecified in the protocol, since choosing after seeing which of the three estimates favors the intervention is otherwise unconstrained.

title: No rule says which of three conflicting estimates to use
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it, noting that the quoted guide records a real conflict between an evidence-certainty selection rule and the convention of using the network estimate once a network has been fitted. The evidence is a single users’ guide, which is a weaker basis than a survey, though the two rules it contrasts are both stated in widely used guidance and the numerical example shows the divergence is not hypothetical.

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text: DEC-25 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text:
Statement
Converting a fitted network meta-analysis into a treatment recommendation is done by conventions that do not share a decision objective. Ranking on highest expected value is optimal for a risk-neutral decision maker and ignores uncertainty; SUCRA and P-score blend mean effect and uncertainty in a way that answers no stated decision question; and GRADE’s instruction to prefer the more certain of two conflicting estimates can return an incoherent recommendation set. The gap was named in a 2024 review of the field as the need for a definition of optimality that accommodates multiple treatment recommendations while penalizing uncertainty, whether the evaluative function is efficacy, cost-effectiveness or something else. A proposal now exists: loss-adjusted expected value, with a two-stage rule that first identifies treatments superior to the reference and then those within a minimally important difference of the best, compared against GRADE and three probability-based rankings on stylized examples and 10 network meta-analyses used in NICE guidelines, where an expected-value decision maker would recommend 4 to 14 treatments and the loss-adjusted rule 0 to 3 fewer (median 2), and where GRADE failed to recommend the highest expected-value treatment in 3 of the 10 cases. What is not settled is the rest of the problem: the proposal is confined to risk aversion and excludes a risk-seeking posture, it is not extended to net benefit or cost-effectiveness, alternative approaches to risk aversion in the wider literature were not compared, and no guidance body has adopted any rule. No certainty or confidence label has an established mapping onto the ranking it is supposed to inform, so a committee reading a hierarchy alongside a set of GRADE ratings is still combining them by judgment.

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text:
Why it is open
The rule sits between a fitted synthesis model and the recommendation a committee issues, and neither the statistical methodology literature nor the appraisal guidance claims that interface, so nothing obliges either to converge on an answer. Penalizing uncertainty requires a loss function, and eliciting one for a population-level guideline decision is contested; the alternatives, namely mean-variance trade-offs, rules capping the probability of a poor outcome, and explicit risk-aversion parameters, all introduce inputs whose values are to some extent arbitrary, which is why none has been taken up in this literature. Risk posture may itself depend on baseline health, with evidence that individuals are risk-seeking at low levels of baseline health, so a single risk-averse rule may be wrong exactly where the decisions are gravest. The evaluative function that matters for reimbursement is net benefit rather than efficacy, and moving a decision rule onto that scale requires the economic model as well as the network, which puts it outside what a synthesis paper normally carries.

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ades et al. 2024, Twenty years of network meta-analysis: Continuing controversies and recent developments, Research Synthesis Methods
States the gap directly: further research is needed to find a definition of optimality that accommodates multiple treatment recommendations while penalizing uncertainty, whether decisions rest on efficacy, cost-effectiveness or another evaluative function.


Ades et al. 2025, Treatment recommendations based on network meta-analysis: Rules for risk-averse decision-makers, Research Synthesis Methods
Introduces loss-adjusted expected value and a two-stage rule using a minimally important difference, defines properties of a valid ranking under uncertainty, and compares against GRADE and three probability rankings on 10 NICE network meta-analyses; it excludes risk-seeking postures, does not compare mean-variance or maximum-probability alternatives, and states that extension to net benefit and to baseline-dependent risk posture is ongoing research.


Salanti et al. 2011, Graphical methods and numerical summaries for presenting results from multiple-treatment meta-analysis: an overview and tutorial, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Introduces SUCRA, the incumbent convention that mixes effect size and uncertainty without reference to a decision problem.


Rucker and Schwarzer 2015, Ranking treatments in frequentist network meta-analysis works without resampling methods, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Gives the P-score, the frequentist counterpart, so the same objection applies in both frameworks.


Brignardello-Petersen et al. 2020, GRADE approach to drawing conclusions from a network meta-analysis using a minimally contextualised framework, BMJ
Specifies how GRADE turns network estimates into categorized conclusions using certainty ratings and a threshold, the incumbent rule that the loss-adjusted comparison finds can privilege more uncertain treatments; the partially contextualized companion is doi 10.1136/bmj.m3907.


Claxton 1999, The irrelevance of inference: a decision-making approach to the stochastic evaluation of health care technologies, Journal of Health Economics
Establishes the decision-theoretic argument that adoption decisions should follow expected net benefit rather than inferential thresholds; the precedent on the net-benefit scale that a network decision rule would have to connect to.


Epstein 2019, Beyond the cost-effectiveness acceptability curve: The appropriateness of rank probabilities for presenting the results of economic evaluation, Health Economics
Examines whether rank probabilities are an appropriate presentation of economic evaluation results, the same objection posed on the cost-effectiveness side.


Chalkou et al. 2023, Decision Curve Analysis for Personalized Treatment Choice between Multiple Options, Medical Decision Making
Supplies a decision-analytic route for choosing among multiple options with an explicit threshold, developed for prediction rather than for network synthesis output.


Naci et al. 2014, Evidence-Based Prescribing: Combining Network Meta-Analysis With Multicriteria Decision Analysis to Choose Among Multiple Drugs, Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes
Attaches an explicit multicriteria value function to network output, showing one way of naming an objective and the weights it requires.


Dias et al. 2013, Evidence Synthesis for Decision Making 6: Embedding Evidence Synthesis in Probabilistic Cost-Effectiveness Analysis, Medical Decision Making
Shows how a network posterior enters a probabilistic cost-effectiveness model, the pathway through which a loss-adjusted rule would have to be extended to net benefit.


Phillippo et al. 2018, Sensitivity of treatment recommendations to bias in network meta-analysis, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
Defines decision-invariant thresholds for a recommendation, which presuppose a decision rule and therefore inherit whichever convention is chosen.

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Test the existing proposal rather than add another: run loss-adjusted expected value, plain expected value, SUCRA, P-score and the GRADE contextualized frameworks over a common set of simulated networks with known truth, and score them on realized decision error and on the size of the recommended set, a comparison nobody has run. Extend the loss adjustment to the net-benefit scale, where the evaluative function is already defined and the cost-effectiveness literature supplies the loss, so the rule can be used for reimbursement rather than only for efficacy ordering. Let the risk penalty depend on baseline health rather than fixing it, and report whether the recommendation set is stable to that dependence, since the fixed-penalty version may be wrong for life-threatening conditions. Fix a reporting convention that names the decision rule and its parameters alongside the recommendation, so that a recommendation set can be reproduced from the posterior by someone who did not fit the model.

title: No agreed rule turns an NMA posterior into a recommendation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it as a well-posed gap at the posterior-to-recommendation interface, quoting the 2024 review that names the missing definition of optimality. It is partially addressed because the same group published a concrete rule in 2025, evaluated on 10 NICE networks; what remains is that the rule is untested against realized decision error, confined to risk aversion, not extended to net benefit, and adopted by nobody.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text: DEC-23 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text:
Statement
GRADE and CINeMA rate the certainty of each pairwise relative effect a network meta-analysis produces; the treatment hierarchy is a separate output with its own decision use, and no rating framework covers it. Several partial devices exist and do not agree with one another: normalized entropy per treatment, credible intervals for SUCRA and predictive P-scores, rank-clustering models that admit ties, ranking metrics adjusted for a minimally important difference, and the precision of treatment hierarchy (POTH), a network-level scalar with a leave-one-treatment-out residual and a simulation reference distribution. Nothing states which of these a report must present, what value is too uncertain to rank on, how the answer changes when the ranking metric changes, or what a decision maker should do when the pairwise estimates are rated high certainty and the hierarchy is not. The quantity is neither degenerate nor self-interpreting: across 267 published networks POTH runs from 0.096 to over 0.999 with a median of 0.671 and an interquartile range of 0.528 to 0.833. Ranking output is the part of a network meta-analysis that reaches guideline panels, press releases and clinical summaries, and it is published as an ordered list with no certainty attached to the ordering itself.

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text:
Why it is open
A hierarchy is a nonlinear functional of the whole joint posterior, and the GRADE and CINeMA domains are defined comparison by comparison, so per-comparison ratings cannot be aggregated into a rating for an ordering. The candidate metrics measure different objects: entropy and rank intervals are per treatment, POTH is per network, minimally-important-difference adjustment changes the estimand rather than the uncertainty, and rank clustering changes the rated object from an ordering into a partition. None is on a scale comparable across networks without a reference distribution, so thresholds cannot be fixed by convention the way GRADE’s four levels were. The hierarchy question itself is not settled either: several distinct formalizations of which treatment is best have been described, and a certainty rating cannot precede a decision about which one is being rated. Ranking is also the output most attractive to report and least attractive to qualify, so nothing pushes an uncertainty statement into the abstract where the ordering appears.

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wigle et al. 2025, Precision of Treatment Hierarchy: A Metric for Quantifying Certainty in Treatment Hierarchies From Network Meta-Analysis, Statistics in Medicine
Defines POTH with a leave-one-treatment-out residual and a simulation-based null, notes that hierarchies from SUCRA and P-score are typically reported without any measure of certainty, and reports the empirical distribution across 267 published networks (minimum 0.096, maximum above 0.999, median 0.671, interquartile range 0.528 to 0.833); implemented in the CRAN package poth.


Salanti et al. 2011, Graphical methods and numerical summaries for presenting results from multiple-treatment meta-analysis: an overview and tutorial, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Introduces SUCRA, the ranking summary whose hierarchies are the object a certainty framework would have to rate.


Rucker and Schwarzer 2015, Ranking treatments in frequentist network meta-analysis works without resampling methods, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Gives the P-score, the frequentist analogue of SUCRA, so that the same reporting habit holds in both frameworks.


Trinquart et al. 2016, Uncertainty in Treatment Rankings: Reanalysis of Network Meta-analyses of Randomized Trials, Annals of Internal Medicine
Reanalyzes published networks to show that rank uncertainty is large and routinely omitted, establishing the empirical size of the problem a decade before a hierarchy-level metric existed.


Wu, Shih and Tu 2021, Using Normalized Entropy to Measure Uncertainty of Rankings for Network Meta-analyses, Medical Decision Making
Proposes normalized entropy as a per-treatment uncertainty measure for a treatment’s place in the hierarchy, one of the competing devices with no rule saying when to use it.


Veroniki et al. 2018, Is providing uncertainty intervals in treatment ranking helpful in a network meta-analysis?, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Examines whether ranking uncertainty intervals help interpretation, which is the reporting question a framework would have to answer rather than leave to preference.


Rosenberger et al. 2021, Predictive P-score for treatment ranking in Bayesian network meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Gives a predictive ranking metric whose intervals are continuous rather than discrete, a further alternative on a scale not comparable with the others.


Pearce and Zhou 2025, RaCE: A rank-clustering estimation method for network meta-analysis, Research Synthesis Methods
Estimates clusters of treatments that cannot be distinguished, changing the reported object from a strict ordering to a partition and so changing what a certainty rating would apply to.


Curteis et al. 2025, Ranking of treatments in network meta-analysis: incorporating minimally important differences, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Adjusts ranking metrics so that treatments differing by less than a clinically important amount are treated as equivalent, altering the hierarchy itself rather than its uncertainty.


Salanti et al. 2022, Introducing the Treatment Hierarchy Question in Network Meta-Analysis, American Journal of Epidemiology
Shows that which treatment is best has several distinct formalizations, so a certainty framework must first fix which hierarchy question it rates.


Chiocchia et al. 2020, Agreement between ranking metrics in network meta-analysis: an empirical study, BMJ Open
Measures how far published hierarchies depend on the choice of ranking metric, which is one of the sensitivities a certainty framework would need a domain for.


Davies and Galla 2021, Degree irregularity and rank probability bias in network meta-analysis, Research Synthesis Methods
Shows that network topology alone biases rank probabilities, a structural threat to a hierarchy that no per-comparison certainty domain captures.

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Fix the rated object first, using the existing taxonomy of hierarchy questions, since the certainty of a full ordering, of a best-treatment claim and of a top-k set are different quantities with different failure modes. Define domains by what actually degrades a hierarchy rather than by analogy to the pairwise domains: overlap of the effect posteriors, which POTH already measures; the contribution of low-certainty comparisons to the ordering; sensitivity of the order to the choice of ranking metric; and sensitivity to a minimally important difference. Calibrate thresholds against the empirical distribution across the 267 published networks rather than by convention, and require any published ordering to carry a hierarchy-level precision statement alongside it. Test the resulting rating by whether it separates orderings that survive a leave-one-study-out refit or a change of ranking metric from those that do not, which is the operating characteristic none of the current metrics has been shown to have.

title: The treatment hierarchy is published without a certainty rating
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted that POTH and related quantities are useful partial measures of hierarchy precision but do not constitute a certainty framework with domains, interpretation thresholds and reporting rules. It is partially addressed rather than open because five distinct devices for hierarchy uncertainty were published between 2016 and 2025; what none supplies is the rule that says which to report and what value is too uncertain to act on.

CrossRef gives 2020 online and 2021 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

CrossRef gives 2021 online and 2022 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text: DEC-21 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text:
Statement
When no direct reference-versus-placebo trial exists, equivalence and non-inferiority margins in biosimilar development are derived by applying the fixed-margin (95-95) method to an anchored indirect estimate and then retaining a conventional fraction of the effect. The fraction is selected by clinical justification rather than derived: in a published biosimilar case study, retaining 40%, 50%, 60% and 70% of the effect yields equivalence margins of (0.688, 1.454), (0.732, 1.366), (0.779, 1.283) and (0.829, 1.206), and 60% is chosen on the stated ground that it accounts for potential departure from the constancy assumption. Nothing links the size of that fraction to the size of the departure the indirect route can actually carry, so the same 60% is used whether the common comparator is nearly identical across the two trials or substantially different. Summing the two trials’ variances widens the interval and moves the margin conservatively, but that prices sampling error only; population and treatment-version differences between the anchor trials do not shrink with sample size. No method maps an assumed violation of cross-trial transportability into the derived margin, and no convention reports the margin as an identified set or as the violation at which the equivalence conclusion would flip. Because the margin is prespecified and fixed before the confirmatory trial reads out, an error in it cannot be corrected afterwards and determines directly whether biosimilarity is declared.

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text:
Why it is open
The preservation fraction was invented for the direct-evidence case, where it discounts sampling uncertainty and the constancy of the active comparator’s historical effect; carrying it to an indirect estimate silently asks one number to absorb a second and different assumption. The size of a transitivity violation is not identified from the two trials that produced the estimate, so a derived fraction would have to be a function of an assumed bias rather than an estimated one, which converts a single agreed number into a sensitivity analysis that regulators would have to be willing to accept in a prespecified protocol. Margin setting is negotiated with an agency case by case, so a fraction that has survived review before needs no justification beyond having survived review. The tipping-point machinery that would express the answer exists and is implemented for network meta-analysis decisions, but it has never been applied to a prespecified regulatory margin, where the quantity to be tipped is fixed in advance rather than read off a fitted model.

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hemmelmann et al. 2025, Implementation of the Anchor-Based Indirect Comparison Method for Equivalence Margin Derivation in Biosimilar Development, Pharmaceuticals
Implements anchored indirect margin derivation for a biosimilar, tabulates the equivalence margin at 40%, 50%, 60% and 70% preservation, and selects 60% on clinical justification as covering potential departure from the constancy assumption; the departure itself is never quantified.


FDA guidance for industry, Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials to Establish Effectiveness (2016)
Defines the fixed-margin (95-95) approach and the practice of preserving a fraction of the active comparator’s effect, for the setting in which a direct comparator-versus-placebo estimate exists.


EMA, Guideline on the choice of the non-inferiority margin (CPMP/EWP/2158/99)
The European guidance on margin selection; it treats constancy of the historical effect as a judgment about the comparator rather than as a quantity that could be varied and priced.


Rothmann et al. 2002, Design and analysis of non-inferiority mortality trials in oncology, Statistics in Medicine
Derives the fixed-margin construction and the retention-fraction argument that the indirect application reuses without modification.


Snapinn and Jiang 2007, Preservation of effect and the regulatory approval of new treatments on the basis of non-inferiority trials, Statistics in Medicine
Analyzes what preservation of effect means for approval, establishing that the fraction encodes a policy judgment about acceptable loss rather than a statistical correction, which is why it does not absorb a transportability violation.


Phillippo et al. 2018, Sensitivity of treatment recommendations to bias in network meta-analysis, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
Derives decision-invariant bias-adjustment thresholds, the smallest change in the evidence that flips a decision; this is the machinery a derived margin would use, developed for network decisions rather than for a prespecified regulatory margin.


Bucher et al. 1997, The results of direct and indirect treatment comparisons in meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
The anchored estimator whose summed variance is the only channel through which uncertainty about the indirect route currently reaches the margin.


Hashim et al. 2021, A systematic review of noninferiority margins in oncology clinical trials, Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research
Documents the range of retention fractions and justifications used in practice, showing how weakly the fraction is tied to any measured quantity even in the direct-evidence case.

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Derive the fraction rather than negotiate it: write the margin as a function of an assumed transportability violation on the log scale, and define the preservation fraction as the value that holds the type I error of the equivalence claim at the nominal level across a stated range of that violation. Report the pair consisting of the margin and the violation at which the equivalence conclusion flips, which is threshold analysis applied to a prespecified regulatory quantity rather than to a fitted network estimate. Calibrate the plausible range from observable evidence: the same common comparator appears in both anchor trials, so the difference in its arm outcomes bounds part of the violation and is visible before the confirmatory trial starts. Simulate the operating characteristics of 50% and 60% preservation under realistic anchor mismatch to establish whether the conventional fractions are conservative or anticonservative for the indirect case, since at present neither has been checked.

title: The effect-preservation fraction is not calibrated to indirect bias
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted that conventional preservation fractions provide no formal mapping from a quantified constancy or transportability departure to the derived margin. The evidence is a single applied methods paper, though its own tabulation of margins across preservation fractions makes the sensitivity of the answer to an unjustified choice explicit.

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text: DEC-19 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text:
Statement
The proportion contribution matrix, evidence flow and per-study importance are all defined from the frequentist two-stage projection matrix H, and no analogue to H exists in Bayesian network meta-analysis; the derivation states that limitation itself and offers the construction as a source of useful approximations rather than as a Bayesian quantity. This matters beyond bookkeeping: CINeMA’s per-comparison within-study-bias and indirectness judgments are computed from that matrix, so the GRADE-style certainty machinery the field relies on is frequentist-only. Bayesian synthesis is the framework used for most health technology assessment submissions and the only one available for multilevel network meta-regression and component models, so contributions there are obtained by refitting the network frequentist-style and importing the answer. Nothing validates that the imported number approximates how the Bayesian posterior actually depends on each study, and no study characterizes the discrepancy as a function of the heterogeneity prior, network sparsity or prior informativeness. The nearest Bayesian-native quantity is a posterior-to-prior variance ratio for a disconnected contrast, which measures how far the data move the prior but does not attribute the movement to studies or comparisons. Every subsequent contribution method, including shortest-path and leave-one-out contribution analysis for component networks, extends the frequentist construction rather than replacing it. There is therefore no posterior-native, validated study or comparison contribution measure, and no reported column for the prior, which in a Bayesian fit is itself a source of the estimate.

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text:
Why it is open
H exists because the frequentist network estimate is a fixed linear map of the direct estimates; a posterior is not a linear function of the data, so there is no matrix to decompose and no unique way to divide the posterior among studies. Under a random-effects model with a prior on heterogeneity the weight a study receives is itself a random quantity, so any contribution figure is a posterior summary and requires a prior decision about which functional is being summarized. The candidate replacements, namely leave-one-study-out posterior distance, Kullback-Leibler divergence and prior-to-posterior variance decomposition, each answer a different question, none is on the same zero-to-one-hundred-percent scale as the contribution matrix, and none has published operating characteristics. Meanwhile the frequentist import is cheap and produces a number CINeMA accepts, so nothing in practice forces the harder derivation. The problem is also invisible in output: a contribution table computed by refitting looks identical to one computed from the model that produced the reported estimates.

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Research
Derives the proportion contribution matrix from the frequentist hat matrix and states that deriving the contribution of evidence sources in a Bayesian network meta-analysis is not straightforward because no analogue to H exists, offering the method only as a source of useful approximations.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2020, In network meta-analysis, most of the information comes from indirect evidence: empirical study, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Applies the contribution matrix across 213 published network meta-analyses, establishing it as the field’s working provenance quantity; the computation is frequentist throughout.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, CINeMA: An approach for assessing confidence in the results of a network meta-analysis, PLOS Medicine
Builds per-comparison confidence judgments for within-study bias and indirectness on the contribution matrix, which is what makes the frequentist-only construction consequential for certainty assessment.


Rucker et al. 2020, The statistical importance of a study for a network meta-analysis estimate, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Defines study importance for a network estimate through the change induced by removing a study, again from the frequentist design rather than from a posterior.


Beliveau and Gustafson 2021, A Theoretical Investigation of How Evidence Flows in Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Disconnected Networks, Bayesian Analysis
Supplies the closest Bayesian-native evidence-flow quantity, the ratio of posterior to prior variance for a disconnected contrast, and shows evidence cannot flow across a true disconnection under weak priors; it measures prior versus data influence and does not attribute information to individual studies.


Yang et al. 2026, Evidence contributions in component network meta-analysis from the shortest-path approach, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Extends evidence-contribution tracing to component network meta-analysis by adapting the shortest-path decomposition, keeping the frequentist projection as the foundation.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Gives a leave-one-out route to contribution in component networks, showing the alternative constructions the field is exploring are still defined on the frequentist fit.


Donegan et al. 2018, Graphs of study contributions and covariate distributions for network meta-regression, Research Synthesis Methods
Displays study contributions alongside covariate distributions for network meta-regression, the reporting form a Bayesian contribution measure would have to reproduce.

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define contribution as a functional of the posterior rather than of a design matrix: for each decision contrast report the movement of the posterior when a study is removed or downweighted, anchored so that removing nothing scores zero and removing all direct evidence for that contrast scores one, using a symmetric divergence rather than Kullback-Leibler alone. The standardized information-sharing metrics that anchor a borrowing measure between splitting and lumping supply a working template for that anchoring and can be adapted from population sharing to study-level attribution within a network. Validate by simulating networks in which the frequentist contribution is known, computing the posterior-based quantity, and reporting the discrepancy as a function of the heterogeneity prior, network sparsity and prior informativeness, which also tells current CINeMA users how much error the frequentist import carries. Add an explicit prior column, since in a Bayesian fit the prior contributes information and the frequentist matrix has no cell for it.

title: Evidence contribution has no definition inside a Bayesian fit
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it on the ground that the quoted paper states the absence of an H analogue and characterizes what it offers as an approximation rather than a Bayesian contribution calculation. The evidence is a single methods paper, which is a weaker basis than a survey, although the frequentist-only construction is visible in every contribution method published since.

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text: DEC-17 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text:
Statement
Every measure now used to attribute a network estimate to its sources is computed with the between-study variance and any residual variances fixed at their point estimates: the proportion contribution matrix built from the hat matrix, percentage study weights, the borrowing-of-strength statistic, the pseudo-path and leave-one-out contribution measures for component networks, and edge-influence calculations in population-adjusted work. Riley et al. 2018, deriving percentage study weights for multi-parameter meta-analysis models, state the omission outright: the derivation ignores uncertainty in variance parameter estimates and assumes the information matrix for the mean parameters is independent of that for the residual and between-study variances, with variance components held fixed at their full-model values when the per-study information matrices are formed, and further consideration of the issue is needed. The reported provenance of a contrast is therefore a conditional quantity whose own uncertainty is neither propagated nor reported, and nothing is known about how far the attributed shares move across the plausible range of tau. That matters because tau is typically estimated from a handful of studies and is itself very imprecise, and because contribution figures are decision-relevant outputs rather than descriptions: they drive per-comparison certainty judgments in CINeMA and are used to justify excluding or downweighting a dominant study. No interval, no sensitivity curve and no reporting convention exists for a contribution percentage.

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text:
Why it is open
Contribution measures are functions of a weight matrix that itself depends on the estimated variance components, so their sampling distribution is a nonlinear function of a variance estimate whose own distribution is skewed and badly approximated when the number of studies is small; a delta-method interval would be deployed exactly where the delta method is least trustworthy. The obvious alternatives are expensive or unavailable: a nonparametric bootstrap has to refit the whole network and re-estimate tau for every replicate, and in the Bayesian setting there is no analogue of the hat matrix, so the flow-based machinery cannot simply be evaluated draw by draw without first being redefined. There is also no agreed target quantity: it is unsettled whether what should be reported is the contribution at the estimated tau, its posterior distribution, or its range over a plausible tau interval, and the three license different statements to a committee. And because contributions are read as descriptive summaries rather than as estimates, nobody has felt obliged to attach uncertainty to them, so the omission has propagated from the original derivation into every measure built on top of it.

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Riley, Ensor, Jackson and Burke 2018, Deriving percentage study weights in multi-parameter meta-analysis models, Statistical Methods in Medical Research 27:2885-2905
Derives percentage study weights for meta-regression, network meta-analysis and one-stage individual participant data models by decomposing Fisher’s information for the mean parameters, with variance components held fixed. States explicitly that the derivation ignores uncertainty in variance parameter estimates and that further consideration of the issue is needed.


Jackson, White, Price, Copas and Riley 2017, Borrowing of strength and study weights in multivariate and network meta-analysis, Statistical Methods in Medical Research 26:2853-2868
Defines the borrowing-of-strength statistic as the percentage reduction in the variance of a summary result attributable to indirect or correlated evidence. It is computed from the same fitted variance components and inherits the same conditioning.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Research 7:610
Builds the proportion contribution matrix from the hat matrix, whose entries depend on the degree of between-study heterogeneity. Notes that no analogue of the hat matrix exists in a Bayesian network meta-analysis, which is why a per-draw version of the measure is not simply available.


Rucker et al. 2020, The statistical importance of a study for a network meta-analysis estimate, BMC Medical Research Methodology 20
Defines per-study importance as the variance reduction from adding a study, uniquely defined and easily calculated for one-stage and two-stage models. It is exact given the variance components and silent about their uncertainty.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, CINeMA: An approach for assessing confidence in the results of a network meta-analysis, PLOS Medicine 17:e1003082
Uses contribution percentages as the input to per-comparison certainty judgments, which is the mechanism by which the unreported conditionality reaches a decision.


Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology 25
Computes component-effect contribution as normalized variance inflation under deletion of each direct comparison, at a single fitted heterogeneity value. The newest members of this family inherit the same conditioning.


Yang et al. 2026, Evidence contributions in component network meta-analysis from the shortest-path approach, BMC Medical Research Methodology 26
Computes component-effect contribution as flow over pseudo-paths derived from the component-level hat matrix, which depends on the fitted between-study variance in the same way the treatment-level hat matrix does.

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Start with the sensitivity question, which needs no new theory and settles whether the rest is worth doing: recompute the contribution matrix, the percentage study weights and the borrowing-of-strength statistic across the confidence or credible interval for tau in a set of published networks, and report how often the identity of the top contributing comparison changes and how far individual shares move. For inference, extend the information-matrix decomposition to include the block for the variance parameters rather than assuming independence between it and the block for the mean parameters, and benchmark the resulting intervals against a parametric bootstrap that re-estimates tau in each replicate. For Bayesian fits, define contribution per posterior draw through a draw-specific weight matrix, which delivers a posterior distribution for the contribution directly and gives the component-network measures an interval at the same time. Then require contribution tables used in certainty assessment to carry an interval, or an explicit statement that they are conditional on a single heterogeneity estimate, in the same way that effect estimates are required to carry one.

title: Evidence-provenance measures do not propagate heterogeneity uncertainty
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it, noting that the quoted derivation names the ignored variance-parameter uncertainty itself and that provenance measures can be decision-relevant outputs rather than descriptive calculations. The evidence is a single methods paper; what carries it beyond that is that the same conditioning is visible in each of the other contribution measures named here, none of which reports uncertainty in its shares.

text: DEC-15 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No certainty-of-evidence framework rates component effects
text:
Statement
GRADE for network meta-analysis and its CINeMA implementation are defined for a treatment contrast: within-study bias is aggregated over the studies contributing to that contrast, imprecision is judged against a clinically important range for it, incoherence comes from its loops, and indirectness from the studies informing it. A component main effect has none of those referents. It is a linear functional of the whole design matrix, no single study estimates it, every contributing study carries several other components, and the decision usually concerns a combination of components whose certainty is not a function of the individual components’ ratings. Reporting-bias machinery has the same problem: comparison-adjusted funnel plots, Egger-type tests and ROB-ME all operate on treatment comparisons and have no component-level analogue. Applied reviews therefore improvise or omit: one built a bespoke modified GRADE anchored on each direct comparison’s proportional contribution to the component estimate and deferred the justification to unpublished work, one attempted GRADE, found it highly subjective for a component synthesis and abandoned it in deviation from its protocol, one judged GRADE inappropriate and drew no certainty conclusions at all, and others applied CINeMA to the standard network contrasts while leaving the component estimates, which are the primary output, unrated. A Cochrane protocol and a Cochrane overview that used component network meta-analysis both state the position in terms: there is very little guidance and no consensus on the preferred method for evaluating the certainty of component network meta-analysis evidence, and consensus is still needed on how to assess certainty and possible publication bias. The reporting-bias domain is the part of the framework with no component-level input at all: funnel plots, comparison-adjusted funnel plots, Egger-type regressions, network selection models and ROB-ME all require a study-level effect estimate paired with its standard error for a single treatment contrast, while a component main effect is a linear functional of the whole design matrix that no single study estimates, so there is no effect-versus-precision pair to plot, regress or model. Applied component analyses therefore either omit the assessment entirely or borrow judgments made at the pairwise contrast level in contributing reviews and assume they transfer to the component coefficients, and what is needed is a definition of the small-study or selection-mechanism null at component level together with evidence on how selective publication of whole multicomponent interventions propagates through an additive design matrix into individual component effects.

title: No certainty-of-evidence framework rates component effects
text:
Why it is open
The unit a certainty framework rates has to be the unit the evidence attaches to, and for component models these differ: trials randomize regimens, the model reports components, and until recently there was no way even to say how much of a component estimate came from which comparison. That input has now arrived, since Yang et al. 2026 (doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02766-8) define pseudo-paths and a flow allocation that decompose a component effect into study-level contributions, but a contribution measure is not a rating rule and supplies only two of the six domains. Two domains resist transfer for structural reasons rather than for want of effort: incoherence has no loop analogue at the component level, because the additivity constraint replaces the loop as the testable restriction and cannot be tested at all in a disconnected network, and imprecision needs a clinically important range for a component increment, a quantity nobody elicits. Rating a combination is a further step, since it is a joint statement about several component effects plus the assumption that they add, and no rule composes component ratings into a rating for the package that would actually be delivered. Because component analyses are commissioned to say which parts of a complex intervention to fund, an unrated primary output is a decision-relevant hole rather than a documentation gap, and two reviews of the same evidence would grade it differently or not at all.

title: No certainty-of-evidence framework rates component effects
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
Defines CINeMA, the six-domain confidence framework for network meta-analysis, and keys the within-study-bias and indirectness judgments to the percentage contribution matrix. Every judgment is made for a treatment contrast; nothing in it is defined for a component effect or a component combination.


Brignardello-Petersen et al. 2018, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Advances the GRADE approach for rating certainty in every pairwise comparison of a network, including when the indirect estimate need not be rated and how incoherence is handled at the comparison level. All four advances are stated for a contrast.


Puhan et al. 2014, BMJ
The original GRADE working group approach to rating the quality of treatment effect estimates from a network meta-analysis, from which the contrast-level structure that component models cannot inherit derives.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, F1000Research
Derives the proportion contribution matrix that CINeMA uses to attribute study-level bias and indirectness to a network contrast. It is defined over direct comparisons, so it returns nothing usable for a component parameter.


Yang et al. 2026, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Extends the shortest-path contribution approach to component network meta-analysis through pseudo-paths and a flow-allocation algorithm, giving the first quantitative decomposition of a component effect into study contributions, with the flow-weighted sum reproducing the fitted component effect. Supplies an input a certainty framework needs, not the framework.


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
Defines additive and interaction component network meta-analysis and implements both in netmeta, so the estimand that needs a certainty rating is precisely specified even though no rating rule exists for it.


O’Malley et al. 2025, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (protocol CD016145)
States that at present there is very little guidance and no consensus on the preferred method for evaluating the certainty of component network meta-analysis evidence, and proceeds without one.


Hartmann-Boyce et al. 2021, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (CD013229.pub2)
Cochrane overview and network meta-analysis of behavioral smoking-cessation interventions using component models; states that consensus is still needed on how to manage, evaluate and present component analyses within Cochrane reviews, explicitly including methods for assessing certainty and possible publication bias.


Nunns et al. 2025, Journal of Medical Internet Research
systematic review with component network meta-analysis of digital weight-loss interventions; records that because of the nature of component network meta-analysis it was unable to test for the presence of publication bias, so the component estimates it reports carry no reporting-bias assessment


Hartmann-Boyce et al. 2022, Obesity
component network meta-analysis of behavioral weight management program characteristics; states that there is no way to test for publication bias in component network meta-analysis and that it cannot be ruled out, an independent statement of the same absence in one of the largest applied component analyses


Chaimani and Salanti 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
the comparison-adjusted funnel plot, the network-level small-study-effects diagnostic in routine use; it plots each study’s treatment-contrast effect against its precision after centering on the comparison-specific summary, so it requires a study-level estimate of a single contrast and has no component-level analogue


Mavridis et al. 2014, Statistics in Medicine
a selection model for publication bias across a full network, modeling the probability that a study is published as a function of its contrast-level effect and precision; the selection mechanism is parameterized on treatment comparisons, so there is no component-level version to fit


Page et al. 2023, BMJ (ROB-ME)
structured assessment of risk of bias due to missing evidence in a synthesis; operates on the synthesis of one treatment comparison and supplies no rule for judging missing evidence about an incremental component effect

title: No certainty-of-evidence framework rates component effects
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Start from what the contribution machinery now makes available: define a component-level analogue of the percentage contribution matrix from the pseudo-path decomposition, then key within-study bias and indirectness to it exactly as CINeMA does for contrasts. Replace the loop-based incoherence domain with an additivity domain that downgrades on the magnitude of the nested lack-of-fit statistic where additivity is testable, and applies a fixed downgrade where the network is disconnected and the assumption cannot be tested at all. Elicit clinically important ranges for component increments so imprecision has a referent, or state in the instrument that the domain is unratable and require that to appear in the summary of findings. Derive a composition rule that turns a set of component ratings plus the additivity judgment into a rating for a delivered combination, and require component reviews to publish a summary-of-findings table for the combinations they recommend. Test the resulting instrument for inter-rater reliability on the published component reviews that improvised their own ratings, which provide a ready comparison set with known disagreement.

The two supporting quotes are direct statements of absence by a Cochrane protocol and by a Cochrane overview that used component network meta-analysis, corroborated by five applied reviews that each improvised a bespoke rating or omitted one.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Statement
Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record: 78% of 117 oncology MAICs did not report the source of the individual patient data and 66% conducted no systematic review to select the compared trials (10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088), and outcome-model fitting results were adequately reported in 3 of 18 analyses that required a model (10.1002/jrsm.1653). Independent verification does not require public release, though: secure reviewer access to the protocol, inputs, code and environment would support replication, so the requirement is auditability rather than publication. Whether a public protocol or statistical analysis plan is required in most HTA settings was checked by no auditor and is not asserted here. Machine-readable provenance is partly demonstrated rather than absent: the component ML-NMR path in cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package that is not on CRAN, stores engine and package versions, a Stan-source hash, the seed, the integration count, assumptions and priors in the fit object, while no path in it records a git commit, a dependency lock, an extraction audit trail or a failed-model history.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Why it is open
Submission dossiers are confidential and prepared under commercial pressure, so a prespecified protocol would fix analytic choices before the results are known and remove flexibility that currently exists. Extraction of aggregate data from publications is manual and its audit trail is rarely retained, so the inputs cannot be verified independently even in principle. Reporting failed models exposes what was tried and rejected, which is precisely what a reviewer needs and a submitter would rather omit, and no agency asks for it. The provenance that software does capture is uneven within a single package, so a reader cannot rely on its being present.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Farinasso et al. 2025
Sources the data-provenance component with measured figures: 69% of 117 oncology MAICs used pseudo-IPD, 78% did not report the source of the IPD, and 66% conducted no systematic review to select trials.


Truong et al. 2023
Sources the claim that model specification is not reported in enough detail to be reproduced or checked: results of the model-fitting procedure were adequately reported in 3 of 18 analyses (16.7%).


cpaic (development package, audited at commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package on GitHub, confirmed by an auditor not to be on CRAN. Its component ML-NMR fit objects store engine and package versions, a Stan-source hash, the seed, the numerical-integration count, assumptions, priors and refit arguments, partially implementing a machine-readable manifest; its MAIC path does not retain target standard deviations, seed or successful-bootstrap counts, and no path records a git commit, dependency lock, extraction audit trail or failed-model history.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require what makes independent verification possible under confidentiality: reviewer access to the protocol or statistical analysis plan, a documented extraction audit trail, executable code with the environment, versions and seeds, and disclosure of prespecified or materially different model attempts, convergence failures and exclusion rules with counts. Treat the machine-readable manifest as a convenience rather than a prerequisite, since executable code plus a locked environment is the authoritative specification and a separate manifest can drift; where one is used, make it package-wide instead of confined to a single analysis path. Reserve independent replication for high-stakes submissions.

title: Published PAIC analyses cannot be reconstructed from the record

Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “ITC submissions are not reproducible or independently checkable” The title asserts submissions are not independently checkable, which the audit rejected as too absolute since secure reviewer access supports replication without public release.
The source said. “Decision-grade ITC submissions cannot be reproduced or independently verified: a public protocol or statistical analysis plan, a data provenance and extraction audit trail, code with package versions, commit hashes, seeds and a lock file, a machine-readable model manifest, disclosure of all failed models and excluded simulation replicates, and independent review or replication for high-stakes submissions are all absent from standard practice.”
What was wrong with it. The source said decision-grade ITC submissions cannot be reproduced or independently verified and that a machine-readable model manifest is absent from practice. GPT-5.6 Sol found the absolute framing wrong, since secure reviewer access supports replication without public release, and found a partial manifest already implemented in cpaic; the literature auditor could not verify the claim that a public protocol is not required in most HTA settings, so it has been dropped rather than repeated.
