title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text: CMU-01 Overstated Medium-high priority Promising

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text:
Statement
Multilevel network meta-regression integrates the individual-level model over each aggregate study’s covariate distribution, and that integration error is now quantified and separated from Markov chain Monte Carlo error rather than left unmanaged: multinma has checked it automatically since version 0.6.0 (2024-01-24), running half the chains at n_int and half at n_int/2 so an R-hat failure can be ascribed either to the sampler or to too few integration points, an algorithm formalized in Phillippo et al. (doi:10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169). What is not resolved is cost and coverage. For general likelihoods, and flexible survival models in particular, each aggregate-study individual carries its own integral, cumulative integration-error plots are unsupported there, and adaptive integration, calibrated variational approximation, GPU or parallel Stan, and likelihood emulation have never been evaluated for ML-NMR. No single reported summary covers sampler convergence, integration accuracy, hierarchical shrinkage, and population-specific predictive accuracy at once.

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text:
Why it is open
Cost is driven by likelihood and gradient evaluations rather than by the number of saved draws, and it grows with integration points, studies, covariates, and the flexibility of the outcome model, so analysts cut integration points and convert a visible runtime cost into an invisible bias in the likelihood. The premise that the aggregate-data likelihood never has a closed form is false for Gaussian identity-link models; the burden is real for the non-Gaussian and survival cases. The diagnostics that do exist are layer-specific: sampler checks interrogate the chains, int_check interrogates the grid, and neither speaks to hierarchical shrinkage or to whether population-specific predictions are accurate, so a reviewer must assemble several checks and no software assembles them. In cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, the integration diagnostic compares quasi-Monte Carlo prefixes against the same finite grid, is unavailable for survival, and does not quantify residual full-grid error or runtime.

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020, Multilevel network meta-regression for population-adjusted treatment comparisons, JRSS-A
defines ML-NMR with quasi-Monte Carlo integration, reports empirical integration-error rates of order N^-1 over the whole posterior, and reports runtime of around 5 minutes for the plaque psoriasis example


Phillippo et al. 2025, Multilevel network meta-regression for general likelihoods (arXiv:2401.12640), JRSS-A
gives the split-chain algorithm that separates numerical integration non-convergence from MCMC non-convergence when per-individual aggregate-data integrals make cumulative-error plots infeasible, and documents its implementation in multinma


multinma 0.6.0 release notes (2024-01-24), commit dmphillippo/multinma@6be4758
adds int_check, enabled by default, which runs half the chains at n_int and half at n_int/2 and ascribes R-hat or ESS warnings to either sampler non-convergence or insufficient integration accuracy; lowers the default to 64 points and stops saving cumulative integration points by default


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commit 9d150e9
implements a quasi-Monte Carlo stability plot (estimate at the first N points minus the estimate at all points) for non-survival models and automatic checks of divergences, tree depth, E-BFMI, R-hat and ESS across every sampled parameter block

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The integration-error diagnostic exists, so the work is to lower the cost it prices and to widen the checks it does not cover. Benchmark adaptive integration, calibrated variational approximation, GPU and parallel Stan backends, and likelihood emulation against exact ML-NMR fits, since none has been evaluated in this setting. Extend cumulative integration-error reporting to general likelihoods and survival models, where it is currently unsupported, and report runtime next to residual integration error so the trade-off is made knowingly. Add hierarchical cross-validation and level-specific PSIS diagnostics for the shrinkage and population-prediction layers that no current check reaches.

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 3 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. For flexible survival ML-NMR with one integral per aggregate-study individual, runtime is a real burden and methods to reduce it (adaptive integration, calibrated variational approximation, GPU/parallel Stan, emulation) have not been evaluated; and no single reported summary simultaneously covers sampler convergence, integration accuracy, hierarchical shrinkage, and population-specific prediction accuracy.
The source titled this. “ML-NMR integration cost and integration error are unquantified” The title says integration error is unquantified, but multinma has separated integration error from Monte Carlo error by default since version 0.6.0.
The source said. “Fitting multilevel network meta-regression requires numerical integration of the individual-level model over the covariate distribution of every aggregate study, which makes the model expensive and introduces an integration error that is distinct from Monte Carlo sampling error. Neither the runtime nor the integration error is routinely managed or quantified, and no single diagnostic covers the several layers on which such a fit can go wrong.”
What was wrong with it. The source said integration error is neither routinely managed nor quantified nor separable from Monte Carlo error. All three auditors found that outdated: multinma has made exactly that separation by default since 0.6.0 (2024-01-24, the int_check argument), and Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579) already reported empirical integration-error rates over the whole posterior and a runtime of about 5 minutes for its worked example.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Phillippo et al. 2020 (Europe PMC PMC7362893) and the general-likelihoods ML-NMR preprint PDF (arXiv 2401.12640, now JRSS-A 10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169). Both contradict the framing. The 2020 paper states the QMC error rate, demonstrates empirical integration error over the whole posterior, and reports runtime (‘around 5 min’; ‘not markedly increased over an equivalent full IPD network meta-regression’). The general-likelihoods paper has a dedicated section 2.3 ‘Assessing integration error’ giving an algorithm that splits chains across n_int and n_int/2 and uses R-hat to separate MCMC non-convergence from integration non-convergence, and states multinma implements it. multinma NEWS 0.6.0 (2024-01-24) confirms this is on by default via int_check, and plot_integration_error() exists (test-plot_integration_error.R in the repo). So integration error is quantified, separated from MC error, and automated. Genuinely open: runtime reduction (adaptive integration, calibrated variational approximation, GPU/parallel Stan, emulation) for which I found no ML-NMR evaluation, and coverage of hierarchical shrinkage and population-specific prediction in one diagnostic. Cites arxiv:2401.12640: Provides an operational diagnostic that separates numerical integration error from MCMC error and is implemented by default in multinma; also published as JRSS-A doi 10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169.. Cites cran:multinma NEWS 0.6.0 (2024-01-24): Integration-accuracy checking is automatic and enabled by default, and attributes warnings to either sampler non-convergence or insufficient integration accuracy..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is correct subject to identification, correct model specification, and adequate AgD covariate distributions. C2 is conditional: integrating an individual-level model avoids the usual aggregate plug-in bias, but AgD-only interaction information can remain ecological. C3 inflates severity because identification and transportability may be more fundamental than computation. C4-C6 are correct for non-Gaussian and flexible survival paths. C5 correctly distinguishes error in the approximated posterior target from MCMC error conditional on that target. C7 is defensible only as saying no single scalar validates every layer; a dashboard can summarize multiple diagnostics. C8 is plausible but workload-dependent. The universal no-closed-form premise is false for Gaussian identity models and some analytic moments, and cost scales with likelihood and gradient evaluations rather than saved draws. At 9d150e9, cpaic already exposes integration and sampler diagnostics. Its integration plot compares QMC prefixes with the same finite full grid at fixed posterior draws, is unavailable for survival, and does not quantify residual full-grid posterior error or runtime. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Provides an implemented diagnostic for stability as the number of Sobol integration points increases, partially resolving the claim that integration accuracy is wholly unmanaged.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Automatically checks and stores several major sampler diagnostics across all sampled parameter blocks..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The core claim that ML-NMR integration error is neither managed nor separable from MCMC error is outdated for the multinma implementation path. Since multinma 0.6.0 (CRAN 2024-01-24), default int_check runs half the chains at n_int and half at n_int/2 and ascribes R-hat/ESS failures either to MCMC non-convergence or to insufficient integration points; plot_integration_error already existed for cumulative QMC error. Phillippo (2025/2026 JRSSA general-likelihoods paper, section 3.3) formalizes this split-R-hat algorithm, notes the older cumulative-error plots become untenable for per-individual AgD integrals, defaults n_int=64, and documents multinma warnings when N-tilde is insufficient. Claims that ML-NMR yields population-specific effects and avoids ecological bias remain faithful to Phillippo et al. 2020. What remains open is not basic integration-error diagnostics but: (i) a single review-facing summary that also covers hierarchical shrinkage and population-specific predictive accuracy; (ii) adaptive integration, variational approximations with calibration, GPU/parallel Stan, likelihood emulation, and sparse designs as routine cost reducers; (iii) survival models, where cumulative integration points are not saved and plot_integration_error is unsupported. Searches of arXiv/medRxiv and multinma NEWS through 2026 found no shipped adaptive/VI/GPU ML-NMR solver. Cites dmphillippo/multinma@6be475898729f1ccdf88e275c99bbd1f9a143e81: Ships default automatic separation of integration insufficiency from MCMC non-convergence via split n_int vs n_int/2 chains and R-hat/ESS warnings; lowers default n_int to 64; disables cumulative integration saving by default.. Cites doi:10.1093/jrsssa/qnaf169: Formalizes assessing integration error with a split-chain R-hat algorithm when per-individual AgD integrals make cumulative-error plots infeasible; documents multinma implementation.. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Defines ML-NMR as hierarchical IPD+AgD synthesis with QMC integration; earlier source for empirical integration-error plots and for C1–C2 method claims..

title: ML-NMR integration cost is unaddressed for flexible survival models
section: How the evidence falls in time
text:
How the evidence falls in time
2 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2020 to 2024. The most recent paper to touch this reports progress on it, and every paper calling it open is older.
Does the later work answer the earlier work? Put to an independent reviewer with the older and newer claims side by side, it judged that the later work answers a component of it, leaving a named part (high confidence). The later survival-model case study directly quantifies fitting time, memory use, integration-point sufficiency, and a memory-saving diagnostic strategy. It is a case-study solution to an important portion of the computational-cost question, but does not settle general scalable or accuracy-and-coverage methodology. What remains: Evaluations of adaptive integration, calibrated approximation or emulation approaches, scalable computation, coverage, and a unified diagnostic for sampler convergence, integration accuracy, shrinkage, and population-specific prediction.

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text: CMP-34 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text:
Statement
The component design matrix is fixed by discretionary coding decisions taken before any model is fitted. Graded features such as dose, session length, contact frequency and program duration are forced into binary indicators, sparse components are merged into related ones, and components present in nearly every arm are dropped because they generate no contrast. Every dropped or merged component remains part of the interventions actually delivered, so its effect is absorbed into the reference arm or into the retained coefficients, which then answer a different question from the one the report states. The reductions are large and documented: the BE:COME program reduced its expert-selected component list to 11 component areas by excluding anything ambiguous, unsuitable for a dichotomy or showing too little variation between programs, dropping frequency of weight monitoring outright because every intervention arm monitored weight, and then reduced those 11 to 7 on an identifiability screen, so that pre-assessment, multidisciplinary delivery, program duration and personalized physical activity advice left the model while remaining in every delivered program; an earlier component review of psychological preparation for surgery collapsed a seventh category, hypnosis, into relaxation because too few trials used it, and reported no analysis of what the merged coefficient then estimates. No rule, sensitivity analysis or reporting convention governs these decisions, and no published component network meta-analysis reports how its conclusions would change under a different coding. What is missing is both a statement of the estimand a component coefficient targets under a given coding and a procedure for propagating the coding choice into the reported intervals.

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text:
Why it is open
The choices are made before any model is fitted, so no model can price them: the likelihood conditions on the design matrix and the discarded alternatives never enter it, and propagating them requires refitting over a space of codings that somebody must first enumerate and that nobody has defined. Two requirements conflict. A coding fine enough to preserve what was delivered makes the design rank-deficient or weakly identified, and a coding coarse enough to be estimable changes the estimand, so the identifiability screens that force the coarsening are doing their job and the resulting shift has nowhere to be recorded. The estimand itself is unstated: what a component coefficient means when the reference arm silently contains the dropped content has not been written down, so there is no target for a sensitivity analysis to be a sensitivity about. Dichotomization of graded predictors is long known to be harmful in ordinary regression, but here it is not a nuisance-variable issue, because the dichotomized quantity is the estimand.

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Gregg et al. 2026, Health Technology Assessment (BE:COME)
documents the component selection process for a behavioral weight management component network meta-analysis, excluding components that were ambiguous, unsuitable for a dichotomy or insufficiently variable, and records the exclusion reasons component by component


Jaiswal et al. 2025, Health Technology Assessment
the component analysis built on that selection; reduces the 11 shortlisted components to 7 on identifiability grounds, dropping pre-assessment, multidisciplinary delivery, program duration and personalized physical activity advice, with no sensitivity analysis over the retained coding


Freeman et al. 2018, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
component network meta-analysis of psychological preparation for surgery that collapsed the Cochrane review’s seventh component, hypnosis, into relaxation because of the low number of trials including it; the merge is stated but its effect on what the relaxation coefficient estimates is not analyzed


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
defines the treatment-by-component matrix as an analyst-supplied input to the model; the coding enters as data and is never estimated, so nothing in the fit records its arbitrariness


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
supplies the estimability screening that forces components and interactions out of the model, the mechanism that converts an identifiability problem into an unrecorded estimand change


Michie et al. 2013, Annals of Behavioral Medicine
the Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy v1 of 93 hierarchically clustered techniques, a standard vocabulary in which a candidate component list and its reduction could be expressed and versioned


Hoffmann et al. 2014, BMJ (TIDieR)
requires interventions to be described in enough detail to replicate them, including materials, procedures, provider, mode, intensity and tailoring; the reporting precedent a component coding standard would extend to the synthesis stage


Royston, Altman and Sauerbrei 2006, Statistics in Medicine
documents the cost of dichotomizing continuous predictors in regression, including loss of information and cut-point dependence; the general result whose component-model analogue has not been quantified

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text:
Probable solution or research direction
State the estimand explicitly: define the component coefficient as a contrast between two regimens that differ in the coded component and agree on the rest of the coded design, with the uncoded content left as it was in the contributing arms, and require the report to name the content absorbed into the reference. Make the coding a versioned, published object: the full candidate component list, the rule applied to each one, retained, dichotomized at a stated cut, merged into which component, or dropped for which reason, and the identifiability verdict that forced any reduction, expressed in an existing intervention ontology and intervention-reporting vocabulary. Run the coding multiverse: refit over a prespecified set of alternative codings, different cuts for graded components, alternative merges, and restoration of near-universal components as a shared term, and report the range of each component effect and of the resulting hierarchy, as analytic multiverses are already reported for evidence-set assembly. Quantify the cost by simulation: generate data with graded component effects, code them under the rules seen in practice, and report the bias in the retained coefficients as a function of the dose spread within a component and the prevalence of the dropped ones.

title: No sensitivity or reporting standard for discretionary component coding
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted it as a genuine estimand problem, distinct from ontology availability, component misclassification and post hoc interaction selection, while noting that its universal claims would ultimately need a broader review of component network meta-analysis practice; the evidence is one detailed applied program plus a second component review that merged a component for sparsity.

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text: CMP-32 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text:
Statement
Designing evidence for a component network requires knowing how much information a planned set of trials will supply about a component main effect or a component-by-component interaction, and how to allocate units across combination arms to obtain it. For a component design formed as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, the information about a component contrast depends on which combinations are randomized, in what proportions, with how many units, and on the between-study heterogeneity; it is not a function of total sample size. No published procedure computes the power or expected precision of a component contrast under a planned design, and none allocates units across combination arms so that a specified set of component main effects and interactions is estimable at a target precision. Groups now assembling component evidence prospectively design around the gap: a collaborative network trial of ten randomized implementation trials sized each trial for its own two-group logistic comparison and recorded that no established sample-size method exists for component network meta-analysis, even though the pooled component model with strategy-covariate interactions is the point of the collaboration. The two adjacent literatures each solve a different problem. Network meta-analysis design frameworks size and configure a new trial against an existing network in terms of treatment-level comparisons and say nothing about which combination arms make a component contrast estimable, while the component-side machinery, row-space screening and leave-one-comparison-out identifiability, is diagnostic on a design that already exists rather than prospective.

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text:
Why it is open
The design question is combinatorial rather than scalar. The decision variable is a subset of the possible combination arms together with their allocations, and the objective is a function of the whole information matrix over several component contrasts at once, so this is a constrained optimal-design problem; nobody has written down the criterion, let alone solved it under feasibility constraints. The variance of a component contrast also depends on the between-study heterogeneity of a network that does not yet exist, so a planning input must be assumed; that is true of network design generally but bites harder here because heterogeneity and component structure enter through the same design matrix. Prospective component evidence is new: master protocols, collaborative network trials and multiphase optimization designs have only recently begun to be assembled around a pooled component model, so until now there was no consumer for the method. Factorial trial design solves the single-trial version but not the network version, in which combinations are spread across trials that differ in population and background care and the pooled analysis borrows across them.

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Barnes et al. 2024, Frontiers in Public Health
protocol for a collaborative network trial of ten randomized implementation trials feeding a pooled component analysis; states that there are no established methods for sample size calculations for component network meta-analysis, and sizes each trial for its own pairwise contrast instead


Salanti et al. 2018, Trials
conditional trial design: plans a future randomized trial against an existing network so that the updated network reaches a target precision or conclusiveness; expressed in treatment-level comparisons with no component structure


Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis and Salanti 2016, Statistics in Medicine
plans future studies from the precision of network meta-analysis results, giving the network covariance machinery a component design method would reuse, again at treatment-contrast level


Hu, Wang and Ye 2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology
optimizes the power and sample allocation of a subsequent trial using information from an existing network meta-analysis; optimizes allocation across treatment arms of one new trial rather than across combination arms of a planned component network


Ye 2023, OssaNMA (CRAN)
implements optimal sample size and allocation with a network meta-analysis, the closest available tooling; it has no component design matrix and no component contrast target


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
gives the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, from which the information matrix a prospective design method needs is directly available


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
screens inestimable interactions in an existing component design and simulates connected and disconnected networks; diagnostic rather than prospective, and its scenario generator is the natural validation bed for a design method

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text:
Probable solution or research direction
State the problem as optimal design: given a candidate set of combination arms with allocations and an assumed heterogeneity and outcome model, compute the covariance of the fitted component contrasts from the component information matrix, then optimize the allocation under a c-optimality criterion targeting the specified component contrasts, with the row-space screen as a hard feasibility constraint and trial-level practicality as a side constraint. Deliver the power calculation first, because that is what trialists are blocked on: for a planned network, return the power to detect a specified component main effect or interaction at a stated heterogeneity. Build it by extending existing network planning tools rather than starting over, since conditional trial design and the methods for sizing a subsequent trial against a network already carry the network covariance; the change is to replace the treatment-contrast target with a component contrast through the combination matrix. Validate by simulation on the published component network scenario designs, reporting achieved power and estimability against the planned values.

title: No sample-size or allocation method for component NMA
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it from a single source, which is a weaker basis, but that source is a trial protocol whose authors state plainly that no established sample-size methods exist for component network meta-analysis and who therefore sized ten trials for pairwise contrasts; the reviewer accepted it, noting that factorial and treatment-level network planning methods address pieces of the problem without optimizing a planned network of combination arms for specified component contrasts.

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text: CMP-30 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text:
Statement
The additivity equation for a multicomponent treatment holds relative to exactly one treatment, the anchor, and Wigle and Beliveau 2022 prove that additivity cannot hold for two distinct anchors at once, so different anchors define different models rather than different parameterizations of one model. The anchor is a separate object from the reference treatment: changing the reference is a reparameterization that consistency makes harmless, whereas changing the anchor changes which vector of true relative effects the model asserts, and therefore changes the mechanism the model is fitting. Existing methods choose it in one of two ways and neither is examined in application. The Welton-type Bayesian additive model is anchored, fixing the anchor to the modeler’s chosen first treatment; the frequentist netmeta model is unanchored, its weighted least squares fit with a Moore-Penrose inverse selecting whichever anchor fits the data best, an anchor that need not be a treatment in the network and may be zero. Under a misspecified anchor the measured consequences are severe: bias did not shrink with sample size, coverage of several relative effects fell well below nominal and decreased as the per-arm sample size rose from 50 to 500, reaching zero for one contrast, and average SUCRA values put the wrong treatment ahead. The diagnostic that would catch it does not exist: in one of the two simulated networks the DIC failed to prefer the unanchored model over a misspecified anchored one in any scenario, and because no frequentist anchored component model has been developed, no likelihood-ratio test of a specified anchor is available either.

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text:
Why it is open
Candidate anchors index non-nested models that agree over most of the network and differ only on the multicomponent arms, which are the sparsest cells, so a global fit criterion averages the discriminating information away; that is the structural reason DIC fails rather than an artifact of one simulation. Clinical knowledge does not settle the choice either, because the anchor is a claim about the scale on which component effects add, not about which treatment is inactive, so an analyst has no basis for the confidence that the anchored model requires. The unanchored route sidesteps the problem by estimating the anchor, but it spends a parameter to do so and has not been studied in the disconnected and sparse networks where component models are most used and where the estimated anchor may itself be weakly identified. The distinction is recent and was expressly overlooked in the literature before 2022, so there has been little time and little awareness; the standing recommendation is still to use an anchored model when the modeler is confident in the anchor, with no procedure offered for becoming confident.

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wigle and Beliveau 2022, Statistics in Medicine
introduces the anchor treatment, proves in its appendix that additivity can hold for only one anchor at a time, classifies existing component models as anchored or unanchored, proposes two Bayesian unanchored models, and measures the bias, coverage and ranking failures of a misspecified anchor and the failure of DIC to detect it; states that methods to assess the chosen anchor are needed


Welton et al. 2009, American Journal of Epidemiology
the original additive component model for complex interventions, in which the anchor is fixed to the modeler’s chosen reference treatment by construction and is never tested


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
frequentist component network meta-analysis in netmeta; the weighted least squares fit with a Moore-Penrose inverse estimates the anchor implicitly, and supplies a likelihood-ratio test of the additive model against the standard network model but none of the anchor


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
evaluates component model selection in 1000 simulated connected and disconnected networks; the selection cascade operates over interaction structures and contains no step that examines or varies the anchor


Balduzzi et al. 2023, Journal of Statistical Software
documents the netmeta component workflow that applied reviews use, including the inactive-treatment declaration analysts make; no anchor sensitivity or anchor test is exposed


Wigle et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.15142
builds treatment and component hierarchies from component models and characterizes which hierarchy questions are estimable; the hierarchies inherit whatever anchor the underlying model asserts, which is the output that anchor misspecification was shown to corrupt

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Characterize the observable implications that separate two anchors: for a given network, identify the set of contrasts on which anchored models with different anchors make different predictions, and build a score or likelihood-ratio test from those contrasts alone rather than from a global fit criterion. That test needs a frequentist anchored component model, which does not exist and is a well-posed first deliverable. In the Bayesian route, either place a prior over candidate anchors and report the posterior over them, or fit the unanchored model and report the posterior of the implied anchor with a prior-sensitivity check, so an unstated modeling choice becomes a reported quantity. Until a test exists, make anchor sensitivity routine: refit under every plausible anchor and report the range of each target contrast and of the resulting hierarchy, which existing software makes cheap. Extend the published simulation to disconnected networks and to networks with few multicomponent arms, reporting bias, coverage and rank recovery for the estimated anchor as well as for the effects.

title: No diagnostic for anchor choice in additive component models
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it from a single source, which is a weaker basis, but that source is a methods paper containing a proof that additivity holds for only one anchor and a simulation quantifying the cost of choosing wrongly; the reviewer accepted that the anchor is a substantive identifying restriction rather than a harmless reference choice, and the source’s own discussion states that a method to test the suitability of a chosen anchor is needed and that no frequentist test is available.

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text: CMP-28 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text:
Statement
Component network meta-analysis codes each treatment as a binary incidence vector over components, so two regimens containing the same component at different doses, intensities, session counts or program durations receive identical rows of the combination matrix and their difference is absorbed into heterogeneity or into an interaction term. The frequentist component line and the dose-response line have remained separate in practice: a 2026 frequentist dose-response network meta-analysis had to exclude 80 multicomponent studies from a 282-trial Cochrane network because the two structures cannot presently be combined, and names the joint model as future work. One implementation now exists. cdtmbnma, released on CRAN in July 2026 in a single version, fits Bayesian component model-based network meta-analysis with explicit component dose-response and dose-dependent interaction surfaces, additive, bilinear or saturating pairwise interactions, and prediction at unobserved dose combinations, for arm-level continuous and binary outcomes. It is an unreviewed package with no methods paper of its own, no frequentist counterpart, no population-adjusted or survival route, and no identification results: nothing states when a dose-indexed component contrast is estimable, and the row-space screens in use are defined for a binary component design. The gap bites hardest in the disconnected case that motivates component models, where a shared component is the only bridge across the gap and is delivered at different doses on each side, so the additive bridge identifies the cross-gap contrast only under an unstated dose-invariance assumption that no current screen tests or records.

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text:
Why it is open
A dose-indexed component model changes what estimability means. The design is no longer a binary incidence matrix whose row space settles the question, and the analogue for a component-by-dose design with a nonlinear shape per component has not been derived for any outcome family. Fitting a shape per component also multiplies the parameter count on networks that are already sparse, which pushes the model into the weak-identification regime, and nobody has characterized when such a model is identified at all rather than rescued by a prior. The covariate the model needs is frequently missing from the reports: dose, session count and contact time are extracted from heterogeneous intervention descriptions with no standard vocabulary, so an applied component review often cannot populate a dose column even where the estimator exists. The two machineries were also developed as alternative bridge families rather than as a joint structure, in the same package family but with no shared interface, so until 2026 there was no implementation to test any theory against.

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou, Rucker and Schwarzer 2026, BMC Medical Research Methodology
frequentist dose-response network meta-analysis; excludes 80 multicomponent studies and 3 studies lacking dose data from a 282-trial network because components and dose levels cannot presently be modeled jointly, and names the joint component and dose-response model as future work


Pitre 2026, cdtmbnma 0.2.1 (CRAN, published 2026-07-22)
Bayesian component model-based network meta-analysis with component dose-response and dose-dependent interaction surfaces, study-level random effects and prediction at unobserved dose combinations, for arm-level continuous and binary outcomes; a single-author package with no accompanying methods paper, no estimability screen and no simulation evidence


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
formalizes component network meta-analysis as the product of the comparison design matrix and the binary treatment-by-component matrix, the coding that makes dose invisible


Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2025, netdose (CRAN)
frequentist dose-response network meta-analysis in the same package family as netmeta, with no component design matrix and no interface to one


Mawdsley et al. 2016, CPT: Pharmacometrics and Systems Pharmacology
model-based network meta-analysis placing parametric dose-response functions on treatment effects; supplies the dose-response half of the joint model at treatment rather than component level


Pedder et al. 2019, Research Synthesis Methods
model-based network meta-analysis of time-course relationships across multiple treatments; the closest existing precedent for placing a parametric shape on an effect inside a network

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Derive estimability conditions for a component-by-dose design: state the analogue of the row-space condition for a specified shape family, linear, exponential, Emax or restricted cubic spline, by outcome family, and give the conditions under which a cross-subnetwork contrast is identified when the bridging component is observed at different doses on each side of the gap. Add a component-by-dose design option to the frequentist component workflow so the estimator exists outside one Bayesian package, and benchmark the two against a simulation in which the true component effect is dose-dependent, scoring the bias that binary coding induces as a function of the dose spread within each coded component. Require applied component reviews to report the distribution of dose, intensity and duration within every coded component, which makes the dose-invariance assumption that binary coding imposes visible even where the joint model cannot be fitted.

title: Component NMA has no dose-response dimension
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed it from a single methods source whose authors excluded multicomponent studies and named the joint model as future work, and the reviewer accepted it as a real methods gap; it is recorded as partially addressed because a Bayesian component dose-response implementation reached CRAN in July 2026, while the identification conditions, the frequentist and population-adjusted routes, and any empirical evaluation remain absent.

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text: CMP-26 Partially addressed Very high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Statement
cpaic is an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, and its evidence base is a local, gitignored factorial simulation over synthetic examples whose summaries omit Monte Carlo standard errors, with no real full-IPD benchmark in the repository and no evidence of independent replication. The repository is not bare: it contains tracked analytic, adversarial, and recovery unit tests and a continuous integration workflow that checks agreement between its two Stan backends. The report’s ten-item minimum validation standard is internally consistent as a list, but several items restate the established ADEMP standard for simulation studies rather than being bespoke requirements, and a public factorial CNMA simulation benchmark already exists for the non-adjusted case.

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Why it is open
Synthetic data generated from the model family the estimator assumes can confirm that the code implements the model, not that the model recovers truth under realistic violations, and when the author of the theory writes the only implementation, agreement between theory and program is guaranteed rather than informative. Without committed generators, scenario manifests, seeds, raw outputs, and Monte Carlo standard errors, a reported operating characteristic cannot be checked, rerun, or extended by anyone else. Several validation items require resources the author cannot unilaterally obtain, including full-IPD gold standards, connected empirical networks suitable for bridge deletion, and independent replication, and adversarial scenario design is itself an open task because it requires knowing which violations matter most, which is what the validation is supposed to reveal.

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Morris, White and Crowther 2019
codifies the ADEMP standard for planning and reporting simulation studies, including predeclared estimands, data-generating mechanisms, comparison methods, performance measures, and Monte Carlo error


Petropoulou et al. 2023
provides a public factorial CNMA simulation benchmark with disconnection-construction scripts for connected and disconnected networks, though not for population-adjusted component models


netmeta
provides the frequentist component NMA engine cpaic depends on


maicplus
provides the weighting engine cpaic depends on


cmdstanr
optional Stan backend; the Stan models are implemented inside cpaic and fitted with rstan by default, so cmdstanr is not the Bayesian engine

title: Unreleased cpaic has no tracked simulation benchmark or replication
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Move the existing local factorial simulation into a public version-controlled repository under continuous integration, with generators, manifests, seeds, and raw outputs, and report Monte Carlo standard errors with predeclared estimands, following the ADEMP structure rather than presenting these as bespoke requirements. Validate against full-IPD gold standards and by empirical bridge deletion in connected networks, and obtain independent review and replication, treating the ten items as a strong evidence agenda rather than as individually non-waivable preconditions, since equivalent analytic or external validation can sometimes substitute.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text: CMP-24 Partially addressed Medium priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Statement
edge_influence() in cpaic, an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, asks whether a given IPD edge contributes to a requested target contrast. Its diagonal-weight calculation is exact for two-arm common-effect models with fixed weights and approximate for multi-arm studies, because the underlying frequentist CNMA fit uses within-study covariance; under random effects the fitted tau-squared is included in the weights, so the residual approximation comes from not re-estimating tau under perturbation rather than from ignoring shrinkage. Exact contribution machinery already exists for CNMA component effects and for study importance in NMA; what those do not cover is contribution to a target-specific, population-adjusted cross-gap contrast.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Why it is open
The approximation drops the correlation structure introduced by multi-arm trials and the re-estimation of heterogeneity under perturbation, both of which redistribute information across edges in ways a first-order calculation misses, and either can change an influence ranking. The diagnostic matters precisely because it exposes edges with excellent effective sample size that nonetheless carry no weight for the cross-gap contrast, a question standard MAIC overlap and weight diagnostics cannot answer, so an incorrect ranking undermines the one tool that answers it. The published exact decompositions operate on component effects in an unadjusted CNMA, not on a target-specific population-adjusted contrast, so they cannot simply be called.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Yang et al. 2026
gives an exact decomposition of which studies and comparisons contribute to each component effect in CNMA using pseudo-paths and the component-level hat matrix; does not cover population-adjusted target-specific contrasts


Rucker et al. 2020, study importance
defines an exact, uniquely defined per-study influence measure for a specified NMA estimate as the reduction in that estimate’s variance when the study is added, for one-stage and two-stage models


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018
establishes the flow-network proportion-contribution matrix showing how much each direct treatment effect contributes to each NMA estimate


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; provides edge_influence() to test whether an IPD edge contributes to a requested target contrast, using inverse-variance weights that include the fitted tau-squared and are approximate for multi-arm studies

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing exact contribution machinery, the flow and pseudo-path decomposition for component effects and the variance-reduction definition of study importance, to a target-specific population-adjusted contrast, rather than deriving a new influence measure from scratch. Where an exact extension is not available, compute influence from the model Jacobian and Hessian or by posterior perturbation of the observed edge, including re-estimation of heterogeneity. Report the approximation status alongside each ranking, since the diagnostic is already exact in the two-arm common-effect case.

title: Edge influence is approximate for multi-arm and random effects
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “cpaic’s edge_influence() diagnostic asks whether a given IPD edge actually contributes to the requested target contrast, but its computation is approximate in multi-arm and random-effects settings, so influence rankings may not match exact fitted influence.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated edge influence as a novel diagnostic with no prior art and said random-effects shrinkage is ignored. The literature auditor found three established exact methods, including a component-level decomposition whose flow-weighted sum matches the CNMA component estimate within numerical tolerance (doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02766-8; doi:10.1186/s12874-020-01075-y; doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3); GPT-5.6 Sol found that the implementation does include the fitted tau-squared in its weights and is exact for two-arm common-effect models.
Dissent. codex dissented (open): C1 and C2 are correct with qualification. The source explicitly describes the diagonal-W calculation as approximate for multi-arm studies because discomb() uses within-study covariance. For two-arm common-effect models with W fixed, the displayed linear influence is exact. Under random effects, cpaic does include the fitted tau-squared in W; remaining approximation arises if exact perturbation influence is defined to include re-estimation of tau, not because random-effects weighting is ignored. Such omissions can change rankings. C3 is algebraically possible and is demonstrated by the package tests: ESS measures within-edge weight dispersion, whereas target influence is a network-design leverage quantity and can be zero. C4 is correct because ordinary MAIC overlap and weight diagnostics do not evaluate downstream leverage for a requested cross-gap contrast. This is a useful diagnostic refinement, but not a defect in the fitted estimator itself.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The claim ‘Standard MAIC diagnostics do not answer whether an adjusted edge contributes to the requested target contrast’ is correct - effective sample size says nothing about network position. But the entry treats edge influence as a novel diagnostic and cites no prior art, and there is a lot. title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text: CMP-22 Partially addressed High priority Emerging

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Statement
IPD availability may be informative rather than random, and the premise has empirical support: a survey of 31 IPD meta-analyses found that 16 (52 percent) did not obtain all the individual participant data requested, five of those did not mention it as a limitation, and only six examined how the trials without IPD might affect conclusions. Component PAIC conditions on the supplied IPD and provides neither a selection model for availability nor grouped leave-IPD-out validation. Nonrandomness has to be demonstrated or posited as a sensitivity assumption rather than assumed categorically: availability can be modeled where it depends on observed trial-level variables, and only selection on unobserved IPD quantities is unidentified without additional data or assumptions.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Why it is open
The IPD edges are the ones that get population-adjusted and the ones that inform interaction parameters, so a selection mechanism on availability propagates into which parts of covariate space are informed by causal evidence rather than by aggregate association. Selection depending on unobserved IPD characteristics cannot be estimated from within the network, because the trials with unobserved IPD are precisely the ones that would identify it. Federated approaches or a full selection model require access or assumptions that are currently unavailable, and no leave-IPD-out facility exists in component PAIC software to at least measure the dependence.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ahmed, Sutton and Riley 2012
surveys 31 IPD meta-analyses and documents that most did not obtain all requested individual participant data and few assessed the impact, establishing that IPD availability is not random


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; conditions on the supplied IPD studies without modeling why IPD are available, and provides observation-level leave-one-out only, with no grouped leave-IPD-out facility

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Implement grouped leave-IPD-out validation first, since it measures how conclusions depend on which trials contributed individual data even though it does not identify or correct the mechanism. Model availability where it depends on observed trial-level characteristics, and treat selection on unobserved characteristics as an explicit sensitivity assumption with a stated selection model rather than as an unmodeled default. Pursue federated methods that let non-sponsor trials contribute individual-level information without releasing data, which is the only route that addresses the cause rather than the symptom.

title: IPD availability may be informative rather than random
text:
Our study

Which trials supply individual data, and what selection on it does
The question put to it. When the trials that supply individual data are selected on observed trial variables or on their own effect modification, how biased is the interaction evidence, does combining with aggregate trials help, and can a leave-IPD-out diagnostic reveal it?
What it found. Selection of which trials supply individual data on an observed trial variable caused no bias, but selection on the trials’ own effect modification biased the within-trial interaction evidence by up to 0.14 (true 0.3), with coverage down to 0.59. Combining with the across-trial association in all trials halved the bias. A leave-IPD-out influence diagnostic did not respond to the selection, so the problem is invisible without a stated selection model.
Results.

Selection on the observed trial variable only: within-trial bias -0.003 to 0.003.
Selection on the latent interaction: within-trial bias 0.027 to 0.142; combined 0.014 to 0.065.
Leave-IPD-out influence 0.026 to 0.046, varying with the IPD share but not with selection strength (correlation with bias -0.85 at half the trials supplying data).

Design.

Estimand

Mean treatment-by-covariate interaction and the effect at covariate 1

Methods compared

pooled within-trial interaction from IPD trials, combined within-trial and across-trial estimator, leave-IPD-out influence diagnostic

Data-generating mechanism

Twelve trials with trial-specific interactions and IPD availability depending on an observed trial variable and on the latent interaction; within-trial and combined estimators; leave-IPD-out influence. 18 cells, 1000 replicates each.

Replicates

1000 per scenario, 18,000 in total


What this does not answer. Pairwise continuous-outcome meta-analysis rather than component ML-NMR; no selection-model sensitivity analysis; one network size. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text: CMP-20 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Statement
For an aggregate Poisson arm, component ML-NMR multiplies total exposure by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If unweighted participant moments are supplied, that is exact only when exposure has zero covariance with the modeled individual rate; full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary, and treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is already absorbed by each arm’s own total exposure. The problem is within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates, which is what differential follow-up by prognosis produces, and publications almost never report exposure-weighted covariate summaries. This is a property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood rather than of any one package: multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Why it is open
The integration over the aggregate covariate distribution uses reported unweighted moments while the Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, and sicker patients typically contribute less follow-up, which is exactly the association that breaks the zero-covariance requirement. The correct input, exposure-weighted covariate summaries, is essentially never published, and the current interface neither labels which weighting a supplied moment set represents nor models the weighting itself. There is no diagnostic that tells an analyst whether the omitted covariance is material for their contrast.

text:
Probable solution or research direction
Label the weighting convention in the interface, so an analyst who can obtain exposure-weighted covariate moments can supply them and make the existing likelihood correct, and request those summaries from data holders as a reporting item. Where only unweighted moments exist, model exposure and covariates jointly so the person-time weighting is generated by the model rather than assumed away. Add a sensitivity calculation for the magnitude of the exposure-rate covariance that would move a target contrast, since the severity is entirely conditional on that quantity.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Our study






NoteA study is running



Question. The aggregate Poisson likelihood multiplies an arm’s total exposure by its mean modeled rate, which is exact only when exposure and rate are uncorrelated. The error is the factor 1 + rho CV(T) CV(lambda) per arm. How much bias does that put on a transported rate ratio at plausible levels of differential follow-up, and do exposure-weighted covariate summaries remove it?
Design. A minimal anchored network, individual data on A versus C and arm totals on B versus C, with lognormal exposure solved so each arm’s exposure-rate correlation and dispersions take registered values exactly. 234 attainable cells crossing the control-arm correlation, its difference in the treated arm, CV of exposure, CV of the rate and arm size; unweighted, exposure-weighted and borrowed-slope integration and a sensitivity bound. 1000 replicates per cell.
The protocol is registered before any result is seen: read it.

title: Poisson aggregate likelihood needs zero exposure-rate covariance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “Poisson AgD likelihood assumes exposure independent of covariates” The title states independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition, but the audit showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate.
The source said. “The Poisson aggregate-data likelihood in component ML-NMR assumes exposure time is independent of covariates. When exposure depends on prognosis or on treatment, the exposure-weighted covariate moments that actually drive the rate differ from the unweighted moments reported in publications.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition and framed the issue as package-specific. GPT-5.6 Sol read the Poisson Stan code at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate, not independence, and that supplying exposure-weighted covariate summaries through the existing moment fields makes the same likelihood correct; the literature auditor noted the same requirement applies to multinma’s Poisson models, so this is field-level rather than a defect of one implementation.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm’s own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The statistical point is correct and non-trivial: a Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, published covariate moments are person-weighted, and the two coincide only under independence of exposure and covariates, which is exactly what differential follow-up by prognosis violates. I found no paper addressing exposure-weighted covariate moments in an aggregate-data integrated likelihood. Caveat for the editor: this is a field-level property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood, not a cpaic defect. multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset (its 0.8.0 NEWS records a bug fix to that offset), and the same independence assumption applies there, so framing it as ‘cpaic’s Poisson aggregate-data likelihood assumes…’ understates the reach of the problem. The claim that joint exposure and covariate models are not implemented in cpaic is a code fact I cannot verify from public sources.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm’s own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. cpaic man/cmlnmr.Rd and NEWS state that Poisson aggregate arms use E * mean(exp(eta)) over unweighted covariate integration points and assume exposure independent of covariates; there is no interface for exposure-weighted moments or a joint exposure–covariate model. Literature search for Poisson AgD ML-NMR with person-time depending on covariates did not surface an evaluated method that closes this for component ML-NMR. The statistical claim that exposure-weighted moments differ from unweighted moments under dependence is standard rate epidemiology, not a solved software gap. Queries: Poisson aggregate exposure covariate independent ML-NMR; cpaic poisson exposure; person-time weighted covariate moments NMA. All three claims remain supported; problem open.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text: CMP-18 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Statement
Component survival models place time-invariant component effects on the hazard, with flexible piecewise and M-spline baselines that vary the study-specific baseline hazard but do not create time-varying treatment or component effects. Combination-therapy components can produce delayed, waning, or crossing effects, and if two components have different time profiles the additive combination of their time-constant summaries has no clear correspondence to the combination’s actual hazard trajectory. Non-proportional hazards is not an open gap at the non-component level: multinma has supported it since 0.6.0 (2024-01-24) through aux_regression, which allows treatment and covariate effects on shape parameters and spline coefficients across a wide family of baseline hazards. Cure and multistate models are absent from both.

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Why it is open
Allowing time-varying component effects multiplies the parameters that must be assumed constant across subnetworks, so it worsens the untestable-constancy problem that makes the bridge work in the first place. The bridge itself becomes time-dependent when components have different time profiles, which means the cross-gap contrast has to be reported as a trajectory rather than a number. Decision-relevant summaries such as restricted mean survival time then depend on extrapolation beyond the observed follow-up, and cure and multistate structures that would discipline that extrapolation are not implemented in component or non-component ML-NMR.

text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing auxiliary-parameter regression approach to component effects, so component-specific shape parameters and spline coefficients can carry delayed, waning, and crossing profiles, and state explicitly which of those parameters the bridge now requires to be constant across subnetworks. Make restricted mean survival time an estimand rather than a derived quantity, since it is the summary that survives non-proportionality. Cure and multistate component models are genuinely new work, absent from the non-component packages as well.

title: Proportional or time-constant component effects may fail
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Component survival models assume component effects that are proportional or constant over time. Combination-therapy components commonly produce delayed, waning, or crossing effects, so a single time-constant component parameter can misrepresent the whole survival experience.”
What was wrong with it. The source proposed building time-varying effects and flexible hazard models as though none existed. The literature auditor found that multinma 0.6.0’s aux_regression already implements non-proportional hazards for ML-NMR via regression on auxiliary parameters, so the gap is specific to component effects; GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 that piecewise and M-spline baselines give flexible baselines but not time-varying component effects, and declined to assess the word ‘commonly’.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The clinical premise (combination therapies show delayed, waning or crossing effects) is uncontroversial, and the structural point that time-varying component effects multiply the parameters requiring cross-subnetwork constancy is a good one I found nowhere else. But non-proportional hazards in population-adjusted synthesis is not an open gap at the non-component level: multinma added survival models in 0.6.0 (2024-01-24) with exponential, Weibull, Gompertz, log-normal, log-logistic, gamma, generalised gamma, M-spline and piecewise-exponential baselines, and its aux_regression argument allows treatment and covariate effects on shape parameters and spline coefficients, which is exactly a time-varying treatment effect. Phillippo et al. 2025 add that under effect modification marginal hazard ratios are intrinsically time-varying. So the entry should be scoped to component effects specifically. Cure and multistate models are indeed absent from multinma as well, so that sub-claim generalises beyond cpaic. Cites cran:multinma 0.6.0 (2024-01-24), aux_regression argument: Non-proportional hazards in ML-NMR are implemented via regression on auxiliary parameters (shape parameters and spline coefficients) across a wide family of baseline hazards; not available for component effects..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1, C3, and C4 are supported. cpaic records proportional hazards as a survival assumption, and the Stan survival linear predictor contains time-invariant component effects and component-by-covariate interactions. Piecewise and M-spline baselines allow flexible study-specific baseline hazards but do not create time-varying treatment or component effects. No time-varying-effect, cure, or multistate likelihood is implemented. C2 is technically correct: delayed, waning, or crossing effects can violate this structure. The empirical word ‘commonly’ was not assessed, and ‘very high’ severity is conditional on material non-proportionality and on the decision estimand; it is not an automatic defect in every survival analysis.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Treatment-level non-proportional hazards NMA/ML-NMR advanced in 2025 (Phillippo et al., arXiv:2509.10383; multinma M-spline NPH, treatment effects on spline coefficients or stratification). That closes part of the survival-NMA NPH agenda but not the stated component-PAIC problem: additive time-constant component effects on the hazard, with delayed/waning/crossing combination profiles, plus cure and multistate components in cpaic. cpaic 0.1.0 still documents piecewise/M-spline baselines with time-constant component effects and proportional hazards for survival. No time-varying component-effect, cure, or multistate implementation in cpaic or a component ML-NMR package was found. Queries: Phillippo 2025 M-spline NPH; cpaic proportional hazards; time-varying component NMA survival; cure multistate component NMA. Claims C1–C4 about cpaic remain accurate; adjacent treatment-level NPH software does not make the component problem solved.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text: CMP-16 Unverifiable High priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Statement
cpaic, an unreleased development R package on GitHub (choxos/cpaic@9d150e9) that a reader cannot install from CRAN, declares at most one between-study heterogeneity parameter tau when random effects are requested and applies it to all study-arm deviations, with no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity. Its Gaussian component ML-NMR likelihood uses one residual sigma across all IPD rows, although aggregate arms use their own supplied standard errors and the two-stage routes fit study-specific regressions, so the shared residual scale is narrower than stated. A common tau is also the near-universal default in netmeta and multinma, so this is a field-level convention rather than a package idiosyncrasy.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Why it is open
A single tau borrows strength across parts of a network that may not be exchangeable, so a heterogeneous subnetwork can inflate uncertainty in a homogeneous one and vice versa, and in a disconnected network that directly changes how much support the bridge appears to have. Forcing one residual scale across IPD studies that differ in instruments, populations, and follow-up transfers weight between studies and makes model-based intervals wrong even where the mean model is right. Allowing structured heterogeneity or study-specific scales immediately runs into identifiability, because sparse disconnected networks rarely have enough studies per stratum to estimate several variance components, so shrinkage is needed and prior dependence returns.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Allow heterogeneity structured by component, component class, or subnetwork with shrinkage across strata, and add identifiability checks that flag a variance component driven entirely by its prior, since that is the binding constraint in sparse networks. Support study-specific or hierarchically shrunk residual scales for the IPD likelihood and robust residual distributions so heavy tails and unequal precision do not distort weighting. Report the diagnostic separately from the correction, so an analyst can see whether stratum-specific heterogeneity is supported before fitting it.

title: Unreleased cpaic shares one tau and one IPD-row residual variance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “cpaic assumes a single heterogeneity and residual variance” The title implies an installable package and a single residual variance across all studies, but cpaic is a GitHub development package and the shared sigma covers IPD rows only.
The source said. “cpaic’s models assume one common between-study heterogeneity parameter across the network and, for continuous outcomes, one Gaussian residual standard deviation shared across all studies. Different component classes or subnetworks may plausibly have different heterogeneity, and unequal true residual variances distort study precision and network weighting.”
What was wrong with it. The source said the single residual standard deviation is shared across all studies and that it biases both the point estimate and its interval. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and narrowed both: the shared sigma covers IPD rows only, since aggregate arms use supplied se_agd and the two-stage routes fit study-specific regressions, and residual heteroskedasticity misallocates precision and invalidates model-based uncertainty without by itself implying biased mean-effect coefficients under a correct conditional mean model. The literature auditor added that a common tau is the standard default in netmeta and multinma too.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): When random effects are requested, C1-C3 are supported for cML-NMR: every Stan family declares at most one tau and applies tau[1] to all study-arm deviations; no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity scale exists. C4 and C6 require qualification. The Gaussian cML-NMR likelihood has one sigma across all IPD observations, but aggregate arms use their separately supplied se_agd values, and cMAIC/cSTC fit study-specific regressions rather than sharing this sigma. Unequal IPD residual variances do misrepresent relative precision, efficient weighting, and model-based uncertainty. However, heteroskedasticity alone does not imply biased mean-effect coefficients when the conditional mean model is correct, contrary to the report’s narrative. The priority is conditional on material variance or heterogeneity differences and the amount of evidence each affected stratum contributes.

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. Every claim here is about cpaic’s internals (single heterogeneity parameter, single residual standard deviation, absence of structured or study-specific scales). cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository, so I have nothing to read and this belongs to the source-code auditor. On the literature side the statistical assertions are textbook and safe: a common tau borrows strength across possibly non-exchangeable parts of a network, and forcing a common residual variance misallocates precision weights. I did not retrieve a specific paper on comparison-specific or class-specific heterogeneity variances in network meta-analysis in this session, so I will not cite one; note only that a common tau is the near-universal default in netmeta and multinma too, so this is a field-level convention rather than a cpaic idiosyncrasy, and the entry would be stronger if it said so. The identifiability tension the entry raises (too few studies per stratum in sparse disconnected networks) is genuine and, as far as I found, unaddressed.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. When random effects are requested, C1-C3 are supported for cML-NMR: every Stan family declares at most one tau and applies tau[1] to all study-arm deviations; no component-, class-, or subnetwork-indexed heterogeneity scale exists. C4 and C6 require qualification. The Gaussian cML-NMR likelihood has one sigma across all IPD observations, but aggregate arms use their separately supplied se_agd values, and cMAIC/cSTC fit study-specific regressions rather than sharing this sigma. Unequal IPD residual variances do misrepresent relative precision, efficient weighting, and model-based uncertainty. However, heteroskedasticity alone does not imply biased mean-effect coefficients when the conditional mean model is correct, contrary to the report’s narrative. The priority is conditional on material variance or heterogeneity differences and the amount of evidence each affected stratum contributes.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. cpaic 0.1.0 (README, cmlnmr Rd, NEWS) still fits one common tau and one network-wide Gaussian residual sigma; no component-class, subnetwork, or study-specific residual hierarchy is implemented. Broader NMA has class-effect and hierarchical heterogeneity models (e.g. class-effects NMA practice literature), but those are not component-PAIC residual or component-structured tau models and do not close the stated cpaic gap. No CRAN/GitHub change in multinma/maicplus/netmeta/cpaic was found that adds study-specific residual scales inside component ML-NMR. Queries: cpaic tau sigma; multinma study-specific residual; structured heterogeneity component NMA 2024–2026; class-effects NMA residual variance. Claims C1–C6 are faithful software/limitation statements; the methodological problem remains open as stated.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present
