title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Statement
Interaction parameters informed only by aggregate data can be regularized into finite posterior intervals by the prior, so a proper credible interval is not evidence that the likelihood contributed anything. Implemented component PAIC already ships partial mitigation: plot_prior_posterior() compares each prior with its posterior, prior_sensitivity() quantifies how far target contrasts move when priors are tightened or loosened, and estimable_effects_at() separates no first-order information from IPD-supported and aggregate-only information. What is missing is a default numerical summary: prior-to-posterior contraction per interaction parameter and an effective likelihood rank, reported without the analyst having to ask.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Why it is open
A proper prior yields a proper posterior under ordinary integrability conditions, so the usual output gives no signal that the likelihood contributed nothing, and the parameters where this bites hardest are exactly the weakly identified interaction terms that a bridged component model depends on. The existing diagnostics are visual or require a deliberate refit, so an analyst who does not run them sees a clean interval with no warning attached. Prior-to-posterior contraction and effective likelihood rank are the summaries that would make this visible by default, and neither is computed.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Promote the existing prior-versus-posterior comparison and prior-sensitivity refit from optional diagnostics to default reported output, and add numerical prior-to-posterior contraction for every interaction parameter plus an effective likelihood rank for the fitted model. Attach to each reported interaction the label of whether it is identified by IPD, by aggregate arms, or by neither, which the estimability screen already computes. Calibrate these summaries specifically to interaction parameters in a bridged component model, since the generic Bayesian workflow versions are already standard.

title: Aggregate-data-only interactions may be prior-driven
text:
Our study

Prior-to-posterior contraction and effective likelihood rank measure information, not bias
The question put to it. CMP-14 asks for two default summaries, prior-to-posterior contraction per interaction and an effective likelihood rank, so an analyst sees when an aggregate-only interaction is held up by its prior. Would those summaries tell the analyst whether the reported interval covers?
What it found. Not reliably, and the reason is structural. On an exact identity-link arm of 504 scenarios and a logit arm of 72, no threshold on contraction, on either effective-rank reading, or on the estimability screen separates scenarios whose 95% interval covers nominally from those that fail. The summaries are functions of Fisher information and the prior, so within one design they are exactly constant while coverage ranges from 0 to 0.96. They partly catch the failure they were designed for: contraction flags 59% of failures caused by a tight prior. They catch none of the 142 failures caused by a biased route, where the ecological route carries between-study confounding or the additivity route a synergy, because confounding moves the posterior mean and not its information. A clean contraction says the likelihood spoke, not that it was right. Every result is exploratory.
Results.

All four registered statistics (contraction, target-level likelihood ratio, whole-model effective rank, estimability screen) take values shared by failing and nominal scenarios on both arms, so no threshold on any of them separates the classes. On E1 there are 251 failing and 169 nominal scenarios; on E2, 41 and 12.
On the identity link with known residual variance the posterior covariance does not involve the outcomes. Within one information state, spread, network size and prior, contraction, target ratio and effective rank are exactly constant across discordance and synergy levels while coverage ranges over 0.956.
Decomposed by cause (post hoc), 109 E1 failures come from a prior of SD 0.1 pulling a true interaction of 0.4 toward zero and 142 from a biased route. Contraction flags 58.7% of the first and 0% of the second; target ratio 41.3% and 0%; effective rank 56.0% and 0%.
Scenario pairs matched on spread, size and prior whose contraction differs by less than 0.02 differ in coverage by up to 0.951 on E1.
On the logit arm the rules score far better on average (contraction Youden 0.805 against 0.220 on E1) because 34 of its 41 failures sit at the tight prior and it has only 12 nominal scenarios. The overlap persists.
Three aggregate routes identify an interaction on the logit link, through differences in covariate means, covariate variances or baseline risk; only the first works on the identity link. None is randomized.

Design.

Estimand

The within-trial interaction of the target component, true value 0.4; coverage of its nominal 95% interval

Methods compared

prior-to-posterior contraction, target-level likelihood to prior precision ratio, whole-model effective likelihood rank, estimability screen, source survival (post hoc candidate)

Data-generating mechanism

Exact computation on a four-component network, one scalar covariate, twelve arms in every state. The target interaction is identified by its own IPD trial, by a combination arm under additivity, by the between-study contrast in aggregate covariate means, by differing covariate variances (logit only), or not at all. E1: identity link, known variance, 504 scenarios crossing state, covariate spread, network size, interaction prior SD, discordance and synergy. E2: logit link, asymptotic, 72 scenarios.

Replicates

Exact and asymptotic computation: 504 E1 scenarios and 72 E2 scenarios, no Monte Carlo replicates


What this does not answer. Nothing here is confirmatory: E1 was computed before its protocol existed, E2’s separation rules were rebuilt after its output was read, and the cause decomposition was added for the manuscript. E1 is exact for a design realized at its quadrature nodes and E2 is asymptotic, so no posterior was sampled and neither is an average over realized designs. The exact invariance of the summaries holds for known-variance Gaussian models; with estimated variances or random effects they would move with a departure and whether that movement could ever warn is untested. One target component, one covariate, one network geometry, a normal within-study covariate law on the logit arm, and departures acting on the mean only. The protocol went through thirteen rounds of critique; the manuscript has not been peer reviewed.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Interaction parameters informed only by aggregate data can be regularized into finite posterior intervals by the prior rather than by the likelihood. A finite credible interval may therefore reflect the prior rather than information in the data.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no diagnostic in standard output separates prior-driven from likelihood-driven interaction estimates. GPT-5.6 Sol found three at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 (plot_prior_posterior(), prior_sensitivity(), estimable_effects_at()), so the gap narrows to their being optional rather than default and to the absence of numerical contraction and likelihood-rank summaries; it also corrected the wording, since a prior regularizes a posterior but never makes the likelihood identify a parameter.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The statistical content is uncontroversial Bayesian bookkeeping: a proper prior always yields a proper posterior, so a finite credible interval is not evidence of likelihood information. I found no paper offering a routine prior-versus-likelihood diagnostic for effect-modifier interactions in ML-NMR or CNMA, and no source asserting that absence, so the ‘no diagnostic in standard output’ claims are unverifiable rather than established. Two caveats for the editor. The generic remedies named (prior-to-posterior contraction, prior predictive checks, prior sensitivity) are standard Bayesian workflow rather than a research gap, so the novel part is specifically calibrating them to interaction parameters in a bridged component model. And the claim about what cpaic’s documentation recognises cannot be checked: cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository. Confidence is capped because I read no text bearing directly on this entry.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Proper-prior/proper-posterior language also requires ordinary posterior-integrability conditions rather than holding as an unrestricted theorem. The report understates existing mitigation: plot_prior_posterior() directly compares each prior and posterior, prior_sensitivity() quantifies contrast movement under changed priors, and estimable_effects_at() distinguishes IPD, aggregate, and absent first-order information. These are optional rather than default numerical contraction or likelihood-rank summaries, so the remaining work is useful but is a diagnostic-roadmap item, not automatically a very-high-severity correctness failure. title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text: CMP-12 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Statement
When a multi-arm trial’s contrasts are population-adjusted one at a time, the within-study covariance induced by a shared arm and a shared weighting step is not recovered by naive variance formulas, so standard errors and network precision would be wrong. Current implementations avoid the error by refusing the capability rather than by solving it: both the component MAIC and component STC routes reject IPD studies with more than two arms, so multi-arm IPD trials must be split or dropped. The covariance is handled natively on the synthesis side of frequentist CNMA and in the one-stage ML-NMR likelihood, which keeps multi-arm trials inside a single arm-level model; what is missing is a two-stage adjusted estimator that carries it, and any multi-arm handling in component PAIC.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Why it is open
Population adjustment reweights or re-fits per contrast, and a two-stage route that processes one contrast at a time has no natural place to carry the induced correlation, so multi-arm studies must be split, which double counts the shared arm, or dropped, which discards evidence. A stratified bootstrap could recover the covariance only if replicates are carried jointly across a trial’s contrasts rather than per contrast, which requires multivariate estimating equations or an arm-level likelihood and therefore changes the two-stage architecture. Until then the practical cost is lost evidence rather than wrong intervals.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use a multivariate bootstrap or stacked estimating equations that carry all of a trial’s contrasts jointly, so the two-stage route can accept multi-arm IPD studies with the correct correlation structure. Alternatively move to a one-stage arm-level component likelihood, where the full contrast covariance is produced by the model rather than reconstructed afterwards, which is how the non-component version already handles multi-arm trials. Either way the fix should lift the current two-arm restriction rather than adding a variance correction on top of it.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Our study

Splitting a multi-arm trial’s adjusted contrasts is conservative for one contrast and anticonservative for another
The question put to it. When a three-arm trial’s population-adjusted contrasts share an arm and a weight vector, what is lost by treating them as independent, is the error ever anticonservative, and is dropping the trial cheaper?
What it found. Ignoring the within-trial covariance errs in a direction set by the contrast, not by how the arms’ effect modification aligns. The trial’s own B-versus-C interval became conservative in every scenario, while the network A-versus-B interval, which borrows through the trial, fell below nominal in 15 of 30 scenarios. The shared-weighting part of the covariance took both signs but never reversed a contrast’s error. Dropping the trial widened the network interval by 29% to 91%.
Results.

Split, trial-alone d_BC: coverage 0.957 to 1.000, above nominal beyond 3 MCSE in 29 of 30 scenarios and below in none; DESIGN.md’s alignment-sign prediction is withdrawn by its registered test.
Split, network d_AB: coverage 0.4 to 3.7 points below the stacked sandwich, below nominal beyond 3 MCSE in 15 of 30 scenarios against 0 for the stacked sandwich.
The shared-weighting covariance term was -22% to +15% of the Monte Carlo covariance, dominated by the shared-arm term.
Joint sandwiches recovered 0.76 to 1.15 (stacked) and 0.73 to 1.12 (weights fixed) of the Monte Carlo covariance; stacked trial-alone intervals covered 0.919 to 0.960.
Dropping the trial was unbiased and widened the network d_AB interval by a median 53%.

Design.

Estimand

d_AB, d_AC and d_BC in the target population

Methods compared

split (covariance zero), joint sandwich, weights fixed, stacked sandwich, drop the trial

Data-generating mechanism

Three-arm individual-data trial weighted by MAIC to a target, plus aggregate A-versus-C and B-versus-C trials in the target; 30 scenarios crossing effect-modification strength, its alignment across arms, target shift and shared-arm size; split, weights-fixed, stacked and drop analyses, network by generalized least squares.

Replicates

1000 per scenario, 30,000 in total


What this does not answer. Continuous outcome, linear modification, one three-arm trial in a fixed two-trial aggregate network; four-arm trials, the one-stage ML-NMR comparator and a bootstrap are not run, and target moments are fixed. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: No two-stage adjusted estimator carries multi-arm covariance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Two-stage adjustment loses multi-arm within-study covariance” The title asserts the covariance is lost in practice, but the audit found both component routes reject multi-arm IPD studies outright, so it is a refused capability rather than a wrong-standard-error defect.
The source said. “When a multi-arm trial’s contrasts are population-adjusted one at a time in a two-stage workflow, the within-study covariance among those contrasts can be lost or misstated, so standard errors and network precision can be wrong. The same limitation appears as a hard restriction in the cSTC route, which accepts only two-arm IPD studies.”
What was wrong with it. The source implied that adjusted multi-arm contrasts are emitted with lost covariance. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and found both cmaic() and cstc() reject IPD studies with more than two arms, so this is a refused capability rather than a current wrong-standard-error defect; the literature auditor added that the one-stage fix is published and implemented for non-component networks (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579) and that netmeta’s CNMA machinery already adjusts multi-arm weights.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. I found no paper that recovers within-study covariance among multi-arm contrasts after two-stage population adjustment, so that specific gap is real. Two qualifications. First, the multi-arm covariance problem is already solved on the synthesis side of CNMA: Petropoulou et al. 2023 record that in the netmeta CNMA machinery ‘For multi-arm studies, the weights are assumed to be adjusted as described in [Rucker and Schwarzer]’, so the loss is introduced by the adjustment stage, not by component modelling. Second, the one-stage alternative avoids the problem entirely: ML-NMR keeps multi-arm trials inside a single arm-level likelihood, and Phillippo et al. 2020 give the limitation of the two-stage route as a motivation for it. So the practical need is met for non-component networks; what is open is a two-stage estimator that carries the covariance, and any multi-arm handling in a component PAIC. The claim that cSTC accepts only two-arm IPD studies is a code fact I cannot check. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Handles multi-arm trials natively within a one-stage NMA likelihood, so the covariance is never discarded; does not solve the two-stage or component case..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C1, C2, and C6 are correct for a workflow that estimates several shared-arm contrasts separately and passes only their marginal variances onward. C3 and C4 are source-confirmed: cMAIC jointly re-estimates weights and its arm-only outcome model within arm-stratified bootstrap replicates, fails closed below the success threshold, and both cMAIC and cSTC reject IPD studies with more than two arms. Consequently, current cpaic does not silently emit multi-arm adjusted contrasts with incorrect covariance; it avoids the error by refusing that capability. Joint multi-arm adjustment remains an open feature, but this is a roadmap limitation rather than a current wrong-standard-error defect. C5 is an empirical prevalence claim outside the assigned lens and was not assessed. title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text: CMP-10 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text:
Statement
No component-additive PAIC produces target-standardized arm outcomes or marginal contrasts. ML-NMR already does this for non-component networks: multinma has provided marginal_effects() since 0.7.0 (2024-05-07), which standardizes absolute predictions over a target population’s covariate distribution and contrasts them, including hazard, survival probability, median survival, and RMST contrasts, and Phillippo et al. 2025 state that ML-NMR is currently the only population-adjustment method producing both conditional and marginal estimates in any decision target population. Once treatment effects are decomposed into components, no equivalent path exists: component STC centers modifiers at supplied target means and reports the treatment coefficient, and component ML-NMR returns a conditional linear-predictor contrast at one covariate profile. Evaluating a component regression at target covariate means is exact only under an identity link and linearity in covariates, so it is not a substitute.

title: Component PAIC lacks a marginal target-standardized estimand path
text:
Why it is open
The correct operation is g-computation or posterior standardization, integrating the fitted model over the whole target covariate distribution for every posterior draw, which requires that distribution rather than only its means and therefore inherits the target-reconstruction problem and its uncertainty. The proposed arm-mean formula also requires an identified or externally supplied target baseline alpha*, which study-specific intercepts do not provide. Because the choice between conditional and standardized output changes the reported number, this is an estimand decision rather than a presentation preference, and decision modelers currently apply conditional component coefficients to marginal baselines, which is incoherent on non-collapsible scales.

text:
Probable solution or research direction
Port the existing ML-NMR standardization path to the component case rather than building it from scratch: integrate the component-additive model over an explicit user-supplied target distribution for every posterior draw, returning arm-level risks, means, rates, and survival curves, plus differences and ratios, survival probability differences, and RMST differences. Resolve the target baseline explicitly, since the component decomposition does not supply alpha*. Propagate uncertainty from model parameters and, where the target distribution is estimated or reconstructed rather than fixed, from that reconstruction as well, and retain conditional component effects as model parameters rather than as the policy estimand.

Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Component STC evaluates a fitted conditional outcome regression at target covariate means and component ML-NMR returns conditional link-scale component effects, so neither route produces a marginal, target-standardized quantity of the kind HTA decision models require. title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text: CMP-08 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Statement
For linear observed-contrast models, target estimability is characterized exactly by row-space membership of the target-specific contrast vector v(m,x) = (1, x’) Kronecker m with m = C_t - C_u. Implemented component PAIC applies an augmented target-dependent row-space diagnostic that is exact for specified non-survival IPD regressions and only a first-order design screen for aggregate-data and survival likelihoods, and it labels which verdict is which. Once a nonlinear inverse link is integrated over a covariate distribution, no published conditions characterize local or global identification by outcome family and integration structure, so a target functional can pass the screen and still be unidentified.

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Why it is open
Once the inverse link is nonlinear and integrated over a covariate distribution, the map from parameters to the observed-data distribution is not linear in the parameters, so a design-based row-space criterion no longer characterizes identification. Deriving conditions requires analyzing the observed-data information of an integrated aggregate likelihood, which depends on the outcome family, the covariate distribution, and the integration scheme, so results must be stated case by case rather than once. The complementary numerical diagnostics that would substitute in the interim, singular values of the observed-information matrix and likelihood or posterior profiles for a requested contrast, are not computed by any component PAIC implementation the auditors read.

title: Identification beyond row-space screens in nonlinear component ML-NMR
text:
Probable solution or research direction
A methodological paper should derive local and global identification conditions for nonlinear component ML-NMR by outcome family and integration structure, since that is the part with no results. In the interim, supplement the row-space screen with Jacobian and Fisher-information rank diagnostics, observed-information singular values, and likelihood or posterior profiles for each requested target contrast, together with prior-data conflict diagnostics that detect when the prior rather than the data supplies the answer. The precedent for the design-level screens already exists in frequentist CNMA, where an algorithm identifies inestimable interactions so that only estimable ones enter interaction models.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Statement
Component PAIC as implemented takes covariates as observed values with no calibration or latent measurement-error model, and derives the component matrix by deterministically parsing treatment labels with no probability model for component assignment. Because a bridge exists exactly when two subnetworks share a component, a coding error can change the design matrix, its rank, and its row space, and so can create or remove shared-component paths rather than merely perturbing a coefficient. Not every miscoding changes connectivity, and measurement error in a variable that is not an effect modifier need not bias the estimand, so the concern is conditional on which covariate or component is uncertain.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Why it is open
Component coding is currently a deterministic analyst decision with no uncertainty attached, so the network topology is treated as known when it is inferred from trial reports. Covariate measurement error additionally biases the weighting step and attenuates the interaction terms that carry effect modification, and the direction depends on the unknown error structure, so a post hoc correction has nothing to key on. The mature general machinery for this problem, regression calibration, SIMEX, and Bayesian measurement-error and misclassification models, has not been applied to population-adjusted or component synthesis in any work the auditors could retrieve.

cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; takes covariates as observed with no calibration or latent measurement-error model, and builds the component matrix by deterministic label parsing with no probability model for assignment

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Introduce probabilistic component coding so that assignment uncertainty propagates into the design matrix, the row space, and therefore the estimand, and report how often the cross-gap contrast becomes non-estimable under plausible codings. Add covariate calibration models for effect modifiers using existing measurement-error machinery, prioritizing the modifiers that actually load the requested contrast. Because the concern is conditional, the first deliverable is a diagnostic that identifies which coding and measurement uncertainties would matter for a given target contrast.

title: Measurement error and component misclassification are ignored
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source said. “Component methods ignore measurement error in covariates and misclassification in how interventions are coded into components. Component misclassification can create an apparent bridge between subnetworks where none exists, or destroy a real one.”
What was wrong with it. The source stated the absence at field level and implied any miscoding changes the bridge. GPT-5.6 Sol confirmed the absence at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 but scoped it to that package, and qualified the mechanism: not every miscoding changes connectivity, and measurement error does not bias every estimand; the literature auditor searched and found no measurement-error or misclassification method for MAIC, STC, ML-NMR, or CNMA and no source asserting the absence, so recorded it as unverifiable at field level.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: Dismantling cognitive-behaviour therapy for panic disorder: . New citations: 10.1017/S0033291717003919

Literature and prior-art check

open / unverifiable. I searched PubMed and the web for measurement error or misclassification methods in MAIC, STC, ML-NMR or CNMA and found nothing that models covariate measurement error in the weighting step or treats component coding probabilistically. The general statistical machinery (regression calibration, SIMEX, Bayesian measurement-error models, misclassification priors) is of course mature, but I retrieved no application to population-adjusted or component synthesis, so I cannot supply a locator. The claim is a ‘no method exists’ claim and no source I found asserts the absence, so per calibration it is unverifiable rather than supported. The substantive observation that misclassifying a component changes network topology rather than a coefficient is a genuine and, as far as I can tell, unpublished point; it is the strongest part of the entry. Entry has no prior_work at all, which is a presentation weakness rather than a factual error.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 is source-confirmed at 9d150e9. Covariates enter cMAIC, cSTC, and cML-NMR as observed values without a calibration or latent measurement-error model, while build_C_matrix() deterministically parses the supplied labels with no probability model for component assignment. C2 is correct: changing a component assignment changes C and can consequently create or remove shared-component paths, alter rank, or change the row space, although not every miscoding changes connectivity. The cpaic-specific part of C3 is supported; the claim about every existing component NMA/PAIC package is outside this audit. Measurement error is not guaranteed to bias every estimand, for example when the mismeasured variable is not an effect modifier, but it can attenuate interaction estimates, leave true imbalance after weighting, and invalidate transport. This is decision-critical when coding or modifier measurement is genuinely uncertain; for carefully curated, effectively error-free inputs it is a lower-priority roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Searched for probabilistic component coding, misclassification models that randomize the CNMA design/combination matrix, and covariate measurement-error correction inside component NMA/PAIC. General measurement-error and exposure-misclassification methods exist for meta-analysis and IPD (e.g., Jrsm work on misclassification adjustment), but none were found that (a) treat component assignment as uncertain topology or (b) ship in netmeta, multinma, gemtc, MBNMAdose, or a public cpaic. Queries: ‘component network meta-analysis misclassification’, ‘probabilistic component coding NMA’, ‘measurement error effect modifiers PAIC CNMA’, plus 2024–2026 journal and package scans. No merged PR or CRAN release notes close this gap. C1–C3 therefore remain open as stated; confidence is moderate because absence-of-evidence for a niche software feature is harder to prove exhaustively than a positive locator.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=1)

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text: CMP-04 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Statement
Forward selection of component and interaction structures, as implemented in the netmeta CNMA workflow, makes a sequence of data-driven decisions whose uncertainty is not carried into the reported intervals. Petropoulou et al. 2023 measured the failure in disconnected networks: forward selection recovered the correct interaction model in only 12.0 to 15.2 percent of runs under mild additivity violation and 21.6 to 26.3 percent under strong violation, and tended to select sparse, often additive, models even when additivity was violated. In connected networks the measured coverage penalty was modest. Where an analyst selects a structure externally and then reports intervals conditional on it, those intervals omit selection uncertainty and are optimistic.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Why it is open
Post-selection intervals condition on the selected structure and ignore the sequence of decisions that produced it, so they are too narrow and the chosen structure is unstable under resampling. In a disconnected network the candidate structures are also poorly separated by the data, because the contrasts that would discriminate between them are the ones spanning the gap, so selection instability translates into instability of the bridge rather than of nuisance terms. No selection-aware inference has been developed for component structures, and the auditors found no application of projection predictive inference or stacking to CNMA additivity structures.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023
evaluates forward CNMA model selection in 1000 simulated connected and disconnected networks and quantifies its failure in the disconnected case


netmeta
supplies the frequentist component NMA machinery, including the forward-selection routine whose uncertainty is not propagated

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Replace forward selection with shrinkage priors, projection predictive inference, or stacking across candidate additivity structures, and report selection-aware uncertainty so the reported interval includes the cost of having chosen a structure from the data. Because the failure is documented specifically for disconnected networks, the first target should be selection-aware inference for the cross-gap contrast rather than for the whole network fit. Where selection is done outside the fitting package, the resulting intervals should be labeled as conditional on the chosen component coding.

title: Additivity model selection can be unstable
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 2 findings from 2 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed.
The source said. “Selecting which components and which interactions enter the additive model by forward selection inflates optimism and can fail outright in sparse disconnected graphs. The uncertainty introduced by the selection step is not carried into the reported intervals.”
What was wrong with it. The source attributed the selection step to cpaic. GPT-5.6 Sol read choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and found no forward, stepwise, projection-predictive, or stacking routine there: the package builds a fixed binary component matrix from the supplied treatment labels, so there is no in-package selection whose uncertainty could be propagated, and the problem belongs to the analyst’s upstream choice and to netmeta’s forward-selection workflow; the literature auditor supplied the missing source and the measured failure rates, doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 2 surviving findings from: Bayesian models for aggregate and individual patient data co; Supplementary appendix to Furukawa et al., Dismantling, opti. New citations: 10.1002/sim.9372, 10.1016/S2215-0366(21)00077-8 (parent article; the supplement itself carries no DOI)

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The entry cites only ‘netmeta’ but the claim has a direct published evidence base it does not cite: Petropoulou, Rucker, Weibel, Kranke, Schwarzer 2023 evaluated the forward CNMA selection strategy in 1000 simulated connected and disconnected networks. Their disconnected-network result is stronger than the entry’s: forward selection recovered the correct interaction model in only 12.0-15.2 percent (mild violation) and 21.6-26.3 percent (strong violation) of runs, and ‘Forward selection tended to select sparse (often additive) CNMA models for disconnected networks even if additivity was mildly or strongly violated.’ So ‘can fail in sparse disconnected graphs’ is established, not conjectural. Caveat on ‘inflates optimism’: in CONNECTED networks the measured penalty was modest - coverage for the selected CNMA fell outside Monte-Carlo limits only at moderate heterogeneity, and per-comparison coverage was ‘somewhat smaller … however, not dramatically different’. Selection-uncertainty propagation is still unsolved, so the problem stands. ‘Projection predictive inference and stacking have not been applied to component NMA’ - I found no counterexample, but absence is unverifiable. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Establishes empirically (not fixes) that forward CNMA selection fails in disconnected networks; the missing citation for this entry’s central claim..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

not-a-problem / misattributed. C1 is generally correct: naive inference after forward selection is optimistic and conditions on the selected structure. C2 is also possible when candidate component models are rank-deficient, saturated, or numerically unstable. The attribution to current cpaic in C3 is wrong, however. At 9d150e9, cpaic deterministically constructs a binary C matrix from the supplied treatment labels and fits that fixed structure; NAMESPACE and the R sources contain no forward, stepwise, projection-predictive, stacking, or component-structure selection routine. There is therefore no package selection step whose uncertainty cpaic intervals could propagate. If an analyst performs external selection first, the resulting cpaic intervals are conditional on that externally chosen coding, but that is a different and conditional problem. C4 is a literature-coverage claim outside the assigned lens.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. The main prior-art hit is Petropoulou et al. 2023 (and the related netmeta forward-selection machinery), which evaluates forward selection of CNMA structures and finds poor selection of the correct interaction structure under mild additivity violation, degraded performance with heterogeneity, and bad performance when the network is disconnected. That paper characterizes instability; it does not replace forward selection with selection-aware intervals, projection predictive inference, or stacking for component structures. netmeta still exposes netcomb/discomb and selection utilities without post-selection inference for the bridge. Searches for projpred, stacking, or Bayesian model averaging applied to CNMA additivity structure (RSM/SIM/BMC MRM 2023–2026, arXiv, CRAN) found no applied work. Claims C1–C2 are supported by that simulation evidence; C3 is consistent with netmeta/cpaic not advertising selection-aware intervals; C4 remains true as a gap. Status stays open: the problem is documented, not solved.

text:
Source
Derived from C:L1384, scope:field-level (CNMA model selection); affects cpaic of the reviewed corpus.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text: CMP-02 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Statement
Once population adjustment is added to a component bridge, cross-subnetwork constancy is required for the interaction projection that loads the requested contrast, not only for component main effects: for a target profile x, the quantity (C_t - C_u)’ Gamma x must be stable in addition to the corresponding main-effect projection. The assumption count grows with adjusted covariates but is smaller than the number of interaction terms, because zero target values, zero component loadings, and interactions supported by covariate variation in two subnetworks all reduce it. The combined assumption set is strictly stronger than main-effect constancy only when a nonzero relevant interaction is present. Phillippo et al. 2022 show that in a connected network the shared-effect-modifier assumption can be examined and relaxed one covariate at a time; that machinery has no analogue across a disconnection.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Why it is open
Interaction parameters are estimated from less information than the corresponding main effects, so requiring the target-relevant projection of them to be stable across a gap that carries no evidence compounds an already weak identification problem. Component cML-NMR as implemented uses a single shared interaction matrix with no subnetwork index and no hierarchical alternative, so a drifting interaction has nowhere to go except into the shared parameter. No published diagnostic distinguishes a genuinely shared interaction from one whose apparent stability is an artifact of shrinkage or of limited covariate range within each subnetwork, and no target-specific interaction-drift tipping surface exists in any component PAIC software found by the auditors.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2023
assesses and relaxes the shared effect modifier assumption one covariate at a time in a connected ML-NMR network; no analogue exists across a disconnection


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; fits one global component-by-modifier interaction matrix shared across all subnetworks in cML-NMR, with no subnetwork-specific drift and no interaction tipping surfaces

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Fit hierarchical subnetwork-specific interaction matrices Gamma_s that shrink toward a common value rather than being forced equal, with reference or zero-mean constraints so Gamma and the drift blocks are separately defined. Add interaction-drift sensitivity expressed on the projection that loads the requested contrast, with target-specific tipping surfaces showing which covariate values make the conclusion fragile. Report, for each requested contrast, which interaction directions are supported by covariate variation in more than one subnetwork, since those are the only ones with any cross-gap evidence.

title: Adjusted component bridges need interaction constancy across the gap
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Component-by-modifier constancy is a strictly stronger assumption” The title asserts the assumption is strictly stronger unconditionally, but the audit restricted that to cases where a nonzero relevant interaction is present.
The source said. “Once population adjustment is added to a component bridge, cross-subnetwork constancy is needed not only for component main effects but for every relevant component-by-effect-modifier interaction, so the untestable surface grows with the number of adjusted covariates. Component ML-NMR therefore stacks CNMA assumptions on top of transportability, an integration distribution, and stable component-by-modifier interactions.”
What was wrong with it. The source said every component-by-modifier interaction must be constant and that disconnection makes each one unverifiable. GPT-5.6 Sol restricted this to the interaction projection (C_t - C_u)’ Gamma x that loads the requested target, noted that interactions supported by covariate variation in two subnetworks can be compared, and confirmed at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 that the package fits one global gamma[C,Q] with no subnetwork index; the literature auditor added Phillippo et al. 2022 (doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162), which shows the connected-network analogue is assessable.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Phillippo et al. 2022’ -> ‘Phillippo et al. 2023’ 10.1177/0272989X221117162 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2022 online and 2023 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I searched PubMed, arXiv and the netmeta/multinma literature for any published component + population-adjustment model; the closest published object is Rucker/Schmitz/Schwarzer 2021, which compares CNMA against a matching method but does not fit component-by-modifier interactions. I found no paper that formalises or tests cross-subnetwork constancy of interaction matrices, so the problem is open. The core claim (‘interaction constancy is strictly stronger than main-effect constancy’) is a logical containment, not an empirical finding, and is defensible as stated. Supporting context the entry omits: Phillippo et al. 2022 (Med Decis Making) report that in a CONNECTED network the shared-effect-modifier assumption can be assessed and relaxed one covariate at a time (‘A shared effect modifier assumption may also be necessary for identifiability’; they ‘relax the shared effect modifier assumption for each covariate in turn’). That machinery has no analogue across a disconnection, which strengthens rather than weakens the entry. The claims naming cpaic’s internals are unverifiable from literature: cpaic is not on CRAN and I found no public repository. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162: Does NOT solve it. Supplies the missing citation showing shared-effect-modifier assumptions ARE assessable in connected networks, sharpening the claim that they are not across a gap..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. At choxos/cpaic@9d150e9, C5 is source-confirmed: .cpaic_fixed_design() creates one global component-by-modifier block, and each Stan model has one matrix gamma[C,Q] with no subnetwork index or hierarchical gamma_s. Interaction-drift tipping surfaces are absent, and bridge_fragility() expressly excludes Lambda, supporting the cpaic-specific part of C6. C9 and C10 are also correct: reported effects are conditional contrasts (C_t-C_u)’(beta+Gamma x), while aggregate likelihoods integrate over study covariate distributions. C1-C4 and C11 nevertheless need rank and estimand qualifications. Only the projection (C_t-C_u)’Lambda_s x relevant to the requested target must be stable; zero target values, zero component loadings, and estimable linear combinations reduce the assumption count. Interactions supported by covariate variation in multiple subnetworks can be compared, so disconnection does not make every interaction unverifiable. The combined main-effect-plus-interaction assumption set is strictly stronger only when a nonzero relevant interaction is introduced. For C8, the integration distribution is required for aggregate-study likelihood construction, but cpaic has no marginal target-standardization path and needs only a covariate profile for its reported target contrast. Software-wide nonexistence in C6 is outside this audit.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Sought component-by-effect-modifier interactions that vary by subnetwork, hierarchical Gamma_s, interaction-drift tipping surfaces, or component ML-NMR software beyond a shared interaction matrix. Public search found no CRAN package named cpaic (404 on cran.r-project.org/package=cpaic) and no published component-ML-NMR with hierarchical subnetwork-specific interaction matrices or target-specific interaction-drift fragility tools. Multinma and related PAIC/ML-NMR work address population adjustment for whole treatments, not the stacked CNMA-plus-modifier-constancy surface described here. Veroniki et al. 2026 and Rücker et al. 2020 discuss interaction CNMA for component–component terms, not component-by-covariate constancy across a disconnection. Queries covering Research Synthesis Methods, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv, and package ecosystems (multinma, maicplus, netmeta, gemtc, MBNMAdose, crossnma) through 2026 returned no evaluation that identifies or bounds Lambda^(s) from disconnected evidence. Claims that population adjustment multiplies untestable cross-gap stability assumptions (C1–C4, C8–C11) remain faithful; software claims about cpaic (C5–C6) are consistent with the absence of a public package implementing hierarchical interaction drift, but cpaic itself was not independently retrievable. Interaction-drift fragility (C7) is still only a proposal.

text: ADJ-20 Partially addressed Medium priority Speculative

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Statement
No method exists for indirectly comparing dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences across studies. The estimand, however, is definable: a policy contrast is the target-population difference between the values of two well-specified policies, so what is missing is cross-study identification and data rather than the definition. Identification requires compatible policies, treatment histories and outcomes, plus consistency, positivity, suitable sequential randomization or exchangeability, and transportability; longitudinal histories are generally needed, though sequentially randomized designs carry different confounding assumptions and sufficiently detailed regime-level estimates could sometimes support a second-stage synthesis.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Why it is open
Sequential decision estimands generally require longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounder data at the individual level, which trial publications and most shared individual data do not contain. Existing network structures encode fixed-regimen contrasts, so a policy contrast cannot simply be attached to them; prespecified policies could in principle enter as network nodes, but only once the transport and sequential exchangeability conditions are checked, and no convention exists for doing so. Reinforcement learning supplies neither identification nor the missing data.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
What has been tried
No prior work is identified for this problem in the reviewed sources.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Treat sequential-regime comparison as a long-term program that starts from the policy-value contrast rather than from a new definition: specify which policies are being contrasted, in which population, and what compatibility across trials would require. Then specify the longitudinal treatment and confounder data such a comparison needs, and test whether prespecified policies can enter existing network structures as nodes before building bespoke estimators.

title: Reinforcement learning and dynamic regimes for adaptive sequences
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source said. “Reinforcement learning and dynamic treatment regime methods are proposed for comparing adaptive treatment sequences rather than fixed regimens across studies. The report labels this long-term research.”
What was wrong with it. The source said what an indirect comparison of two adaptive strategies even means has not been defined. GPT-5.6 Sol showed the estimand is already definable as a contrast of policy values in a target population, so the open work is cross-study identification, data and convention rather than the definition itself.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: Two-stage Bayesian network meta-analysis of individualized t. New citations: 10.1177/09622802251387430

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no method for indirectly comparing dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences across studies, and no definition of what such an estimand would be in an evidence network. Treatment sequences are modeled in HTA cost-effectiveness models, and dynamic treatment regimes are a mature single-study literature, but the two have not been joined for indirect comparison in anything I retrieved. The entry’s diagnosis is correct on both counts I could check: sequential-regime estimands require longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounder data at the individual level, which trial publications do not contain, and the target of inference changes from a fixed-regimen contrast to a policy over time, so it cannot be attached to existing network structures. This is a negative search result rather than a positive finding, so confidence is moderate; but the claim being made here is weak and well hedged, which is the right posture for a ‘long-term research’ item.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C3, and C4 are supportable in qualified form. A policy contrast is already mathematically definable, for example as the target-population difference between V(pi1)=E[Y under pi1] and V(pi2)=E[Y under pi2]. The assertion that the target of inference has not been defined is therefore false as a general statement. Cross-study identification requires well-defined and compatible policies, treatment histories and outcomes, consistency, positivity, appropriate sequential randomization or exchangeability conditions, and transportability. C2 is also too absolute: longitudinal histories are generally needed for primary estimation, but sequentially randomized designs require different confounding assumptions, and sufficiently detailed regime-level estimates may sometimes support a second-stage synthesis. Existing network machinery could treat prespecified policies as treatment nodes when those conditions hold, although this would not be ordinary fixed-regimen ITC. Reinforcement learning supplies neither identification nor missing data. General PAIC methods remain a legitimate long-term research program, not a current decision-grade requirement.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No cited prior_work. Dynamic treatment regimes and clinical RL are large mature fields for single-source longitudinal IPD (reviews through 2025 on RL for DTRs in healthcare), but they do not define or implement an indirect comparison of adaptive policies across trials that publish only fixed-regimen contrasts and sparse IPD. Search for network meta-analysis / indirect comparison of dynamic treatment regimes or adaptive sequences found no standard estimand definition, required data structure for multi-study sequential comparison, or software path that reuses existing NMA graphs for policy-vs-policy contrasts. C1 remains a long-horizon possibility. C2–C3 correctly state that sequential-regime comparison needs longitudinal treatment and time-varying confounders and is not ordinary fixed-regimen ITC. C4 is a report label consistent with missing estimand and data. title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text: ADJ-18 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Statement
No application of simulation-based inference to bridge disconnected evidence through a mechanistic or pharmacometric model exists, so the entry stands open; the generic method is mature and surveyed (arXiv:1911.01429), and the non-simulation-based version of the idea is already routine in evidence synthesis as model-based meta-analysis and dose-response NMA, where a parametric dose-response curve connects arms that are not directly compared (MBNMAdose). Simulation-based inference approximates posterior, likelihood or likelihood-ratio quantities within a specified simulator; it does not itself identify a bridge, so it can support one only where mechanistic assumptions and data already define it. The misspecification claim needs care: a misspecified simulator does not return a well-calibrated posterior, it returns a posterior calibrated only relative to the wrong model, and the approximation can add miscalibration of its own.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Why it is open
The inferential guarantee is inherited from the simulator, so a mechanistic model that is wrong produces a bridge that carries the error without signaling it. Calibration of the inference procedure itself is computationally expensive and rarely performed, so in practice neither the model nor the approximation is checked. The result is a bridge whose apparent precision is a property of the simulator, the prior and the approximation rather than of the evidence.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Develop simulation-based inference for pharmacometric and disease-process bridges across disconnected evidence, benchmarked against the dose-response and model-based network meta-analysis approaches that already perform the same bridging job with tractable likelihoods. Make simulator-misspecification checks and explicit calibration of the approximation mandatory, and report the bridge’s sensitivity to the mechanistic assumptions alongside the estimate so the inherited error is visible.

title: Simulation-based inference for mechanistic and pharmacometric bridges
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Simulation-based inference is proposed to approximate intractable likelihoods in mechanistic or pharmacometric models, so that disease-process or exposure-response models can act as bridges between disconnected pieces of evidence. The report labels it emerging.”
What was wrong with it. The source said a misspecified simulator returns a well-calibrated posterior for the wrong model; GPT-5.6 Sol corrected this, since calibration holds only relative to the assumed simulator and the approximation adds error of its own. The literature auditor also named the near neighbor the source omitted, dose-response and model-based network meta-analysis, which already bridges arms that are not directly compared.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no application of simulation-based inference to bridge disconnected evidence via a mechanistic or pharmacometric model, so the entry stands open. The generic method is mature and well surveyed (Cranmer, Brehmer & Louppe, ‘The frontier of simulation-based inference’, arXiv:1911.01429), and the adjacent, non-SBI version of the idea already exists in evidence synthesis as model-based meta-analysis and dose-response NMA (MBNMAdose), where a parametric dose-response curve connects arms that are not directly compared; the entry does not mention this near neighbour. The two limitation claims are correct and standard in the SBI literature: the posterior is only as good as the simulator, so a misspecified mechanistic model yields a well-calibrated posterior for the wrong model, and calibration checks of the inference procedure itself are computationally expensive and often skipped. Confidence is moderate because I read surveys and abstracts, not full texts.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C3, C4, and C5 are correct in qualified form. SBI approximates posterior, likelihood, or likelihood-ratio quantities within a specified simulator; it does not itself identify a bridge between disconnected evidence. C2 therefore holds only when mechanistic assumptions and data already define that bridge. Simulator misspecification does not imply that SBI returns a well-calibrated posterior: even an algorithm validated under the simulator is calibrated only relative to that model, while approximation error can introduce additional miscalibration. Posterior precision depends on the observations, simulator, prior, and approximation, not on the simulator alone. Calibration cost is method- and scale-dependent. The PAIC adaptation remains open but is an optional computational roadmap item unless an analysis actually relies on such a mechanistic bridge.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No cited prior_work. Simulation-based / likelihood-free inference is mature in machine learning and physics, and mechanistic/pharmacometric models are standard in model-informed drug development, but search did not find an evaluated SBI pipeline that bridges disconnected trial evidence for ITC/PAIC with mandatory simulator-misspecification checks and calibration reporting tied to a transported effect. C1 is true of SBI in general (capability, not a solved ITC problem). C2 remains a proposal. C3–C4 correctly restate well-known SBI failure modes (misspecified simulator yields calibrated wrong-model posteriors; calibration is expensive and often skipped). C5 is a report maturity label. A proposal-without-ITC-evaluation does not close the problem. Queries: simulation-based inference + (pharmacometric|disease model|meta-analysis|indirect treatment|evidence bridge); likelihood-free MIDD NMA 2023–2026; arXiv stat.ME SBI bridging trials.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text: ADJ-16 Confirmed open High priority Emerging

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Statement
Versioned ontologies for intervention components, doses and schedules already exist: the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology family, built on Basic Formal Ontology and released through OBO Foundry, covers intervention content, delivery mode, source, schedule and dose, setting and target population, with the Behaviour Change Technique Ontology as its content layer (PMC10427801; pmid:33447665), while ATC/DDD, SNOMED, CDISC and COMET cover drugs, doses, trial data structure and outcome sets. What is missing is an ITC-specific vocabulary bound to component network meta-analysis design matrices and effect-modifier definitions, an operational boundary between appropriate and inappropriate LLM roles, and a provenance chain in which every extracted datum carries its source span, an extraction confidence flag and a human verification state through to the analysis object. The LLM half is empirically supported: extraction studies report high headline accuracy alongside errors in roughly one outcome cell in five and observed hallucinations, LLM extraction for evidence synthesis is now evaluated in the methods literature (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710), and provenance is the standard mitigation, though raw model confidence is not calibrated and must not be read as evidence of correctness.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Why it is open
No existing vocabulary is bound to component network meta-analysis design matrices or to effect-modifier definitions, so component coding errors and version drift still enter analyses silently; ontology work produces no effect estimate, so it attracts less methodological effort than estimator work while blocking it. Permitted and forbidden LLM roles produce identical-looking output: a model that suggests candidate modifiers and one that selects them return the same list, and one asked for a missing target correlation supplies a plausible number rather than refusing. Once extracted values reach an analysis dataset they are indistinguishable from hand-curated ones, and no current pipeline, data format or synthesis package carries span-level provenance and verification state through to the analysis object, so the verification regime that would make machine extraction acceptable cannot be checked. The role boundary is a governance proposal rather than a finding, and it has no enforcement mechanism.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




The Behaviour Change Technique Ontology: Transforming the Behaviour Change Technique Taxonomy v1 (2023)
A versioned, OBO-Foundry-aligned ontology of intervention components, part of a family covering delivery mode, schedule and dose, setting and target population. Contradicts the claim that no shared versioned component vocabulary exists; it is not bound to component NMA design matrices.


Ontologies relevant to behaviour change interventions: a method for their development (2021)
Documents the versioning and maintenance methodology behind that ontology family.


Gartlehner et al., Res Synth Methods 2024 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710)
Evaluation of large language model data extraction for evidence synthesis, named by the recency auditor as the reference for the LLM half; extraction studies of this kind report high headline accuracy alongside a material per-cell error rate, which is why provenance and human verification state are the mitigation.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing ontology families rather than starting a new one, binding component, dose, schedule, outcome and modifier terms to component network meta-analysis design matrices and machine-readable analysis specifications. Codify the permitted and forbidden LLM roles as an operational standard, with tooling that structurally prevents moment invention, unreviewed modifier selection, similarity-based transitivity claims and unverified component mappings. Implement a provenance schema in which every extracted datum carries its source span and human verification state into analysis datasets and reporting objects, and keep any model confidence flag labeled as uncalibrated.

title: No ITC component vocabulary or datum-level extraction provenance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “Ontologies, LLM extraction roles, and datum-level provenance” The title lists ontologies as missing, but the audit found the versioned Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology family already covering components, doses and schedules.
The source said. “The machine-readable evidence layer for ITC is missing three things: versioned ontologies and knowledge graphs for treatments, components, doses, outcomes and effect modifiers; an operational boundary between appropriate LLM roles (extraction, ontology population, candidate modifier generation, auditable extraction suggestions, assumption-versus-text comparison) and inappropriate ones (inventing missing target moments, selecting modifiers without expert review, asserting transitivity from semantic similarity, replacing statistical estimation, producing unverified component mappings); and datum-level provenance carrying a source span, a confidence flag and a human verification state.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no shared versioned vocabulary for components, doses, schedules, outcome definitions or modifier definitions. The literature auditor found the Behaviour Change Intervention Ontology family, which is exactly that (PMC10427801; pmid:33447665), so the gap narrows to an ITC-specific vocabulary bound to component design matrices and to the datum-level provenance chain.

What is missing is an ITC-specific vocabulary bound to component NMA design matrices and effect-modifier definitions, and the datum-level provenance chain. The LLM half is well supported empirically: extraction studies report high headline accuracy but errors in roughly one in five outcome cells and observed hallucinations, and provenance/citation is the standard mitigation. The permitted/forbidden role list is a sensible governance proposal, not a finding.

What is missing is an ITC-specific vocabulary bound to component NMA design matrices and effect-modifier definitions, and the datum-level provenance chain. Cites pmc:PMC10427801: A versioned, OBO-Foundry-aligned ontology of intervention components, part of a family covering delivery mode, schedule and dose, setting and target population. Contradicts the claim that no shared versioned component vocabulary exists.. Cites pmid:33447665: Documents the versioning and maintenance methodology behind that ontology family..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1-C3 and C5-C17 are sound as infrastructure and role-boundary claims, provided LLM ontology construction and extraction are treated as assistance rather than authoritative decisions and receive domain review. C18 and C20 are strong provenance requirements. Retaining a confidence flag under C19 can aid auditability, but raw LLM confidence is generally not calibrated and must not be treated as evidence of correctness. The two maturity descriptions in C4 and C21 match the report. The claims that no shared vocabulary or suitable pipeline currently exists are landscape claims, not consequences of statistical theory, and cannot be established under this audit’s technical-only lens. The remaining work is chiefly infrastructure and governance; it is important for scalable automated evidence engineering but not a prerequisite for every manually curated decision-grade analysis.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. No cited prior_work in the problem card. Search of RSM/JCE/medRxiv/arXiv and SR-automation literature shows active LLM extraction for evidence synthesis (e.g. Gartlehner et al., Res Synth Methods 2024, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1710; follow-on Annals 2025 AI-assisted extraction; TrialMind-style pipelines with source linking), and emerging provenance / span-return designs in clinical LLM operations literature, but none of that closes the three-part machine-readable ITC layer as stated. There is still no shared, versioned ontology/KG covering treatments, components, doses/schedules, outcomes, and effect modifiers that ITC/CNMA packages consume; no community operational standard that structurally forbids moment invention, unreviewed modifier selection, similarity-based transitivity, or unverified component maps; and no synthesis package or standard analysis object that propagates span-level source, confidence, and human verification state through to the final ITC/PAIC report. C1–C3 and C5–C17 are proportionate research-agenda framing (ontologies do not identify causal effects; LLMs extract and hallucinate; inventing moments or replacing estimation is inappropriate). title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text: ADJ-14 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Statement
Federated individual-data synthesis is not prospective. DataSHIELD has run privacy-preserving individual-data meta-analysis for years, including federated Cox models for survival (PMC9166323); Bayesian Federated Inference reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries (doi:10.1002/sim.10072; doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.6; arXiv:2402.02898; CRAN package BFI); and federated target-trial emulation is published and validated across 192 hospitals and five health systems (doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y), which confirms the source’s own claim that federated target-trial methods are appearing in clinical research. What is unsolved is the specific object: federated Bayesian ML-NMR, where each posterior draw needs numerical integration over covariate distributions held by different custodians, together with federated posterior predictive checking and characterized approximation error. The ranking claim, that asymmetric individual-data access is the biggest practical limitation in PAIC, is unsupported; it is one major limitation.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Why it is open
Bayesian ML-NMR requires repeated evaluation of a joint likelihood with numerical integration over covariate distributions, and splitting that across custodians who cannot exchange records forces a choice between exact protocols whose cost compounds per sampling iteration and approximations whose posterior error is uncharacterized; general nonlinear ML-NMR also has no finite sufficient statistic to aggregate, so secure exactness is relative to a specified finite-precision computation and threat model. Model checking compounds the problem, because posterior predictive checks normally need the data being predicted and the analyst never sees it. Federation does not remove the reasons the data differ: site heterogeneity in measurement, case mix and definitions persists and is now harder to inspect, and no shared standard supplies harmonized component and outcome definitions. Every participant must also run compatible infrastructure under an agreed protocol, which is an organizational problem before it is a statistical one.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Li et al., Federated target trial emulation using distributed observational data for treatment effect estimation, npj Digital Medicine 2025
Federated protocol design, federated inverse-probability weighting and federated Cox models across 192 hospitals and five health systems; the reference for the entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing.


dsSurvival: Privacy preserving survival models for federated individual patient meta-analysis in DataSHIELD (2022)
Federated individual-data meta-analysis for survival outcomes without pooling records. Does not cover ML-NMR’s integration over covariate distributions or federated posterior predictive checks.


Jonker, Pazira & Coolen, Bayesian federated inference for estimating statistical models based on non-shared multicenter data sets, Stat Med 2024
Reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries, without sharing patient-level records.


Bayesian Federated Inference for regression models based on non-shared medical center data, Res Synth Methods 2025
Extends Bayesian federated inference to regression models under heterogeneous populations.


Bayesian Federated Inference for regression models based on non-shared multicenter data sets from heterogeneous populations (preprint, 2024)
Preprint with details of the federated regression construction and package illustration.


BFI (R package)
Shipped implementation of Bayesian federated inference, so the machinery is available rather than prospective.

title: Federated ML-NMR and federated model checking do not exist
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the federated Bayesian machinery that exists rather than building federation from scratch: apply Bayesian Federated Inference and DataSHIELD-style protocols to ML-NMR’s integration step, and characterize exact versus approximate distributed computation so the approximation error is known rather than assumed small. Define federated posterior predictive checks, handle site-specific missingness and measurement, harmonize component and outcome definitions, and quantify secure-computation cost against the analytic gain. Treat asymmetric individual-data access as one major constraint among several rather than as the ranking premise for the program.
