Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Federated and secure computation for multi-sponsor IPD synthesis” The title treats federated computation for multi-sponsor IPD synthesis as prospective, but the audit found federated Bayesian inference, survival meta-analysis and target-trial emulation already published.
The source said. “Asymmetric IPD access is named the biggest practical limitation in PAIC. Federated learning and secure multiparty computation are proposed so that trial custodians contribute gradients, likelihood summaries or exact secure sufficient statistics instead of row-level records, letting ML-NMR and other IPD models be fitted across sponsors and jurisdictions.”
What was wrong with it. The source described federated learning and secure computation as proposals and called asymmetric individual-data access the biggest practical limitation in PAIC. Auditors found federated Bayesian inference, federated survival meta-analysis and federated target-trial emulation already published, and GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the superlative as an uncited comparative claim; what remains open is federated ML-NMR and federated model checking.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Federated IPD evidence synthesis is not prospective: DataSHIELD has run privacy-preserving IPD meta-analysis across sites for years, including federated Cox models for survival IPD meta-analysis (dsSurvival, PMC9166323), where ‘the individual-level data remain within each site and only non-disclosive aggregated data are shared’. The entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods ‘are already appearing in clinical research’ is confirmable and should be cited: ‘Federated target trial emulation using distributed observational data for treatment effect estimation’ (npj Digital Medicine 2025, doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y), validated across 192 hospitals (eICU/MIMIC-IV) and five NYC health systems. What is genuinely unsolved is the specific object: federated Bayesian ML-NMR, where each posterior draw requires numerical integration over covariate distributions held at different custodians, and federated posterior predictive checking. The caveat is the superlative ‘Asymmetric IPD access is the biggest practical limitation in PAIC’, which I could not verify against any source that ranks limitations. Cites doi:10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y: Supplies a real reference for the entry’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing; federated protocol design, federated IPTW and federated Cox across 192 hospitals.. Cites pmc:PMC9166323: Covers federated IPD meta-analysis for survival outcomes without pooling records. Does not cover ML-NMR’s integration over covariate distributions or federated posterior predictive checks..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is an unsupported comparative superlative; asymmetric IPD access is a major limitation, not demonstrably the biggest. C2 and C7 are feasible when site likelihoods decompose and custodians agree on a common model and protocol. C13 needs qualification: general nonlinear ML-NMR has no universal finite sufficient statistic, and SMPC exactness is relative to the specified finite-precision computation and threat model, although secure aggregation of local likelihood or gradient evaluations is possible. C3 describes facilitation, not access itself. C4 through C6 and the qualified forms of C14 and C15 are sound. C8 through C10 are too broad as open theoretical claims: exact distributed likelihood evaluation, local posterior-predictive discrepancies, and missing-data models are conceptually available, while model-specific approximation error, privacy-preserving checks, measurement harmonization, and implementation remain open. C11 is an uncited literature-state claim outside this audit’s permitted evidence, C12 is promotional, and C16 accurately reports the labels. Federated ML-NMR adaptation remains open and potentially high-value, but Very high is a roadmap priority rather than a demonstrated decision-grade severity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Federated Bayesian analysis of non-pooled multi-center IPD is no longer only speculative: Bayesian Federated Inference (BFI) reconstructs what a pooled Bayesian analysis would have found from local posterior summaries without sharing records (Jonker, Pazira, Coolen, Statistics in Medicine 2024; Research Synthesis Methods 2025 regression extension; CRAN package BFI; survival extension 2025). Federated target-trial emulation for distributed observational treatment-effect estimation is also published (Li et al., npj Digital Medicine 2025), confirming the report’s claim that federated target-trial methods are already appearing in clinical research. These works partially resolve C2, C3, C11, and parts of C7/C14 for multi-center regression-style and TTE analyses. They do not close federated ML-NMR: repeated joint likelihood evaluation with numerical integration over covariate distributions, characterized exact-vs-approximate distributed Bayesian error, federated posterior predictive checks when the analyst never sees the data, harmonized component/outcome definitions, or SMPC cost characterization specific to evidence-synthesis MCMC. Site heterogeneity and governance remain unsolved by federation itself (C4–C6 still hold). Asymmetric IPD access remains a dominant practical PAIC constraint; calling it the single biggest limitation is slightly absolute but directionally supported. Cites 10.1002/sim.10072: Establishes BFI so multi-center Bayesian models can be combined from local inferences without sharing patient-level data.. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.6: Extends BFI to regression models under heterogeneous populations; CRAN BFI software.. Cites arXiv:2402.02898: Preprint/details for BFI regression and package illustration.. Cites 10.1038/s41746-025-01803-y: Demonstrates federated target-trial methods in clinical research, as the report claims..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Statement
Most of the quantities this entry calls computable but not computed are computed and published. Connectivity and minimal path length between treatments are in Thom et al. (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329); contrast-specific evidence paths and per-study contribution are in Papakonstantinou et al. (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3) and shipped as netmeta::netcontrib; component estimability has a signal-flow graph in Li, Shih and Tu (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), written in answer to the same complaint this entry makes; and precision-based ranking of the next study design is in Nikolakopoulou et al. (doi:10.1002/sim.6608). The development package cpaic, which lives on GitHub and cannot be installed from CRAN, already computes connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast estimability and contrast-specific edge influence. What is genuinely open is that these diagnostics are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, that articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration are still missing, and that there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study’s individual data to acquire.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Why it is open
The quantities exist in papers and in scattered implementations but not in standard NMA output, so an analysis can rest entirely on one articulation edge or one study without that dependence appearing anywhere a reviewer would see it. Component networks are worse, because information flows through the component design matrix rather than through visible treatment edges; note also that null-space dimension is a linear-algebra property of that matrix rather than a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not settle whether a requested contrast is estimable. Acquisition decisions remain informal because expected information gain and the value of individual-data placement cannot come from topology alone: they require a target contrast and population, a sampling model, priors and a decision utility, and no such machinery has been built for evidence networks. Design also cannot substitute for data, since where no evidence exists for the required contrast an optimal design still requires someone to collect it.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Automated methods to test connectedness and quantify indirectness of evidence in network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124
Graph algorithms for connectivity, indirect connection and minimal path length between treatments, covering the articulation and minimal-bridge questions, with R and Stata code.


Papakonstantinou et al., Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Res 2018;7:610
Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, that is, vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib.


Li, Shih & Tu, Graphical evaluation of evidence structure within a component network meta-analysis, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607
Signal-flow graph over components showing which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence, written in response to the same complaint this entry makes about component networks.


Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti, Planning future studies based on the precision of network meta-analysis results, Stat Med 2016;35:219
Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, covering the design-prioritization half of this entry.


netmeta::netcontrib reference manual
Shipped implementation of the contribution matrix in network meta-analysis, evidence that per-study contribution is available to practitioners today.


Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio & Welton, Value of Information for Clinical Trial Design: The Importance of Considering All Relevant Comparators, PharmacoEconomics 2024
Value-of-information trial design that accounts for the full comparator set, the natural starting point for ranking candidate bridging studies by expected decision value.


cpaic connectivity, estimability and edge-influence diagnostics (development package, GitHub commit 9d150e9)
Unreleased development package, not installable from CRAN. Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, per-contrast row-space estimability, and a contrast-specific edge-influence diagnostic that reports whether individual data inform the contrast at all.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Make the existing diagnostics routine rather than rebuilding them: bring connectivity, contribution, component estimability and design-precision tools into standard reporting for treatment and component networks, and add what is genuinely missing, articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration. Build expected-value-of-information methods on top by specifying the target contrast, population, sampling model, priors and decision utility, so candidate new edges, individual-data acquisitions and bridging studies can be scored by their effect on identification and on the decision. Existing value-of-information work for multi-comparator trial design (doi:10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0) is the natural starting point.

title: Routine NMA output omits graph diagnostics and value of information
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Connectivity, evidence-flow contribution, component estimability graphs and precision-based design of the next trial are all published and partly implemented in netmeta; what is missing is that they are not routinely reported in NMA outputs, and there is no value-of-information machinery for deciding which study’s IPD to acquire.
The source titled this. “Graph and value-of-information diagnostics for network design” The title names graph diagnostics as an open item, but the audit found connectivity, evidence-flow and component-estimability methods published and partly shipped in netmeta.
The source said. “The report lists computable structural quantities that evidence and component networks should report (articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific paths of component information, vulnerability to removal of a study or component, centrality of IPD placement, expected information gain from adding an edge) and proposes Bayesian experimental design and active learning to rank which IPD to acquire or which bridging trial to run.”
What was wrong with it. The source listed articulation treatments, minimal bridge sets, null-space dimension, contrast-specific information paths and vulnerability to study removal as computable but not computed. The literature auditor found four published methods covering most of them, one of which ships in netmeta, and GPT-5.6 Sol found rank, null space, bridging components, per-contrast estimability and edge influence already implemented in the unreleased cpaic development package; what survives is routine reporting and value of information for individual-data acquisition.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Corrected

statement: corrected a factual claim netmeta exports netimpact(), which measures a study’s importance by the loss of precision when it is removed, citing Rucker et al. 2020. Removal vulnerability has shipped on CRAN for years and does not belong on a list of what is missing. Previously: “Most of the quantities this entry calls computable but not computed are computed and published. Connectivity and minimal path length between treatments are in Thom et al. (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329); contrast-specific evidence paths and per-study contribution are in Papakonstantinou et al. (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3) and shipped as netmeta::netcontrib; component estimability has a signal-flow graph in Li, Shih and Tu (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), written in answer to the same complaint this entry makes; and precision-based ranking of the next study design is in Nikolakopoulou et al. (doi:10.10”

Corrected

proposed_direction: corrected a factual claim Same correction as the statement: removal vulnerability is implemented. Previously: “Make the existing diagnostics routine rather than rebuilding them: bring connectivity, contribution, component estimability and design-precision tools into standard reporting for treatment and component networks, and add what is genuinely missing, articulation and minimal cut-set enumeration and removal vulnerability. Build expected-value-of-information methods on top by specifying the target contrast, population, sampling model, priors and decision utility, so candidate new edges, individual-data acquisitions and bridging studies can be scored by their effect on identification and on the deci”

closure-upheld

10 findings from the reading assert this problem is open; the closure was re-examined and stands Put to an independent reviewer with the closing auditors’ reasoning, the work they relied on, and the new findings in view together. The findings overwhelmingly establish poor routine reporting and incomplete uptake, not that connectivity, contribution, estimability, or next-study design methods are unavailable. They therefore restate the closure’s surviving claim that existing diagnostics are scattered and not standard output. None disputes the cited graph, evidence-flow, component-estimability, or precision-based design work, and none provides the still-missing IPD-acquisition value-of-information machinery. The evidence is thus weaker than, or fully encompassed by, the closure’s counterevidence and residual. (reviewer confidence: high)

Flagged for reopening

24 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Most of the listed ‘computable but not computed’ quantities are computed, published and shipped. Connectivity, indirect connection and the minimum number of steps between a treatment pair: Thom, White, Welton & Lu, Res Synth Methods 2019;10:113-124 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329), with R code and a Stata implementation. Contrast-specific paths of information and vulnerability to removing a study: Papakonstantinou et al., F1000Res 2018;7:610 (doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3), the proportion contribution matrix, shipped as netmeta::netcontrib. Component estimability specifically: Li, Shih & Tu, Res Synth Methods 2023;14:596-607 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623), a signal-flow graph over components, motivated by the exact complaint in this entry’s why_open. Freeman et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023;23:208) add CNMA-UpSet, heat map and circle plots. Design-side: Nikolakopoulou, Mavridis & Salanti (Stat Med 2016;35:219, doi:10.1002/sim.6608) compute which study design and sample size to run next from NMA precision, extended in Trials 2019 (doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2). Genuinely open: null-space dimension reporting, centrality of IPD placement, and formal VOI for IPD acquisition. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1329: Graph algorithms for connectivity, indirect connection and minimal path length between treatments, i.e. articulation and minimal-bridge questions.. Cites doi:10.12688/f1000research.14770.3: Contrast-specific paths of evidence and per-study contribution, i.e. vulnerability to removal of a study; implemented as netmeta::netcontrib.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1623: Directly answers the component-network complaint: a signal-flow graph over components that shows which component effects are identifiable and which need more evidence.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.6608: Ranks candidate future study designs and sample sizes from network structure and precision, i.e. the design-prioritization half of this entry..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is straightforward for articulation treatments, but an articulation component needs an explicit bipartite or hypergraph definition and is not equivalent to statistical estimability. C2 and structural leave-one-out versions of C6 are computable once the bridge set is defined. C3 is a design-matrix linear-algebra calculation, not a graph algorithm, and nullity alone does not determine a requested contrast. C4 requires a model and weighting rule and can be non-unique in cyclic or rank-deficient networks. C5 and C7 cannot be obtained from topology alone: expected information gain and the inferential value of IPD require a target contrast and population, sampling model, sample size, overlap, priors, and usually a decision utility. C8 through C10 are sound with those ingredients, and C11 reports the source label. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, cpaic_connectivity already returns connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, rank, null space, and per-contrast estimability, while edge_influence reports contrast-specific edge weights and whether IPD placement informs the contrast. Thus the blanket claim that the quantities are not computed is false, although articulation or cut-set enumeration, removal vulnerability, and model-based value-of-information design remain open. Very high is justified for estimability and fragility diagnostics, not for the entire active-learning bundle. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements treatment-network connectedness, subnetworks, bridging components, component-design rank and null space, and per-contrast row-space estimability.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements a contrast-specific estimating-weight diagnostic and identifies whether an IPD edge contributes to the requested contrast..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Pieces of the agenda already exist; the integrated reporting-and-design stack does not. Value-of-information methods for multi-comparator / network-aware research prioritization and trial design are active (e.g. Heath, Manolopoulou, Baio, Welton, PharmacoEconomics 2024 on VOI when all relevant comparators matter; longer Welton/Ades-style EVSI tradition). That partially substantiates ranking candidate bridging trials or evidence acquisitions by expected information for decision. Graph algorithms can in principle compute articulation points, bridges, and related connectivity; NMA practice already has leave-one-out / influence style checks and geometry plots (netmeta and CINeMA ecosystem). What remains open is the report’s full computable suite as standard output: articulation treatments and components, minimal bridge sets, component-design-matrix null-space dimension, contrast-specific component information paths, IPD-placement centrality, and design scores tied to those quantities. I found no 2024–2026 package release or merged PR that implements that diagnostic battery for treatment and component networks as routine reporting. Design still cannot invent missing likelihood for a contrast. Cites 10.1007/s40273-024-01372-0: Shows VOI-based trial design should account for the full comparator set (network-relevant), supporting information-gain ranking of new evidence relative to multi-arm decision problems.. Cites 10.1002/sim.10072: Not a graph-diagnostic resolver; listed only if needed for multi-source computation. Prefer omit if empty required—use only VOI paper as primary..

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Statement
The study-aware causal forest already exists: Multi-Study Causal Forest (arXiv:2502.02110) is built to borrow individual patient data across studies when the sources of heterogeneity differ, and causal forests are routinely fitted to pooled multi-trial individual data. What is not done is aggregating the fitted conditional average treatment effect to an external HTA target population inside an indirect comparison, and no work applies causal discovery to a treatment network. Neither method selects a causally sufficient transport adjustment set, resolves unmeasured transport bias, or stays reliable with sparse events and few informative environments, so both remain hypothesis-generation aids.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Why it is open
Aggregating a fitted conditional effect to a declared target distribution needs the target covariate distribution, overlap and a transport argument, none of which the forest supplies. Discovered heterogeneity can reflect between-study differences rather than modification, and neither method distinguishes a causal interaction from one induced by an unadjusted study-level factor. Causal discovery returns observationally equivalent graphs with different transport implications; randomized treatments can orient some edges, but nothing in the output selects an adjustment set or certifies transportability. The identifying signal for cross-study structure is the number of distinct environments, and evidence networks supply few.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Multi-Study Causal Forest (MCF): A flexible framework for data borrowing in the presence of varying treatment effect heterogeneity (2025)
Covers the study-aware causal forest for effect-modifier discovery across studies. Does not cover aggregation of the fitted conditional effect to an external target population within an indirect comparison.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Take the existing multi-study causal forest and add what an indirect comparison needs: standardization of the fitted conditional effect to a declared external target distribution, with overlap and transport assumptions stated. Quantify how many trials and events are required before discovered structure is stable, and validate against known-truth simulations. Treat all output as candidate hypotheses for expert review and sensitivity analysis, requiring external confirmation before a discovered modifier enters an adjustment set.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Our study

Modifier discovery across trials: no penalty is both stable and powerful, and study-level heterogeneity creates a false modifier that more trials entrench
The question put to it. Are effect modifiers discovered from pooled trial data stable and correct enough to use, and do study-level confounders create false modifiers that more data do not remove?
What it found. No. Lasso discovery at the minimum-error penalty found the true modifiers but added 1.7 to 2.8 false ones among seven null covariates, and sets from independent datasets agreed with Jaccard similarity 0.37 to 0.57; the one-standard-error rule was stable only by selecting nothing (a single modifier found in 3% to 5% of analyses). With an unmeasured study-level cause of effect heterogeneity, pooled discovery selected the covariate whose trial means tracked it in 69% of analyses with 3 trials and 93% with 12 at the same total size, and raised false discoveries among the other covariates from 1.7 to 2.8 per analysis to 3.6 to 3.9; trial-specific treatment effects removed both.
Results.

Usability condition (stability at least 0.8 with at most 0.5 false modifiers in every cell) failed for every method and penalty.
Pooled minimum-error discovery selected the confounded covariate in 0.69, 0.81, 0.93 of analyses with 3, 6, 12 trials (one true modifier); within-trial discovery 0.14 to 0.46, the rate of any null covariate.
Pooled minimum-error target bias under confounding 0.023 to 0.057; one-standard-error rule biased toward no modification by 0.09 to 0.21.

Design.

Estimand

Selection of true and false effect modifiers, stability of the selected set, and the target mean difference at covariate means 0.5

Methods compared

pooled lasso, minimum-CV penalty, pooled lasso, one-SE rule, within-trial lasso, minimum-CV penalty, within-trial lasso, one-SE rule

Data-generating mechanism

Three to twelve trials at a fixed total of 2400 patients, one or three true modifiers among ten candidates, study-level confounding absent or present; pooled and within-trial lasso at two penalty rules; power, false discoveries, stability and target error. 12 cells, 300 replicates each.

Replicates

300 per cell, 12 cells, two datasets per replicate


What this does not answer. Lasso only (no multi-study causal forests); continuous outcome; linear modification; one overlap level; post-selection inference for the target not studied here. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: Data-driven modifier and causal-structure discovery with few trials
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Study-aware causal forests are proposed to discover effect modifiers and aggregate conditional average treatment effects to a target population, and causal discovery algorithms to generate candidate DAGs and interaction structures across studies. Both are offered as replacements for pre-specified modifier lists but are labeled hypothesis-generation aids rather than selection procedures.”
What was wrong with it. The source proposed study-aware causal forests as something still to develop and labeled them ‘Promising-emerging’; the literature auditor found a published multi-study causal forest (arXiv:2502.02110), so the forest half is not awaiting adaptation and the open part is aggregation to an external target. GPT-5.6 Sol also corrected the claim that few trials and rare events compromise validity: they damage power, stability and calibration, while a large randomized trial can still identify within-trial conditional effects.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The ‘study-aware causal forest’ is already published: ‘Multi-Study Causal Forest (MCF): A flexible framework for data borrowing in the presence of varying treatment effect heterogeneity’ (arXiv:2502.02110), which is explicitly built to borrow individual patient data across studies when the sources of heterogeneity differ. Causal forests are also routinely fitted to pooled multi-trial IPD (e.g. the type 2 diabetes application, BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2023; the psychiatry tutorial, Int J Methods Psychiatr Res 2025). So the forest half is not a proposal awaiting adaptation; what remains open is aggregating the fitted CATE to an external HTA target population inside an indirect comparison. I found nothing applying causal discovery to a treatment network, and the entry’s limitations (few trials, rare events, observational equivalence of returned graphs, inability to distinguish modification from between-study confounding) are all standard and correct. The caveat is the ‘Promising-emerging’ label for causal forests, which understates the multi-study work already done. Cites arxiv:2502.02110: Covers the study-aware causal forest for effect-modifier discovery across studies. Does not cover aggregation of the CATE to an external target population within an indirect comparison..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 is feasible with sufficiently large randomized IPD, study-aware fitting or splitting, overlap, and a declared target covariate distribution. C2 is not a guaranteed improvement, and C3 confuses low information with validity: few trials and rare events primarily damage power, stability, calibration, and transport assessment, while a large randomized trial can still identify within-trial CATEs. C4 is correct for unmeasured transport factors. C5 and C6 are defensible only as candidate generation. C7 holds for purely observational discovery without added interventional, temporal, functional-form, or background-knowledge restrictions; randomized treatments and multiple interventions can orient some edges, so observational equivalence does not categorically prevent all orientation. C8 applies when cross-study shifts are the identifying signal, not simply because the individual-level sample came from few trials. C9 and C10 reproduce the labels. Calling either approach a replacement for pre-specified, causally justified modifiers is unsound, and Medium-high is inflated for tools restricted to hypothesis generation.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Causal forests are actively used on single RCTs and in multi-study synthesis contexts (e.g. Van Vogt et al. 2025 BMC Medical Research Methodology application; broader multi-study causal ML surveys 2024), and causal discovery remains a general tool for candidate DAGs. Neither closes the stated ITC problem. Forests still need substantial within-study signal and do not remove hidden confounding or certify that discovered heterogeneity is modification rather than study-level confounding; discovery still returns observationally equivalent graphs with different transport implications. No 2024–2026 work makes study-aware causal forests or multi-study discovery a reliable adjustment-set selector under typical NMA study counts and rare events. Treating output as hypothesis generation (as the report does) is still the honest status. Queries: causal forest network meta-analysis; study-aware causal forest IPD meta-analysis; causal discovery multi-trial transportability.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text: ADJ-08 Overstated High priority Promising

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Statement
Both halves of this machinery are long established in evidence synthesis rather than emerging. Bayesian nonparametric random effects for non-normal heterogeneity go back to Burr and Doss (JASA 2005) and Branscum and Hanson (pmid:18162115), with a 2024 review and simulation study of meta-analysis models that relax normality (arXiv:2412.12945); commensurate priors are already in NMA (JRSS-C 2018;67:1047) and robust mixture priors are standard (pmid:25355546). What is unvalidated is their use to bridge a disconnected subnetwork: with no shared contrast the commensurability parameter has nothing to be identified from, and the posterior for the cross-gap contrast is supplied by the assumed bridge and its prior.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Why it is open
Across a disconnected gap there is no likelihood contribution for the contrast of interest, so the posterior in that direction is determined by the assumed bridge and its prior, even where other parameters remain data-informed. A nonparametric prior aggravates the presentation problem because it looks agnostic while still supplying the structure that produces a finite estimate. Dynamic borrowing normally lets the data adjudicate how similar two sources are, but with no shared contrast there is nothing to adjudicate with, so the commensurability parameter is weakly identified. The exchangeability assumption that licenses the borrowing cannot be tested from the disconnected data, though it can be calibrated externally.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Branscum & Hanson, Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis using Polya tree mixture models, Biometrics 2008
Shows that flexible non-normal random-effects distributions in evidence synthesis are an established rather than emerging capability.


Power and Commensurate Priors for Synthesizing Aggregate and Individual Patient Level Data in Network Meta-Analysis, JRSS-C 2018;67:1047
Commensurate priors for controlled borrowing already exist inside NMA; the novelty in this entry is confined to the disconnected case.


arXiv:2412.12945 (2024 methodological systematic review and simulation study of meta-analysis models relaxing the random-effects normality assumption)
Reviews and evaluates meta-analysis models that relax the normal random-effects assumption, further evidence that the flexible-heterogeneity half is mature.


Schmidli et al. (pmid:25355546), robust mixture meta-analytic-predictive priors
Robust mixture priors for dynamic borrowing from historical controls, named by the literature auditor as the standard reference for the robust-prior half.


jarbes (R package)
Named by the recency auditor as shipped Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis tooling, evidence that the machinery is available rather than prospective.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use nonparametric mixtures and commensurate or robust-mixture priors where the network is connected and the likelihood can inform them, and where it is disconnected require an explicit prior-versus-likelihood decomposition reporting how much of the estimate comes from the prior. Calibrate externally in settings where the bridge can be checked, for example by severing edges in connected networks and comparing the borrowed estimate against the known contrast. The contribution is the disconnected-gap protocol and its calibration evidence, not the priors, which already exist.

title: Nonparametric and commensurate priors in disconnected evidence
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Bayesian nonparametric random-effects models and commensurate/robust priors are established tools in meta-analysis and NMA; what is unvalidated is their use to bridge a disconnected subnetwork, where the commensurability parameter has no shared contrast to be identified from.
The source said. “Bayesian nonparametric priors are proposed for flexible study and population mixtures and for non-normal random-effects distributions, and commensurate or robust-mixture priors for letting a disconnected subnetwork borrow imperfectly from another rather than assuming full exchangeability or full independence. Both place additional structure in the prior at precisely the point where the likelihood is silent.”
What was wrong with it. The source labeled Bayesian nonparametrics ‘Emerging’ and commensurate priors ‘Promising’ and treated both as proposals; the literature auditor showed they have been in use in evidence synthesis for one to two decades (pmid:18162115; JRSS-C 2018;67:1047; pmid:25355546). Only the disconnected-subnetwork application is novel, and GPT-5.6 Sol added that a proper posterior in a likelihood-unidentified direction should not be called identification.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Both halves of the ‘proposed’ machinery are long established in evidence synthesis, which makes the maturity labels wrong. Bayesian nonparametric random effects in meta-analysis date to Burr & Doss (JASA 2005) and Branscum & Hanson, ‘Bayesian nonparametric meta-analysis using Polya tree mixture models’ (Biometrics 2008, PMID 18162115); a 2024 methodological systematic review plus simulation study of meta-analysis models relaxing the random-effects normality assumption exists (arXiv:2412.12945). Commensurate priors are already in NMA: ‘Power and Commensurate Priors for Synthesizing Aggregate and Individual Patient Level Data in Network Meta-Analysis’ (JRSS-C 2018;67:1047), and robust mixture MAP priors are standard (Schmidli et al., PMID 25355546). So ‘Emerging’ for Bayesian nonparametrics and ‘Promising’ for commensurate priors both understate maturity by 10-20 years. What is genuinely open is the disconnected-subnetwork application, and the entry’s diagnosis is corroborated: work on Bayesian disconnected NMA finds the standard approach unusable under vague priors and dependent on moderately informative ones, i.e. the posterior for the disconnected contrast is prior-driven. Cites pmid:18162115: Flexible non-normal random-effects distributions in evidence synthesis are an established, not emerging, capability.. Cites https://academic.oup.com/jrsssc/article/67/4/1047/7058351: Commensurate priors for controlled borrowing already exist inside NMA; the novelty in this entry is confined to the disconnected case..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 and C4 are technically sound capabilities. C2 and C5 are conditional, not guaranteed improvements: flexible or robust priors trade parametric restriction for prior and hyperparameter sensitivity and need enough likelihood information. C3 should not call a proper posterior identification. For a contrast outside the likelihood-identified subspace, the hierarchical or bridge prior supplies the otherwise unidentified direction, although other parameters can remain data-informed. C6 is too absolute. Exchangeability for the actual missing cross-gap contrast cannot be tested by that disconnected likelihood, but empirical calibration is possible with external or connected networks and edge-severing exercises, as the proposed direction itself recognizes. C7 and C8 accurately reproduce the report’s labels. Transparent prior attribution and sensitivity remain open and are decision-critical only when the target decision uses a cross-gap posterior; the general High priority is otherwise a roadmap judgment.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search finds mature building blocks, not a closed ITC gap. Bayesian nonparametric mixtures for flexible random-effects / non-normal heterogeneity exist in pairwise meta-analysis (Dirichlet-process / DPM style work; recent bias-corrected BNP in Biometrical Journal 2025; CRAN jarbes). Commensurate and robust-mixture dynamic borrowing are well established for historical controls when a shared endpoint/likelihood contributes information (Hobbs et al.; recent robust-mixture / SAM literature 2023–2025). None of this removes the structural fact that a disconnected contrast has no likelihood contribution for the bridge: the posterior remains prior-driven, and the commensurability parameter is weakly identified when there is no shared contrast with which to adjudicate similarity. I found no 2024–2026 NMA/ITC paper or multinma/crossnma/gemtc/netmeta feature that validates exchangeability across a disconnected subnetwork gap or that supplies an accepted prior-versus-likelihood decomposition for that case. C1 and C4 are true as method existence claims outside pure disconnected ITC; C3 and C6 correctly describe why the problem remains open; maturity labels C7/C8 are report-internal taxonomy and were not re-verified against a report file. Queries: Bayesian nonparametric Dirichlet process NMA; commensurate/robust mixture disconnected NMA; crossnma disconnected borrowing; jarbes BC-BNP.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text: ADJ-06 Confirmed open Very high priority Promising

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Statement
Instead of picking one synthetic target distribution consistent with the reported marginals, distributionally robust optimization would define the set of laws whose moments lie in the admissible moment set and which sit within a divergence distance of a reference distribution, then report the infimum and supremum of the treatment effect over that set. No work in evidence synthesis does this; the generic machinery exists elsewhere, including distributionally robust generalization of heterogeneous treatment effects across sites (arXiv:2412.11136) and distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation (arXiv:2512.12781), but none takes reported marginal means and proportions as moment constraints and bounds a PAIC effect. Two limits belong in the statement: the bounded set is the intersection of the moment constraints and the divergence ball, so it is not an interval over every moment-compatible law, and the resulting range describes target-law ambiguity rather than sampling uncertainty.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Why it is open
Current practice fixes the unreported correlation and tail structure by fiat when it reconstructs a target distribution, so a point estimate hides a family of equally compatible target laws, and for non-collapsible measures the marginal effect depends on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables (arXiv:2210.01757). Computing the bounds means optimizing an effect functional over an infinite-dimensional constrained set, and the bounds can be infinite or undefined if outcome behavior outside the observed support is left unrestricted. The ambiguity set has no accepted calibration: a loose set contains implausible target laws and gives an interval too wide to inform a decision, while a tight set encodes an unverifiable assumption, so justifying the set reintroduces the judgment the method was meant to remove.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




arXiv:2412.11136 (distributionally robust generalization of heterogeneous treatment effects across sites, minimax regret over a multisite uncertainty set)
Generic machinery the entry would draw on: distributionally robust optimization over a set of plausible target distributions. Does not take published marginal summaries as moment constraints.


arXiv:2512.12781 (distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation)
Generic distributionally robust treatment-effect estimation. Does not bound a PAIC effect over target laws compatible with reported summaries.


Remiro-Azocar, Transportability of model-based estimands in evidence synthesis, Stat Med 2024;43(22):4217-4249
Establishes that marginal effects for non-collapsible measures depend on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables, which is why unreported dependence structure matters here.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define the ambiguity set from the admissible target moment set plus a divergence ball around a reference distribution, and report the induced interval as target-law ambiguity, labeled separately from sampling uncertainty. Develop tractable optimization for the infimum and supremum, restrict outcome behavior outside the observed support so the bounds stay finite, and establish conventions for the divergence radius. Build elicitation and justification procedures for the set so it can survive review in a real submission, applying the method first where the effect measure is non-collapsible or interactions are nonlinear.

title: Distributionally robust bounds over compatible target laws
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Instead of picking one synthetic target distribution consistent with the reported marginals, distributionally robust optimization would define the set of distributions whose moments lie in the admissible moment set and which sit within a divergence distance of a reference distribution, then report the infimum and supremum of the treatment effect over that set. This is a direct treatment of uncertainty in unreported correlations and tails.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed two claims: the reported range covers only the intersection of the moment constraints and the divergence ball rather than all moment-compatible laws, and non-collapsibility makes marginal effects depend on the covariate distribution without guaranteeing a wide range. The source also cited nothing for the generic machinery it draws on; the auditors named it.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I searched for distributionally robust bounds constructed from an ambiguity set of target laws consistent with published summary statistics and found nothing in evidence synthesis. What exists is the generic machinery the entry would draw on: DRO over plausible target distributions for generalizing heterogeneous treatment effects across sites (arXiv:2412.11136, minimax regret over a multisite uncertainty set), DRO treatment-effect estimation (arXiv:2512.12781), and Wasserstein ambiguity sets whose radius calibration is itself an active problem. None of these takes reported marginal means and proportions as moment constraints and reports the infimum and supremum of a PAIC effect over the compatible set, which is the entry’s specific proposal. The entry’s stated obstacles are also accurate: the ambiguity-set calibration problem is acknowledged in the DRO literature, and the dependence of non-collapsible effects on unreported joint structure is established (Remiro-Azocar, arXiv:2210.01757, shows marginal effects for non-collapsible measures depend on the joint distribution of modifiers and prognostic variables). I read abstracts only, hence the moderate confidence.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The proposed optimization is mathematically coherent when the ambiguity set is nonempty, the target effect functional is identified and integrable over its support, and the extrema exist. It can expose sensitivity to unreported dependence and tail behavior. The bounded set is the intersection of the moment constraints and divergence ball, however, so C3 is not literally an interval over every moment-compatible law. Divergence direction, reference support and radius can strongly constrain which correlations and tails vary. Non-collapsibility makes marginal effects depend on the prognostic covariate distribution, but does not guarantee a wide range. The resulting bounds describe target-law ambiguity, not sampling uncertainty, and can be infinite or undefined if outcome behavior outside observed support is unrestricted. Calibration and computation remain genuine open work.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Distributionally robust and ambiguity-set methods for treatment effects under model or distributional risk appear in general causal/ML venues, but no retrieved PAIC/HTA method defines an ambiguity set from published target moments plus a divergence ball, optimizes inf/sup of the target-population effect for non-collapsible measures or nonlinear interactions, calibrates the radius for reimbursement use, and ships software usable with MAIC/STC/ML-NMR. The report’s institutional caveats (loose sets uninformative; tight sets reintroduce judgment) remain live. Queries: DRO treatment effect target population moments; distributionally robust PAIC MAIC; ambiguity set covariate correlations tails causal; RSM/SiM/Value Health 2024–2026 DRO ITC.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R12:supported

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text: ADJ-04 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Statement
No published STC or ML-NMR analysis uses BART or a Gaussian process as the outcome surface, so that adaptation is open. All the proposals share one limit: standardizing a fitted surface over a target distribution with mass outside the source support is extrapolation however flexible the learner, and BART’s behavior outside the observed support is prior-driven rather than evidential (arXiv:2204.10963). The conformal half needs narrowing. Ordinary split-conformal prediction does not itself detect unsupported covariate profiles, since an interval can keep the same width far outside source support, and the covariate-shift repair already exists: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes and Ramdas (NeurIPS 2019) show the guarantee rests on exchangeability and restore it by likelihood-ratio weighting, which is the natural route with PAIC weights.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Why it is open
A flexible learner fits only where data exist; outside that region BART’s priors and a Gaussian process’s kernel and prior mean produce plausible predictions and prior-driven intervals that are modeling artifacts, and Gaussian-process uncertainty is calibrated conditional on the kernel, prior and likelihood rather than automatically. Fitted interactions are predictive structure rather than identified effect modification. Conformal coverage does not transfer under the covariate shift a transport problem creates by construction, and the weighted repair needs estimable density ratios and target support, which is exactly what is in doubt. Gaussian-process inference also scales poorly in data and integration points, which collides with the numerical integration burden already present in ML-NMR.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift, NeurIPS 2019
Canonical source for the claim that conformal coverage does not transfer under shift, and supplies the likelihood-ratio-weighted repair that is the natural route for PAIC. Does not address the ITC problem itself.


Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference (2022)
Direct evidence that BART’s behavior outside the observed covariate support is prior-driven rather than evidential. Does not address the ITC problem itself.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build BART and Gaussian-process outcome standardization for STC and ML-NMR paired with mandatory support and out-of-distribution diagnostics, and use weighted conformal prediction with the PAIC weights so the coverage claim is stated correctly rather than assumed. The open work here is adapting an existing shift-aware conformal method, not inventing a diagnostic. Make behavior in unsupported target regions visible instead of smoothed over, address Gaussian-process cost with sparse or approximate methods, and forbid reading fitted interactions as causal effect modification.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Our study

Weighted conformal prediction keeps its marginal guarantee under shift by returning infinite intervals where the source has no data
The question put to it. Does weighted conformal prediction give valid intervals for target patients under covariate shift, including where the source has no data?
What it found. No. Weighted conformal intervals kept marginal coverage over the target (0.904 to 0.919 at nominal 0.9), but beyond the source’s largest covariate value they covered 0.70 at a small shift and 0.83 at a moderate one, and at the largest shift they covered 0.99 only because 83% of those intervals were infinite. The method makes the support problem visible; it does not solve it. Estimating the density ratio changed nothing.
Results.

Beyond the source’s range: split conformal 0.63 to 0.68; weighted 0.70, 0.83, 0.99 at target means 0.5, 1, 1.5.
Infinite intervals beyond the range: 0%, 11% and 83% at the three shifts (true ratio); 0%, 14% and 82% with the estimated ratio.
Calibration ESS matched n exp(-mu^2) at mu 0.5 and 1 and exceeded it at 1.5 (51 against 32).

Design.

Estimand

Coverage of 90% prediction intervals for target patients’ outcomes, overall and beyond the source’s covariate range

Methods compared

split conformal, weighted conformal with the true density ratio, weighted conformal with a logistic-regression density ratio

Data-generating mechanism

Spline outcome model with curvature where the source is thin; ordinary, true-ratio weighted and estimated-ratio weighted split conformal intervals at three target shifts; coverage overall and beyond the source’s range, infinite intervals and calibration effective sample size. 3 cells, 500 replicates each.

Replicates

500 per shift, 3 shifts


What this does not answer. Prediction intervals for individual outcomes rather than a marginal treatment effect; one covariate and one outcome model; no BART or Gaussian process arm; no support diagnostic scored as a classifier. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: Flexible outcome surfaces and support diagnostics in standardization
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “BART and Gaussian processes are proposed as flexible nonlinear outcome and treatment-by-covariate surfaces for standardization in STC and ML-NMR, with GPs also covering dose-response curves, and conformal prediction is proposed as the diagnostic that flags target profiles the source data do not support. All three inherit one problem: standardizing a fitted surface over a target distribution with mass outside the source support is extrapolation however flexible the learner is.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented conformal prediction as the diagnostic that flags target profiles the source data do not support. GPT-5.6 Sol pointed out that a split-conformal interval can retain the same width far outside source support, so it is not an out-of-support detector, and the literature auditor supplied the weighted-conformal repair for covariate shift (Tibshirani et al., NeurIPS 2019) that the source did not cite.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): I found no published use of BART or Gaussian processes as the outcome surface inside STC or ML-NMR standardization, so the ITC-specific proposal stands open. The supporting claims are each backed by retrievable work outside ITC. BART is routinely used to fit the outcome model on trial data and predict potential outcomes in a target population in the generalizability literature; its extrapolation behavior outside the covariate support is a known, separately studied failure mode (arXiv:2204.10963, ‘Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference’). The conformal claim is exactly right and has a canonical source: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, ‘Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift’ (NeurIPS 2019), which shows the standard guarantee rests on exchangeability and must be repaired by likelihood-ratio weighting; note this also means a route exists (weighted conformal with the MAIC odds weights), which the entry does not mention. I did not verify the ‘Promising’/‘Speculative diagnostic’ labels; those are claims about the source report, not the literature.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. I found no published use of BART or Gaussian processes as the outcome surface inside STC or ML-NMR standardization, so the ITC-specific proposal stands open. The supporting claims are each backed by retrievable work outside ITC. BART is routinely used to fit the outcome model on trial data and predict potential outcomes in a target population in the generalizability literature; its extrapolation behavior outside the covariate support is a known, separately studied failure mode (arXiv:2204.10963, ‘Local Gaussian process extrapolation for BART models with applications to causal inference’). The conformal claim is exactly right and has a canonical source: Tibshirani, Barber, Candes & Ramdas, ‘Conformal Prediction Under Covariate Shift’ (NeurIPS 2019), which shows the standard guarantee rests on exchangeability and must be repaired by likelihood-ratio weighting; note this also means a route exists (weighted conformal with the MAIC odds weights), which the entry does not mention. I did not verify the ‘Promising’/‘Speculative diagnostic’ labels; those are claims about the source report, not the literature. Cites https://candes.su.domains/publications/downloads/WeightedCP.pdf: Does NOT resolve the ITC problem. It is the canonical source for the entry’s claim that conformal coverage does not transfer under shift, and it supplies the weighted-conformal repair the entry should cite as the natural PAIC route.. Cites arxiv:2204.10963: Does NOT resolve the ITC problem. It is direct evidence for the claim that BART’s behavior outside the observed covariate support is prior-driven rather than evidential..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1-C8 and C11 are broadly correct with model-dependent qualifications: BART and Gaussian processes can represent flexible surfaces, but neither supplies causal effect-modifier interpretation, support or extrapolation validity. Gaussian-process uncertainty is conditional on the kernel, prior and likelihood, not automatically calibrated. C9-C10 are too strong. Ordinary conformal prediction does not inherently detect unsupported covariate profiles; a split-conformal interval can retain the same width far outside source support. Exchangeability failure removes its usual coverage result, while covariate-shift variants require additional assumptions, estimable density ratios and target support. The critical issue is positivity and visible model dependence; adopting BART or GPs is principally a modeling roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No retrieved 2024–2026 STC/ML-NMR implementation pairs BART or GPs as routine outcome surfaces with mandatory support diagnostics inside multinma or equivalent PAIC software. General BART/GP and conformal literature is active (including GP plus conformal calibration work), but conformal coverage under transport/covariate shift requires extra assumptions and is not solved as a PAIC product. The report’s own caveats (extrapolation remains extrapolation; conformal exchangeability fails by construction under shift; GP cost versus ML-NMR integration) match the broader ML literature and are not resolved by a PAIC-specific package. C1–C11 read as research proposals plus correct limitations, not closed methods. title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text: ADJ-02 Overstated Very high priority Promising

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Statement
Standard transport estimators assume an individual-level sample from the target population and HTA targets are usually described only by published summaries, but that obstruction is no longer untouched. Chen et al. (doi:10.1111/biom.13825) reweight to target summary moments, Yan et al.’s TADA (doi:10.1002/pst.70029) transports survival effects from target aggregate data while adjusting for covariate-dependent censoring, and Vo et al. (arXiv:2503.05634) and Shi et al. (arXiv:2605.27272) extend causally interpretable meta-analysis to trials whose individual data are inaccessible. What is missing is a general-purpose transportability library that plugs into the NMA stack: the only NMA-integrated transport is multinma’s own ML-NMR, which requires a copula reconstruction of the target joint covariate distribution from published marginals, while TransportHealth and similar stacks are separate codebases rather than drop-ins for multinma, netmeta or gemtc.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Why it is open
Published marginals identify the target joint distribution only in special cases. Unless the reported summaries happen to identify every target expectation the estimand and model require, the dependence structure and nonlinear expectations must be assumed rather than estimated, and that assumption’s contribution to uncertainty is not propagated into the interval. The existing aggregate-target estimators are built for a single source trial and a specified estimand rather than for a connected network with multi-arm structure. Transport software and NMA software are developed as separate stacks, so an estimate produced by one cannot enter an evidence network fitted by the other without manual re-implementation.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Yan et al., Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data From the Target Population, Pharm Stat 2025
TADA: two-stage weighting that transports a survival effect when only target aggregate data exist, adjusting simultaneously for censoring bias and effect-modifier imbalance. Evaluated and applied; not integrated into an NMA package.


Yan et al., Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data from the Target Population (preprint, 2025)
Preprint version of TADA with assumptions, theory, simulations and an NSCLC case study under target aggregate data only.


Chen et al., Entropy balancing for causal generalization with target sample summary information, Biometrics 2023
Weighting transport of the average treatment effect using target summary-level moments only. Not survival PAIC and not NMA software.


Vo et al., Integration of aggregated data in causally interpretable meta-analysis by inverse weighting (2025)
Transport and standardization across trials where individual data are inaccessible for some studies, by extending moment-based PAIC methods.


Shi, van Amsterdam, Dahabreh et al., Causally-interpretable meta-analysis using aggregate data (2026)
Causally interpretable meta-analysis and indirect comparison in a target population from aggregate trial data only.


multinma package documentation (Phillippo)
Counter-evidence to the claim that no transportability software interoperates with mainstream NMA packages: multinma produces population-adjusted effects for any study population in the network or for an external target population.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the estimators that exist rather than build new ones: take TADA and target-moment entropy balancing to the estimands and outcome types HTA needs, and derive the extra uncertainty induced by reconstructing a joint distribution from marginals so that it appears in the reported interval. Characterize when reported summaries are sufficient for the required target expectations and when they are not, and pair the insufficient case with sensitivity analysis. Then make the result interoperable with mainstream NMA packages so a transported estimate can enter an evidence network directly.

title: No general-purpose transport library plugs into the NMA stack
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. There is no general-purpose transportability library that plugs into the NMA stack; the only NMA-integrated transport is multinma’s own ML-NMR, which requires a copula reconstruction of the target joint covariate distribution from published marginals.
The source titled this. “Transport estimators and software for aggregate-only targets” The title lists transport estimators for aggregate-only targets as missing, but the audit found TADA and three further estimators published, narrowing the gap to NMA-integrated software.
The source said. “Standard transportability estimators assume an individual-level sample from the target population, but HTA targets are described only by published summaries. The report proposes extending target-aggregate-data methods such as TADA and building transportability software that interoperates with existing NMA packages instead of standing alone.”
What was wrong with it. The source, which cited nothing, said TADA needs extension before it can be used and that no transportability software interoperates with mainstream NMA packages. The literature auditor found TADA published, evaluated and applied (doi:10.1002/pst.70029) alongside three further aggregate-target estimators, and multinma documenting population-adjusted effects for an external target population; the claim was unattributed in the source, is now sourced, and narrows to the absence of a general-purpose transport library that interoperates with the NMA stack.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Target-AgD transport is no longer empty. Chen et al. (Biometrics 2023) give entropy balancing from target summary moments; Josey-style calibration and related AgD transport work predate that. Yan et al. TADA (Pharm Stat 2025; arXiv:2412.12335) is a two-stage MoM plus IPCW method for transporting survival effects with covariate-dependent censoring when only target AgD exist, with simulation and a case study, code on GitHub, and inclusion as a module in TransportHealth (Park et al. 2025). Le et al. (arXiv:2408.04854) address transporting aggregate trial results in causally interpretable meta-analysis. C2 remains supported for standard IPD-target transport estimators. C3 is partly overstated because TADA and Chen already exist for key estimands; further extension for full PAIC/NMA estimands and uncertainty from reconstructed joints is still needed. C4 remains largely supported: TransportHealth and CausalMetaR are transport stacks, not drop-ins for multinma/netmeta/gemtc. C5 remains supported for ITC-network validation and NMA interop. Queries: TADA transport AgD; Chen entropy balancing target summary; TransportHealth; CausalMetaR multinma interop; DIPW Quan; NMA package release notes 2024–2026.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The entry names TADA and then says it needs extension; TADA is published and evaluated: Yan et al., ‘Target Aggregate Data Adjustment Method for Transportability Analysis Utilizing Summary-Level Data From the Target Population’ (Pharm Stat 2025, doi:10.1002/pst.70029; arXiv:2412.12335), a two-stage weighting framework applied to transport a KM curve to an Ontario NSCLC target. Two further 2025-2026 estimators cover the aggregate case: Vo et al. (arXiv:2503.05634) integrate aggregate trials with inaccessible IPD into causal meta-analysis by extending PAIC moment methods; Shi, van Amsterdam, Dahabreh et al. (arXiv:2605.27272) build causally-interpretable meta-analysis from marginal and one-at-a-time subgroup effects plus covariate summaries. The claim I cannot let stand is ‘No transportability software currently interoperates with mainstream NMA packages.’ multinma is a mainstream NMA package that performs the transport itself: its documentation states population-adjusted effects ‘can be produced for any study population in the network, or for an external target population.’ Standalone packages (TransportHealth, generalize) exist alongside it. Cites doi:10.1002/pst.70029: TADA exists, is evaluated and applied; the aggregate-only-target obstruction is partly addressed for a single source trial with a survival outcome.. Cites arxiv:2503.05634: Transport/standardization across trials where IPD is inaccessible for some studies, by extending PAIC moment-based methods.. Cites arxiv:2605.27272: Causally-interpretable meta-analysis and indirect comparison in a target population from aggregate trial data only..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2 is generally correct but not categorical. Aggregate summaries can suffice when they identify the target expectations required by the chosen outcome or effect model, such as when the relevant conditional contrast lies in the linear span of reported balance functions. Otherwise, marginal summaries do not identify the target joint distribution, dependence structure or nonlinear expectations. Individual-level target data and density estimation are therefore common requirements, not universal ones. C3 and C5 are plausible development assessments but unsourced; C4 is an unsupported universal software claim. The genuine open core is identification and uncertainty propagation under insufficient target summaries, plus usable network integration.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Target-AgD transport is no longer empty. Chen et al. (Biometrics 2023) give entropy balancing from target summary moments; Josey-style calibration and related AgD transport work predate that. Yan et al. TADA (Pharm Stat 2025; arXiv:2412.12335) is a two-stage MoM plus IPCW method for transporting survival effects with covariate-dependent censoring when only target AgD exist, with simulation and a case study, code on GitHub, and inclusion as a module in TransportHealth (Park et al. 2025). Le et al. (arXiv:2408.04854) address transporting aggregate trial results in causally interpretable meta-analysis. C2 remains supported for standard IPD-target transport estimators. C3 is partly overstated because TADA and Chen already exist for key estimands; further extension for full PAIC/NMA estimands and uncertainty from reconstructed joints is still needed. C4 remains largely supported: TransportHealth and CausalMetaR are transport stacks, not drop-ins for multinma/netmeta/gemtc. C5 remains supported for ITC-network validation and NMA interop. Cites 10.1002/pst.70029: Operational AgD-target transport for survival with MoM participation weights and IPCW; software prototype (TADA/TransportHealth). Not full PAIC-into-NMA interop.. Cites arxiv:2412.12335: Preprint/version of TADA with assumptions, theory sketch, simulations, and NSCLC case study under target AgD only.. Cites 10.1111/biom.13825: Weighting transport of ATE using target summary-level moments only (binary/continuous-style generalization). Not survival PAIC/NMA network software..
