title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adapt the existing MAIC-level multiple imputation and tipping-point workflow rather than inventing one, and state the congeniality conditions between the imputation model and a component transport likelihood that integrates over a target distribution. Add inverse probability of censoring weighting for outcome missingness with explicit treatment of its interaction with adjustment weights, and let imputation uncertainty flow into the standardized target estimand rather than being handled outside the model. Specify MNAR sensitivity parameters that are interpretable for both outcome and effect-modifier missingness and report how they propagate jointly with the population-adjustment and bridging assumptions.

title: Missing data and MNAR sensitivity are unaddressed in component PAIC
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No missing-data framework has been made congenial with component transport: multiple imputation and MNAR tipping-point sensitivity have been applied in ordinary MAIC, but nothing specifies how imputation models should be made compatible with a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, nor how a single MNAR sensitivity parameter propagates simultaneously through the adjustment step, the covariate overlap, and the bridging assumption.
The source said. “Component PAIC has no full missing-data module and no sensitivity analysis for missing-not-at-random mechanisms. Complete-case handling of missing covariates or outcomes changes the effective analysis population and therefore the overlap between the IPD study and the target population, and MNAR mechanisms can only be addressed through explicit sensitivity parameters that are not offered.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no compatible multiple imputation exists and that MNAR can only be addressed through explicit sensitivity parameters. The literature auditor found multiple imputation plus MNAR tipping-point and E-value analysis already done inside a MAIC (doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w), so the gap is congeniality with component transport rather than missing-data methods as such; GPT-5.6 Sol added that MNAR identification can also come from parametric restrictions, instruments, refreshment samples, or validation data, so sensitivity parameters are important but not the only route.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict left unchanged

verdict left unchanged Later work reports progress, but on the chronology review the second reviewer judged it ‘different-question’ at high confidence: The later paper demonstrates imputation and delta-adjusted MNAR sensitivity for an ordinary MAIC, not a component PAIC or component transport model. It therefore does not establish how those procedures interact with component likelihoods or shared component effects.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Framed at field level (‘Component PAIC has no full missing-data module and no sensitivity analysis for MNAR’), the entry is too strong. Esnault et al. 2025 report an applied MAIC in which missing covariates were handled by multiple imputation inside a prespecified propensity-score workflow, and missingness was probed by quantitative bias analysis including an explicit MNAR tipping-point analysis, with roughly half of ECOG performance status missing; they describe it as ‘the first in-depth application of QBA in the context of MAIC’. So multiple imputation plus MNAR sensitivity has been done in a population-adjusted indirect comparison, just not congenially with a component transport model. The genuinely open parts survive: congeniality between an imputation model and a likelihood that integrates over a target covariate distribution and shares component parameters across subnetworks, the multiplicative interaction of IPCW with MAIC weights, and how a single sensitivity parameter propagates through adjustment, overlap and the bridge simultaneously. Cites doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w: Demonstrates multiple imputation of missing covariates plus MNAR tipping-point and E-value sensitivity analysis inside a MAIC; does not address congeniality with component transport..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1, C2, C4, and C6 are supported. cmlnmr() rejects missing effect modifiers and outcomes and explicitly says it does not impute; cSTC relies on standard regression handling, which can yield complete-case fits, and no cpaic path supplies MNAR sensitivity parameters. Complete-case selection can alter both the represented IPD population and its overlap with the target. C3 is an unsupported universal nonexistence claim: absence from cpaic does not show that compatible multiple-imputation procedures do not exist. C5 is also too absolute. Observed data alone generally cannot nonparametrically identify the missing values or distinguish MAR from MNAR without additional assumptions or information, but identification can come from imposed parametric restrictions, instruments, refreshment samples, validation data, or other external information; explicit sensitivity parameters are therefore important but not logically the only possible approach. This is potentially very high severity with material missing effect modifiers or outcomes, but not when missingness is negligible or absent.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. No full missing-data module or MNAR sensitivity framework for component PAIC/cpaic was found. Adjacent MAIC practice now includes multiple imputation and delta-shift/tipping-point MNAR QBA (Esnault et al. 2025, BMC Med Res Methodol; doi:10.1186/s12874-025-02500-w), so claim C3 as a blanket ‘MI methods compatible with component transport do not exist’ is slightly strong: MI+MAIC workflows exist, but congenial MI under component transport with target integration and shared component parameters across subnetworks is still not a published, evaluated method. MNAR remains structurally untestable (C5); effect-modifier missingness still distorts overlap and adjustment (C2, C6). cpaic has no MNAR or full MI module (C1, C4). Queries: MNAR MAIC ML-NMR 2024–2026; Esnault MAIC missing; multiple imputation component transport; cpaic missing data. Problem open for component PAIC; MAIC-level MI/MNAR sensitivity is partial adjacent prior art only.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text: CMP-23 Overstated High priority Emerging

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Statement
The bridge fragility threshold BFT = |D - tau| / sum_c |m_c| is the smallest common per-component main-effect drift, under a worst-case axis-aligned box bound, that moves a target contrast D to a decision threshold tau. It is computed per posterior draw, so it does propagate within-model parameter uncertainty; what it does not cover is interaction drift, covariance-shaped or correlated drift, and structural model uncertainty. Decision-consequence machinery is not missing from the field: decision-invariant threshold analysis for network meta-analysis has existed since Phillippo et al. 2018, is on CRAN as nmathresh, and has been applied to covariate-adjusted networks and combined with GRADE. What no method does is perturb the structural component-bridging parameter itself and report the resulting decision regret.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Why it is open
The single-number threshold assumes all components can drift by the same amount and independently in the worst direction, which is a deterministic uncertainty set rather than the most plausible configuration, and in a population-adjusted analysis drift in effect-modification parameters can matter more than main-effect drift. The extended expressions for component-specific box drift, ellipsoidal drift r times sqrt(m’ Sigma_Delta m) with symmetric positive-definite Sigma_Delta, and interaction drift are analytically standard but need inputs no data source supplies: component-specific bounds, a drift covariance, and plausible interaction drift. Calibrating those from connected networks with repeated components requires an explicit exchangeability and transport model, which anchors rather than validates the sensitivity values, and no calculation reports regret conditional on the untestable bridge.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2018
establishes decision-invariant bias adjustment thresholds and intervals for network meta-analysis, defined on the treatment recommendation rather than the effect scale


nmathresh 0.1.6
released R implementation of decision-invariant threshold analysis, including for random-effects models


Holper 2020
applies threshold analysis to covariate-adjusted network recommendations and integrates it with GRADE


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; computes the box-bound bridge fragility threshold per posterior draw in bridge_fragility(), accepts arbitrary link-scale thresholds, and reports posterior probabilities, p_best, and rank probabilities but no net benefit, wrong-decision probability, or value of information

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend fragility to component-specific, ellipsoidal, and polyhedral drift sets and to joint main-effect and interaction drift, since the formulas are standard and the missing ingredient is the inputs. Connect the existing decision-invariant threshold machinery to the bridging parameter rather than rebuilding decision analysis: nmathresh perturbs data, and what is needed is the same treatment of the structural drift, reported as net benefit, probability of a wrong decision, value of information, and bridge-conditional regret. Calibrate plausible drift distributions from connected networks containing repeated components across contexts while stating that this anchors rather than validates the assumption, and consider whether the net-benefit layer belongs in a downstream decision model rather than in the effect-estimation package.

title: Bridge fragility ignores interaction and correlated component drift
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No sensitivity analysis perturbs the structural component-bridging parameters themselves: decision-invariant threshold analysis for network meta-analysis already exists and operates on the treatment recommendation rather than the link-scale effect (Phillippo et al. 2018, R package nmathresh), and the box and ellipsoidal worst-case bias formulas are standard dual-norm results, so what is genuinely absent is drift-specific inputs, interaction-drift and correlated-drift versions, and a regret calculation conditional on an untestable bridge.
The source titled this. “Bridge fragility covers only main-effect box drift, not decisions” The title says the fragility measure does not cover decisions, but it is computed against a user-supplied decision threshold and the package already reports decision probabilities and rankings.
The source said. “The bridge fragility threshold BFT = |D - tau| / sum_c |m_c|, for target contrast D, component loading m, and decision threshold tau, is the smallest common per-component main-effect drift under a worst-case box bound that moves the contrast to the decision threshold; it covers neither interaction drift, correlated drift, nor model uncertainty. Outputs are organized around link-scale effects rather than decision consequences such as net benefit, probability of a wrong decision, or value of information.”
What was wrong with it. The source said outputs are organized around link-scale effects rather than decision consequences and that the extended worst-case expressions are unavailable. The literature auditor found decision-invariant threshold analysis already established and released (doi:10.1111/rssa.12341; cran:nmathresh; doi:10.1002/jrsm.1393), and noted the box and ellipsoidal bias formulas are elementary dual-norm results rather than open problems; GPT-5.6 Sol added that choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 already accepts arbitrary decision thresholds and reports posterior probabilities, p_best, and full rank probabilities, and that BFT is computed per posterior draw.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that decision-consequence machinery does not exist is wrong at field level. Threshold analysis for network meta-analysis has existed since Phillippo et al. 2018 and is on CRAN as nmathresh, described as computing ‘decision-invariant bias adjustment thresholds and intervals for Network Meta-Analysis’, identifying the smallest data changes that would alter the conclusion. That is precisely a decision-fragility calculation, it is defined on the treatment recommendation rather than on a link-scale effect, and it has been extended to covariate-adjusted networks and combined with GRADE (Holper 2020). The BFT is nonetheless a genuinely different object - it perturbs a structural bridging parameter rather than a data point - and I found nothing that does that, so the entry keeps a real open core. But the two extended worst-case formulas the entry gives (box bound sum |m_c| d_c and ellipsoidal bound r sqrt(m’ Sigma m)) are elementary dual-norm results, not open problems, and framing them as unavailable overstates the gap; what is missing is the inputs, as the entry itself says elsewhere. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12341: Establishes decision-invariant threshold analysis for NMA: thresholds are defined on the treatment decision, not the effect scale, so ‘no decision-consequence machinery exists’ is false.. Cites cran:nmathresh 0.1.6: Working software implementation of decision-invariant threshold analysis, including for random-effects models.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1393: Shows threshold analysis already applied to covariate-adjusted network recommendations and integrated with a certainty-of-evidence framework..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1, C2, C3, C5, and C6 are mathematically correct, with C6 requiring a symmetric positive-definite Sigma_Delta. The box result follows from the L1 support function and is attainable by choosing each drift sign against m; it is a deterministic uncertainty set, not a probabilistic independence assumption. C4 is correct for interaction drift, covariance-shaped drift, and structural model uncertainty, but BFT is calculated per posterior draw and therefore does propagate within-model parameter uncertainty. C8 requires an explicit exchangeability and transport model; connected-network estimates can anchor a prior but cannot validate its applicability, as C9 correctly states. The decision-capability gap is overstated: cpaic already accepts arbitrary link-scale thresholds, reports posterior robustness, posterior probabilities, p_best, and full rank probabilities. It lacks net benefit, wrong-decision probability, value-of-information, and drift-fragility analyses for rankings. Those consequences are important for HTA, but they may properly reside in a downstream decision model rather than this effect-estimation package. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Implements the stated first-generation box-bound bridge fragility threshold for every posterior draw.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Already supplies a population-specific probability-of-being-best output..

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text: CMP-25 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text:
Statement
Bayesian component ML-NMR integrates an individual-level outcome model over aggregate covariate distributions with fixed Sobol quasi-Monte Carlo points, a cost structure inherited from ML-NMR rather than invented for component models, and its survival work scales as the number of aggregate rows times the number of integration points. The Stan likelihood loops serially over that grid with no within-chain parallelization, and no adaptive quasi-Monte Carlo scheme is implemented in component or non-component packages. Two of the proposed remedies are already in place: noncentered random effects are the default and a prior-sensitivity refit under tighter and looser priors is provided. Divergences arise from posterior geometry and weak identification rather than from the integration alone, and the claim that the cost precludes broad simulation studies is not backed by a benchmark.

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text:
Why it is open
The aggregate likelihood requires a numerical integral inside every likelihood evaluation, so cost grows with integration points, aggregate studies, and posterior draws simultaneously, and survival likelihoods with flexible baselines and censoring make each evaluation expensive. Divergences concentrate in weakly identified interaction and drift parameters, which is exactly where the prior matters most, so computational failure and prior dominance are entangled and hard to diagnose separately even with a prior-sensitivity refit available. The remaining computational levers, adaptive quasi-Monte Carlo and within-chain parallelization through mechanisms such as Stan’s reduce_sum, are absent from component and non-component implementations alike.

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020
proposes the general quasi-Monte Carlo numerical integration approach for the ML-NMR aggregate likelihood, from which the component version inherits its cost structure


multinma 0.6.0 NEWS, default integration points
lowered the default number of integration points from 1000 to 64 on the grounds that the previous default was excessive, showing the cost is real and managed upstream


cmdstanr
optional Stan backend for the component ML-NMR models, which are fitted with rstan by default


cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)
unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; integrates the aggregate likelihood over fixed Sobol quasi-Monte Carlo points with a serial Stan loop and no within-chain parallelization, and provides noncentered random effects by default plus prior_sensitivity()

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Add adaptive quasi-Monte Carlo integration and within-chain parallelization, which are the two proposed items that are genuinely missing, and benchmark the result so the claim about simulation feasibility rests on measurement rather than assertion. Keep the noncentered parameterization and prior-sensitivity refit as defaults and extend them with a diagnostic that separates divergence caused by posterior geometry from prior dominance in the weakly identified directions. Surrogate or emulator models with validation are worth exploring only once a benchmark shows where the cost actually binds.

title: Component ML-NMR integration has no parallel or adaptive scheme
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source titled this. “Aggregate-likelihood integration is slow and prior-entangled” The title asserts the integration is slow and prior-entangled, but the audit found no benchmark behind the runtime claim and traced divergences to posterior geometry rather than integration.
The source said. “Bayesian component ML-NMR integrates an individual-level outcome model over aggregate covariate distributions by quasi-Monte Carlo; for complex survival likelihoods this can diverge or be too slow to permit broad simulation studies, and results can be sensitive to priors.”
What was wrong with it. The source proposed noncentered parameterizations and prior-sensitivity diagnostics as future work; GPT-5.6 Sol found both already implemented at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9, with noncentered as the default for random effects, and noted the runtime claim has no benchmark behind it. The literature auditor added that the quasi-Monte Carlo cost is inherited ML-NMR structure (doi:10.1111/rssa.12579) and is actively managed upstream, where multinma 0.6.0 lowered the default number of integration points from 1000 to 64.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The computational structure is as described and inherited from ML-NMR rather than invented here: Phillippo et al. 2020 state ‘Motivated by the complexity of the closed form integration, we propose a general numerical approach using quasi-Monte-Carlo integration’, so the nested-integral cost is a property of the method, not of cpaic. Evidence that the cost is real and actively managed upstream: multinma 0.6.0 lowered the default number of integration points from 1000 to 64 on the grounds that the old default ‘was excessive’. I found no mention of within-chain parallelisation or adaptive quasi-Monte Carlo anywhere in the multinma changelog either, so that gap generalises beyond cpaic; Stan’s reduce_sum makes it available in principle. The entanglement argument (divergences concentrate in weakly identified interaction and drift parameters, which is where the prior matters most) is plausible and I found nothing addressing it. Claims about cpaic’s own runtime behaviour are for the code auditor; cpaic is not publicly available.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. C2 is source-confirmed: aggregate covariates use fixed Sobol quasi-Monte-Carlo points. C3 is also correct: the Stan likelihood loops serially over a fixed n_int grid and contains no reduce_sum or other within-chain parallelization; parallel chains are not within-chain parallelism. C1 is plausible and explicitly acknowledged by the package: survival work scales as nrow(agd) times n_int, and random-effects survival fits can produce divergences. The claim that this precludes broad simulations is not supported by a benchmark, however, and HMC divergences arise from posterior geometry and weak identification rather than from QMC integration alone. The problem is partially mitigated already: noncentered random effects are the default, integration-error diagnostics exist, and prior_sensitivity() refits under tighter and looser priors. Adaptive QMC and within-chain parallelization remain open. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: The proposed noncentered parameterization is already the default for random effects.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Provides explicit refitting under tighter and looser priors to separate prior-driven movement from a single fitted result..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text: CMP-27 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text:
Statement
The combination matrix in component network meta-analysis and component population-adjusted comparison records only whether a component is present in a regimen. Two regimens delivering the same components in a different order, or with different intra-regimen timing, occupy the same row, so they map to one node, one parameter and one estimate, and any ordering effect is absorbed into heterogeneity or into the component main effects with no diagnostic able to report that it has been. The distinction is not recoverable by relaxing additivity: two orderings of one component set have identical component sums and identical two-way interaction columns, so interaction component models cannot separate them, and the row-space estimability screen evaluates the contrast between them as the zero vector and reports no problem rather than reporting inestimability. The devices used in practice neither scale nor identify: an extra binary column such as phase-based is not separately identified whenever phasing co-occurs with a fixed component set and has no agreed definition, and an order indicator per component set grows factorially in the number of components. No published component model states what an order-indexed component parameter would be, no identification result says what evidence structure would estimate one, and no screen flags a network in which regimens sharing a component set but differing in order have been silently merged into one node. Applied reviews record the limitation and stop: an individual-participant component network meta-analysis protocol states that its model cannot discern the effect of component ordering and does not expect enough data to explore it, and a mixed-methods review of interventions for complex traumatic events reports that phasing appears to affect effectiveness while saying it does not know whether phasing is an intervention or a higher-order theoretical construct.

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text:
Why it is open
The obstacle is representational before it is empirical. An additive model over a presence-absence design cannot express a permutation, so encoding order requires a new parameterization rather than an extra term, and the natural candidates all have identification problems: ordered component pairs multiply the parameter count, permutation indicators are unidentified unless several orders of the same set were randomized, and a single phase indicator is collinear with the component set in exactly the trials that motivate it. The evidence structure that would identify a precedence effect is a head-to-head randomization of two sequences of the same components, which is rare because trials are designed to test whether a package works rather than in which order to deliver it. What a component effect means under ordering is also undefined, since the causal reading of adding component c already requires a well-defined and stable component intervention, and a position index forces a decision about whether component c delivered first and delivered second are two versions of one component or two components. Because the design matrix reports no failure, the field gets no signal that anything is wrong: the analysis returns an estimate with an interval, and the merged orderings surface only as heterogeneity that a random-effects model absorbs without complaint.

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
Defines additive and interaction component network meta-analysis and implements both in netmeta by adding interaction columns to the combination matrix. The design remains presence-only, and the interaction columns are identical for two orderings of the same component set, so the extension that relaxes additivity does not touch order.


Welton et al. 2009, American Journal of Epidemiology
The original component synthesis of complex interventions, classifying psychological interventions in coronary heart disease into six component types and estimating effects for components and their combinations. Establishes the presence-absence encoding that later component models inherit.


Efthimiou et al. 2022, Statistics in Medicine
Bayesian component network meta-analysis for aggregate and individual patient data, presenting the ability to recombine components into a treatment never tested in a trial as a distinctive feature. The combination matrix carries no position index, so a recombined regimen has no delivery order either.


Furukawa et al. 2018, BMJ Open (protocol)
States that the proposed component model cannot discern the effect of the ordering of the components and that enough relevant data are not expected, with a plan to modify the model only if enough data become available for the best-represented components.


Furukawa et al. 2021, Lancet Psychiatry
The delivered individual-participant component network meta-analysis from that protocol, 76 randomized trials with 48 supplying individual data, reporting incremental effects of therapeutic components and delivery formats. No ordering or sequencing parameter appears in the model or the results.


Melton et al. 2020, Health Technology Assessment (INCiTE review)
Codes phasing as an additional binary component alongside the content components it reorders, reports that phasing as well as intervention content appears to affect effectiveness, and states that it is unclear whether phasing is itself an intervention or a higher-order theoretical construct.


Freeman et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Develops component-specific visualizations, the CNMA-UpSet plot, heat map and circle plot, that show which component combinations trial arms actually delivered. They display the presence-absence data structure faithfully, which is exactly why delivery order does not appear in them either.

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write the estimand first: define an order-indexed component parameter, for example a main effect per component plus a precedence effect for each ordered pair that co-occurs, and state whether component c delivered first and delivered second are one component in two versions or two components, because the identification argument differs. Then characterize identification by giving the condition on the observed set of ordered regimens under which a precedence contrast lies in the row space of the extended design, which is the direct analogue of the existing estimability screen and runs on the same machinery. Ship the cheap part immediately: a merge diagnostic that flags every node in a fitted component network whose contributing arms deliver the same component set in different documented orders, so silent merging becomes visible even where nothing can yet be estimated. Where precedence is not identified, bound it by reporting how far the target regimen contrast could move under a precedence effect of stated magnitude, in the way omitted-interaction bounds are proposed for additivity. Extraction has to change alongside the model, since trial reports would need to record delivery order and intra-regimen timing in a machine-comparable field before any of this has data behind it.

title: Component models cannot represent delivery order or sequencing
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Two independent readers proposed this and the reviewer accepted both, holding that presence-only component encodings cannot distinguish protocols containing the same components in a different fixed order and that neither additivity tests nor ordinary component interactions solve it. Both sources are applied reviews stating the limitation of their own analyses rather than methods papers, which is a weaker basis than a methodological demonstration; the supporting observation is that no paper in the component methods literature proposes an order-indexed parameterization either.

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text: CMP-29 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text:
Statement
The transitivity and coherence machinery of network meta-analysis is defined over treatment contrasts: design-by-treatment interaction models, node-splitting, back-calculation of direct against indirect estimates, and comparison of effect-modifier distributions across the studies contributing to a contrast. None of it has a component-level analogue. A component effect is a linear functional of the whole design matrix that no single trial estimates, so there is no loop structure over components from which an incoherence statistic could be formed, and the transitivity threat is component-specific because which components a trial implements is associated with study-level context such as era, setting, case mix and funder, an association randomization within trials does not break. BMJ methods guidance on component network meta-analysis states the point in its own limitations: the assessment of transitivity and consistency in the network is an open methodological question, alongside certainty of evidence for component effects, which this catalog treats as a separate problem. The consequence is visible in applied reports, where a component hierarchy is presented with no assessment of whether transitivity holds at component level, while the intervention-level estimates in the same paper carry full GRADE or CINeMA ratings. What exists on the estimation side is a global additivity check, the likelihood-ratio comparison of the additive component model against the standard network model, which is one number for the whole network and localizes nothing, plus contribution analyses that decompose each component estimate into direct and additivity-derived evidence proportions without turning that decomposition into a coherence or transitivity judgment.

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text:
Why it is open
Incoherence in a network is defined by comparing two estimates of the same contrast built from disjoint evidence paths, and a component effect admits no such duplication: every study containing the component also contains others, so the evidence does not partition into two independent estimates of the same component to compare. The global additivity test exists precisely because the local one does not, and it answers a different question. Transitivity at component level is an assumption about the joint distribution of effect modifiers across studies grouped by component presence, and that grouping is not randomized, so any check must be an observational meta-regression that is underpowered in exactly the sparse networks where component models are used. There is also no consumer specifying what such a diagnostic should output, because the component certainty framework that would consume it has not been defined. Methods work on component models has concentrated on estimation, model selection and estimability, leaving the appraisal layer untouched.

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Veroniki et al. 2026, BMJ
methods guidance on analyzing complex interventions with component network meta-analysis; states in its limitations that CINeMA and GRADE have not been formally extended to component estimates and that the assessment of transitivity and consistency in the network remains an open methodological question


Mao et al. 2025, BMC Medical Research Methodology
leave-one-out contribution analysis for component network meta-analysis, decomposing each component estimate into direct and additivity-derived evidence proportions; supplies the evidence-structure input a component-level indirectness or imprecision judgment would need


Yang et al. 2026, BMC Medical Research Methodology
shortest-path evidence contributions in component network meta-analysis; positions itself as groundwork toward assessing certainty in component models, which confirms that the target does not yet exist


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
provides the likelihood-ratio comparison of the additive component model against the standard network model, the only additivity check in routine use; it is global rather than per component


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
simulates connected and disconnected component networks and measures how often additivity is wrongly rejected as heterogeneity rises, the closest thing to an operating characteristic for the global check and the natural test bed for a local one


Higgins et al. 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
the design-by-treatment interaction model for incoherence, defined over treatment contrasts and designs, with no component analogue


Dias et al. 2010, Statistics in Medicine
node-splitting, the local incoherence check that separates direct from indirect evidence for one contrast; the template a component-level split would have to replace, since components have no loops


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
CINeMA, which rates confidence in a network estimate by aggregating study-level bias, heterogeneity, incoherence, indirectness and imprecision over the studies contributing to a treatment contrast; the framework whose inputs a component-level diagnostic would have to supply

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define a per-component coherence statistic by splitting the evidence along a line the design supplies rather than a loop: compare the estimate obtained from the trials that vary the component within a randomization against the estimate obtained from the rest of the network, which is the component analogue of node-splitting, and derive or simulate its null distribution under additivity. Specify a component-level transitivity check as a standard output: report, for each component, the distribution of candidate effect modifiers across the studies contributing to it, and test whether component presence is associated with those modifiers after conditioning on the fitted model. Wire the existing contribution analyses into a reported direct-versus-additivity-derived proportion for every component effect a review interprets, since that quantity is already computable and is the natural input to an indirectness judgment. Evaluate all three on the published connected and disconnected component simulation designs, scoring them as classifiers of true additivity violation rather than by recovery of a known model.

title: No component-level transitivity and coherence assessment
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted it; the evidentiary basis is a single source, which is a weaker footing, but that source is BMJ methods guidance stating in its own limitations that transitivity and consistency assessment in component network meta-analysis is an open methodological question, and two contribution-analysis papers from 2025 and 2026 position themselves as groundwork toward it.

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text: CMP-31 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text:
Statement
The only estimability diagnostic in use for component network meta-analysis is a binary linear-algebra test: whether a requested contrast vector lies in the row space of the component design, checked by comparing the rank of the design with the rank of the design augmented by that vector, as implemented in netmeta and in the 2026 component-hierarchy workflow. A component design can pass that test and still be so nearly rank-deficient that the component effects are not practically identified, and no contrast-specific measure of near-collinearity is defined, reported or given a threshold in this literature: not the condition number, not the smallest singular value of the design or of the information matrix, not a variance inflation attributable to each component column, not prior-to-posterior contraction for the requested contrast. Exact rank deficiency is the rare case; the common case in applied component networks is a component almost always co-administered with another, which leaves the design formally full rank. Because the screen is binary it returns estimable and the analysis proceeds, so the failure surfaces downstream as non-convergence or an implausible interval and is then handled by deleting the offending columns and refitting: a 2026 BMJ component review excluded both delivered-by components, healthcare professional and community member, from a subgroup model because it failed to converge owing to high correlation between them, a condition an exact-rank screen never flags, and a 2026 obesity review fitted a sparse disconnected technical-level component network with the Moore-Penrose inverse, which returns a finite answer regardless. Standard errors and the fitted covariance matrix do carry indirect warning after the fact, so the failure is not invisible; what is missing is a prospective contrast-specific weak-identification diagnostic, a convention for reporting it next to each component effect, and a rule for what to do when it is bad other than silently removing components.

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text:
Why it is open
Near-collinearity is a continuum with no natural cut, and the thresholds that exist elsewhere are rules of thumb calibrated for prediction models with independent observations, not for a weighted network design carrying between-study heterogeneity and multi-arm correlation, so they cannot be transplanted without new calibration. The quantity that matters is contrast-specific rather than model-wide: the same design can identify one component contrast well and another badly, so a single scalar condition number does not answer the question a report asks. Nothing forces the issue at fit time, because the Bayesian route always returns a finite interval supplied in part by the prior and the frequentist pseudoinverse always returns a number. The remedy is unspecified as well: dropping a column changes the estimand of every retained component, so a diagnostic issued without an accompanying rule would formalize an existing bad practice rather than replace it.

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wigle et al. 2026, arXiv:2605.15142
sets out the row-space estimability step for treatment and component hierarchies, implemented by comparing the rank of the design with the rank of the design augmented by the contrast; the check is exact and binary, and no near-singularity measure accompanies it


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
defines the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix and fits it by weighted least squares with a Moore-Penrose inverse, which returns finite estimates whether or not the design is close to singular


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
supplies the algorithm that screens out inestimable interactions before fitting, and the simulated connected and disconnected component networks a weak-identification diagnostic could be calibrated on; the screen itself is exact-rank


Davies et al. 2026, BMJ
component network meta-analysis of vaccine uptake interventions whose 2020-onwards subgroup model failed to converge for both delivered-by components because of high correlation between them, so both were excluded from that model; the failure mode an exact-rank screen does not flag


Xie et al. 2026, Obesity Reviews
fits a technical-level component network described as sparse and disconnected using the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, illustrating that the software returns component estimates without any practical-identification warning


Balduzzi et al. 2023, Journal of Statistical Software
documents the netmeta component functions that applied reviews use; the output carries standard errors but no contrast-level identification measure or threshold

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define a contrast-specific weak-identification measure and calibrate it. For each requested contrast, report the variance under the fitted design relative to its variance under a reference design in which the component varies independently, giving a component variance inflation factor on an interpretable scale; report the smallest singular value of the design restricted to the subspace the contrast spans; and in the Bayesian route report prior-to-posterior contraction for the same contrast. Calibrate thresholds by simulation over the published component network scenario designs, scoring the diagnostic as a classifier of realized error, meaning bias and interval coverage for that contrast, rather than by whether it recovers a known rank. Ship it alongside the row-space verdict in the frequentist component workflow and in the component-hierarchy tooling, and require it to be reported for every component effect a review interprets. Replace the delete-and-refit habit with penalization toward a shared component effect or a declared merge, both of which change the estimand explicitly rather than silently.

title: No practical-identification diagnostic for component effects
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it from a single methods preprint, supported by two 2026 applied reviews that display the failure and the ad hoc response, and the reviewer accepted the gap while narrowing the claim: standard errors and covariance matrices give indirect warning after fitting, so what is absent is a prospective contrast-level diagnostic with a reporting and remediation convention rather than any warning at all.

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text: CMP-33 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text:
Statement
In a component network meta-analysis the component design is the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, so a component coefficient is a linear combination of study-level contrasts. When a component’s indicator varies across the arms of at least one trial, its coefficient inherits randomized identification; when the indicator is constant within every trial and varies only across trials or across subgroups defined by background therapy, the same coefficient is identified by a between-study comparison and is observational. Existing estimability machinery answers a different question, whether a target contrast lies in the row space of the full design, and returns estimable in both cases. No implementation partitions the component parameter space into the subspace supported by within-study randomized variation and its complement, and no applied report states which of its component effects fall in which part, so randomized and non-randomized component columns are presented on one forest plot under one interpretation. The stakes are concrete: a 2024 heart failure network defined beta-blocker and renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitor components from trial-level background-therapy prevalence, counting a population as exposed when at least 50 percent of it was on the drug class at baseline, a quantity that cannot vary within a randomization, and then reported a quadruple combination including beta-blockers as the most effective regimen. The partition is computable from the design alone: restrict the comparison design matrix to within-study contrasts, form the resulting component design, and ask which component contrasts lie in its row space.

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text:
Why it is open
The presumption that a network of randomized trials yields randomized comparisons holds for treatment contrasts and fails for component contrasts formed across trials, and because nobody has flagged the difference nobody has asked for the partition. The obstacle is not derivation, which is a short linear-algebra exercise, but consequence: the screen would label a substantial share of published component effects as observational, and there is no established way to present the two kinds side by side or to downgrade the second, because the component certainty framework that would consume the label does not exist. The components that never vary within a trial, background therapy, setting, delivery context and era, are also the ones reviews most want to compare, so the labeling cost falls precisely on the results people care about. The general result that across-trial associations for treatment effect modifiers are ecological and can differ from within-trial ones is long established, but it has been carried into covariate interaction models rather than into the component design matrix.

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Zafeiropoulos et al. 2024, JACC: Heart Failure
defines background-therapy components from trial-level prevalence with a 50 percent threshold and reports combination regimens built from them, an applied instance in which component columns carry no within-trial randomized variation


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Biometrical Journal
gives the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component matrix, which is exactly the factorization the proposed partition would restrict


Petropoulou et al. 2023, BMC Medical Research Methodology
screens component and interaction estimability by row-space membership of the full design, returning the same verdict whether the support is within-study or between-study


Berlin et al. 2002, Statistics in Medicine
shows that group-level meta-regressions for treatment effect modifiers are subject to ecological bias and can differ from the individual-level relationship, the general result this problem applies to component columns


Phillippo et al. 2020, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
multilevel network meta-regression avoids aggregation bias for covariate interactions by integrating an individual-level model over each study’s covariate distribution, the precedent for taking within-study versus across-study information seriously at covariate level


Mao et al. 2025, BMC Medical Research Methodology
leave-one-out contribution analysis for component estimates; supplies the machinery for the continuous version of the partition, namely the share of information about each component contrast coming from within-study contrasts

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Implement the partition and report three verdicts instead of two. Restrict the comparison design matrix to within-study contrasts, form the within-study component design, and classify each requested component contrast as randomized if it lies in the row space of that restricted design, between-study if it lies only in the row space of the full design, and inestimable otherwise. Report a continuous version alongside the categorical one, namely the proportion of the information about each component contrast that comes from within-study contrasts, which existing component contribution analysis can compute. Require applied component reviews to state the verdict for each reported component effect and to accompany every between-study component effect with the transitivity discussion an observational meta-regression would demand. Use the screen prospectively as well, since it identifies exactly which component contrasts a proposed new trial would move from the between-study subspace into the randomized one.

title: No screen separates randomized from between-study component identification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted it, agreeing that full-design estimability does not reveal whether a component contrast rests on within-trial randomized contrasts or only on between-study variation and that general cautions about the causal reading of component coefficients supply neither the subspace diagnostic nor a reporting rule; the evidence is a single applied network, a weaker basis than a methods source, although the design argument is checkable without it.

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text: CMP-35 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text:
Statement
Two published algorithms compute the contribution of a direct comparison to a component effect in component network meta-analysis, and they measure different quantities. Yang et al. 2026 adapt the shortest-path approach: a pseudo-path is a set of directed edges whose non-negative linear combination isolates one component, flow is allocated to pseudo-paths in order of increasing length using the component-level hat matrix, and the flow-weighted sum of pseudo-path estimates reproduces the fitted component effect within numerical tolerance. Mao et al. 2025 instead delete each direct comparison in turn, recompute the variance of every component effect, and normalize the induced precision leverage to sum to one hundred percent per component; the later of the two papers states that precision leverage and pathway-based evidence flow are distinct conceptual dimensions of contribution rather than approximations of a common target, and its own validation found no inherent relationship between precision leverage and linear weighting, agreeing closely in an artificial network where every comparison was given variance one (R-squared 0.99) and only loosely in a real network with heterogeneous variances (R-squared 0.67). Neither definition has an axiomatic characterization, no criterion says which one to report, and no study measures how far they disagree on the same network. The flow allocation is additionally order-dependent: when several pseudo-paths have equal length, the order in which they are selected can change the resulting allocation because edge flow is exhausted before all paths are explored, so the published proportions are not a function of the fitted model alone. The leave-one-out redistribution rules that apply when deleting an edge destroys component identifiability are described by their own authors as empirically justified but resting on heuristic assumptions without a rigorous mathematical foundation. Contribution numbers are the intended input to certainty assessment for component conclusions, so what a certainty rating rests on currently depends on which of two algorithms was run and, for one of them, on an enumeration order.

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text:
Why it is open
Both paradigms are legitimate and they answer different questions: flow allocation asks which randomized comparisons a component estimate is algebraically assembled from, while leave-one-out precision leverage asks how much precision each comparison supplies, and nothing external adjudicates between how much evidence and how much information. In ordinary network meta-analysis the analogous ambiguity is a choice among path weightings on a real treatment graph, where graph-theoretic intuition and an interpretable notion of a path are available; in component networks the paths are algebraic constructs with fractional coefficients over a design matrix, so the intuition that grounds the treatment-level choice does not carry over and there is no obvious axiom to appeal to. The order dependence is not a numerical tolerance issue: it is intrinsic to a greedy algorithm that exhausts edge capacity, so removing it requires either a canonical tie-breaking rule with a justification or an allocation that is invariant by construction. Nobody has run the empirical comparison that would settle how often the two rankings differ, and neither author group has an incentive to, since each published its definition as the answer to the same question.

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Mao et al. 2025, A leave-one-out algorithm for contribution analysis in component network meta-analysis, BMC Medical Research Methodology 25
Defines contribution as normalized precision leverage: each direct comparison is deleted in turn, the variances of all component effects are recomputed, and the induced variance inflation is normalized to sum to one hundred percent per component. Reports that precision leverage has no inherent relationship to linear weighting (R-squared 0.99 under equal variances, 0.67 in real data), and states that its redistribution rules for edges whose removal destroys identifiability rest on heuristic assumptions.


Yang et al. 2026, Evidence contributions in component network meta-analysis from the shortest-path approach, BMC Medical Research Methodology 26
Defines contribution as evidence flow over pseudo-paths, sets of directed edges whose non-negative linear combination isolates a component, allocated iteratively from the component-level hat matrix; the flow-weighted sum reproduces the fitted component effect within numerical tolerance. States as a limitation that when multiple pseudo-paths of equal length exist, the order of selection can alter the flow allocation.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, Estimating the contribution of studies in network meta-analysis: paths, flows and streams, F1000Research 7:610
Establishes the flow-network proportion contribution matrix for treatment-level network meta-analysis that the component version generalizes, including the equal-split approximation for stream flow that the component setting inherits.


Rucker et al. 2020, The statistical importance of a study for a network meta-analysis estimate, BMC Medical Research Methodology 20
Gives a uniquely defined per-study importance measure as the reduction in the variance of a specified network estimate when the study is added, and emphasizes that it is not a percentage contribution summing to one hundred percent and must not be read as a weight for effect estimation. This is the variance-paradigm ancestor of the component leave-one-out measure and shows that uniqueness is achievable once the target quantity is pinned down.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, CINeMA: An approach for assessing confidence in the results of a network meta-analysis, PLOS Medicine 17:e1003082
Consumes contribution percentages as the input to per-comparison certainty judgments, which is the downstream use that makes the choice of definition consequential rather than descriptive.


Rucker, Petropoulou and Schwarzer 2020, Network meta-analysis of multicomponent interventions, Biometrical Journal 62:808-821
Formalizes the component design as the product of the comparison design matrix and the treatment-by-component combination matrix, the structure over which both contribution definitions are computed and the reason component pseudo-paths carry fractional coefficients.

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write down the axioms a contribution allocation for component effects should satisfy before choosing between the two candidates: efficiency, so shares recompose the estimate or sum to one; a null-edge property, so a comparison that cannot affect the component receives zero; symmetry under relabeling; and invariance to the order in which pseudo-paths are enumerated. Then check which published definition satisfies which, and note that a Shapley value over edges, with the characteristic function taken as the precision of the component effect obtainable from a subset, is order-independent by construction and is the obvious repair for the variance paradigm. In parallel run both algorithms over the same set of published component networks and report the rank correlation and the number of comparisons whose contribution rank changes, since that is the quantity a certainty assessor needs and it requires no new theory. For the flow method specifically, either adopt a canonical enumeration of equal-length pseudo-paths and prove the allocation invariant to it, or average over enumerations and report the spread. Require every published contribution table to name the definition used and, where flow is used, the tie-breaking rule.

title: No unique definition of evidence contribution for component estimates
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it, judging that pathway-based flow and leave-one-out precision leverage are distinct notions rather than interchangeable estimators and that a criterion for selecting, reconciling or labeling them is a genuine gap. The evidence is a single paper, which is a narrow base; what strengthens it is that the paper it contrasts itself with is separately published and that each of the two states the relevant defect, order dependence and heuristic redistribution, in its own limitations.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Statement
In population-adjusted network and bridge models a proper prior with a finite, positive marginal likelihood yields a proper posterior even along directions the likelihood cannot identify, so a narrow credible interval can reflect the prior rather than the evidence, and a clean R-hat does not rule that out. The diagnostics that would expose it already exist as general Bayesian workflow tools: power-scaling sensitivity (Kallioinen et al., arXiv:2107.14054, with the priorsense package on CRAN) and multinma’s plot_prior_posterior(), shipped since version 0.1.0. What is missing is their application here: the literature and recency auditors found no power-scaling or per-parameter contraction analysis of PAIC bridge or disconnected-network models, and no released ITC package computes a contraction measure or benchmarks a decision contrast against a prior-only fit.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Why it is open
The posterior blends prior and likelihood and nothing in a printed interval separates them, so a well-behaved posterior for a cross-gap contrast or an aggregate-only interaction is formatted exactly like an evidence-based estimate. Convergence diagnostics interrogate the sampler rather than the likelihood’s contribution, though the exemption is not total: Kallioinen et al. note that a case with both an uninformative prior and a noninformative likelihood will usually announce itself through fitting problems. The gap is wiring and practice rather than method: no released ITC package computes power scaling or prior-to-posterior contraction, so running either on a bridge model is bespoke work, and because prior dominance grows with scenario severity a single check on one benign dataset says nothing about the cases that matter.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Kallioinen, Paananen, Burkner and Vehtari 2024, power-scaling sensitivity for priors and likelihoods, Statistics and Computing (arXiv:2107.14054)
defines power-scaling sensitivity: prior sensitivity with little or no likelihood sensitivity is the signature of a likelihood that is noninformative relative to the prior; notes that a jointly uninformative prior and likelihood usually shows up as fitting problems instead


priorsense R package
implements power-scaling prior and likelihood sensitivity diagnostics for fitted Bayesian models; named by the recency auditor as available but not wired into ITC packages


multinma R package, plot_prior_posterior() since version 0.1.0
plots prior against posterior for model parameters, a partial prior-versus-posterior facility that stops short of a numerical contraction measure or power scaling


cpaic, unreleased development package on GitHub (not on CRAN), commits 7563a64 and a99b718
returns NA instead of a finite summary for contrasts the component design does not identify, and adds prior predictive checks plus refits under tighter and looser prior scales as an empirical identification diagnostic; it implements no formal power scaling, no numerical contraction measure, and no prior-only benchmark fit

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Apply the existing tools rather than build new ones. Run power-scaling sensitivity and per-parameter prior-to-posterior contraction on PAIC bridge, component and disconnected-network models, benchmark each decision contrast against a prior-only fit, and report contraction for the contrasts that carry the decision and not only for model parameters, since contraction is parameterization-dependent. Wire these into released packages so they stop being bespoke scripts, and evaluate them conditional on scenario severity rather than at one benign scenario.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Our study

Do prior-sensitivity diagnostics catch the analyses that are actually wrong?
The question put to it. In a population-adjusted network a proper prior yields a proper posterior even where the likelihood identifies nothing, so a narrow interval can reflect the prior rather than the evidence. The diagnostics that would expose this exist. What are their operating characteristics: do they flag the analyses whose intervals actually miss the truth, and how often do they cry wolf?
What it found. At the thresholds the literature suggests, they miss most of it. Pairing each warning with whether that replicate’s own interval missed, a composite of four diagnostics has sensitivity 0.37 at a false-alarm rate of 0.16, falling to 0.13 outside two engineered geometries; the one sensitive rule fires on half the sound analyses too. Used as continuous scores the same statistics reach AUC 0.51 to 0.78, so this is a failure of thresholds rather than of the statistics. What no threshold repairs is that these diagnostics measure the prior’s influence while the harm comes from the prior’s location: with disconnected evidence and a tight prior four standard deviations from the truth, going from 100 to 400 per arm drops the warning rate from 0.98 to 0.01 while coverage stays near zero.
Results.

Prespecified verdict: diagnostics fail at the thresholds the literature suggests. Composite sensitivity 0.366 (MCSE 0.002), false alarm 0.158; 0.127 and 0.025 outside the engineered positive controls.
Sensitivity and specificity trade off completely. Tight-and-loose prior refitting catches 0.83 of misses outside the controls and fires on 53% of covered replicates. Contraction, the prior-only benchmark and power-scaling keep false alarms low and catch almost nothing.
The composite adds almost nothing over its best component: 0.366 against contraction’s 0.363, at a higher false-alarm rate. Requiring two of four rules to agree neither buys specificity nor recovers sensitivity.
More data makes the warning quieter while the answer stays wrong. Disconnected evidence, tight prior, true interaction four prior SDs away: coverage near zero at both sample sizes, warning rate 0.98 at 100 per arm and 0.01 at 400. Contraction is what every diagnostic reads as reassurance.
A first implementation measured power-scaling by posterior mean shift and found sensitivity 0.000 everywhere. That was our error: with a zero-centred prior, scaling the prior up and the likelihood down give identical posterior means, so the standard rule can never fire. Measured distributionally it works, and the verdict does not depend on the amendment.
The structural rank screen is the only rule with no false alarms at all, and it is blind to every failure where the contrast is estimable and the answer is still wrong.

Design.

Estimand

Target-population marginal C versus B mean difference, and the conditional interaction coefficient

Methods compared

no-diagnostic baseline, structural rank screen, prior-to-posterior contraction, prior-only benchmark, power-scaling sensitivity, tight and loose refit, composite rule

Data-generating mechanism

A conjugate Gaussian population-adjusted network in which every piece of evidence reduces without loss to a normal observation, so the posterior and every power-scaled posterior are exact and no diagnostic is contaminated by MCMC noise. 120 scenarios crossing the evidence available about the weakly identified treatment, arm size, whether the truth agrees with the zero-centered prior, prior scale, and the target population. 2000 replicates each.

Replicates

2000 per scenario, 240,000 datasets and 480,000 contrast evaluations


What this does not answer. The other half of CMU-02, wiring these diagnostics into released software, is untouched; neither multinma nor cpaic is run. The model is conjugate Gaussian with an identity link, a correctly specified linear mean and known variances, so nothing transfers directly to a non-conjugate posterior where MCMC error enters and the diagnostics behave differently. Only automated thresholds are evaluated; a plot read by an experienced analyst is a different instrument. Thresholds were taken from the source literature and not tuned. CMP-14 is touched only for the generic aggregate-only interaction, not for component models, and IDN-06 is not addressed at all because this design contains no within-versus-between discrepancy.
Peer review. 2 rounds, two independent reviewers. The reports, the point-by-point responses and the editorial decision are published in full: read the review.

title: Priors, not data, can drive posteriors in weakly identified models
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “In population-adjusted network and bridge models a proper prior guarantees a proper posterior even for contrasts the likelihood cannot identify, so a narrow credible interval can reflect the prior rather than evidence. Prior predictive checks, power-scaling sensitivity, and per-parameter prior-to-posterior contraction are not routinely reported, so a reader cannot tell which quantities the data actually informed.”
What was wrong with it. The source implied the diagnostics themselves were absent. Power scaling (Kallioinen et al. 2024, arXiv:2107.14054; priorsense on CRAN) and multinma’s plot_prior_posterior() have existed for years, and the source-code auditor found that cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub and not on CRAN, already returns NA for structurally non-identified contrasts and ships prior predictive checks and tight/loose prior refits; the other two auditors found nothing equivalent in released ITC packages, and that disagreement stands. The propriety claim was also narrowed: a proper prior gives a proper posterior when the marginal likelihood is finite and positive, not unconditionally.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): I read the power-scaling paper in full (arXiv 2107.14054; Kallioinen, Paananen, Burkner, Vehtari, Stat Comput 2024) and the SBC test-quantities paper (arXiv 2211.02383). Kallioinen supports the diagnostic claim directly: prior sensitivity with little or no likelihood sensitivity is the signature of a likelihood that is noninformative relative to the prior. Modrak et al. independently corroborate the core worry: standard rank-based SBC ‘could never detect … when the posterior is equal to the prior’. Both are generic Bayesian-workflow tools, not ITC methods. I found no application of priorsense or power-scaling to PAIC bridge or disconnected-network models; PubMed returns nothing, and multinma’s R/ directory and NEWS contain no priorsense or power-scaling entry, so the tooling is genuinely not wired in. Caveats: (i) the absence claim cannot be verified, only unrefuted; (ii) ‘convergence diagnostics do not detect weak identification’ holds for a proper informative prior but not universally, since Kallioinen notes fully uninformative cases ‘will likely be detectable from model fitting issues’; (iii) multinma has shipped plot_prior_posterior() since v0.1.0, a partial prior-vs-posterior facility. codex dissented (overstated): C1-C3 are correct for ordinary Bayesian models with a finite, positive marginal likelihood: a proper prior can regularize a likelihood-null direction and produce finite credible intervals. A proper prior alone is not an unrestricted mathematical guarantee of posterior propriety. C4 is correct in the important one-way sense that good convergence does not establish identification, although weak identification can sometimes cause poor geometry. C5 is useful but contraction is parameterization-dependent and should also be assessed for decision contrasts. C6 measures sensitivity to power perturbations; it is not a definitive identification test. C7 is an unsubstantiated literature-practice claim and is stale as a package-capability claim because cpaic wires in related diagnostics. C8 and C9 are reasonable. At 9d150e9, cpaic returns NA for design-nonidentified contrasts, offers per-contrast tight/loose-prior refits, prior predictive fitting, and per-parameter prior/posterior plots. It does not implement formal prior or likelihood power scaling, a numerical contraction measure, or a benchmark against a separate prior-only fit for every contrast.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I read the power-scaling paper in full (arXiv 2107.14054; Kallioinen, Paananen, Burkner, Vehtari, Stat Comput 2024) and the SBC test-quantities paper (arXiv 2211.02383). Kallioinen supports the diagnostic claim directly: prior sensitivity with little or no likelihood sensitivity is the signature of a likelihood that is noninformative relative to the prior. Modrak et al. independently corroborate the core worry: standard rank-based SBC ‘could never detect … when the posterior is equal to the prior’. Both are generic Bayesian-workflow tools, not ITC methods. I found no application of priorsense or power-scaling to PAIC bridge or disconnected-network models; PubMed returns nothing, and multinma’s R/ directory and NEWS contain no priorsense or power-scaling entry, so the tooling is genuinely not wired in. Caveats: (i) the absence claim cannot be verified, only unrefuted; (ii) ‘convergence diagnostics do not detect weak identification’ holds for a proper informative prior but not universally, since Kallioinen notes fully uninformative cases ‘will likely be detectable from model fitting issues’; (iii) multinma has shipped plot_prior_posterior() since v0.1.0, a partial prior-vs-posterior facility.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1-C3 are correct for ordinary Bayesian models with a finite, positive marginal likelihood: a proper prior can regularize a likelihood-null direction and produce finite credible intervals. A proper prior alone is not an unrestricted mathematical guarantee of posterior propriety. C4 is correct in the important one-way sense that good convergence does not establish identification, although weak identification can sometimes cause poor geometry. C5 is useful but contraction is parameterization-dependent and should also be assessed for decision contrasts. C6 measures sensitivity to power perturbations; it is not a definitive identification test. C7 is an unsubstantiated literature-practice claim and is stale as a package-capability claim because cpaic wires in related diagnostics. C8 and C9 are reasonable. At 9d150e9, cpaic returns NA for design-nonidentified contrasts, offers per-contrast tight/loose-prior refits, prior predictive fitting, and per-parameter prior/posterior plots. It does not implement formal prior or likelihood power scaling, a numerical contraction measure, or a benchmark against a separate prior-only fit for every contrast. Cites choxos/cpaic@7563a6429c93f97120a9ae8107c3a62f6c9382e7: Prevents a finite posterior summary from being reported for a contrast that the component design does not identify.. Cites choxos/cpaic@a99b718a79eda5937dc0734cddfbe632022e277e: Adds prior predictive checks and refitting under tighter and looser prior scales for target contrasts..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The identification and presentation claims (proper priors yield finite posteriors without likelihood information; disconnected-network contrasts can be prior-driven; posteriors alone do not show estimability; R-hat does not detect weak identification) remain standard Bayesian results and were not overturned by 2024–2026 ITC literature. Power-scaling sensitivity (Kallioinen et al. 2024; R package priorsense on CRAN) and prior-to-posterior tools (including multinma plot_prior_posterior) exist as general Bayesian workflow pieces, so C5–C6 and C8 are methodologically available rather than uninvented. What the agenda correctly flags as open is routine application and package wiring for weakly identified PAIC/bridge/disconnected models, and evaluation conditional on scenario severity: searches across RSM/SiM/MDM/Value in Health, arXiv stat.ME, and maicplus/multinma/gemtc docs found no standard PAIC reporting of per-parameter contraction, power-scaling, or prior-only benchmarks for decision contrasts. Proposal of diagnostics is not solution of the ITC practice gap.

title: Computational diagnostics and Monte Carlo error go unreported
text:
Statement
Simulation studies frequently publish performance summaries without the computational context that produced them or the Monte Carlo standard errors of the summaries themselves, but the measured base rates come from outside this field: a review of 321 psychology articles, 100 of them with simulation studies, found that 77% did not report the uncertainty of performance measures, 19% reported convergence, and 2% gave full computational-environment information. No equivalent review of ITC or PAIC simulation studies was found, so the field-specific version of the claim is an extrapolation. The prescription and the tooling are in any case solved: Siepe et al. (doi:10.1037/met0000695) supply an ADEMP-based reporting and preregistration template with MCSE formulae and a repetition-count calculation, and SimDesign on CRAN already re-simulates non-convergent replicates, captures errors and warnings, and records the session environment. Within ML-NMR the integration-error component is no longer unaddressed, since multinma’s int_check has been on by default since 0.6.0.

title: Computational diagnostics and Monte Carlo error go unreported
text:
Why it is open
Computational diagnostics are treated as workflow hygiene rather than as study results, so they are inspected privately and dropped from the write-up and a reader cannot tell whether a reported bias or coverage figure came from converged fits. Performance measures are themselves estimates, and without the MCSE of the difference between two methods an apparent ranking cannot be separated from replicate noise, while the replicate-level output that would let a reader recompute a different measure is discarded once the summary table exists, even though storing it is cheap. Failures and integration error concentrate in the hardest cells, so per-scenario reporting matters more than an average and the missing numbers flatter methods exactly where they are stressed. The residual problem is adoption in this field: templates, MCSE formulae and simulation frameworks that capture all of this are available and unused.

title: Computational diagnostics and Monte Carlo error go unreported
text:
Probable solution or research direction
