title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text: DEC-32 Confirmed open High priority Established Tractability 3/5

title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text:
Statement
Threshold analysis is offered as the decision-linked alternative to GRADE for network meta-analysis: for each study estimate or contrast it computes how far the evidence would have to move before the recommendation changes and what the new recommendation would be, and the algebraic version needs only the network estimates and the decision rule. The machinery holds the uncertainty structure fixed and determines the influence of the evidence on the point estimates only, so any decision rule that depends on precision rather than on the expected effect has no analytic threshold: recommend only if an interval excludes the null, or excludes a minimally important difference, or if the probability of being best exceeds a cut-off. The influence of a study on the width of an interval, as opposed to its location, is therefore absent from the output, and nothing separates a recommendation that is fragile to bias from one that is fragile to imprecision. That distinction bites where recommendations are already marginal: in the migraine prophylaxis guideline used to introduce the method the smallest threshold was a change of 0.09 headache days on one contrast, and 6 of 11 studies had thresholds lying inside their own confidence intervals, so ordinary sampling variation would suffice to flip the recommendation. Numerical methods are named as the required route but none has been supplied, and no subsequent tipping-point work provides a precision-indexed threshold. Loss-based decision rules that price posterior uncertainty explicitly have since been proposed for network meta-analysis, which makes the omission more consequential rather than less, because such rules are precision-sensitive by construction.

title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text:
Why it is open
The closed-form result exists because the recommendation is a function of the posterior mean through a linear map, so thresholds can be inverted algebraically; a rule that reads a variance or a tail probability breaks exactly that structure, which is why numerical methods are required and why nobody has produced them cheaply. A precision perturbation is also not one-dimensional in the way a bias perturbation is: changing one study’s variance re-weights the whole network and shifts every other contrast’s precision as well as its own, so there is no single scalar threshold to report and the analyst must first decide what to hold fixed. The interpretation is unsettled even if the computation were done, because a variance is not a quantity a reviewer can adjust on judgment the way a suspected bias is, and what a precision threshold would mean substantively, or what evidence would justify a given perturbation, has not been posed. The same method’s other named limitation, that algebraic thresholds are unavailable for general cost-effectiveness decision rules, has also gone unaddressed, which suggests the numerical machinery both problems need has simply not been built.

title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2019, Annals of Internal Medicine
Argues threshold analysis should replace GRADE for assessing confidence in guideline recommendations based on network meta-analysis and demonstrates it on two NICE guidelines; states that the algebraic approach determines the influence of the evidence on the point estimates and not on the uncertainty, and that decision rules based on statistical significance require numerical methods.


Phillippo et al. 2018, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
The algebraic threshold analysis itself: invariant intervals for each data point or contrast, plus simultaneous multi-dimensional thresholds, all defined on the point estimates with the variance-covariance structure held fixed.


nmathresh, CRAN
Reference implementation of algebraic threshold analysis for network meta-analysis, computing study-level and contrast-level thresholds and invariant intervals; it has no facility for perturbing variances or for precision-indexed decision rules.


Ades et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Loss-adjusted expected value, a decision rule subtracting the Bayesian expected loss computed from the posterior of the contrast, evaluated on 10 NICE networks; a rule whose output depends directly on precision and for which no threshold analysis exists.

title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Specify the perturbation space explicitly: the natural object is a change in one study’s variance, or in the between-study heterogeneity, with the point estimates held fixed, and the output is the smallest such change that flips the recommendation. Because the network re-weights under any variance change, this is a small numerical search rather than an inversion, and it is cheap enough to run over every study in a network with existing code. Report the two sensitivities side by side, how far a study’s estimate must move and how much its precision must change to alter the recommendation, so a reviewer can tell whether the fragility is one an appraisal of bias could address at all. Define the corresponding threshold for interval-based, probability-based and loss-adjusted rules, and validate the resulting thresholds against brute-force recomputation on published networks. Where a recommendation proves precision-sensitive, the actionable output is a sample-size or further-research statement rather than a risk-of-bias judgment.

title: Threshold analysis can perturb an estimate’s location but not its precision
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted that sensitivity of a decision to variance, interval width or ranking probability is materially different from sensitivity to point-estimate location. The claim rests on a single source, but that source is the method’s own developers stating the limitation, and no subsequent work supplying a precision-indexed threshold was found.

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text: DEC-34 Partially addressed Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text:
Statement
A network meta-analysis reaches guideline panels, reimbursement committees and clinicians as a display rather than as a posterior, and no display carries a measured reading-error rate. A systematic survey of 200 reviews published in 2020 and 2021 counted 1133 presentation formats in use, with forest plots in 108 reviews (54.0 percent), league tables in 93 (46.5 percent) and the surface under the cumulative ranking curve in 69 (34.5 percent), while a structured evidence summary appeared in 10 (5.0 percent) and covered benefits and harms together in 3 (1.5 percent). New formats keep arriving, among them the rank-heat plot, the Kilim plot, spie charts, color-coded multi-outcome tables and interactive summary tools, and each is introduced with a worked example rather than with evidence that a reader extracts the right answer from it. Development studies stop at acceptability and preference: the GRADE network summary-of-findings table came out of four rounds of semistructured interviews with 32 stakeholders, two color-coded multi-outcome formats were refined by qualitative content analysis with 26 participants against a single exemplar network in acute pain, and the MATCH-IT interactive tool was revised over five cycles of think-aloud testing with 26 physicians, 24 of whom (94 percent) reported no or sparse prior experience of interpreting a network meta-analysis. One randomized comparison exists: 149 third-year medical students were assigned to two MATCH-IT versions differing in color coding and in which outcomes appear on entry, 82.5 percent answered at least 4 of 5 interpretation items correctly and 75.8 percent reached the recommendation an expert panel had reached, and the design contrast made no difference to interpretation or to understandability. Nothing compares display families against each other on one network, nothing scores whether a reader recognizes that a top-ranked treatment is imprecisely estimated or that a contrast is carried entirely by indirect evidence, and nothing has been run on the panels and committees the displays exist to serve.

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text:
Why it is open
A comprehension study needs an answer key, and the field has not agreed what a correct reading of a network result is. Scoring whether a reader took the right message from a ranking display presupposes a position on what a ranking licenses, and that position is contested: the same fit yields orderings that differ by ranking metric and by whether uncertainty is penalized, so the answer key would encode a judgment the field is still arguing about. The audience that matters is also the audience that cannot be recruited at scale, since guideline panels and reimbursement committees have members in the tens, read a display once inside a deliberation that is itself the outcome of interest, and cannot be randomized without disturbing the process being measured; the substitute available in hundreds is students, who are not the audience. Display work is done by the groups that build displays, and a head-to-head trial can only demote one of the entrants, so no one whose format is in use has an incentive to run it and no funder treats presentation evaluation as a methods output. The comparison also has no natural unit, because a league table and a rank-heat plot answer different questions from one fit, so a trial must first fix the question, which is the step on which agreement is missing.

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Lovsletten, Wang, Pitre, Odegaard, Veroniki, Lunny, Tricco, Agoritsas & Vandvik 2024, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 173:111445
Systematic survey of 200 systematic reviews with network meta-analysis published 2020 to 2021 across 158 journals; counts 1133 presentation formats, forest plots in 108 reviews (54.0 percent), league tables in 93 (46.5 percent), SUCRA in 69 (34.5 percent), structured evidence summaries in 10 (5.0 percent) and in 3 (1.5 percent) across benefits and harms, absolute effects in 16 of 133 reviews reporting dichotomous outcomes (11.7 percent) and certainty ratings inside a presentation format in 26 (13.0 percent). Establishes what is in use; measures no comprehension.


Stokke Hunskaar, Lovsletten, Muller & Vandvik 2024, BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine 29(1):29-36
The only randomized comparison of network meta-analysis display design. 149 third-year medical students were randomized between two MATCH-IT versions, one using color coding to categorize interventions by magnitude and direction of effect with all outcomes shown on entry and one with neither; 82.5 percent (n=123) answered at least 4 of 5 interpretation items correctly, 75.8 percent (n=114) recommended what an expert panel recommended, and the design alternatives were preferred but had no bearing on interpretation or understandability. Compares two variants of one tool, not display families, and in students.


Lovsletten, Stokke Hunskaar, Heen, Bekkering, Vanden Poel, Zeraatkar, Vermandere, Aertgeerts, Delvaux, Achille, Busse, Agoritsas & Vandvik 2024, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 172:111399
Qualitative user testing of MATCH-IT over five development cycles with 26 practicing physicians in Norway, Belgium and Canada, 24 of whom (94 percent) had no or sparse prior experience of interpreting network meta-analysis; think-aloud plus semistructured interview with directed content analysis. Reports proof of concept and names comparison of MATCH-IT with similar tools and formats as the next step, which has not been done.


Phillips, Sadeghirad, Busse, Brignardello-Petersen, Cuello-Garcia, Kenji Nampo, Guo, Bzovsky, Bannuru, Thabane, Bhandari & Guyatt 2022, BMJ Open 12(6):e056400
Design validation of two color-coded formats for presenting minimally and partially contextualized network results across multiple outcomes, using qualitative content analysis of interviews with 26 participants including 20 practicing clinicians. Ends with two formats each preferred by a substantial group and no criterion for choosing between them; validated against a single exemplar network.


Yepes-Nunez, Li, Guyatt, Jack, Brozek, Beyene, Murad, Rochwerg, Mbuagbaw, Zhang, Florez, Siemieniuk, Sadeghirad, Mustafa, Santesso & Schunemann 2019, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 115:1-13
Develops the GRADE summary-of-findings table for network meta-analysis through four rounds of semistructured interviews with 32 stakeholders who conduct or use meta-analysis, yielding six candidate tables and one judged highly acceptable. The endpoint is acceptability, not accuracy of reading.


Veroniki, Straus, Fyraridis & Tricco 2016, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 76:193-199
Introduces the rank-heat plot for many treatments across many outcomes in one figure and states that research on the understanding of the available approaches for presenting treatment ranking by clinicians, guideline developers and policy makers is needed and critical, because different approaches may complicate inference and decision-making. That research has not been carried out.


Daly, Mbuagbaw, Thabane, Straus & Hamid 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology 20(1):266
Proof-of-concept framework plotting each treatment’s performance across outcomes as a spie chart whose coverage area represents the probability of ranking best overall, illustrated on dietary-fat and psoriasis networks. Concludes that formal validation in the decision-making context and statistical comparisons with other recent approaches are required, and neither has followed.


Seo, Furukawa, Veroniki, Pillinger, Tomlinson, Salanti, Cipriani & Efthimiou 2021, Research Synthesis Methods 12(1):86-95
The Kilim plot for multi-outcome network results, conveying uncertainty through a truncated color scale rather than intervals; states that it gives no relative effects and shows no confidence intervals, so what a reader can and cannot infer from it is a design decision that was never tested.


Carrasco-Labra, Brignardello-Petersen, Santesso, Neumann, Mustafa, Mbuagbaw, Etxeandia Ikobaltzeta, De Stio, McCullagh, Alonso-Coello, Meerpohl, Vandvik, Brozek, Akl, Bossuyt, Churchill, Glenton, Rosenbaum, Tugwell, Welch, Garner, Guyatt & Schunemann 2016, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 74:7-18
Randomized trial among 290 systematic review users comparing a new and the current summary-of-findings table format on item-by-item understanding, accessibility, satisfaction and preference, with 63 percent and 62 percent more correct answers for the new format on understanding risk difference and understanding certainty. This is the design template the network display literature has not executed; it was run on pairwise tables.


Kossmeier, Tran & Voracek 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology 20(1):26
Comprehensive review, taxonomy and feature analysis of graphical displays for meta-analysis and systematic reviews, correlating functionality features across the inventory; identifies displays that remain usable at medium to large numbers of studies while still identifying each study and its effect as rare. Maps the design space without evaluating any display against readers.

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Fix the readings before the formats: name the small set of judgments a display must support, which treatment the evidence best supports, how uncertain that ordering is, what the absolute difference is at a stated baseline risk and horizon, and which contrasts rest on indirect evidence alone, then derive the answer key for each from the fitted model rather than from opinion. Run on displays the design already executed for tables: the randomized trial that compared summary-of-findings formats among 290 review users and scored understanding item by item transfers directly to a comparison of league table, forest plot against a common comparator, rankogram or cumulative ranking curve, rank-heat plot and an interactive summary, all built from one network at fixed certainty ratings. Report accuracy per reading with the direction of the error and the time taken, so that a display can be described the way a diagnostic is described and a review can state which readings its chosen format supports and which it does not. Recruit guideline panelists and health technology assessment reviewers as the primary stratum even at sample sizes in the low hundreds, and report student samples separately rather than as evidence about committees. The cheap first step is to start with the two formats that dominate the surveyed corpus of 200 reviews, the forest plot and the league table, since those are what readers actually meet.

title: Network meta-analysis displays are tested for acceptability, not for accuracy
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. This rests on labeller-reported absence rather than on a source arguing for it: 6 of 12 gap labellers independently named it after failing to find it while attaching future-work sentences to the registry, and the supporting sentences span 15 distinct papers from 2014 to 2026, most of them proposals of a display conceding that their own format was never evaluated with readers. Checked against the registry, where DEC-05 asks what a committee page should contain, OUT-21 asks what a set of absolute effects must have in common, DEC-23 and DEC-29 concern the certainty and the distortion of the hierarchy, and DEC-30 concerns the reliability of credibility labels; none asks whether any display is read correctly. The verdict is partially-addressed rather than confirmed-open because quantitative evaluation is not wholly absent: one randomized trial with 149 medical students compared two variants of one interactive tool, and three qualitative user-testing and design-validation studies exist with 26, 26 and 32 participants. What remains unevaluated is the choice between display families, the accuracy of any of them against a defined answer key, and behavior in the panels and committees that use them. Provenance here is weaker than for neighboring entries, since no source argues the gap as a methodological problem; the evidence is a repeated admission inside display proposals that validation was not done, plus one explicit call that the research is critical because different presentations may lead to different decisions.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text: DIA-02 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Statement
A global effective sample size is a scalar function of the weight distribution, so it does not encode where in covariate space the support lies or whether the supported region is relevant to the decision contrast. Reporting is demonstrably incomplete in practice: of 117 oncology MAICs reviewed by Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088), only three fulfilled all NICE recommendations and the distribution of weights was among the least reported items. The claim that software reports ESS alone and never computes contrast-specific influence is too strong: cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, already exports a weight panel with effective sample size, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration and residual balance, plus an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast. What remains missing is a definition set agreed across packages and the support-geometry diagnostics that no package computes: region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted moments.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Why it is open
Effective sample size is the squared sum of the weights divided by the sum of their squares, so it is invariant to where the weights sit in covariate space; the same value can come from a broad shifted distribution or from a decision-relevant subgroup with no source support at all. Balance is conventionally reported on the moments that were matched, which is tautological, while balance on the omitted moments is the informative check and is usually skipped. Because no body owns the definitions and at least three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment have been proposed, two analyses of the same evidence can report incomparable numbers, and no empirical knowledge accumulates about which diagnostic values predict bias.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Farinasso et al. 2025, Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Studies in Oncology: A Scoping Review Focused on Reporting Quality
Scoping review of 117 oncology MAICs finding that only three fulfilled all NICE recommendations and that the distribution of weights was among the least reported items; sources the previously unattributed claim that diagnostic practice is heterogeneous and incomplete.


Three new methodologies for calculating the effective sample size when performing population adjustment, 2024
Proposes three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment, evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. The literature auditor retrieved this at title and venue level only.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Exports a weight-quality panel (ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, residual balance) and an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast, documented as approximate for multi-arm networks.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Standardize and extend what exists rather than specify a panel from scratch: agree one definition set across packages, starting from the multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific influence already implemented in cpaic, and add the support-geometry diagnostics no package computes, namely region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance between source and target support, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted as well as fitted moments. Require the agreed panel in publications and submissions. Evaluate each member of the panel in simulation for its ability to predict realized error, and drop the ones that only describe the fit.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Our study

The reported weight panel cannot see where support is missing
The question put to it. Every member of the overlap panel MAIC reports (Kish ESS, ESS percentage, entropy efficiency, maximum weight, top-share) is a symmetric function of the weights, so none can depend on where in covariate space the source fails to cover the target. Does that blindness matter in an ordinary covariate law, or do weight concentration and support geometry move together tightly enough that the panel is an adequate proxy?
What it found. It matters. Two source populations that remove the same mass at the same threshold, one in the effect-modifying coordinate and one in a prognostic coordinate, give panels that agree to within 1.6% while one estimate is biased by 0.016 on the marginal risk difference and the other by less than 0.0001, and material error is 24 times as frequent in the first. Across the two placements every panel member sits within 0.005 of chance; region-specific ESS separates them almost perfectly and sliced optimal transport cost at 0.73, but a convex hull distance maximized over coordinates is as blind as the panel. The registered within-arm primary outcome reads the other way (panel 0.574, best geometric 0.592, rule returns refuted) because within one arm the hole placement is fixed and the outcome measures sampling noise, not geometry. Both readings are reported. Balance on the omitted moment, the comparator most likely to overturn the headline, was never fairly tested.
Results.

The manipulation works in a plain multivariate normal law. With strong effect modification, a hole in the modifying coordinate biases MAIC’s marginal risk difference by 0.0164 and a same-sized hole in a prognostic coordinate by -0.0001, while every panel member agrees between the two arms to within 1.6%. The refuting sentence, that such a counterexample needs configurations that do not occur, fails.
Across the two hole placements, over 16,000 replicates, the best panel member separates them at 0.505 against 0.5 for chance, standard error 0.004. Region-specific ESS separates them at 1.000 and sliced optimal transport cost at 0.726. Convex hull distance, though it reads position, separates at 0.503 because it is a maximum over coordinates and both arms remove an identical wedge.
The registered primary, AUROC against material error within the high-modification arm, returns refuted: best panel member 0.574, best geometric 0.592, a gap of 0.018 against a registered materiality of 0.10. Within one arm every replicate shares the hole placement, so the registered outcome asks which replicate drew a bad sample, and a concentration measure answers that as well as anything. The registered outcome was the wrong measurement for the proposition; it is reported as registered, not relabeled.
Two of three controls failed on parts of the grid. At eight covariates and moderate overlap MAIC’s own error exceeds the 0.03 material threshold in 0.289 of replicates with no hole at all, the same threshold-below-noise defect IDN-05 documented. Leaving the modifier’s second moment unmatched breaks the symmetry the manipulation rests on and the panels diverge by up to 91%. The analysis runs on the 12 of 48 cells the controls leave, all at good overlap.
Two of the three ESS definitions implemented are the same statistic when weights are normalized, so the measured comparability spread is Kish against entropy ESS: median 1.55 times, 90th percentile 3.50, maximum 15.5 on identical data.
A post hoc probe prices the rescue of the failed strata by the upper Clopper-Pearson bound: 48,000 source records at dim3/moderate and 192,000 at dim8/moderate. It was not run.

Design.

Estimand

Target-population marginal risk difference, and material error above 0.03 as the classifier label

Methods compared

Kish ESS, ESS percentage, entropy efficiency, maximum weight, top 5% share, balance on an omitted moment, region-specific ESS, coordinatewise convex hull distance, sliced optimal transport cost

Data-generating mechanism

Target covariates independent standard normal in 3 or 8 dimensions; source shifted by 0.25 or 0.60 with a wedge above the 90th percentile removed from the effect-modifying coordinate, from a prognostic coordinate, or not at all. Binary outcome on the logit scale with one modifying coordinate. 48 cells crossing dimension, hole placement, overlap, balancing set and modification strength, source size 16,000. Nine diagnostics scored by AUROC within the high-modification arm and across the two hole placements.

Replicates

2000 per cell, 96,000 replicates; 24,000 on the 12 cells the controls leave


What this does not answer. Balance on the omitted moment, the free check registered as most likely to overturn the headline, was not tested: every cell where it had anything to see was removed by the matched-multiset control. Region-specific ESS was handed the easiest instance, since the region it examines is the region the hole empties, so its near-perfect separation is an upper bound; a hole in a high-modification region the analyst did not think to examine is untested and there it would fail like the panel. No diagnostic is calibrated to a threshold. The analysis subgrid was chosen by a mechanical rule written after the run was read. The realized high-modification hole holds 22% of the modification mass against a registered 25%. MAIC weights only, a binary outcome, normal covariates, one rectangular hole, good overlap only after the null control, and two of the three published ESS definitions. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument · Code and data: studies/DIA-02-the-whole-weight-panel-is-a-multiset-functional · Protocol: registered before the run

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
What this project measured
Study studies/DIA-02-the-whole-weight-panel-is-a-multiset-functional. Its primary outcome and controls were fixed before the run; the rule restricting the analysis to the cells the controls leave standing was written after it, as its protocol records. 48 cells, 2000 replicates each, 96,000 replicates. Nine diagnostics: the five reported panel members, all symmetric functions of the weight multiset, against four candidates that read position as well as weight.
The manipulation. Two source populations remove the same mass at the same threshold on exchangeable standard normal coordinates and differ only in which coordinate carries the hole: the one that modifies the treatment effect, or a purely prognostic one. The first is biased by +0.01639 on the target marginal risk difference; the second by -0.00009, which is zero to five decimal places. Material error, meaning the transported effect wrong by more than 0.03 absolute risk, occurs on 0.106 of replicates in the first and 0.005 in the second, against 0.003 with no hole at all.
Result on the registered primary: refuted. Section 7 registered the AUROC of each diagnostic against material error within the modifying-hole arm. There the best panel member reaches 0.574 (max_weight) and the best geometric candidate 0.592 (ess_region), a gap of 0.018 against a registered materiality of 0.10. By the registered rule the panel discriminates as well as the geometric diagnostics, and the proposition is refuted.
Result on the study’s own control: confirmed, emphatically. Section 8 registered a separate check, that at matched multisets every panel member must be numerically identical across the two support arms. Read as a discrimination task over 16,000 replicates, every panel member sits within 0.005 of chance (max_weight 0.505, ess_kish 0.502, entropy_eff 0.501, top_share 0.500) with a standard error of 0.005, while ess_region separates the two arms at 1.000 and optimal-transport cost at 0.726. The blindness is measured, not merely unrejected.
The disagreement is the finding. Within one arm every replicate shares one hole placement, so the only thing varying is sampling noise and the outcome asks which replicate drew a bad sample. A concentration measure answers that about as well as anything. The proposition is about comparing analyses at different placements, and only the cross-arm comparison varies it. The registered primary outcome was the wrong measurement for the question the study was built to ask, and the study’s own control was the right one. That is recorded rather than repaired by relabeling the control as primary after the fact.
The refuting sentence in the design fails. Two analyses differing by 0.016 in bias were built at a panel matched to 2% in an ordinary covariate law, not a contrived one, so the invariance bites in practice and not only in principle.
Two of three controls failed, and the failures cost three quarters of the grid. The matched-multiset control failed wherever a modifier’s second moment was left unmatched, by up to a 0.908 relative difference, because dropping that moment breaks the coordinate symmetry the manipulation rests on. The null control failed at dim8/moderate, where MAIC’s own sampling error exceeds the 0.03 threshold on 0.288 of replicates with no support hole at all, and at dim3/moderate at 0.021. The source size had been registered from a noise floor measured at the middle of the grid, and the middle is not the worst corner. This is the same defect IDN-05 documented, of a threshold set below its own measurement noise, and it is worth naming twice because such a floor reads as a finding. The analysis drops failing strata on the controls’ own evidence rather than on the results, leaving 12 of 48 cells and 24,000 replicates.
The comparability half, quantified for the first time. Three published ESS definitions computed on identical data disagree by a median factor of 1.55, a 90th percentile of 3.50, and a maximum of 15.48. The complaint that two analyses of the same evidence can report incomparable numbers had never been given a size.
The exclusion is not a boundary artifact. dim3/moderate is dropped on a null rate of 0.0213 against a 0.02 cut, a few Monte Carlo standard errors above it. Adding it back moves the panel from 0.5046 to 0.5024 and ess_region from 0.9999 to 0.9997, so the cut is not doing the work.
What this does not answer. Four limits, three of them live. hull_gap is a geometric diagnostic and is blind anyway, at 0.503, because it maximizes over coordinates and both arms remove an identical wedge; reading position is not sufficient if the reading is then aggregated away. balance_omitted, registered as the cheap comparator most likely to overturn the headline, was never given anything to see: the cells where it has content are exactly the ones the matched-multiset control eliminated, so the comparison the design wanted did not run. ess_region’s 1.000 is an upper bound, not an estimate of field performance: the region it examines and the region the hole empties are the same construction, so perfect separation is what the arithmetic requires. Two things keep that from being circular, namely that the region comes from the effect-modifier structure MAIC already requires naming rather than from knowledge of the hole, and that in the prognostic-hole arm the hole lies outside the examined region and the statistic correctly reads near-normal instead of firing on any hole at all. What is untested is a hole in a high-modification region the analyst did not think to examine, which is where this diagnostic would fail exactly as the panel does. And no diagnostic here is calibrated: separating two placements is not a threshold.

title: No agreed ESS definition and no support-geometry diagnostics
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from unverifiable to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source titled this. “ESS reported alone and overlap diagnostics are not standardized” The title says software reports effective sample size alone, which the audit judged too strong given an implemented multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence.
The source said. “Overlap is summarized by a single effective sample size, which cannot show the geometry of covariate support, where the analysis is extrapolating, or whether the supported region is relevant to the target contrast. The definitions and displays of overlap, ESS, extrapolation and modifier-balance diagnostics also differ between packages and publications, so two analyses of the same evidence report incomparable numbers.”
What was wrong with it. The claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced: the literature auditor supplied Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088) for heterogeneous and incomplete diagnostic reporting, and a 2024 paper proposing three competing ESS calculations (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) for the non-standardization of ESS itself. GPT-5.6 Sol read cpaic at commit 9d150e9 and found a multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence already implemented, so the ESS-only claim fails there; the two auditors disagreed on whether the entry as written was supported or overstated, and the weaker reading is published here.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): This entry is source_unsourced; I found real references that support it. Farinasso et al. 2025 scoping-reviewed 117 oncology MAICs and reports that only 3 fulfilled all NICE DSU recommendations and that among the least reported items was the distribution of weights, with mean sample-size reduction 44.9%. That is direct published evidence that diagnostic reporting practice is heterogeneous and suboptimal. Independently, a 2024 BMC Med Res Methodol paper proposes three new ESS calculations for population adjustment, which is itself evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. I found no PAIC package or publication reporting local (region-specific) ESS, optimal-transport cost, convex-hull distance, out-of-distribution maps, balance on omitted moments, or influence alignment between IPD study edges and the decision contrast; those remain absent, though absence found by search is weaker evidence than the reporting review. codex dissented (overstated): C4 through C7 follow directly from ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2): the same weights can be reassigned to different covariate locations without changing ESS, despite different local support and contrast relevance. The claim that software reports only ESS and never computes contrast-specific influence is already false for cpaic at the requested commit. It exports weight_diagnostics() with ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, and residual balance, plus edge_influence() for a named treatment contrast. The latter is documented as approximate for multi-arm networks. Local ESS, convex-hull distance, density ratios, and transport costs are complementary diagnostics requiring careful definitions and validation, not established replacements for ESS. Cross-package standardization and fuller support-geometry diagnostics remain open.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text: DIA-04 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Statement
ADEMP already requires estimands to be defined and instructs analysts to consider whether each method is appropriate for the estimand identified, and Section 3.4 of Morris et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/sim.8086) works through the marginal-versus-conditional example that produces exactly the spurious bias this entry describes. What ADEMP does not provide is a structured per-scenario identification map recording which estimands are identified under the data-generating mechanism and under each fitted method’s own assumptions, and no journal or software requirement enforces one, so PAIC simulations routinely omit it. The underlying dispute has already been argued in public in this field, in the exchange over the anchored population-adjustment simulation and the reply on target estimands for efficient decision making (doi:10.1002/sim.8965), so reviewers do have ground on which to demand the mapping.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Why it is open
In PAIC the compared estimators target different populations (index trial, comparator trial, decision target) and different conditional or marginal contrasts, so a single scalar true value is ambiguous and non-identification can be reported as estimator bias. ADEMP’s instruction to check method-to-estimand compatibility is prose guidance rather than a required per-scenario artifact, so it is easy to skip and reviewers have nothing concrete to insist on. What is actually needed is a way to distinguish four things that all surface as bias: estimand mismatch, non-identification under the generating mechanism, model misspecification, and finite-sample bias.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Morris et al. 2019, Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
Defines the ADEMP framework; its Methods element already instructs investigators to consider whether each method is appropriate for the estimand or target identified, and Section 3.4 works the marginal-versus-conditional example that produces spurious bias. It does not formalize a per-scenario identification map.


Target estimands for efficient decision making: Response to comments on Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study, 2021
A published exchange in the PAIC literature about which estimand a simulation’s true value refers to and whether the compared methods target it, showing the dispute is already live rather than unrecognized.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write a PAIC-specific extension of ADEMP rather than a competing framework: a per-scenario identification table stating, for each method, which estimand it targets and whether that estimand is identified under the data-generating mechanism, so that every reported bias is labeled as estimand mismatch, non-identification, misspecification or finite-sample bias. Do not restrict bias reporting to estimands a method claims to identify, since robustness simulations legitimately score every method against the policy-relevant estimand under deliberate assumption violation; label the cell rather than remove it. Attach the table to the simulation protocol so that journals and reviewers have something specific to require.

title: ADEMP has no identification map for simulation estimands
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. ADEMP tells analysts to consider whether each method is appropriate for the stated estimand, but provides no structured per-scenario identification map recording which estimands are identified under the data-generating mechanism and under each method’s assumptions; no journal or software requirement enforces such a map, and PAIC simulations routinely omit it.
The source said. “Simulation studies of ITC and PAIC follow ADEMP, but no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to state which estimands are identified under the generating assumptions and which are identified under each fitted method’s own assumptions. Bias is therefore computed against a truth some compared methods never claimed to estimate.”
What was wrong with it. The source said no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to check whether a method can recover the stated estimand; both auditors found this false, since Table 1 of Morris et al. 2019 (doi:10.1002/sim.8086) instructs investigators to identify methods and consider whether they are appropriate for the estimand or target identified, and Section 3.4 uses the conditional-versus-marginal case as its worked example. What is missing is a formalized per-scenario identification map, not the underlying instruction.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Morris, White & Crowther 2019. The five-element claim is right (element three is ‘Estimands and other targets’, slightly broader than ‘Estimands’). But the central claim, that no element of ADEMP forces the analyst to consider whether each fitted method can recover the stated estimand, is contradicted by the paper itself. Table 1 lists under Methods: ‘Identify methods to be evaluated and consider whether they are appropriate for estimand/target identified.’ Section 3.4 devotes a passage to precisely the PAIC failure mode described, using the marginal-versus-conditional logistic regression example, i.e. non-collapsibility. Further, the specific dispute has already been litigated in the PAIC literature: Remiro-Azocar, Heath & Baio’s comment on Phillippo et al.’s simulation and Phillippo et al.’s reply, ‘Target estimands for efficient decision making’, are an explicit argument about bias being computed against a truth a compared method did not target. Reviewers therefore do have ground to demand the mapping. What is genuinely missing is a formalized per-scenario identification map as a required reporting element. Cites 10.1002/sim.8086: The ADEMP Methods element and Table 1 already instruct analysts to check method-estimand compatibility, and Section 3.4 works the exact marginal-vs-conditional example that produces spurious bias in PAIC.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8965: Demonstrates that the PAIC field has already had a public, published argument about which estimand a simulation’s true value refers to and whether competing methods target it..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is correct, and ADEMP does not prescribe a formal per-scenario identification matrix. The report nevertheless overlooks that Morris et al. already require explicit estimands, require methods to be assessed for compatibility with those estimands, and use conditional versus marginal odds ratios as the exact example of a misleading bias comparison. The proposed rule that bias be computed only for estimands a method claims to identify is also too restrictive: robustness simulations legitimately evaluate a method against the policy-relevant estimand under deliberate assumption violation. The necessary distinction is among estimand mismatch, nonidentification, misspecification, and finite-sample bias. A PAIC-specific identification table would improve reporting, but this is a partially addressed reporting extension rather than an unrecognized very-high-priority barrier. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.8086: ADEMP defines the five stated elements and already instructs investigators to check whether each method is appropriate for the chosen estimand, including explicit treatment of conditional-versus-marginal mismatch. It does not formalize a PAIC-specific identification matrix..

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text: DIA-06 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Statement
Factorial simulations have already located the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted indirect comparison: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) sweeps overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size and missing modifiers and reports that MAIC may even increase bias compared with standard indirect comparisons; Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511) locates the bias-variance crossover over 162 scenarios; and Liu et al. 2025 (doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1) runs a 729-scenario full factorial and finds MAIC more biased than naive indirect comparison at low covariate overlap with high covariate strength. What no study does is characterize and contrast the failure signatures of weighting-based, outcome-model-based and machine-learning estimators as overlap deteriorates, or report whether those failures are visible in any reported diagnostic. Flexible learners are absent from this simulation literature entirely.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Why it is open
Adjustment trades a bias term that depends on unobserved cross-study modifier imbalance against an observable variance penalty, so the exact data-specific gain cannot be learned from the data at hand without causal and modeling assumptions, although observed imbalance, prespecified effect modifiers, trial design and external knowledge still inform the decision. Weighting estimators fail by variance explosion and weight concentration while outcome-model estimators fail silently by extrapolating a fitted surface into regions with no data, so the two signatures are not comparable on any single performance measure, and flexible learners make this worse because their extrapolation behavior is set by regularization rather than by an explicit functional form. The existing factorials fix the estimator set narrowly, so the differential behavior near the support boundary is never observed even in the studies that have mapped the crossover region.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Factorial simulation crossing overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size, missing modifiers and covariate distributions across MAIC, STC and ML-NMR, reporting where adjustment fails to pay.


Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021, Methods for population adjustment with limited access to individual patient data: A review and simulation study
162-scenario simulation locating the bias-variance crossover as covariate overlap degrades.


Liu et al. 2025, Is the Use of Unanchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison Always Superior to Naive Indirect Comparison on Survival Outcomes? A Simulation Study
729-scenario three-level full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and covariate strength, identifying the region where MAIC is more biased than naive indirect comparison.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Records a factorial comparison across imbalance and overlap for naive bridging, cSTC and cMAIC; narrow in estimator coverage, and the auditor notes its validation pipeline was not publicly tracked and the result was not independently reproducible from the public commit.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing overlap-by-effect-modification factorials rather than repeat them: hold their design fixed and add outcome-model, ML-NMR, doubly robust and flexible-learner arms, sweep overlap from complete to near-disjoint, and record for each estimator family the onset of bias, the onset of variance inflation, and whether either is visible in any diagnostic the analyst would actually report. Report failure signatures rather than only average performance, so the output is a map of how each family degrades rather than a single winner. Publish the code so the comparison can be re-run as new estimators appear.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Our study

Effective sample size tracks the error an analysis got by chance better than the error it got from adjusting on the wrong covariates
This study was designed against DIA-03 and bears on this entry in part. What it does not answer is stated below.
The question put to it. Every population adjustment arrives with a panel of numbers beside it: effective sample size, the same figure as a percentage, the largest weight, standardized differences before and after adjustment, a distance between populations. A committee reads them as evidence about whether to believe the estimate, and a widely quoted rule says to worry below an effective sample size of about 30 to 35. Scored as classifiers of realized error, with discrimination and calibration, against known truth and under a declared distribution of analyses, what are they worth?
What it found. At the level at which a diagnostic is actually read, one analysis at a time, effective sample size tracks the error a study got by chance far better than the error it got from adjusting on the wrong covariates: AUROC 0.847 against the outcome-noise component and 0.813 against chance covariate imbalance between the source arms, both of which are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, against 0.653 for the transport component that adjustment exists to remove. At the quoted cutoff of 35 it catches between a quarter and a third of material errors in every misspecification stratum, 0.309 where an effect modifier is omitted and the omission is diagnosable in principle, at specificity 0.926. No evaluated fixed cutoff met the registered requirement of sensitivity 0.80 at specificity 0.50 in every stratum. Three of the panel’s members are provably one statistic, since ESS/n = 1/(1+CV^2(w)) exactly and area under the ROC curve is invariant to monotone transformation; a fourth, the post-weighting balance on matched moments, is zero at the solution of the calibration equations and among converged analyses cannot discriminate anything. On a decision-curve basis every rule in the panel is beaten by scrutinizing every analysis, up to an action threshold of 0.3.
Results.

Prespecified verdict: the panel does not classify realized error at the thresholds in use. No rule reached sensitivity 0.80 with specificity 0.50 in every misspecification stratum. ESS below 35 reaches sensitivity 0.251 to 0.326 across strata at specificity 0.909 to 0.926.
The mechanism, registered before the run and holding at the level of a single analysis: effective sample size discriminates the outcome-noise component at AUROC 0.847 and the transport component at 0.653, a gap of 0.194, and the arm-imbalance component at 0.813. The two it reads well are the two that are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, which is what the panel is built from.
Peer review changed this claim and the paper’s title. Scored against SYSTEMATIC transport bias with the design cell as the unit, rather than against the realized transport component of one replicate, effective sample size reaches 0.808 rather than 0.653. That analysis does not rescue the panel either: the statistic that is identically zero reaches 0.708 on it, because 128 cells is a small sample in which the bias and every diagnostic move along the same overlap axis. Both levels are reported and the title now claims only the replicate-level result.
The panel is smaller than it looks, by algebra rather than by simulation. ESS, ESS as a percentage and the coefficient of variation of the weights had identical areas under the ROC curve to 0.0e+00 within a fixed source size. The matched-moment balance statistic never exceeded 1.4e-14 and its apparent AUROC of 0.550 is discrimination of floating-point residual, not of balance.
Silence is where the damage is. Across the 88 cells the ESS rule never fires in, the material-error rate runs from 0.045 to 0.835. The registered version of this claim, a spread across the cells it does fire in, was not met (0.150 against a prespecified 0.30) because those cells are all bad. A first draft called the silent-cell span a stronger version of the registered claim; peer review established that both spans are variation in predictive value, which moves with prevalence and case mix, so neither is a test of whether a threshold transports. That promotion is withdrawn and the leave-one-factor-level-out calibration is the evidence on transportability.
Decision-curve analysis: at action thresholds up to 0.3, flagging every analysis beats every rule in the panel. From 0.4 upwards three distinct statistics beat both alternatives, relative effective sample size, pre-weighting imbalance and Mahalanobis distance; the absolute cutoff that gets quoted is not among them at any threshold examined.
The same statistics work when they measure the actual gap. Pre-weighting imbalance predicts the unadjusted comparison’s transport error at AUROC 0.891, against 0.655 for the same statistic applied to MAIC. These diagnostics are informative about the problem and uninformative about the solution: weighting sets to zero the very quantity they measure.
Our proposal, converting residual imbalance on a measured but unadjusted covariate into the units of the estimand with the source-estimated interaction, reaches 0.937 against the transport component over the diagnosable set where effective sample size as a percentage reaches 0.851. That gain of 0.086 misses the 0.10 we registered and is reported as a miss. Inside the omitted-modifier stratum alone the plain balance check on unmatched covariates beats it, 0.946 against 0.938, because there the covariate is always a modifier and converting imbalance into effect units only adds estimation noise. The conversion earns its keep exactly when the analyst does not know whether the unmatched covariate matters.
An adversarial critique of the design before the run found two arithmetic errors in the protocol: the dispersion factor was not the pure variance instrument it was described as wherever the cross-moment channel was on, and the target trial’s variance was understated by a factor of two to three. Both were confirmed numerically and corrected before any result was seen.
Round one of review found the load-bearing claim of the paper wrong, and all three reviewers found it independently. The arm-imbalance component uses no outcome at all, and the noise component’s variance is exactly sigma^2 (1/ESS_A + 1/ESS_C), so a weight statistic is its natural summary rather than merely correlated with it. Round one also found that the calibration split was perfectly confounded with the dispersion factor, because cells are enumerated with that factor varying fastest; leave-one-factor-level-out replaced it and the previous claim that overlap statistics calibrate worse than weight statistics was withdrawn as an artifact.

Design.

Estimand

Transported A versus C mean difference in the target superpopulation; the anchored A versus B contrast as a secondary reference

Methods compared

MAIC matching means and standard deviations, MAIC matching means only, STC with a heteroskedasticity-consistent variance, no adjustment

Data-generating mechanism

An anchored indirect comparison with a continuous outcome and an identity link, chosen so that the realized error of a linear estimator splits exactly into arm imbalance, transport error and outcome noise, so each diagnostic can be scored against each component separately: two of the three are functions of the covariates, the assignment and the weights, which is what the panel is built from, and the third is what adjustment exists to remove. 128 cells crossing an omitted effect modifier, a cross-moment modifier that no baseline table could reveal, overlap, source size, how correlated the omitted modifier is with the adjustment set, and a target dispersion ratio that destroys effective sample size while adding no bias where the modifier structure is correct. 4000 replicates per cell, four estimators. Primary results are reported within misspecification strata rather than over a mixture, so no investigator-chosen frequency enters the headline.

Replicates

4000 per cell, 512,000 datasets and 2,048,000 estimates


What this does not answer. The second half of DIA-03 is untouched: no PSIS-LOO is computed at any hierarchical level and grouped study-level leave-one-out is no more implemented here than in the packages, so the mismatch between the level at which cross-validation is reported and the level at which the prediction is made remains open. DIA-06 is answered only in part; two estimator families and no adjustment are compared on identical replicates, but ML-NMR, NMI, doubly robust estimators and flexible learners are absent. The outcome is continuous with an identity link, which is what buys the exact error decomposition and is also the largest restriction: nothing here transfers to non-collapsible effect measures or time-to-event outcomes, where part of the error is a collapsibility artifact rather than an adjustment failure. Covariates are normal, comparisons are anchored, conditional constancy holds, and target moments are exact. The deployment weights are a declared judgment and nothing in this program measured them, which is why the primary results are within strata.
Peer review. 2 rounds, two independent reviewers. The reports, the point-by-point responses and the editorial decision are published in full: read the review.

title: Failure signatures across PAIC estimator families are uncharacterized
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Factorial simulations have located the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted indirect comparison, but no study characterizes and contrasts the failure signatures of weighting-based versus outcome-model-based versus machine-learning PAIC estimators as overlap deteriorates, nor reports whether those failures are visible in any diagnostic.
The source titled this. “When adjustment pays, and how each estimator fails, is unknown” The title says when adjustment pays is unknown, but three published factorial simulations already locate the region where MAIC stops improving on an unadjusted comparison.
The source said. “The field cannot say under which conditions population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC or NMA and under which it merely adds variance without reducing bias. Nor has it characterized how MAIC, standardized outcome regression, ML-NMR, doubly robust methods and flexible learners each fail as source-target overlap deteriorates.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no evidence base specifying when population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC; the literature auditor found three factorial simulations that map exactly that region (doi:10.1002/sim.8759, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1511, doi:10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1), and GPT-5.6 Sol found a factorial imbalance-and-overlap comparison of naive bridging, cSTC and cMAIC in the cpaic development package. What survives is the comparative failure-signature question across estimator families.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that there is no evidence base specifying when population adjustment materially improves an ordinary ITC is contradicted by at least three factorial simulations I retrieved. Phillippo et al. 2020 crossed sample size, missing effect modifiers, strength of effect modification, shared-effect-modifier validity, extrapolation validity, between-study overlap (a proxy parameter kappa swept from no overlap to full overlap) and covariate distributions, and reported that MAIC ‘may even increase bias compared with standard indirect comparisons’ - i.e. the region where adjustment does not pay. Remiro-Azocar et al. 2021 ran 162 scenarios and located the crossover explicitly. Liu et al. 2025 ran 729 scenarios in a three-level full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and covariate strength and identified the failure region for MAIC versus naive comparison. What remains genuinely open is the comparative failure-signature question: no study I found sweeps overlap to near-disjoint and records, per estimator family, onset of bias versus onset of variance inflation and whether any diagnostic sees it, and flexible learners are absent entirely. Cites 10.1007/s40258-025-00952-1: 729-scenario full factorial over six factors including covariate overlap and strength; identifies the region where adjustment is worse than not adjusting.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Factorial simulation crossing overlap, effect-modification strength, sample size, missing modifiers and covariate distributions across MAIC, STC and ML-NMR, and reporting where adjustment fails to pay.. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1511: 162-scenario simulation locating the bias-variance crossover as overlap degrades..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2, C5, and C6 are correct qualitative statements. Basic theory already identifies the crossover: without relevant effect modification or source-target imbalance, adjustment cannot remove that bias and may add variance; under positivity failure, weighting becomes concentrated while outcome regression relies on extrapolation and model correctness. Exact data-specific MSE improvement cannot be learned from observed data without causal and modeling assumptions, but adjustment decisions can still use observed imbalance, prespecified effect modifiers, trial design, and external knowledge. At cpaic commit 9d150e9, the README reports a factorial overlap-and-imbalance comparison of naive bridging, cSTC, and cMAIC, so “no evidence base” is false. That evidence is narrow, and the commit itself says its validation pipeline was not publicly tracked. A broad comparison including ML-NMR, doubly robust estimators, and flexible learners remains open. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: The package records a factorial comparison across imbalance and overlap for naive bridging, cSTC, and cMAIC, partially characterizing when adjustment changes bias and uncertainty. It does not cover the full estimator set and was not independently reproducible from the public commit..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

Does the later work answer the earlier work? title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Statement
PAIC simulation generators have begun to include non-normal, bimodal and Gamma covariates and deliberate positivity violations: Phillippo et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/sim.8759) includes Gamma covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep from no overlap to full overlap, Serret-Larmande et al. 2025 (arxiv:2507.12241) runs eight scenarios from ideal conditions to positivity violations with bimodal covariates, and copula (NORTA) generation of comparator covariates from reported summaries is already in use (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13). The premise also needs correcting: matching the full mean vector and covariance matrix of a nonsingular multivariate normal fixes the joint law, so the matched-moments failure mode comes from balancing a finite set of reported moments rather than from Gaussianity as such, and a shared-linear generator can still separate methods on efficiency, variance and finite-sample behavior even though it cannot test robustness to departures. The gap that survives is on the effect-modification side: component-specific, nonlinear-threshold and subnetwork-varying modification, decoupling of the within-study interaction from the between-study ecological gradient, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are all absent.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Why it is open
Data generated under shared linear effect modification cannot evaluate robustness to departures from that structure or demonstrate the benefit of relaxing it, so on the question that matters most the comparison is decided by the generator rather than by the methods. The distinction between a within-study interaction and a between-study ecological gradient exists only with multiple studies and varying covariate distributions, so single-pair templates cannot represent aggregation bias at all. Variables that drive participation but not outcome, and trial-engagement effects, require an explicit selection model that standard generators do not contain.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Serret-Larmande et al. 2025, Assessing the Impact of Covariate Distribution and Positivity Violation on Weighting-Based Indirect Comparisons: a Simulation Study
Runs eight scenarios from ideal conditions to positivity violations with non-normal and bimodal covariate distributions and reports which weighting estimators break, contradicting the claim that PAIC simulations cannot produce the limited-support failure mode.


Phillippo et al. 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study
Includes Gamma-distributed covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep from no overlap to full overlap, contradicting the multivariate-normal-only premise; also varies the validity of the shared effect modifier assumption.


Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Uses NORTA (Gaussian copula) sampling to build comparator covariate distributions from reported summaries, showing that copula generation is already standard practice in this literature.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Take the non-normal, bimodal and copula-based covariate generators that already exist and add explicit control over local support gaps, tail behavior and correlation, so that scenarios matching every reported moment while having disjoint local support can be produced on demand; vary target definition (trial, registry, pooled, overlap), measurement error, differing cut-points and missing target moments with wrong dependence assumptions as factors rather than fixing them. Concentrate new work on the effect-modification side by generating treatment-specific, component-specific, nonlinear-threshold, modifier-by-modifier and subnetwork-varying modification, and explicitly decoupling the within-study interaction from the between-study ecological gradient so aggregation bias becomes measurable. Add participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects through an explicit selection model to test whether adjusting for them inflates variance or induces bias.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Our study

Does the generator’s effect-modification structure decide the method ranking?
The question put to it. When effect modification departs from the shared linear form most simulations use, does the ranking of population-adjustment methods change?
What it found. Not at these magnitudes. The RMSE ordering under shared linear modification was reproduced under threshold, interaction and quadratic modification at every overlap level (rank correlation 0.9 to 1.0, the only change a swap between the two worst methods). STC with linear interactions ranked first everywhere even though the departures biased it by up to 0.12, because weighting methods lost more to variance at poor overlap. The generator decides a ranking only when a departure’s bias exceeds the precision differences between methods.
Results.

Registered verdict REFUTED: Spearman correlation between the linear and departure orderings 0.9 to 1.0 in all 9 comparisons (the analysis first classified one exact 0.9 as below threshold through floating point; rounding fixed it).
STC linear bias under the interaction and quadratic departures at target mean 1.2: 0.12 and 0.10, coverage 0.94; RMSE 0.34 against 0.53 to 0.56 for MAIC.
Quadratic STC did not overtake linear STC under the departures it models: its extra variance exceeded the bias it removed.
Skewed covariates with linear modification reordered methods as much as any modification departure.

Design.

Estimand

Marginal log odds ratio, B versus A, in the target population

Methods compared

unadjusted (Bucher), MAIC on means, MAIC on means and SDs, STC with linear interactions, STC with quadratic and product interactions

Data-generating mechanism

Anchored binary-outcome comparison with reported moments held fixed; linear, threshold, interaction and quadratic modification at three overlap levels, plus skewed covariates; unadjusted, two MAIC and two STC specifications ranked by RMSE and compared by rank correlation. 2000 replicates per cell.

Replicates

2000 per scenario, 32,000 in total


What this does not answer. Moderate departure magnitudes only; treatment-specific, subnetwork and within-versus-between departures need a network and were not run; no ML-NMR. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: PAIC simulations generate only shared, linear effect modification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. PAIC simulation generators have begun to include non-normal, bimodal and Gamma covariates and deliberate positivity violations, but effect-modification generators remain almost entirely shared-and-linear: component-specific, nonlinear-threshold and subnetwork-varying modification, decoupling of within-study interaction from between-study ecological gradient, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are absent.
The source titled this. “Covariate and modifier generators are too benign to break methods” The title says covariate generators are too benign, but the audit found Gamma and bimodal covariates and deliberate positivity violations already in published generators.
The source said. “Simulations generate multivariate normal covariates and shared linear effect modification, so by construction they cannot produce the two failure modes that dominate practice: populations that match on every reported global moment while containing regions of covariate space with no source support, and effect modification that is treatment-specific, component-specific, nonlinear, subnetwork-varying, or driven by an ecological gradient different from the within-study interaction. Non-Gaussian and multimodal marginals, ordinal and skewed variables, tail behavior, rare biomarker subgroups, temporal drift, measurement error, differing cut-points, alternative target definitions, participation-only variables and trial-engagement effects are all absent.”
What was wrong with it. The source said PAIC simulations use multivariate normal covariates and therefore cannot produce matched moments with disjoint support, and that the required copula machinery is missing from simulation code; the literature auditor found Gamma and bimodal covariate scenarios with deliberate positivity violations already published (doi:10.1002/sim.8759, arxiv:2507.12241) and NORTA copula generation already in use (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13). GPT-5.6 Sol corrected the Gaussian argument itself, since matching the full mean and covariance of a nonsingular normal identifies the joint law, and the claim that a shared-linear truth cannot distinguish methods at all.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The premise that PAIC simulations generate multivariate normal covariates ‘so by construction’ cannot produce matched-moments-with-disjoint-support is factually wrong for at least two studies I retrieved. Phillippo et al. 2020 simulated Gamma covariates in dedicated scenarios alongside normal ones and swept an overlap parameter from no overlap to full overlap. Serret-Larmande et al. 2025 ran eight scenarios spanning ideal conditions through positivity violations and non-normal, explicitly including bimodal, covariate distributions, and found MAIC-2 and propensity-score weighting sensitive to positivity violations while MAIC-1 stayed unbiased. Copula machinery is also already in use in this literature: Ren et al. 2025 use NORTA/Gaussian copula sampling to build comparator covariate distributions from reported summaries. The effect-modification half of the entry fares better: Phillippo 2020 varied validity of the shared effect modifier assumption, but I found nothing generating component-specific, nonlinear-threshold, subnetwork-varying modification, nor anything decoupling within-study interaction from an ecological gradient, nor participation-only variables or trial-engagement effects. Cites arXiv:2507.12241: Directly contradicts the claim that PAIC simulations cannot produce the matched-moments/limited-support failure mode: it deliberately simulates non-normal and bimodal covariates with positivity violations and reports which estimators break.. Cites 10.1002/sim.8759: Includes Gamma-distributed covariate scenarios and an explicit overlap sweep, contradicting the multivariate-normal-only premise.. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.13: Shows copula (NORTA) covariate generation from reported marginals is already standard practice in this literature, contradicting ‘requires copula machinery that most simulation code does not contain’..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The core validation concern is real, but several absolutes fail. C1 holds for a finite set of reported moments; a complete moment-determining sequence is a different claim. For nonsingular multivariate normals, matching the full mean vector and covariance matrix fixes the joint law and both populations have support on all of R^p. Matching only marginal means and variances does not fix correlations, however, and finite Gaussian samples can still have severe practical overlap problems. MAIC balances selected moments rather than establishing joint-law equality, while ML-NMR integration requires a specified joint distribution. C3, C5-C6, and C8-C12 are defensible scenario dimensions. C7 is false as written: a shared-linear truth can still distinguish methods on efficiency, variance, regularization, computation, and finite-sample behavior; it merely cannot evaluate robustness to departures or demonstrate the benefit of relaxing the shared-linear assumption. C4’s prevalence claim is outside this technical audit. The proposed expansion is primarily a validation roadmap, not uniformly a very-high-severity defect in every decision analysis.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)
