text: DIA-10 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Statement
No PAIC simulation varies informative IPD availability, selective baseline or outcome reporting, MNAR covariate or outcome missingness, informative censoring, differential loss to follow-up, or sampling error on published target summaries, so access-driven error goes unmeasured and is attributed to method failure by default. Two parts of the original claim need narrowing. A simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error already exists in the reconstruction literature (doi:10.1177/23814683221077643); what is missing is its propagation into PAIC estimator performance. And a sponsor holding IPD for its own trial makes access treatment-dependent without making it depend on the study-specific treatment effect, so an explicit availability model is needed when inference generalizes over studies and availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics, not automatically.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Why it is open
Simulating informative availability requires an explicit model coupling data access to effect-relevant study characteristics, which no PAIC generator contains. Treating published target moments as fixed removes a genuine uncertainty component whenever the estimand is a superpopulation target, and no simulation can show the consequence if the generator never adds sampling error to them. Selective reporting mechanisms are simply absent from the design space, and digitization error, although it has a standard evaluation design of its own in the reconstruction literature, has never been carried through into PAIC estimator performance.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




A Method for Reconstructing Individual Patient Data From Kaplan-Meier Survival Curves That Incorporate Marked Censoring Times, 2022
Illustrates the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error, narrowing the claim that digitization error has no standard generator. Retrieved at title, venue and summary level only.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Add data-access mechanisms to the generator: reconstruction error using the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct design, sampling error on published target summaries wherever the estimand is a superpopulation target, selective reporting of baseline characteristics and outcomes, MNAR covariate and outcome missingness, informative censoring, and differential loss to follow-up. Model informative IPD availability explicitly where availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics rather than assuming sponsor ownership makes it informative. Report how each mechanism degrades estimator and interval performance separately from the primary causal assumptions, so that access-driven error is not attributed to method failure.

title: Data access is simulated as benign rather than informative
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source said. “Simulation designs treat data access as benign: IPD is assumed available at random, published target summaries are treated as fixed and known, and pseudo-IPD is treated as exact. MAR and MNAR covariate missingness, outcome missingness and informative censoring, selective baseline and outcome reporting, informative IPD availability, digitization error, sampling error in target summaries and differential loss to follow-up are not varied.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated digitization error as having no standard generator and sponsor-held IPD as automatically informative; the literature auditor found an established simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design (doi:10.1177/23814683221077643), and GPT-5.6 Sol separated structurally asymmetric access from an effect-informative availability mechanism and noted that fixed target summaries are appropriate when the target is the realized comparator-trial sample rather than a superpopulation.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: A Bayesian hierarchical model for network meta-analysis of m. New citations: 10.1093/biostatistics/kxx025

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. I found no PAIC simulation that varies informative IPD availability, selective baseline or outcome reporting, MNAR covariate or outcome missingness, informative censoring, differential loss to follow-up, or sampling error on published target summaries, so the core of the entry stands. The digitization sub-claim needs narrowing: the pseudo-IPD reconstruction literature does have a standard evaluation design in which curves are simulated, digitized and reconstructed and hazard ratios and survival quantiles are compared with the originals, and there is recent work propagating reconstruction uncertainty into downstream synthesis by bootstrapping pseudo-IPD. So a digitization-error generator is not absent from evidence synthesis generally; what is absent is its propagation into PAIC estimator performance. I retrieved these reconstruction items at title/summary level only, hence the moderate confidence. Cites 10.1177/23814683221077643: Illustrates the existing simulate-digitize-reconstruct evaluation design for digitization error, narrowing the claim that digitization error has no standard generator. Retrieved at title/venue and summary level only..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C2, C4, and C5 identify legitimate and distinct mechanisms. C1, however, confuses a structurally asymmetric data configuration with an informative missing-data mechanism. A sponsor possessing IPD for its own treatment makes access treatment-dependent, but it does not by itself make access depend on the study-specific treatment effect or induce selection bias. An explicit availability model is needed only when inference generalizes over studies and availability depends on effect-relevant study characteristics. C3 also needs an estimand condition: target summaries have sampling uncertainty for inference to a target superpopulation, but they may properly be conditioned on as fixed when the target is the realized comparator-trial sample. Consequently, treating them as fixed does not remove uncertainty from every valid downstream interval. Claims about what simulations usually assume are outside this audit. The access and missingness extensions are valuable, but their necessity and severity depend on the inferential target and actual evidence-acquisition process.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text: DIA-12 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Statement
A standard generator for component nonadditivity exists and has been used to quantify its consequences: Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) adds log-scale interaction departures at mild and strong magnitudes, crosses them with three heterogeneity levels, and reports mean squared error and coverage separately for connected and disconnected networks. Competing bridges have also been compared on the same disconnected network, component additivity against a matching bridge, by Rucker et al. 2020 (doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339). Conditional on a specified drift model the bias is quantifiable rather than unknown: main-effect drift enters the decision contrast as an inner product of the contrast loading with the drift vector, interaction drift as the same loading applied to the drift matrix evaluated at the target covariate value, and cpaic, an unreleased GitHub development package not on CRAN, already maps bounded main-effect drift to a worst-case decision-contrast shift and threshold. What is genuinely open is generating data under one bridge and fitting the competing bridges to rank them by worst-case behavior under misspecification, and any parameterization of drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Why it is open
Each bridge imports a different structural assumption, so their failures are not on a common scale and can only be ranked by generating data under one bridge and fitting the others, which no study has done; applied analysts therefore choose a bridge by data availability rather than robustness. A violation is untestable only when it lies in an observationally equivalent cross-subnetwork direction or the bridge supplies no overidentifying restriction, so a shared component estimable in more than one subnetwork, or an additive model with residual degrees of freedom, can reveal incompatibility, although failure to reject cannot validate the bridge. Drift on component-by-modifier interactions is the violation that interacts with population adjustment and has no parameterization at all, and because drift oriented along the target contrast biases the decision while orthogonal drift may cancel, magnitude alone cannot summarize it.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Supplies a reusable parameterization for generating additivity (bridge) violations at mild and strong magnitudes and quantifies the resulting mean squared error and coverage penalty in disconnected networks.


Rucker et al. 2021, Component network meta-analysis compared to a matching method in a disconnected network: A case study
Compares two competing bridges, component additivity and a matching-adjusted indirect comparison using single-arm observational studies, on the same disconnected network, contradicting the absolute form of the no-evidence claim.


cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9
Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Its bridge_fragility() implements a worst-case mapping from bounded component main-effect drift to decision-contrast movement with a tipping threshold, verified by a regression test; it does not cover interaction drift, hidden synergy, stochastic drift correlation or comparative bridge ranking.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the additivity-violation generator that already exists to cover interaction drift alongside main-effect drift, crossed with drift correlation and with drift direction relative to the target contrast, and extend the existing worst-case main-effect fragility mapping to interaction drift, hidden synergy, treatment-version differences, class outliers, wrong dose-response shape and external-control confounding. Then run the comparative study nobody has run: generate networks under each bridge mechanism in turn, fit all competing bridges, and report bias, decision error and detectability, ranking bridges by worst-case behavior under misspecification rather than by efficiency when correct. Publish the resulting mapping from drift magnitude, correlation and direction to decision-contrast bias as a function of network geometry, in units applied analysts can elicit.

title: No study ranks competing bridges by worst-case misspecification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. A standard generator exists for component nonadditivity and has been used to quantify its consequences, but no study generates data under one disconnected-network bridge and fits the competing bridges to rank them by worst-case behavior under misspecification, and no parameterization exists for drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices.
The source titled this. “Bridge violations have no standard generator or robustness ranking” The title says bridge violations have no standard generator, but a published, code-shared generator for additivity violations already quantifies error and coverage.
The source said. “There is no standard way to generate violations of bridging assumptions in simulation, no quantitative mapping from plausible component nonadditivity or cross-subnetwork drift to bias in the decision contrast, and no evidence on which bridge (baseline-risk exchangeability, reference prediction, component additivity, class exchangeability, dose-response, external controls, expert priors) degrades least dangerously when its assumption is misspecified.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no standard way to generate bridging violations and no quantitative mapping from nonadditivity or drift to decision-contrast bias; the literature auditor found a published, code-shared generator for additivity violations with quantified error and coverage penalties (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) and a head-to-head comparison of two bridges on one disconnected network (doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339), and GPT-5.6 Sol found the drift-to-decision mapping already implemented as bridge_fragility() in cpaic at commit 9d150e9.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

normalized a citation year: ‘Rucker et al. 2020, Component network meta-analysis compared to a matching method in a disconnected network: A case study’ -> ‘Rucker et al. 2021, Component network meta-analysis compared to a matching method in a disconnected network: A case study’ 10.1002/bimj.201900339 is cited with two different years across the registry. CrossRef gives 2020 online and 2021 in print; the issue year is used throughout.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The claim ‘There is no standard way to generate violations of bridging assumptions in simulation’ is contradicted for the component-additivity bridge. Petropoulou et al. 2023 use exactly such a parameterization: log-scale interaction departures added to the additive combination effect, with mild (exp(lambda)=1.5) and strong variants applied to different combinations, crossed with three heterogeneity levels, and scored by mean squared error and coverage separately for connected and disconnected networks. That is a published, code-shared generator plus a quantified mapping from violation magnitude to error in the affected contrasts. The cross-bridge ranking claim fares better but is not untouched: Rucker, Schmitz & Schwarzer 2020 fit the CNMA bridge and a matching/propensity bridge to the same disconnected multiple-myeloma network and compare, and Beliveau et al. 2017 stress-test the random-baseline bridge by disconnecting real networks. What remains genuinely open is a common scale, generating under one bridge and fitting all the others, and specifically drift on component-by-modifier interaction matrices, for which I found no parameterization. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Supplies a standard, reusable parameterization for generating additivity (bridge) violations at mild and strong magnitudes and quantifies the resulting MSE and coverage penalty in disconnected networks.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.201900339: Directly compares two competing bridges (component additivity vs matching-adjusted indirect comparison using single-arm observational studies) on the same disconnected network, contradicting ‘no evidence on which bridge…’ in its absolute form..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C2 and C8-C12 are broadly valid scenario distinctions, but the categorical impossibility and unquantified-bias claims are false. A bridge violation is untestable only when it lies in an observationally equivalent cross-subnetwork direction or the bridge supplies no overidentifying restriction. If a shared component is independently estimable in multiple subnetworks, or the additive model has residual degrees of freedom, heterogeneity or lack-of-fit can reveal incompatibility, although failure to reject cannot validate the bridge or identify the mechanism. Conditional on a specified drift model, bias is mathematically quantifiable: main-effect drift contributes an inner product such as m’Δ, while interaction drift contributes m’Λx. At cpaic 9d150e9, bridge_fragility() already maps a bounded main-effect drift to a worst-case decision-contrast shift and threshold. It does not address interaction drift, hidden synergy, stochastic drift correlation, or comparative bridge ranking, so the broader agenda remains open. Claims about a standard generator or the state of published comparative evidence were not adjudicated. Bridge fragility is critical for decision-grade disconnected comparisons; a universal robustness ranking is roadmap work. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: R/sensitivity.R implements a worst-case mapping from bounded component main-effect drift to decision-contrast movement, and tests/testthat/test-regression.R verifies the threshold arithmetic. This partially resolves the claimed absence of any quantitative drift mapping..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text: DIA-14 Partially addressed Very high priority Emerging

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Statement
Recovering the truth when supplied with the true sensitivity parameters is a necessary implementation check but says nothing about whether a QBA classifies robustness honestly when those parameters are unknown. The measures that would show this are not reported: false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, sensitivity-set truth inclusion, tipping-point error, calibration of probabilistic intervals, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, feasibility across the QBA grid, and Monte Carlo error of the QBA computation itself. Ren et al. 2025 (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.13) exemplifies the practice: the QBA is demonstrated by graphical presentation of point estimates and intervals across assumed bias parameters on a case study, with none of these measures and no simulation evaluation of the method. The further claim that no minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation in PAIC is an absence claim the literature auditor could not verify.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Why it is open
Supplying the true sensitivity parameters removes exactly the uncertainty QBA exists to represent, so the evaluation is circular and every correctly coded method passes. A QBA produces a qualitative verdict, robust or fragile, that ordinary bias and coverage measures cannot score, and false reassurance is the costly error yet stays invisible unless the simulation deliberately places the truth outside the analyst’s assumed region. Evaluating classification honesty requires simulating the elicitation process itself, including ranges, priors, dependence and expert error, a behavioral component that statistical simulation conventions have no vocabulary for.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Ren et al. 2025, Quantitative bias analysis for unmeasured confounding in unanchored population-adjusted indirect comparisons
Exemplifies the reporting practice the entry criticizes: the QBA is demonstrated by scenario exploration on a case study, with none of the classification-honesty measures reported and no simulation evaluation of the method itself.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Score QBA methods as classifiers of robustness against an explicit decision rule, reporting false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, sensitivity-set truth inclusion over simulated data and elicitations, tipping-point error where a tipping point exists and a distance is defined, interval calibration, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, and evaluate estimation at the true parameters separately from classification when the parameters are unknown. Report Monte Carlo error and computational failure of the QBA computation itself, and check support and effective sample size across the QBA grid wherever the QBA changes weighting or the implied target distribution. Fit the required data-generating factors and comparator set to the QBA estimand and mechanism rather than imposing a single universal blueprint.

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Our study

A quantitative bias analysis verdict scored as a classifier
The question put to it. How often does a QBA declare a MAIC decision robust when the true bias would reverse it, how does that depend on the elicited region rather than the method, and does oracle recovery reveal it?
What it found. A QBA’s robust verdict is only as good as the elicited region. When the region contains the true bias the grid never reassures falsely (an exact property); with elicitation errors scaled to the region it reassured falsely at most 17% of the time the true bias reversed the decision, but with the common region centered at zero bias it did so 78%, 37% and 9% of the time at half-widths 0.05, 0.15 and 0.3. Probabilistic QBA avoided false reassurance by calling 62% to 85% of sound decisions fragile. Oracle recovery was nominal throughout and revealed none of this.
Results.

Exact checks: zero grid false reassurance in every replicate whose region contained the true bias and at exclusion probability 0.
Primary (exclusion 0.1, half-width 0.15): grid false reassurance 0.008 (symmetric) and 0.020 (understated); false fragility 0.333 and 0.279. Probabilistic QBA 0.000 and 0.710 to 0.748. Neither dominated.
Refuting sentence fails: oracle coverage 0.951 to 0.961 in every scenario while grid false reassurance under a zero-centered region was 0.776, 0.370 and 0.092.
The probabilistic QBA’s own Monte Carlo error (1000 draws) changed its verdict in 0.9% to 1.6% of analyses.

Design.

Estimand

Robustness classification: whether the decision at the true bias equals the unadjusted decision

Methods compared

no QBA, deterministic grid (equivalent to bounds and tipping point for one scalar bias), probabilistic QBA

Data-generating mechanism

Unanchored MAIC with an unmeasured binary confounder; elicited bias regions with exclusion probability set directly, three error directions and three widths; grid and probabilistic QBA scored on false reassurance and false fragility; 18 cells, 2000 replicates each.

Replicates

2000 per scenario, 36,000 in total, each scored under 21 elicitation settings


What this does not answer. One scalar bias parameter; effect modification and overlap not varied; the elicitation model is assumed. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument · Code and data: studies/DIA-14-qba-scored-as-a-classifier · Protocol: registered before the run

title: QBA is judged on oracle recovery, not honest classification
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding.
The source said. “QBA methods are evaluated by whether they recover the truth when supplied with the true sensitivity parameters, which is only an implementation check, and no minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation studies. The measures that would show whether a QBA is honest are not reported: sensitivity-set truth inclusion, false-reassurance and false-fragility rates, tipping-point or tipping-surface error, calibration of probabilistic QBA intervals, robustness to misspecified sensitivity-parameter distributions, support and ESS failure across the QBA grid, the frequency with which bias cancellation masquerades as validity, decision-reversal classification and expected regret, and the computational failure and Monte Carlo error of the QBA itself.”
What was wrong with it. The source asserted that no published minimum ADEMP standard exists for QBA simulation in PAIC and then prescribed one universal blueprint; the literature auditor recorded the absence claim as unverified rather than confirmed, and GPT-5.6 Sol judged the prescribed data-generating content and comparator set to be one particular benchmark design rather than a necessary minimum, with several proposed measures (tipping-point error, truth inclusion, support and ESS checks) applying only under stated conditions.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: How robust are findings of pairwise and network meta-analysi. New citations: 10.1186/s12916-021-02195-y

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Consistent with the entry: in Ren et al. 2025, the newest QBA method for unanchored PAIC, the evaluation is graphical presentation of point estimates and intervals across assumed bias parameters on a case study, with no false-reassurance or false-fragility rate, no tipping-point error, no interval calibration, no sensitivity-set truth inclusion, and no Monte Carlo error for the QBA computation itself. That is positive evidence of the practice the entry describes. The caveat is the calibration rule: ‘No published minimum ADEMP standard exists for quantitative bias analysis simulation studies in PAIC’ is an absence claim and I found no source that asserts the absence, so I record it as unverified rather than confirmed. The remaining items are normative proposals for a blueprint, which cannot be true or false, only adopted or not. Cites 10.1017/rsm.2025.13: Exemplifies the reporting practice the entry criticizes: the QBA is demonstrated by scenario exploration on a case study, with none of the classification-honesty measures reported and no simulation evaluation of the method itself..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Oracle-parameter recovery is necessary evidence about implementation and identification under correct inputs, but it is insufficient evidence about practical QBA performance when sensitivity parameters are unknown; C1-C2 are therefore sound with that qualification. False reassurance, false fragility, truth inclusion, tipping error, decision classification, feasibility, and computational error are useful distinct targets when the QBA is intended to support a robustness decision. The proposed universal minimum is not technically established, however. C4 and C5 prescribe one large benchmark rather than a necessary ADEMP minimum; a direct QBA may itself be a bounding or partial-identification method. C6 is required for decision classification and regret, not for every inferential QBA. In C9, truth inclusion is a binary property for one fixed sensitivity set and becomes a probability only over simulated data, elicitation, or random sets. Tipping-point error requires existence, uniqueness, and a defined distance for multidimensional surfaces. Support and ESS checks apply when the QBA changes weighting or the implied target distribution, not automatically to every algebraic bias correction. Publication-frequency claims C3, C7, and C8 were not adjudicated. Honest classification is a high-priority validation goal, but the exact blueprint is roadmap guidance rather than a universal standard.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text: DIA-16 Overstated Very high priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text:
Statement
Bridge deletion is an established published design, not an unused idea. Beliveau et al. 2017 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256) disconnects two publicly available connected networks in multiple ways, fits the random-baseline bridge and scores the reconstructed cross-gap comparisons against the connected-network analysis, publishing code so other datasets can be investigated; Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9) removes 20 studies with 34 pairwise comparisons from a Cochrane network to create 19 disconnected variants, refits component models, and reports that the cross-subnetwork estimate is either inestimable or misleading. What does not exist is a curated, maintained public suite with IPD or well-reconstructed pseudo-IPD on both sides of the deleted edge on which PAIC and component methods are routinely scored, together with the factorial hidden-cell design for component additivity. The design is also weaker than the source implies: deletion validates only when the held-out contrast remains in the row space of the training design and all estimates share a population, outcome definition, follow-up and effect scale, and disagreement implicates the joint model rather than the bridging assumption alone.

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text:
Why it is open
The restrictions used exclusively to extrapolate across an unsupported gap are the ones that cannot be tested inside the disconnected data, so the only empirical check on them is an artificial disconnection where the answer is already known. That requires curating connected or factorial networks with enough structure to cut and with IPD or well-reconstructed pseudo-IPD on both sides of the deleted edge; suitable networks are scarce and scattered across indications, no maintained collection exists, and every attempt starts from scratch. The exercise mainly produces evidence against methods, as the published attempts already have, so developers have little incentive to run it.

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Beliveau et al. 2017, Network meta-analysis of disconnected networks: How dangerous are random baseline treatment effects?
A published bridge-deletion validation with shared code: real connected networks are disconnected in multiple ways and the reconstructed cross-gap comparisons are scored against the original connected-network analysis.


Petropoulou et al. 2023, Model selection for component network meta-analysis in connected and disconnected networks: a simulation study
Performs component and bridge deletion on a real Cochrane network, comparing reconstructed cross-subnetwork effects against the held-out connected-network analysis, and reports a negative result in which the reconstructed estimate is inestimable or misleading.

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Assemble the published deletion designs into a standing public suite: curate connected networks suitable for bridge deletion and factorial or multicomponent networks suitable for component deletion, publish the deleted-edge and hidden-cell ground truth, and require that deletion leave the held-out contrast estimable and that reconstruction and the randomized comparison share population, outcome definition, follow-up and effect scale. Score disconnected-network and component methods on reconstruction error and decision agreement with the held-out randomized comparison, reporting the result as evidence about the joint bridging model rather than as a test of the bridging assumption alone. Pair the suite with simulation benchmarks and with the analytic checks, unit tests and independent implementation comparisons that software validation also requires, and use the failures to characterize when additivity is and is not clinically acceptable.

title: No curated public suite for bridge-deletion validation with IPD
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Bridge deletion and disconnection-and-reconstruct validation have been published for random-baseline NMA and for CNMA, with code, and have already produced negative results; what does not exist is a curated, maintained public suite of such networks with individual patient data on both sides of the deleted edge on which PAIC and component methods are routinely scored.
The source titled this. “Deleting a known bridge or component is not used as validation” The title says bridge deletion is not used as validation, but it is a published design with released code that has already produced negative results.
The source said. “The direct empirical tests available for disconnected-network and component methods have not been assembled into a public validation suite: deleting the studies or the treatment that connect two subnetworks, fitting disconnected methods, and comparing the reconstructed cross-gap effect with the held-out randomized evidence; and hiding one component comparison in a factorial or multicomponent network and testing whether CNMA or component PAIC reconstructs it.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated bridge deletion and component deletion as unused; the literature auditor found both published with shared code, in Beliveau et al. 2017 (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1256) and Petropoulou et al. 2023 (doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9), the latter already reporting a negative reconstruction result. GPT-5.6 Sol added that deletion probes rather than proves a bridging assumption and that additivity is testable wherever the design supplies overidentifying contrasts, not only in factorial networks.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Bridge deletion is not an unused idea; it is an established published design with shared code, in two independent lines of work. Beliveau, Goring, Platt & Gustafson 2017 took two publicly available connected networks, disconnected them in multiple ways, fitted the random-baseline bridge to each disconnected version, and compared the reconstructed cross-gap comparisons against the analysis of the original connected network, publishing code so other datasets can be investigated. Petropoulou et al. 2023 did the component version on a real Cochrane postoperative nausea and vomiting network: they removed 20 studies with 34 pairwise comparisons to separate a minimal set, generated 19 distinct disconnected variants, refitted additive and selected CNMA, and compared the reconstructed cross-subnetwork effects against the connected-network standard NMA, finding estimates that were ‘either inestimable … or misleading’. Their overall verdict is a negative reconstruction result. What is genuinely absent is a curated standing public suite with PAIC methods and IPD or pseudo-IPD on both sides of the deleted edge, and the specific factorial hidden-cell design. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1256: A published bridge-deletion validation with shared code: real connected networks are disconnected in multiple ways and the reconstructed cross-gap comparisons are scored against the original connected-network analysis.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9: Performs component/bridge-deletion validation of CNMA on a real Cochrane network, comparing reconstructed cross-subnetwork effects against the held-out connected-network NMA, and reports a negative result..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C1 and C4 describe feasible external predictive checks, but only when deletion leaves the held-out contrast estimable: its component-contrast vector must lie in the row space of the training design, and the reconstruction and randomized comparison must target the same population, outcome definition, follow-up, and effect scale. The comparison probes the joint bridging model; it does not isolate or prove the bridging assumption because sampling error, heterogeneity, transport failure, coding, and outcome-model misspecification also affect disagreement. C3 inflates necessity. Public suites would improve comparability and credibility, but they are not logically necessary for software validation, which also requires analytic checks, unit tests, known-truth simulations, and independent implementation comparisons. C6 is too categorical: a full factorial can identify an interaction contrast and test additivity, while a disconnected network can still contain testable within-subnetwork or overidentifying component restrictions. Only restrictions used exclusively to extrapolate across the unsupported gap are untestable without redundant evidence. C2 and C5 are literature-absence claims not adjudicated here.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text: DIA-18 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text:
Statement
Older-to-newer temporal holdout, fitting component and effect-modifier models on earlier trials and predicting a later one, is not performed in this literature, so there is no empirical estimate of how far constancy survives calendar-time change. What such a holdout tests is narrower than the source claims: it assesses joint out-of-time predictive transportability rather than equality of specific component or effect-modifier coefficients, and it requires the newer trial’s contrast to lie in the estimable row space of the training design with adequate covariate overlap. Prediction error against calendar gap also combines sampling error, ordinary between-study heterogeneity, design and outcome-definition changes and any genuine drift, so it does not by itself identify a decay rate or justify a universal trial-age cutoff. The claim that no published study has done this is an absence claim the literature auditor could not verify.

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text:
Why it is open
Constancy of component effects and effect modification is assumed across studies conducted decades apart, and calendar time bundles changes in standard of care, diagnostic criteria, outcome ascertainment and treatment versions, any of which can break it. Chronology is always recorded, so the holdout is uniquely feasible, yet it is not performed and no estimate of context-specific drift exists. Separating drift from sampling error, ordinary heterogeneity and design change needs repeated holdouts or a hierarchical temporal model rather than a single fit-and-predict exercise, which is more work than the design first appears to require.

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text:
What has been tried
No prior work is identified for this problem in the reviewed sources.

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Run repeated older-to-newer holdouts on networks where the newer contrast is estimable from the earlier design and the estimands align, and report prediction error with its sources separated, using a hierarchical temporal model that distinguishes sampling error and ordinary between-study heterogeneity from systematic temporal drift. Report the results as context-specific drift estimates rather than a universal decay rate, and use them to inform drift priors in subnetwork-specific and hierarchical component models. Treat any inclusion-window recommendation as conditional on indication and outcome, since holdout prediction alone cannot justify a general trial-age cutoff.

title: Constancy assumptions are never tested across calendar time
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 3 findings from 3 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed.
The source said. “Temporal validation, fitting component and effect-modifier models on older trials and predicting a newer trial to test explicitly whether those coefficients survive calendar-time change, has not been carried out, so there is no empirical estimate of how fast constancy decays.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented temporal holdout as a direct test of coefficient constancy that would yield a decay rate and justify inclusion windows; GPT-5.6 Sol narrowed it to a test of joint out-of-time predictive transportability whose error confounds sampling variation, heterogeneity and design change, so isolating drift needs repeated holdouts or a hierarchical temporal model. The literature auditor recorded the absence claim as unverified rather than confirmed, since no source asserts the absence.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 3 surviving findings from: Analysis of adaptive platform trials using a network approac; Estimating relative efficacy in acute postoperative pain: ne; From investigational product to active reference: evolution . New citations: 10.1080/20016689.2019.1603538, 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000001322, 10.1177/17407745221112001

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The mechanism claim is well supported by the wider meta-epidemiological literature, which documents that treatment effect estimates drift with calendar time: recursive cumulative meta-analyses show effects evolving over successive trials, and a meta-epidemiological survey of hundreds of meta-analyses reports that older randomized trials are associated with larger intervention effects. The logical claim, that fitting on older trials and predicting a newer one directly tests constancy of component and effect-modifier coefficients, is true by construction. The claim I cannot confirm is the absence one: ‘No published study tests whether component and effect-modifier constancy survives calendar-time change’ cannot be verified by failing to find one, and I found no source asserting the absence, so I mark that sub-claim unverified rather than confirmed. I retrieved the meta-epidemiological items at title and summary level only, which is why my confidence is at the abstract-reading level.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C3 is technically plausible: calendar time can proxy changes in standard care, populations, measurement, and treatment versions. C1, however, overstates what temporal holdout prediction identifies. It tests joint out-of-time predictive transportability, not equality of specific component or effect-modifier coefficients. Prediction requires the newer trial’s component and interaction contrast to lie in the older training design’s estimable row space and requires adequate covariate overlap. Failure can arise from baseline-risk drift, outcome-definition changes, heterogeneity, or other misspecification; successful prediction does not prove coefficient constancy. Prediction error versus calendar gap also does not by itself identify a decay rate because it combines sampling error, ordinary heterogeneity, design changes, and potential temporal drift. Estimating drift requires repeated holdouts or a hierarchical temporal model that separates these sources. It cannot generally justify a universal trial-age cutoff. C2 is an uncited literature-absence assertion outside this audit. The work is a useful roadmap item, but not a uniquely decisive validation or an automatically High-severity omission.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text: DIA-20 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text:
Statement
Quantitative transitivity screens now reduce a network’s study-level effect-modifier table to within- and between-comparison dissimilarity summaries, and the decision rule they need is a threshold separating tolerable from concerning dissimilarity. No threshold has been derived from dissimilarity data. The published thresholds are read off empirically driven predictive distributions for the I-squared statistic, a statistical-heterogeneity quantity on a different scale from a Gower dissimilarity, and the authors say so and call the choice a tentative suggestion necessitated by the lack of an empirical study of non-statistical heterogeneity across healthcare fields. The consequence is that the substantive conclusion is threshold-driven: across a corpus of 209 published networks, the median-based threshold declares likely intransitivity in every dataset while the third-quartile threshold leaves 26 networks with transitivity likely present. What is missing is a field-, outcome- and comparator-indexed reference distribution of observed study-level dissimilarities, from which a value could be reported as a percentile, together with evidence linking a dissimilarity value to anything downstream: realized inconsistency, indirect-comparison bias or transport error. Without that link the screen returns a number whose sign of trouble is set by an analogy, the same network can be declared concerning or acceptable by changing a defensible convention, and the flag rate is unknown. The raw material for the calibration already exists, since the tracenma R package holds study-level clinical and methodological characteristics extracted from those 209 reviews, and nobody has computed the dissimilarity distribution over it as a reference or related it to any downstream error.

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text:
Why it is open
The obvious calibration target is not observable. A dissimilarity threshold should sit where indirect estimates start to go wrong, but the bias of an indirect estimate is exactly what a network cannot measure: transitivity is untestable in-sample, so the only available proxies are inconsistency in closed loops, which needs the loops the screen exists to protect, and comparison against a gold-standard estimate that most networks do not have. The right object is also not a single cutoff, because tolerable dissimilarity depends on outcome subjectivity, comparator type and study size, which the empirical work already varies informally, so calibration means estimating a family of thresholds and requires a corpus large enough to support that stratification. The scale itself is not comparable across networks, since a Gower dissimilarity depends on which characteristics the systematic review happened to extract, so a percentile computed over a corpus inherits the corpus’s extraction habits unless the extraction set is standardized first. And the borrowed heterogeneity distributions are not a careless choice; they were adopted precisely because no empirical study of clinical and methodological heterogeneity across healthcare fields exists to replace them, so the calibration study has to be built before the threshold can be.

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Spineli, Papadimitropoulou and Kalyvas 2025, Statistics in Medicine
Proposes the dissimilarity-and-clustering approach to transitivity: computes within- and between-comparison dissimilarities from study-level participant and methodological characteristics and applies hierarchical clustering to locate hot spots of potential intransitivity. States that its thresholds, taken from predictive distributions of I-squared, are a tentative suggestion necessitated by the absence of an empirical study of non-statistical heterogeneity across healthcare fields.


Spineli 2024, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Applies the dissimilarity approach across 209 published networks, showing likely intransitivity in all of them under the median threshold and in all but 26 under the third-quartile threshold, and calls for dissimilarity thresholds customized to the healthcare field and to design characteristics such as outcome and treatment-comparator type.


tracenma R package
The released database of study-level aggregate clinical and methodological characteristics extracted from 209 published systematic reviews with network meta-analysis. This is the corpus a reference distribution of dissimilarities would be computed from, and it is already public.


Rhodes, Turner and Higgins 2016, Research Synthesis Methods
Supplies the empirically driven predictive distributions that are currently used as the dissimilarity thresholds. They describe statistical inconsistency and heterogeneity among studies in pairwise meta-analysis, which is a different quantity on a different scale from a study-characteristic dissimilarity.


Turner et al. 2012, International Journal of Epidemiology
Derives predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity from 14,886 Cochrane meta-analyses, stratified by outcome type and intervention comparison. This is the template a dissimilarity reference corpus would follow, and the reason distributions of this shape were available to borrow in the first place.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
CINeMA, whose indirectness and heterogeneity domains currently absorb what a calibrated transitivity screen would report. Its judgments are qualitative and carry no threshold either, so it is an alternative reporting route rather than a calibration.

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Compute the reference distribution first, since the corpus is already released: run the dissimilarity calculation over the tracenma networks and publish the distribution of within- and between-comparison dissimilarity stratified by healthcare field, outcome subjectivity, comparator type and study size, so that a value can be reported as a percentile instead of being compared with a borrowed cutoff. Standardize the set of study characteristics that feeds the dissimilarity, because a percentile is only comparable across networks when the same characteristics enter it. Then calibrate against something downstream: in the subset of networks with closed loops, relate dissimilarity to realized inconsistency; where a contrast has both direct and indirect evidence, relate it to the direct-versus-indirect discrepancy; and in simulation, generate effect-modifier distributions of known imbalance and report the dissimilarity value at which indirect-estimate bias exceeds a stated fraction of the effect. Report the screen as a classifier, with false-positive and false-negative rates at each candidate threshold, rather than as a prevalence statement whose answer is fixed by the cutoff.

title: Transitivity dissimilarity screens have no calibrated threshold
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Two independent readers proposed this from the two papers that define and apply the screen, and the reviewer accepted both, holding it distinct from the in-principle untestability of transitivity because it asks for a reference distribution and calibration against consequential indirect-estimate error. Both primary sources state the calibration is missing: one calls its borrowed thresholds a tentative suggestion necessitated by the absence of an empirical study, the other names field- and design-specific thresholds as deserving investigation and shows its own prevalence result flipping with the cutoff.

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text: DIA-22 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Established Tractability 4/5

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text:
Statement
Empirical comparisons of network meta-analysis models filter the corpus on an inconsistency test before comparing anything. The largest such study drew on a curated database of 456 published networks and retained 118, requiring for any network containing a loop that the design-by-treatment interaction test return a p value above 0.10, on the stated ground that the models being fitted do not allow for inconsistency. The screen is a noisy proxy for the property it selects on: the design-by-treatment interaction test is known to have low power, which is why the cut-off was set at 0.10 rather than 0.05, so the retained set still contains inconsistency while excluding some networks that are consistent. The models under comparison differ precisely in how they propagate loop conflict and how they relate arms across studies, so screening out loop conflict removes the regime in which they would most diverge, and the resulting agreement statistics understate how much model choice matters in the networks analysts actually submit. No published empirical comparison stratifies its agreement measures by degree of inconsistency; the network characteristics investigated to date are connectedness and rareness of events. The result is a literature reporting broadly reassuring agreement between contrast-synthesis and arm-synthesis models without having examined the case where the choice would bite.

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text:
Why it is open
The exclusion is defensible on its own terms, which is why it has persisted: fitting a consistency model to an inconsistent network estimates a quantity the model does not represent, and there is no agreed estimand for what a consistency model returns on an inconsistent network, so a study admitting such networks would first have to say what its agreement measures were about. A replacement design has to index inconsistency on a continuous scale, but the available indices are estimates with low power in exactly the sparse networks where the question matters, so stratifying on measured inconsistency stratifies partly on noise. Real networks carry no known degree of inconsistency, so ground truth is available only in simulation, which trades away the realism that motivates empirical comparison in the first place, and no design gets both. The corpus is a fixed resource of published networks, so widening the inclusion criteria changes composition on size, sparsity and clinical field simultaneously, confounding the comparison with the very characteristics already known to predict discordance. Finally, an empirical comparison can measure disagreement but never error, so even a study covering inconsistent networks could not say which model was right there.

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Karahalios et al. 2017, Systematic Reviews
Protocol for the empirical evaluation: prespecifies five models, five comparison metrics and four candidate modifiers of discordance, states the consistency restriction and its rationale, and separately records that the design-by-treatment interaction test has low power, which is why the cut-off is 0.10.


Karahalios et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
The completed evaluation: 118 networks re-analyzed with three contrast-synthesis and two arm-synthesis models, comparing log odds ratios, standard errors, ranking measures and heterogeneity, and finding that model choice can change the ranking; the network characteristics investigated are connectedness and event rarity, and nothing is stratified by inconsistency because inconsistent networks were excluded.


Higgins et al. 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
The design-by-treatment interaction model that supplies the screening test, framed as a global check on consistency for networks that include multi-arm studies.


Veroniki et al. 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Simulation of which loop characteristics affect detection and estimation of inconsistency; establishes the low power that makes any screen on a consistency test noisy.


Veroniki et al. 2013, International Journal of Epidemiology
Evaluation of the available methods for assessing inconsistency in networks of interventions and how they behave when applied to real networks.


Song et al. 2011, BMJ
Meta-epidemiological study of disagreement between direct and indirect comparisons across many networks; the empirical base rate of loop conflict that a representative corpus would have to reproduce.


White et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
Analytic comparison of arm-based and contrast-based models showing the substantive difference is whether study intercepts are fixed or random, and that random intercepts bring in between-study information that can bias; establishes why the two families would be expected to diverge where evidence conflicts.

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Re-run the existing comparison over the full corpus without the consistency screen, reporting agreement as a function of a continuous inconsistency index rather than as one pooled statistic, and report the previously excluded stratum separately rather than not at all. Pair it with a simulation calibrated to the distribution of loop conflict measured in that corpus, so that where the empirical study can only measure disagreement, the simulation can attribute it to error. Prespecify inconsistency as a modifier of discordance in the same multilevel model that already carries connectedness and event rarity, which needs no new machinery. Publish the network-level inconsistency estimates alongside the agreement measures so that later work can restratify; the corpus, the code and the fitted models already exist, so the cost is re-analysis rather than development.

title: Empirical method comparisons exclude the networks where methods diverge
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from the protocol’s own statement of the exclusion and its rationale, and the reviewer accepted the selection mechanism as a distinct empirical-methods gap while noting that the claim that all stratified comparisons are absent would need a systematic check. The audit confirmed the completed evaluation kept the screen, retaining 118 of 456 networks and stratifying only on connectedness and event rarity.

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text: DIA-24 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text:
Statement
Network meta-analysis reports an estimated inconsistency parameter, or a set of loop and node-splitting discrepancies, with no reference distribution or effect-scale threshold that says whether an estimate of a given size is negligible, moderate or decision-relevant. Presence or absence is therefore decided by whether the discrepancy’s interval excludes zero, a test whose power depends on how much direct and indirect information the loop carries rather than on the size of the discrepancy, so a large discrepancy in a sparse loop is declared absent while a trivial one in a dense loop is declared present. The heterogeneity analogue exists and is used routinely: empirical predictive distributions for the between-study variance by outcome type and clinical area (Turner et al. 2012, doi:10.1093/ije/dys041; Rhodes et al. 2015) let an analyst call an estimate low or substantial, and one such distribution supplied the thresholds of 0.28 on the log odds ratio scale and 0.17 on the standardized mean difference scale used to judge robustness in 107 pairwise and 33 network analyses (Spineli et al. 2021, doi:10.1186/s12916-021-02195-y). Nothing equivalent has been assembled for inconsistency. The empirical record reports prevalence rather than magnitude: 2 to 9 percent of 303 loops in 40 published networks were statistically inconsistent depending on effect measure and heterogeneity estimator, and 16 of 112 trial networks showed statistically significant direct-versus-indirect disagreement. CINeMA supplies the decision half by asking whether direct and indirect estimates differ enough to change a conclusion relative to a user-specified range of equivalence, but that range is elicited case by case and no calibration relates a discrepancy of a given size to a probability of a wrong recommendation.

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text:
Why it is open
Building the reference distribution requires a corpus of networks with comparable outcome definitions and loops of comparable information, and the discrepancy estimated in any one loop is imprecise, so the observed spread of realized discrepancies is confounded with their sampling error; separating the two needs a hierarchical model across networks rather than a tabulation. An inconsistency of a given size also carries no fixed decision meaning, since whether it matters depends on the contrast, the effect scale, the competing treatments and the decision threshold, so a universal cutoff is the wrong object and a decision-indexed criterion needs the economic model that the synthesis does not contain. The test-based habit is self-reinforcing: software prints p-values for node splitting and for the design-by-treatment interaction, and nothing prints an effect-scale comparator. Because inconsistency is a property of a loop rather than of a study, a magnitude judged meaningful for one contrast cannot simply be carried to another contrast in the same network.

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Spineli et al. 2021, BMC Medicine
builds a divergence-based robustness index for missing outcome data and calibrates it against an empirical heterogeneity distribution, then names the inconsistency case as the outstanding one, stating that no recommendations exist for interpreting the estimated inconsistency parameter and that analysts consequently rely on its statistical significance


Turner et al. 2012, International Journal of Epidemiology
derives empirical predictive distributions for between-study heterogeneity from the Cochrane database, indexed by outcome type and intervention comparison; the construction an inconsistency analogue would copy


Rhodes et al. 2015, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
supplies the same empirical predictive distributions for continuous outcomes on the standardized mean difference scale


Turner et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
carries external empirical evidence on heterogeneity into network meta-analysis, demonstrating that the borrowing of an empirical reference distribution into the network setting is feasible; no counterpart exists for the inconsistency variance


Veroniki et al. 2013, International Journal of Epidemiology
evaluates 303 loops from 40 published networks and reports statistical inconsistency in 2 to 9 percent of loops depending on effect measure and heterogeneity estimator, a prevalence rather than a distribution of magnitudes


Song et al. 2011, BMJ
measures inconsistency as the difference in log odds ratio between direct and indirect estimates across 112 independent trial networks and reports statistically significant disagreement in 16 of them, the closest existing empirical basis for a reference distribution


Veroniki et al. 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
shows by simulation which loop characteristics drive detection and estimation of inconsistency, establishing that the significance verdict tracks loop information rather than discrepancy size


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
CINeMA, whose incoherence domain compares direct and indirect estimates against a user-specified range of equivalence and against the significance of their difference; the decision framework exists but the range is supplied case by case and no empirical reference is provided

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Assemble the empirical half first: refit a large corpus of published networks, estimate loop and design-by-treatment discrepancies with their uncertainty, and fit a hierarchical model across networks that separates realized inconsistency from sampling error, reported by outcome type, effect measure and clinical area. Publish the resulting predictive distributions the way heterogeneity priors are published, so an analyst can state where an estimated discrepancy sits among discrepancies observed in comparable networks, and so that a Bayesian analysis can use them as priors on the inconsistency variance. Anchor the decision half separately: for a given network compute the discrepancy that would flip the recommended treatment or move incremental net benefit past its threshold, and report the estimate against that quantity rather than against zero. Both halves are computable from existing collections of published network datasets, and both belong in the software output that currently prints only a p-value.

title: No reference distribution says when inconsistency is large
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed it from a single paper, and the reviewer accepted it as distinct from whether inconsistency can be detected and from whether transitivity is identifiable, since it concerns the magnitude and decision relevance of a detected discrepancy. It is partially-addressed rather than open because CINeMA already asks whether a direct-versus-indirect discrepancy matters relative to a declared range of equivalence and two meta-epidemiological studies report how often inconsistency is detected; what is absent is a magnitude reference distribution and any calibration from discrepancy size to decision error.

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text: DIA-26 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text:
Statement
Inconsistency is a property of a loop rather than of a design, so attributing it to a single design is not identified unless that design sits in more than one loop, and the diagnostic most widely used for the attempt is unreliable. The net heat statistic factorizes approximately into the loop signal times a second factor proportional to the direct-minus-indirect difference for the design, and that second factor shrinks as the network gains loops, so a fixed inconsistency stops being flagged in larger networks: in simulation an inflated ABC-loop effect fell below the plot’s threshold of 8 once seven or more loops were present (Freeman et al. 2019, doi:10.1002/sim.8383). In an individual-participant lung cancer network of 7,531 patients, Cochran’s Q for the network (p = 0.043), the between-design Q (p = 0.034), a Bucher loop test (p = 0.035), a Lu-Ades inconsistency parameter of -0.176 (95 percent credible interval -0.337 to -0.016) and node splitting (p = 0.033) all flagged inconsistency while the net heat plot showed nothing to read. The statistic also has no known sampling distribution and no calibrated mapping from color to importance, and it tends to attribute inconsistency to the comparisons with the least direct evidence. Two replacements appeared in 2026: leave-one-design-out influence diagnostics with a summary value for prioritizing designs and an accompanying test, and a display combining direct and indirect effect sizes, their contributions, their difference and its significance. Neither has been evaluated against the loop-count masking that discredited the incumbent, both have been assessed only by their own authors, and netmeta continues to ship the net heat plot.

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text:
Why it is open
The attribution being asked for is not always identified: where a design belongs to one loop, that loop’s inconsistency cannot be assigned to the design from the data, so any design-level display is reading structure the design-by-treatment interaction model does not separate. A graphical summary and a calibrated test pull against each other, because a statistic scaled for display across a whole network is not on the scale of any single test, and the net heat statistic was constructed for display. Deriving its sampling distribution requires handling multi-arm trials and multiple indirect paths, which the closed-form analysis assumed away, and the derivation is fixed-effect throughout, so behavior under genuine within-design heterogeneity is unknown. The replacements are new, and evaluating them properly means reproducing the adversarial design that exposed the incumbent rather than demonstrating them on networks where the formal tests already agree.

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Freeman et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
derives the net heat statistic in closed form, shows by simulation that it falls below its own threshold as loops are added while the underlying inconsistency is unchanged, exhibits a real network where every formal test rejects consistency and the plot reads clean, and concludes the plot neither reliably signals inconsistency nor identifies the designs causing it


Krahn et al. 2013, BMC Medical Research Methodology
introduces the net heat plot and the design-based decomposition of Cochran’s Q that it displays; still shipped in netmeta as the standard localizing display


Higgins et al. 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
formalizes inconsistency as design-by-treatment interaction, which is the model against which any design-level attribution has to be defined and which bounds what is identifiable


Dias et al. 2010, Statistics in Medicine
node splitting: a calibrated local test of direct against indirect evidence for one comparison, with no network-wide display and no design-level attribution


Veroniki et al. 2014, BMC Medical Research Methodology
quantifies by simulation which loop characteristics govern detection and estimation of inconsistency, giving the design factors any evaluation of a replacement diagnostic must vary


Sasaki and Noma 2026, Statistics in Medicine
proposes leave-one-design-out influence diagnostics, including an averaged studentized residual and MDFFITS, plus a summary value for prioritizing designs and a test based on the same framework, and reports that they located sources of inconsistency accurately in simulation


Wilson et al. 2026, Research Synthesis Methods
supplies a visualization combining direct and indirect effect sizes with their relative contributions, the difference and its uncertainty, and the direction of disagreement, which is close to the graphical-plus-formal combination the critique asked for; implemented in netmeta

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Evaluate the 2026 proposals on the design that discredited the incumbent: fix a true inconsistency in one loop, add loops one at a time, and report detection rate and false attribution rate for the influence measures, the summary value and the new display as the network grows, with multi-arm designs and non-zero heterogeneity present. Make the identification boundary explicit in the output by marking designs that belong to a single loop as unattributable rather than assigning them a color or a rank. Give the plotted quantity a calibrated reference, either a null distribution obtained by parametric bootstrap under the consistency model or a threshold expressed on the effect scale, so a displayed cell can be read as a test rather than as a hue. Whatever survives should ship next to the net heat plot with a documented statement of what each display can and cannot detect, since the incumbent’s failure mode is invisible to its users.

title: No validated diagnostic localizes inconsistency to a design
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed it from a single paper, and the reviewer accepted that the evidence directly supports the unreliability of the net heat plot and that a validated localizing diagnostic remains a genuine need. It is partially-addressed rather than open because two candidate replacements were published in 2026, a leave-one-design-out influence framework and a local-consistency visualization now in netmeta, neither of which has been tested against the loop-count masking that motivated the critique.
