title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text: DIS-02 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text:
Statement
Several bridge families can supply a cross-gap contrast: baseline synthesis and reference prediction, aggregate-level matching, dose-response MBNMA, treatment-class effects, component NMA, external controls and cross-design synthesis, mechanistic bridges, and expert elicitation with external priors, plus at least one the source’s eight-family list omits, multivariate synthesis across treatment lines with target-trial emulation. Among bridge models that target the same estimand and induce the same observed-data distribution within every disconnected component, no statistic computed only from those data can identify the correct cross-gap restriction, so selection requires external scientific information, validation data, or transparent sensitivity analysis. The families are overlapping options rather than mutually incompatible answers: expert priors can overlay any other bridge, and class, dose-response, baseline, and external-evidence structures can coexist. Published selection guidance exists, notably Goring et al. 2016’s framework for choosing among disconnected-network models and Ruecker, Schmitz and Schwarzer 2021’s head-to-head comparison of two families on the same disconnected myeloma network, but no accepted general procedure ranks them.

title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text:
Why it is open
When candidate bridges induce the same observed-data distribution inside every component, they differ only across a gap that contains no evidence, so nothing computable from the dataset separates them. Some bridges do impose within-component restrictions that can be checked, and external or bridge-deletion data can discriminate among them, so the untestability is narrower than a blanket claim, but that leverage disappears for exactly the restriction that carries the gap. What remains missing is a general procedure that takes a network and a decision question and says which bridges it can support: the linking devices sit in scattered literatures, the published guidance is qualitative or case-specific, and the choice determines the estimand as well as the estimate.

title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Beliveau et al. 2017
examines random baseline treatment effects in disconnected networks and finds their use appropriate for the two datasets considered, while cautioning that normality and exchangeability could be inappropriate in datasets it did not observe


Thom et al. 2022
extends baseline-effect and aggregate-level matching methods to disconnected RCTs and single-arm studies and compares them by simulation


Petropoulou et al. 2023
simulates additive CNMA and recommends it for disconnected networks only with strong clinical arguments for additivity


Perren et al. 2026
provides a practical class-effects guide and four-step model-selection algorithm, including the case of networks disconnected at the treatment level but connected at the class level


netmeta (discomb)
provides discomb, additive network meta-analysis for combinations of treatments in disconnected networks, in the frequentist netmeta framework developed at github.com/guido-s/netmeta


Goring et al. 2016
presents a theoretical framework to guide the choice between modeling approaches for disconnected networks, which is the selection guidance the source said did not exist


Ruecker, Schmitz and Schwarzer 2021
compares a component NMA bridge against a matching bridge head-to-head on the same real disconnected network


Bridging disconnected networks of first and second lines of biologic therapies in rheumatoid arthritis with registry data (2022)
a bridge device outside the source’s eight-family taxonomy: Bayesian synthesis across treatment lines using registry data with target-trial emulation

title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build on the existing qualitative guidance rather than restarting: turn Goring et al. 2016’s framework and the published case comparisons into a documented selection procedure that names, for each candidate family, the parameter carrying the gap and the within-component restrictions it does imply and that can therefore be checked. Report the cross-gap contrast under several admissible bridges with partial-identification bounds across them rather than committing to one, noting that discomb in netmeta already supplies a frequentist component bridge for disconnected combination networks. Where the answer stays fragile under every admissible bridge, design a bridging study.

title: No data-driven criterion can rank candidate bridge families
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. No criterion computable from a disconnected dataset can rank candidate bridge families, because the gap contains no evidence against which they could be scored; qualitative selection frameworks (Goring et al. 2016) and case-study comparisons of two families (Ruecker et al. 2021) exist, but there is no accepted general procedure. Disconnected networks are a recurring and growing problem in oncology and rare disease HTA, though no study establishes that they are the majority of unmet evidence-synthesis problems.
The source titled this. “No principled procedure for choosing among bridge families” The title says no principled procedure exists, but the audit found a published selection framework and a published head-to-head comparison of two bridge families.
The source said. “At least eight bridge families can supply a cross-gap contrast: random baseline effects and baseline synthesis, reference prediction and aggregate-level matching, dose-response MBNMA, treatment-class effects, component NMA, external controls and cross-design synthesis, mechanistic or pharmacometric bridges, and expert elicitation with external priors. Which family is defensible for a given problem is unresolved, and in practice disconnected evidence is linked by whichever workaround is easiest to implement.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no accepted criterion for choosing among bridge families and that most unmet HTA evidence-synthesis problems now sit in disconnected networks. The literature auditor found a published selection framework (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1204) and a published head-to-head comparison (doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339), and found no bibliometric study supporting the prevalence claim, which is dropped; GPT-5.6 Sol added that the untestability holds only among bridges that are observationally equivalent within the components, and that the families overlap rather than each answering a different question. The prior_work gloss on Beliveau et al. 2017 is also corrected here, for the reason recorded under DIS-03.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

closure-upheld

10 findings from the reading assert this problem is open; the closure was re-examined and stands Put to an independent reviewer with the closing auditors’ reasoning, the work they relied on, and the new findings in view together. The new literature directly restates the closure’s residual: fit and output comparisons do not identify the correct cross-gap restriction, and selection remains deliberative, assumption-based, or sensitivity-based. The 2021 classification review and the 2023 migraine case study reinforce the absence of an accepted general selector, but do not supply one or show that the closure’s impossibility condition is wrong. Additional bridge families based on multi-outcome borrowing widen the taxonomy but do not alter the statement’s core claim, which is explicitly conditional on candidates inducing the same observed-data distribution within disconnected components. Neither the qualitative frameworks nor descriptive head-to-head comparisons contradict that conditional identification argument. (reviewer confidence: high)

Flagged for reopening

10 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. I verified the netmeta claim: discomb’s CRAN documentation reads ‘Additive network meta-analysis for combinations of treatments (disconnected networks)’ and says it is particularly intended for disconnected networks. The core claim, that no data-driven criterion can rank bridges when the gap contains no evidence, is sound. But two things are overstated. First, ‘there is currently no accepted criterion for choosing among bridge families’ ignores Goring et al. 2016, which explicitly ‘present[s] a theoretical framework to guide the choice between modeling approaches’, and ignores Ruecker, Schmitz and Schwarzer 2021, who compare two bridge families head-to-head on the same disconnected myeloma network. Second, and more seriously, ‘Most unmet HTA evidence-synthesis problems now sit in disconnected networks, especially in oncology and rare disease’ is a bald prevalence claim with no source; I found no bibliometric study establishing it, and publishing it under a named byline is a liability. The eight-family taxonomy is a claim about the source report, not about the literature, and cannot be audited. Cites 10.1002/jrsm.1204: Partially narrows the ‘no criterion for choosing’ claim: supplies a published framework for choosing among disconnected-network models. Cites 10.1002/bimj.201900339: A published head-to-head comparison of two bridge families on the same disconnected network, absent from prior_work. Cites 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2022.06.011: A ninth bridge device in use (multivariate/bivariate synthesis across treatment lines with target-trial emulation) not in the entry’s eight-family taxonomy. Cites cran:netmeta/discomb: Confirms the discomb claim as written.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The eight-family list in C2 is a reasonable descriptive taxonomy, but the families are neither mutually exclusive nor guaranteed to target different estimands. Expert priors can overlay any other bridge, while class, dose-response, baseline, and external-evidence structures can coexist. C3-C4 are therefore too strong: different bridges impose different restrictions and vulnerability patterns, but do not necessarily import bias or answer different questions. C6 holds only when candidate bridges are observationally equivalent on the observed components. Some models also impose within-component restrictions that can be checked, and external validation or bridge-deletion data can discriminate among them. C11 is source-confirmed locally: netmeta exports and implements discomb for disconnected combination networks. C12 and C14 are sound. C13 is speculative because ensemble weights cannot be learned from an evidence-free gap, and averaging is incoherent if estimands differ. C1, C5, C7, C9, and C10 are sourcing, practice, acceptance, prevalence, or universal-absence claims outside this technical audit. Bridge choice remains decision-critical, but a universal data-driven selector is not an attainable solution.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: Dose-response bridges assume a curve that may not transport
text: DIS-04 Confirmed open High priority Promising

title: Dose-response bridges assume a curve that may not transport
text:
Statement
Model-based NMA links treatments across a gap through a shared dose or exposure response function, which is strong when pharmacology supports the curve and exposure scales are comparable; overlapping nominal doses are not sufficient on their own, because overlap helps only on a scientifically comparable exposure scale under a transportable response model. The bridge weakens when nominal dose does not reflect exposure, when formulations, dose intensity, or adherence differ, or when effect modifiers change the curve so that one shared curve becomes a family of population-specific curves, and a wrong curve can produce a precise but artificial link. Pedder et al. 2021 is the canonical treatment: MBNMA supplied estimates for all treatments where NMA could not, and those estimates were consistent with NMA on augmented networks for 15 of 18 datasets, failing in 3 where a more complex dose-response relationship was needed than the available evidence could fit. MBNMA does not necessarily impose one common curve on every treatment, and forcing distinct mechanisms into a single class makes a common curve scientifically doubtful rather than mathematically invalid.

title: Dose-response bridges assume a curve that may not transport
text:
Why it is open
Where doses do not overlap on a comparable exposure scale, the assumed shape of the curve does the identification work rather than summarizing data, so the resulting narrow interval reflects the rigidity of the parametric family and curve misspecification appears as precision rather than as uncertainty. Within-range residual checks and comparisons across alternative curves assess parts of the model, and Pedder et al. showed the bridge can be validated against an augmented network where one can be constructed, but neither reaches the extrapolation across a genuine gap. Effect modification that changes the curve turns a single shared curve into a family of population-specific curves that the standard model does not represent, and there is no internal test distinguishing a genuinely shared pharmacologic curve from a convenient parametric family.

title: Dose-response bridges assume a curve that may not transport
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Follow Pedder et al.’s practice rather than proposing it as new: fit alternative monotonic, Emax, spline, and class-specific curves, report how the cross-gap contrast moves across them, and where a connected analogue can be constructed, validate by deleting the link and comparing against the augmented-network NMA. Model exposure rather than nominal dose where formulations, intensity, or adherence differ, and state the mechanistic argument explicitly when treatments with different mechanisms are given a shared curve rather than treating that as automatically disqualifying. Where the decision warrants it, design a bridging trial with overlapping doses.

title: Dose-response bridges assume a curve that may not transport
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Model-based NMA links treatments across a gap through a shared dose or exposure response function, which is strong when pharmacology supports the curve and exposure scales are comparable. It is weak when nominal dose does not reflect exposure, when formulations, dose intensity or adherence differ, when effect modifiers change the curve, or when treatments with distinct mechanisms are forced into one class, and a wrong curve can produce a precise but artificial link.”
What was wrong with it. The source claimed dose-response bridges are not routinely stress-tested against alternative curves, and cited nothing; the literature auditor supplied doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315, in which Pedder et al. fit MBNMA models with different dose-response relationships and benchmark disconnected-network estimates against NMA on augmented networks, which is both a stress test and a bridge-deletion validation. GPT-5.6 Sol softened two categorical claims: dose overlap alone is not enough without a comparable exposure scale, and MBNMA need not force a single common curve on all treatments.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, yet the canonical paper on exactly this bridge exists and is missing: Pedder, Dias, Bennetts, Boucher and Welton 2021, ‘Joining the Dots’, Medical Decision Making. It supports most of the entry’s claims verbatim (‘MBNMA relies on correct specification of the dose-response relationship, which requires sufficient data at different doses to allow reliable estimation’). But it contradicts claim 9, that dose-response bridges are not routinely stress-tested against alternative curves: the authors ‘fitted MBNMA models with different dose-response relationships’, compared exponential and Emax forms, and benchmarked disconnected-network estimates against NMA on augmented networks, agreeing in 15 of 18 datasets and failing in 3 where a more complex curve was needed. That is both a stress test and a bridge-deletion validation. The underlying problem, that the assumed curve does the identification work and cannot be tested across a genuine gap, stands. The entry should cite Pedder 2021; publishing this gap without it will read as unfamiliarity with the field. Cites 10.1177/0272989X20983315: Missing canonical citation; supplies the source for the entry’s assumption claims and empirically validates the dose-response bridge against augmented-network NMA.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1 and C4-C6 are technically correct with the stated conditions. A disconnected dose-response bridge is identified through parameters shared across the gap, and nonoverlap turns it into extrapolation. Nominal dose may be a poor exposure scale when bioavailability, formulation, adherence, or intensity differ; population effect modification can also make the curve population-specific. C2 needs more than overlapping doses: overlap is useful only on a scientifically comparable exposure scale under a transportable response model. C3 is too broad because MBNMA need not impose one common curve across every treatment; agent-specific curves linked by shared or hierarchical parameters are possible. C7 is also categorical: distinct mechanisms make a common curve scientifically doubtful, but do not mathematically invalidate it if a justified common exposure-response parameterization exists. Within-range residual checks and alternative-curve comparisons can assess parts of the model, but cannot validate the unobserved cross-gap extrapolation. C8 is correct. C9 is a practice-frequency claim outside this audit. The risk is decision-critical when the curve is the identifying bridge; the particular menu of sensitivity models is roadmap implementation.

Decision path

title: Component additivity across a gap cannot be checked from the data
text: DIS-06 Unverifiable High priority Promising

title: Component additivity across a gap cannot be checked from the data
text:
Statement
Component NMA connects treatments through shared components, but sharing components is not sufficient for a cross-gap contrast to be estimable: under strict additive CNMA a treatment effect is c_t’ beta and a target contrast is estimable only when c_a minus c_b lies in the row space of the design X = BC. Petropoulou et al. 2023 found additive CNMA performs well in connected networks when additivity holds and concluded it should be used for disconnected networks only with strong clinical arguments for additivity. Across a gap, any additivity or component-constancy restriction lying in the likelihood null space cannot be tested from those data: the nested Q difference against standard NMA is unavailable because standard NMA cannot be fitted across the gap, and a saturated Q has no power because it is identically zero by arithmetic. Component models that include estimable interaction terms are a different case and are not covered by the word additive.

title: Component additivity across a gap cannot be checked from the data
text:
Why it is open
In a connected network additivity can be tested against standard NMA only when the unrestricted model and the relevant interactions are estimable and residual degrees of freedom remain; across a gap the additive structure is exactly the untested quantity supplying the answer, and the restriction sits where the likelihood is flat. Good performance under simulated additivity says nothing about performance when additivity fails, and the failure mode across a gap is not detectable by fit statistics computed within the observed components. There is no accepted standard for what counts as a strong clinical argument for additivity, so the qualifier attached to the method is not operationalized in practice.

title: Component additivity across a gap cannot be checked from the data
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Before fitting, report which cross-gap contrasts enter the row space of the pooled component design, since a hierarchy built on relative effects that are not uniquely estimable is misleading, and use the estimability workflow of Wigle et al. 2026 for that step. Require an explicit clinical additivity argument before using CNMA across a gap and define what such an argument must contain, since the published recommendation attaches the qualifier without operationalizing it. Pair the estimate with component drift sensitivity rather than a single interval, recognizing that a fragility calculation is a sensitivity analysis and not a test.

title: Component additivity across a gap cannot be checked from the data
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Component NMA connects treatments through shared components and is compelling when interventions are genuinely modular and additive. A simulation study concluded that additive CNMA performs well in connected networks when additivity holds but should be used for disconnected networks only with strong clinical arguments for additivity.”

The literature auditor checked all three source claims verbatim against doi:10.1186/s12874-023-01959-9 and rated the entry supported; GPT-5.6 Sol read the code and narrowed it, since shared components alone do not make a contrast estimable and the untestability is a row-space property rather than a property of disconnection as such. The published text follows the narrower version and the disagreement stands in the audit trail. The auditors also supplied two additions the source omitted: arXiv:2605.15142, which determines which relative effects in a CNMA are uniquely estimable, and doi:10.1002/bimj.201900339, a head-to-head comparison of a component bridge against a matching bridge on a real disconnected network.

Shared components or treatment-network connectedness alone are not sufficient. In a connected network, additivity can be tested against standard NMA only when the unrestricted model and relevant interactions are estimable and there are residual degrees of freedom. title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text: DIS-08 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Speculative

title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text:
Statement
Mechanistic and pharmacometric models can link treatments across a gap through exposure, biomarker response, disease progression, or pathway inhibition, and may be more credible than statistical exchangeability when the mechanism is well established, provided the treatment-to-mechanism mapping, the structural parameters, and the transport assumptions are made explicit. Such a model generates a cross-gap contrast but does not restore randomized identification, and it imports structural model error from the mechanistic model itself. The structural model is not wholly untestable, since observable parameters and predictions can be calibrated or falsified; what cannot be validated internally is the unobserved target contrast. The literature auditor found no published analysis using a fully mechanistic PK/PD, biomarker, or pathway model as the identifying bridge across a disconnected evidence network, and set confidence low because absence cannot be established by not finding one.

title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text:
Why it is open
A mechanistic bridge replaces an untestable statistical assumption with a structural one whose parameters, functional forms, and biological simplifications were fitted for a different purpose, and the evidence synthesis cannot diagnose failure on the cross-gap contrast because that contrast is unobserved by construction. Calibrating the observable parts of the model constrains it but does not bound the extrapolation that carries the answer. The claim of no established practice here is an absence claim neither auditor could verify positively, so it stands as an unfilled niche rather than a proven void.

title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text:

Work

title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Where a connected analogue can be constructed, calibrate a mechanistic bridge prospectively and compare it directly against purely empirical alternatives on the same network, following the augmented-network benchmarking Pedder et al. applied to the semi-mechanistic dose-response bridge. Require the treatment-to-mechanism mapping and the transport assumptions to be stated as identifying assumptions, and report which parts of the structural model were calibrated against observable data and which were assumed. Treat fully mechanistic bridges as a high-risk, high-reward research direction rather than as a routine option.

title: Mechanistic bridges import structural model error
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Mechanistic and pharmacometric models can link treatments across a gap through exposure, biomarker response, disease progression, or pathway inhibition, and may be more credible than statistical exchangeability when the mechanism is well established. They also risk importing structural model error from the mechanistic model itself.”
What was wrong with it. The source said mechanistic bridges are not calibrated prospectively or compared with purely empirical alternatives; that narrows to fully mechanistic bridges, because the semi-mechanistic dose-response bridge was benchmarked against NMA on augmented networks by Pedder et al. 2021 (doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315), and model-based meta-analysis routinely compares treatments never studied head-to-head. GPT-5.6 Sol also corrected the claim that nothing diagnoses failure of the mechanistic model: observable parts of it can be calibrated or falsified, and only the cross-gap contrast is beyond reach.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty and I could not retrieve a paper that uses a fully mechanistic PK/PD, biomarker or pathway model as the identifying bridge across a disconnected evidence network, so the problem is genuinely open and the risk of importing structural model error is uncontroversial. The caveat is claim 4, that mechanistic bridges are not currently calibrated prospectively or compared with purely empirical alternatives. The closest relative, the semi-mechanistic dose-response bridge, was benchmarked against purely empirical NMA on the same data by Pedder et al. 2021, agreeing in 15 of 18 augmented-network comparisons. Model-based meta-analysis in pharmacometrics is a mature field in which exposure-response models are routinely used to compare treatments never compared head-to-head. I did not read that literature closely enough to assert it contains a formal head-to-head calibration study, so I set confidence low and flag claim 4 as needing narrowing to fully mechanistic bridges rather than pharmacometric bridges in general.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. C1-C3 are technically defensible only when the treatment-to-mechanism mapping, structural parameters, and transport assumptions are explicit. Such a model can generate a cross-gap contrast, but it does not restore randomized identification. The structural model is not wholly untestable because observable parameters and predictions may be calibrated or falsified, although an unobserved target contrast cannot be validated internally. C4 is an uncited, field-wide practice claim that this technical audit cannot establish.

text:
Why it is open
Interface, defaults, theory, and validation of an open pull request can all change before merge, so applied analyses built on it are building on a moving target. More fundamentally the feature supplies the cross-gap link through baseline synthesis, so a connected posterior is produced by assumption rather than by randomization, and the released version reaches a similar-looking result from the prior alone. Because the software output looks identical to a connected-network fit in both cases, users cannot see from the result whether identification came from the baseline model, from the prior, or from randomized evidence.

title: No standard ledger names the parameter carrying the gap
text: DIS-12 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising

title: No standard ledger names the parameter carrying the gap
text:
Statement
A bridge ledger should name, for each bridge in use, the identifiable cross-gap functional carrying the information, the identifying assumptions, and a prespecified sensitivity parameter appropriate to that model. Shared baselines, shared component effects, component-by-modifier interactions, class deviations, dose-response transport deviations, and external-control bias functions are defensible examples; the literature auditor checked those rows against Beliveau et al. 2017 and Thom et al. 2022 for baselines, Petropoulou et al. 2023 for additivity, Perren et al. 2026 for class effects, Pedder et al. 2021 for dose-response transport, and Hussein et al. 2023 for the external-control bias parameter. The sensitivity parameters are analysis-specific rather than canonical: a baseline heterogeneity standard deviation estimated from the data is not automatically a sensitivity parameter, and systematic subnetwork nonexchangeability is better represented by a location shift or bias function. In rank-deficient component models the carrying object may be an identifiable row-space functional rather than any individual shared coefficient.

title: No standard ledger names the parameter carrying the gap
text:
Why it is open
Bridge assumptions are distributed across model code, prior specifications, and prose, so a reader cannot reconstruct from the published output which parameter produced the cross-gap answer. There is no agreed vocabulary pairing each bridge with its untestable component and a model-appropriate sensitivity parameter, and the reporting guidance that does exist is scoped to population-adjusted comparisons rather than to disconnected-network bridges. The consequence is that disconnected analyses are published with one narrow interval and no bridge sensitivity, and the fact that the software connected the network is mistaken for evidence of identification.

title: Reported intervals condition on the bridge being exactly true
text:
Statement
Intervals from disconnected-network analyses condition on the bridge model being true unless the model explicitly integrates over a drift or discrepancy parameter, and for the nonidentified part of that uncertainty the interval does not shrink with within-subnetwork sample size at a fixed design. Reporting the contrast as an identified set requires the drift parameterization to be written down: for treatments in subnetworks s and r the contrast is C_t’ beta_s minus C_u’ beta_r, so with beta_s = beta + Delta and beta_r = beta the target is (C_t minus C_u)’ beta plus C_t’ Delta, not (C_t minus C_u)‘(beta + Delta). Once a loading a is defined so that theta = theta_0 plus a’ Delta, box and ellipsoidal drift sets give analytic bounds through the corresponding support functions, with an ellipsoid encoding correlated drift only when a stochastic interpretation is added. Part of this already exists: the cpaic development package computes a per-draw tipping threshold under a uniform box bound with a taken as C_t minus C_u, and nmathresh implements decision-invariant thresholds over data-level bias in connected NMA.

title: Reported intervals condition on the bridge being exactly true
text:
Why it is open
Standard inference propagates sampling variability within the assumed model but treats the identifying bridge as a fixed input, so the interval narrows with sample size while the bridge assumption does not become more credible; richer within-subnetwork variation can inform testable parts of constancy, but not the part lying in the likelihood null space. Partial identification is not routine in evidence synthesis, and the tools that exist stop short: nmathresh perturbs observed data in a connected network rather than a bridge parameter, and cpaic returns a tipping threshold under one uniform box bound on component main effects rather than a full identified set, with no component-specific, interaction, or ellipsoidal drift, and it is an unreleased development package on GitHub not installable from CRAN. The drift set itself must be elicited rather than estimated, and there is no elicitation protocol or calibration evidence for how large a plausible component drift is across treatment contexts or eras.

text:
Probable solution or research direction
Generalize the existing tipping calculation into a full identified set: define the loading from the subnetwork drift parameterization rather than assuming a shared drift, cover component-specific and interaction drift as well as main effects, and compute box and ellipsoidal bounds through their support functions. Do the missing empirical work on the drift sets themselves: elicit clinical limits for the largest plausible change in a component effect across treatment contexts or eras, and calibrate them against networks where a connected answer is available.

title: Reported intervals condition on the bridge being exactly true
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Confidence and credible intervals from disconnected-network analyses condition on the bridge model being true, so the reported uncertainty omits the dominant source of uncertainty in the analysis. When cross-gap constancy cannot be defended pointwise the contrast should instead be reported as an identified set induced by a drift set: for component drift Delta in a set D the identified set is the set of values of (C_t minus C_u) transposed times (beta plus Delta) over Delta in D, with analytic extrema under box constraints and correlated drift representable by ellipsoidal sets.”
What was wrong with it. The source’s algebra was wrong: GPT-5.6 Sol showed the cross-gap contrast under subnetwork drift is (C_t minus C_u)’ beta plus C_t’ Delta rather than (C_t minus C_u)’(beta + Delta), so a shared-drift formula can cancel a component exactly when differential subnetwork drift is what matters, and a valid analysis must define the loading explicitly. Sol also found cpaic already implements a uniform-box tipping threshold, making the software gap partial rather than total, and the literature auditor added doi:10.1111/rssa.12341 and the nmathresh package as existing fragility machinery the proposal should build on rather than restate.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): I found no partial-identification treatment of disconnected networks, so the core problem stands, and the mathematics as stated is elementary and correct: for a linear component model the identified set induced by a drift set is the image of the drift set under the contrast functional, box constraints give analytic extrema, and ellipsoidal sets encode correlated drift. The caveat is that the entry’s proposed ‘tipping-point and fragility surfaces’ already exist in a closely related form that prior_work omits. Phillippo et al. 2018 in JRSS-A derive ‘bias adjustment thresholds which measure the smallest changes to the data that result in a change of treatment decision’, shipped as the CRAN package nmathresh. That is a fragility surface for connected NMA over data-level bias, not over a bridge parameter, so it does not close the problem, but it means the machinery is not being invented from nothing. Hussein et al. 2023 also demonstrate empirically that intervals widen once the assumed structure is relaxed. codex dissented (overstated): C1 is correct for intervals fitted under a fixed bridge assumption, but not for models that explicitly integrate over a drift or discrepancy parameter. C2 holds only for the nonidentified part of bridge uncertainty at a fixed disconnected design; richer within-subnetwork component variation can inform testable parts of constancy. C3 is not the generic algebra for subnetwork drift. If beta_s = beta + Delta and beta_r = beta, then the cross-gap contrast is (C_t-C_u)^T beta + C_t^T Delta, not (C_t-C_u)^T(beta+Delta). A valid analysis must define a loading a such that theta = theta_0 + a^T Delta. title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
text: DIS-16 Overstated Very high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
text:
Statement
Principled study-design machinery exists. Salanti et al. 2018 give a four-step framework identifying the optimal design for a new trial that updates existing evidence while minimizing required sample size, without requiring the trial to include every comparison of interest; Nikolakopoulou et al. 2022 extend it to power and sample allocation for a subsequent trial with a new treatment; and Jackson et al. 2019 supply expected value of partial perfect information and expected value of sample information for Bayesian evidence synthesis, which can in principle rank treatment pairs, IPD acquisition, measured modifiers, subpopulation, sample size, allocation, and biomarker-versus-outcome designs once each candidate has a predictive likelihood, costs, and a decision utility. None of it has been extended to choosing an edge across a disconnected gap, where the objective itself depends on the contested bridge assumption. For a component network the optimal new edge is not necessarily the clinically obvious comparison, but neither is it simply the edge that most reduces null-space dimension: one added edge changes rank by at most one, so all independent candidate edges tie on that criterion, and what matters is whether the decision-critical contrast enters the updated row space and what the study is worth net of its cost.

title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
text:
Why it is open
Value-of-information machinery scores a candidate design against an assumed model, and across a disconnected gap the assumed model contains the bridge whose validity is the question, so the objective function inherits the contested assumption and a design can rank highly precisely because the bridge it relies on was taken for granted. The published trial-design frameworks are built for connected networks and say nothing about which edge to add across a gap, whether to acquire IPD on an existing edge, or how to score a short biomarker bridging study against a long clinical-outcome trial, which also requires a credible surrogate relationship and a valuation of time and cost. The estimability half exists but is not wired to the design question: a contrast is estimable if and only if it is orthogonal to the null space of the design, and cpaic computes rank, null space, and contrast estimability, but nothing enumerates candidate edges or evaluates them, and cpaic is an unreleased development package on GitHub not installable from CRAN.

title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing frameworks to the disconnected case rather than starting over: define candidate designs that add an edge across a gap, acquire IPD on an existing edge, measure an additional modifier, or change subpopulation, and score them with standard expected value of sample information under explicitly stated bridge, surrogate, transport, cost, and decision assumptions. Report the objective under more than one bridge, since ranking under a single assumed bridge inherits exactly the assumption in question. Combine that with row-space estimability screening, using the CNMA estimability workflow to check whether the decision-critical contrast enters the updated design, and report the recommended design alongside the clinically obvious one so the difference is visible to trial planners.

title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Principled frameworks exist for designing a future trial conditional on an existing connected network meta-analysis and for value-of-information research design in Bayesian evidence synthesis, but none has been extended to choosing which edge to add across a disconnected gap, to whether to acquire IPD on an existing edge, or to scoring a short biomarker bridging study against a long clinical-outcome trial when the objective itself depends on the contested bridge assumption.
The source titled this. “No principled design of bridging studies or new network edges” The title says no principled study design exists, but conditional trial design for networks and value-of-information research design are published.
The source said. “The scientifically best solution to a disconnected network may be to collect new evidence, and value-of-information methods could choose which pair of treatments to compare, whether to collect IPD on an existing edge, which effect modifiers to measure, sample size and allocation, which subpopulation maximizes identification of a component interaction, and whether a short biomarker bridge beats a long clinical-outcome trial. For a component network the optimal new edge is not necessarily the clinically obvious comparison; it is the edge that most reduces uncertainty or null-space dimension for decision-critical contrasts.”
What was wrong with it. The source said there is no principled method for choosing which IPD or which bridging trial to obtain; both auditors judged this false as stated, citing doi:10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2, doi:10.1186/s12874-022-01792-6, and doi:10.1080/01621459.2018.1562932. GPT-5.6 Sol also corrected the null-space criterion, since one added edge changes rank by at most one and reducing global nullity need not make the decision-critical contrast estimable, rejected ‘which subpopulation maximizes identification’ as conflating a rank property with expected decision value, and narrowed the software-absence claim to cpaic, which exposes rank, null space, and contrast estimability but has no candidate-edge or value-of-information routine; the literature auditor added arXiv:2605.15142 for determining which CNMA relative effects are uniquely estimable, demonstrated on a disconnected network.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Citation corrected

corrected attribution: ‘Nikolakopoulou et al. 2022’ -> “Hu, Wang, Ye and O’Connor 2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology” CrossRef resolves this DOI to Hu, Wang, Ye and O’Connor, ‘Using information from network meta-analyses to optimize the power and sample allocation of a subsequent trial with a new treatment’.

Citation corrected

corrected attribution: “Hu, Wang, Ye and O’Connor 2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology” -> “Hu, Wang, Ye and O’Connor 2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology” CrossRef resolves this DOI to Hu, Wang, Ye and O’Connor, ‘Using information from network meta-analyses to optimize the power and sample allocation of a subsequent trial with a new treatment’.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. Claim 1, that there is no principled method for choosing which trial to obtain and that such decisions are made opportunistically, is too strong. Salanti, Nikolakopoulou, Sutton et al. (Trials 2018) ‘introduce a four-step framework that aims to identify the optimal design for a new trial that will update the existing evidence while minimizing the required sample size’, explicitly noting the new trial need not include all comparisons of interest; Nikolakopoulou and colleagues (BMC Med Res Methodol 2022) extend this to optimizing power and sample allocation for a subsequent trial with a new treatment; and Jackson, Presanis, Conti and De Angelis give a general value-of-information framework for research design in Bayesian evidence synthesis. Separately, the estimability half of claim 8 now exists: Wigle, Beliveau, Nikolakopoulou and Lin (arXiv 2026) give a workflow for explicitly identifying uniquely estimable relative effects in CNMA, demonstrated on a disconnected network. What remains genuinely open is bridging-specific design: choosing an edge to add across a gap, IPD acquisition, and biomarker-versus-outcome trade-offs under bridge uncertainty. Cites 10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2: Principled, published framework for choosing which comparisons a new trial should include given an existing network, contradicting ‘no principled method’ as stated. Cites 10.1186/s12874-022-01792-6: Extends network-informed trial design to a new treatment entering the network, including allocation and two- versus three-arm choice. Cites arXiv:1703.08994: General value-of-information machinery for research design in evidence synthesis, which the entry treats as not yet existing for this setting. Cites arXiv:2605.15142: Supplies the estimability determination underlying the null-space claim, demonstrated on a disconnected network.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 is false as a blanket technical claim. Standard EVSI or expected-net-benefit-of-sampling defines a principled choice among candidate designs once each design has a predictive likelihood, costs, and a decision utility. It can therefore represent treatment pairs, acquisition of an existing IPD source, measured modifiers, subpopulation, sample size, allocation, and biomarker-versus-outcome designs, making C2 correct in principle. C3 is not well defined: identification is a rank or row-space property, whereas VOI maximizes expected decision value; a subpopulation cannot ‘maximize identification’ without an explicit design, estimand, support condition, and scoring rule. C4 is possible only under a credible predictive or surrogate relationship and appropriate time and cost valuation. C5 is exactly confirmed by the portfolio metadata. C6 is correct. C7 is not generally correct: one added edge changes rank by at most one, all independent candidate edges tie on global null-space reduction, and reducing global nullity need not make the decision-critical contrast estimable or maximize decision value. The relevant algebra is whether the contrast enters the updated row space, followed by decision value net of study cost. At 9d150e9, cpaic exposes B, C, X, rank, null space, and contrast estimability but has no candidate-edge or VOI routine; that supports only a cpaic-scoped version of C8, not the universal software claim. The remaining bridge-specific integration is a legitimate roadmap item, but it is not an absence of principled design theory and is critical only when the current decision is sensitive and new evidence is feasible. Cites 10.1186/s13063-018-2740-2: Provides a network-informed framework for selecting the design and comparisons of a subsequent trial while considering required sample size.. Cites 10.1080/01621459.2018.1562932: Provides EVPPI and EVSI machinery for Bayesian evidence-synthesis models, including comparison of candidate data sources and sample sizes against sampling cost.. Cites choxos/cpaic@9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca: Supplies the rank, null-space, and contrast-specific row-space computations needed to assess estimability after a candidate design change, but does not enumerate or optimize candidate edges..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)

title: No design method chooses which edge to add across a disconnected gap
section: How the evidence falls in time
text:
How the evidence falls in time
6 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2018 to 2023. The most recent paper to touch this reports progress on it, and every paper calling it open is older.
It is also being closed in pieces: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.
Does the later work answer the earlier work? Put to an independent reviewer with the older and newer claims side by side, it judged that the later work answers a component of it, leaving a named part (high confidence). The 2023 connecting-trial paper directly answers a central part of the earlier gap by enumerating candidate edges across a disconnected network and selecting the one minimizing variance for a prespecified cross-gap contrast. Its scope is narrower than the stated open problem: fixed-effect NMA, two-arm trials, one contrast, and variance rather than decision value. What remains: Decision-theoretic selection across candidate designs, including costs and utilities, alternative evidence acquisitions, and objectives that depend on an explicit contested bridge assumption.

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text: DIS-18 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text:
Statement
In a dose-response model-based network meta-analysis used to bridge a disconnected network, each agent’s curve is identified only by the distinct doses published for that agent, and dose coverage is systematically unequal across agents because a sponsor holds unpublished phase II dose-ranging evidence for its own product and not for competitors. The consequence is directional rather than symmetric noise: where an agent’s dose evidence is too sparse the model falls back to a simpler functional form, and the fitted cross-gap contrast then moves in a direction set by which agent was under-covered. The mechanism has been demonstrated rather than hypothesized. In a manipulated migraine network of 70 studies and seven triptan agents, dose-response estimates agreed with the augmented connected analysis in 15 of 18 disconnected datasets, and all three disagreements involved eletriptan, whose relationship needed an Emax curve the sparse disconnected data could not support, so an exponential curve was fitted and pushed its cross-gap effects downward (Pedder et al. 2021, doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315). No reported diagnostic states how many distinct doses inform each agent’s curve, no sensitivity analysis grants the under-covered agent the flexibility the well-covered one receives, and no simulation crosses per-agent dose coverage with which agent belongs to the submitting sponsor. Consistency checking does not fill the gap: node splitting in a dose-response network requires loops a disconnected network does not have, and the number of comparisons where it is possible at all depends on the complexity of the selected dose-response function.

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text:
Why it is open
The asymmetry is a property of the evidence base rather than of the model, so no estimator removes it; correcting it needs either the missing dose-ranging studies or an explicit model for what has not been published. Model-fit statistics cannot choose a functional form for an agent with one or two doses, so the fallback to a simpler curve is forced rather than selected, and the analyst has no way to record that one agent’s curve is better identified than another’s. The diagnostics that exist were built for connected dose-response networks, where redundancy makes consistency checkable, and they disappear precisely in the disconnected case where the curve carries the whole contrast. Nobody has run the simulation because it requires a factor nobody currently varies, per-agent dose coverage crossed with which agent the analysis favors, and because the obvious remedy, publication of phase II dose-ranging results, is outside the analyst’s control.

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Pedder et al. 2021, Medical Decision Making
builds the dose-response bridge, validates it by deleting connecting evidence from a triptans network, and localizes its failure to the one agent whose dose evidence could not support the curve its data required, while naming the sponsor-linked availability asymmetry and proposing no remedy beyond urging publication


Mawdsley et al. 2016, CPT: Pharmacometrics and Systems Pharmacology
establishes the model-based network meta-analysis framework in which dose is modeled as a quantitative shared structure, the machinery whose identification depends on which doses were published


Pedder et al. 2022, Statistics in Medicine
supplies global and node-splitting inconsistency tests for dose-response model-based network meta-analysis, shows that a misspecified dose-response function can itself create apparent inconsistency, and states that the scope for node splitting depends on the complexity of the chosen function and that dose-finding designs offer limited scope to assess consistency


MBNMAdose (CRAN 0.5.1)
implements the dose-response bridge with unrelated-mean-effects and node-splitting checks; nothing in its output reports how many distinct doses inform each agent’s curve or which agents were forced into a simpler form


Chaimani and Salanti 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
gives the comparison-adjusted funnel plot, the routine screen for selective availability in a network, which is indexed by comparison rather than by agent or dose and so cannot detect asymmetric dose coverage


Mavridis et al. 2014, Statistics in Medicine
gives a selection model for publication bias across a full network, showing that machinery for modeling unavailable studies exists and has simply not been directed at which doses of which agent were published

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Report the coverage table first: for every agent, the number of distinct doses, their spread, the studies contributing them and the functional forms those data can support, printed beside the fitted curves so that a reader sees which curve is thin. Add a symmetric-flexibility sensitivity analysis, refitting with the well-covered agent forced into the functional form imposed on the under-covered one, and again with Emax or ED50 shared within a clinically justified class, and report the cross-gap contrast under each. Simulate the asymmetry directly by crossing the number and spacing of doses per agent with the true curve shape and with which agent is the intervention under appraisal, scoring bias and coverage on the bridged contrast rather than on curve parameters. Where the submitting sponsor holds unpublished dose-ranging data, treat its release as a condition of the analysis or model the missing doses explicitly, since the direction of the induced bias is predictable from who holds what.

title: Unequal dose coverage moves a dose-response bridge one way
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it and the reviewer accepted differential dose coverage as an identification and bias problem distinct from whether a dose-response curve transports, while noting that the sponsor-linked direction of bias needs broader empirical and simulation support. The basis is a single manipulated real network, in which every disagreement with the connected analysis involved the one under-covered agent.

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text: DIS-20 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text:
Statement
Every published aggregate-data bridge for disconnected networks, random effects on baseline, reference prediction and aggregate-level matching, is formulated for single-time-point generalized linear models in which the bridged quantity is a scalar baseline parameter such as a log odds. For a time-to-event outcome the bridged quantity is an entire baseline hazard or survival function, and no method specifies how to make baseline hazards exchangeable across subnetworks, how to match a disconnected trial’s hazard function to a connected trial’s, or how to partition heterogeneity across the gap when the treatment effect is itself time-varying, as in fractional-polynomial or spline network meta-analysis. The extension is declined rather than overlooked: after modifying both bridges and evaluating them by deletion and simulation, extension to count and continuous outcomes is described as straightforward while time-to-event network meta-analysis such as fractional polynomials, common in oncology, is said to require more significant modification (Thom et al. 2022, doi:10.1177/0272989X221097081). That same evaluation shows how much accuracy is at stake in the easier scalar case: for disconnected treatments bias ran from -0.16 to 0.392 for aggregate-level matching and from -0.102 to 0.40 for reference prediction against a true effect of 0.5, with coverage as low as 0.30 and 0.64 respectively. Disconnected oncology networks with time-to-event endpoints are the case health technology assessment most often faces, and what decisions there need is a survival curve and a restricted mean rather than a single contrast, so a bridge that returns only a hazard ratio would not close the gap even if it existed.

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text:
Why it is open
A hazard function is infinite-dimensional, so a bridge for it needs an exchangeability model over functions rather than over a scalar: a shared shape with study-specific scale, a hierarchical spline or fractional-polynomial coefficient vector, or a process prior, and each choice imposes a different and untestable restriction on the unobserved cross-gap comparison. Follow-up durations, censoring patterns and administrative cutoffs differ across subnetworks, so two baseline hazards are rarely reported on comparable time supports and matching them requires extrapolating at least one into a region with no data. Aggregate survival evidence usually enters through digitized published curves, which introduces reconstruction error that no bridge currently propagates, and a time-varying treatment effect makes the cross-gap quantity a function of time, so a single bias or coverage number does not describe the failure. The scalar bridges are themselves badly biased and undercovered for disconnected treatments, which weakens the incentive to build the harder version before the easier one works.

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Thom et al. 2022, Medical Decision Making
modifies reference prediction and aggregate-level matching for disconnected trials and single-arm studies, evaluates them by bridge deletion and a 96-scenario simulation, and states that time-to-event network meta-analysis would require significant further modification while count and continuous outcomes would not


Beliveau et al. 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
fits random baseline treatment effects to bridge disconnected components and validates by deleting links from connected networks, entirely within the scalar baseline parameterization


Ouwens et al. 2010, Research Synthesis Methods
gives network meta-analysis of parametric survival curves, where each study contributes shape and scale parameters, which is the natural object a survival bridge would have to make exchangeable


Jansen 2011, BMC Medical Research Methodology
gives fractional-polynomial network meta-analysis with time-varying hazard ratios, the model class named as the hard case for a bridge because the cross-gap quantity becomes a function of time


Guyot et al. 2012, BMC Medical Research Methodology
reconstructs individual event times from published Kaplan-Meier curves, the route by which aggregate survival evidence enters a network and the source of reconstruction error a bridge would have to carry


Freeman and Carpenter 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
fits one-step Bayesian individual-data network meta-analysis of time-to-event outcomes with Royston-Parmar models, showing that flexible baseline hazards can be estimated jointly across a connected network


Phillippo et al. 2025, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series A
extends multilevel network meta-regression to general likelihoods with flexible baseline hazards, supplying absolute-scale survival quantities for connected networks with at least one individual-data study; the disconnected case is not covered


Raja Rajeeswari et al. 2026, Value in Health (ISPOR abstract CO184)
reports work extending multilevel network meta-regression to disconnected networks for time-to-event outcomes in myeloma, evidence that the gap is being worked on but as a conference abstract without a published method or independent evaluation

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Specify the bridged object explicitly: pick a representation of the baseline hazard, piecewise constant, M-spline or fractional polynomial, make its coefficient vector the exchangeable quantity across subnetworks with a declared covariance, and derive what that exchangeability implies for the cross-gap survival contrast at each time point. Build the matching analogue by defining a distance between reported hazard or survival functions on a common time support, with the admissible region declared before matching, rather than matching on scalar baseline summaries that discard the shape. Score on the quantities decisions use, survival probability error at fixed horizons, restricted mean survival difference and extrapolation error, and validate by bridge deletion on connected oncology networks where the cross-gap answer is known. Propagate Kaplan-Meier reconstruction uncertainty through the bridge, since a digitized curve is the input on both sides of the gap and its error is currently absorbed into the point estimate.

title: No aggregate-data bridge exists for disconnected survival networks
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed it from a single paper whose discussion names the extension and declines it, and the reviewer accepted that a scalar baseline bridge does not supply a bridge for an entire baseline hazard function. The basis is that one paper plus a conference abstract announcing work in the same direction, which is a weaker foundation than a record of published attempts.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text: EST-01 Overstated Very high priority Emerging

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Statement
Applied ITC and PAIC practice still defaults the target population to whichever aggregate-data trial reported enough baseline covariates, and reported effects are rarely labeled with the population they refer to. The normative half of the source’s Direction A is not new: NICE DSU TSD18 (Phillippo et al. 2018, doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) has required since 2016 that the target population be stated explicitly and that population-adjusted effects be generated for it, and it names a cohort or registry population relevant to the decision as the appropriate external source. The machinery is not missing either: multilevel network meta-regression estimates every contrast in a network in one externally supplied target population (Phillippo et al. 2020, doi:10.1111/rssa.12579; doi:10.1002/sim.8759), and multinma implements it through relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects(), each of which accepts an arbitrary target via newdata. What survives is the gap between that requirement and practice, together with the substantive judgment of which target to name, which no statistical criterion settles.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Why it is open
The requirement exists but nothing enforces it at the point where the target is actually chosen, so the estimator’s target is still fixed by which trial reported enough baseline variables, and no diagnostic run on the source analysis can flag a target that was never declared. Transporting a whole network to one external population needs IPD for at least one study and a covariate law for the target, so the capability that exists in ML-NMR is unavailable in exactly the aggregate-only networks where the default is most damaging. Choosing among candidate target sources is a policy judgment no statistical criterion settles, and falling back to an overlap population restores comparability only if the whole network shares one declared overlap estimand rather than a different overlap per pair. Because a single unlabeled symbol denotes both the estimated and the required quantity, the substitution leaves no trace for a reviewer to challenge.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo, Ades, Dias, Palmer, Abrams and Welton 2018, Methods for Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Health Technology Appraisal, Medical Decision Making (NICE DSU TSD18)
Requires that the target population for any treatment comparison be stated explicitly and that population-adjusted relative effects be generated for that target, and names a cohort or registry population relevant to the clinical decision as the appropriate source, which is unlikely to match the aggregate-data trial population. It supplies the normative half of Direction A a decade before this agenda; it does not make the declaration a field anyone checks outside NICE submissions.


Phillippo, Dias, Elsada, Ades and Welton 2020, Multilevel network meta-regression for population-adjusted treatment comparisons, JRSS-A
Defines the one-stage individual-level regression that fits aggregate data by integration and produces population-adjusted contrasts for a specified target population across a whole network, which is the machinery the entry described as nonexistent. It requires IPD from at least one study.


Phillippo, Dias, Ades, Belger, Brnabic, Schacht, Saure, Kadziola and Welton 2020, Assessing the performance of population adjustment methods for anchored indirect comparisons: A simulation study, Statistics in Medicine
Simulation evidence that ML-NMR extends to larger treatment networks and produces estimates in any target population, unlike pairwise MAIC and STC.


multinma: Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Individual and Aggregate Data (R package)
Implements ML-NMR, with relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() all accepting newdata describing an arbitrary target population’s covariate distribution, so estimating every network contrast in one declared target is available software rather than a proposal.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Do not rebuild the declaration rule or the network estimator, since both exist. The work is to make the declared target binding: carry the TSD18 requirement into journal and submission templates, label every reported contrast with its population, and treat target-specific prediction from a network model as the default output rather than an option. Where the full decision target lacks covariate support, change the estimand to one common overlap population for the whole network, and use several targets as sensitivity analysis rather than in place of a primary decision target. The measurable question is whether an enforced declaration changes what appears in submissions, not whether the method exists.

title: Target population is unnamed and set by data availability
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Although NICE DSU TSD18 has required since 2016 that the target population be explicitly stated, and although ML-NMR/multinma can estimate every network contrast in one externally supplied target population for anchored comparisons, which is not yet a general solution for unanchored comparisons or for all outcome types, applied ITC and PAIC practice still defaults the target to whichever aggregate-data trial reported enough covariates, and reported effects are rarely labelled with the population they refer to.
The source said. “Population-adjusted analyses adjust to whichever aggregate-data trial population happens to be reportable, while the decision concerns a different population, and the reported effect carries no label identifying the population it refers to. The report’s Direction A instead requires every relevant contrast to be estimated in one externally defined target population P*, chosen from a named source such as a jurisdictional registry, the eligible treatment population, a pooled trial-eligible population, a standardized reference population, or an overlap population where the full target is unsupported.”
What was wrong with it. The source treated both explicit target declaration and one-target network estimation as absent; the literature auditor found both already in place, in Recommendation 6 of NICE DSU TSD18 (doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740) and in ML-NMR as implemented in multinma (https://cran.r-project.org/package=multinma). GPT-5.6 Sol added that the target need not come from an external data source, that an overlap target is acceptable only as one common network estimand rather than pair by pair, and that reporting several targets is sensitivity analysis rather than a substitute for naming a primary decision target.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

scope-narrowed

verdict_rationale: the closure stands, but its boundary was drawn in the wrong place Unanchored-method papers from 2024 and 2025 state that ML-NMR was then applicable to anchored comparisons only, and a 2025 quantitative-bias-analysis paper lists estimation in an arbitrary target population as a remaining need for unanchored PAICs. The closure stands; its counterexample was stated more broadly than the machinery reaches. Replacement wording composed from the reviewer’s description; reviewer confidence high. Previously: “2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Although NICE DSU TSD18 has required since 2016 that the target population be explicitly stated, and although ML-NMR/multinma can estimate every network contrast in one externally supplied target population, applied ITC and PAIC practice still defaults the target to whichever aggregate-data trial reported enough covariates, and reported effects are rarely labelled with the population they refer to.”

Flagged for reopening

19 findings from the reading assert this problem is open while the registry carries overstated Flagged, not applied: reversing an earlier audit’s closure needs the closure’s own evidence re-examined alongside this, which the reading did not do. See documentation/audit/reading/PROPOSED.md.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. I read the full text of Phillippo et al. 2018 Med Decis Making (the peer-reviewed NICE DSU TSD18). Its Recommendation 6 reads: ‘The target population for any treatment comparison must be explicitly stated, and population-adjusted estimates of the relative treatment effects must be generated for this target population.’ It also already names the external source the entry asks for: ‘the target population should be a cohort or registry study population relevant to the clinical decision, which is unlikely to match the population of the [AgD] trial.’ The practice half of the entry survives (Phillippo 2019 NICE review; Serret-Larmande 2023 found 3/133 PAIC articles reported all key methodological aspects). What does not survive is ‘there is no standard machinery for … transporting every contrast in a network to it at once’: ML-NMR does exactly that, and multinma implements relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() with a newdata target population. The claim that the report ‘names exactly five candidate sources’ is self-referential and not externally checkable. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Already mandates explicit target-population declaration for NICE submissions and names registry/cohort populations as the appropriate external source, i.e. the normative half of Direction A predates this agenda by a decade.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.8759: Establishes ML-NMR as machinery that transports all contrasts of a network into a single declared target population.. Cites cran:multinma: Software implementation: relative_effects(), predict() and marginal_effects() all accept newdata describing an arbitrary target population’s covariate distribution..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. C1 describes conventional pairwise anchored MAIC/STC, not ITC or PAIC generally; C2 and C6 are prevalence or adoption claims that this technical audit cannot establish. C3 is a second transport only when a population-indexed effect is reused in another population; a genuinely invariant conditional parameter is different. A coherent multi-treatment decision normally needs a common decision target, but C4 is too absolute: the target need not come from an external data source, and some decisions legitimately require several populations. C5’s count of five is textually true but methodologically vacuous. C7 is acceptable only as an explicit change to a common network overlap estimand; pair-specific overlap targets destroy contrast comparability. C8 is useful sensitivity analysis, not a substitute for choosing a primary decision target. Target declaration and common-target network standardization already have methodological and software machinery, so the technical problem is partly solved; data support and disciplined use remain. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X17725740: Already requires an explicit target population and effects generated for that target, resolving the claim that no target-declaration machinery exists.. Cites doi:10.1111/rssa.12579: Provides one-stage network machinery for population-adjusted contrasts in a specified target population.. Cites cran:multinma: Implements target-specific prediction and marginal-effect calculations for a network, so the capability is not absent..
