title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text: EVB-01 Partially addressed High priority Promising

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Statement
Individual patient data enter a network non-randomly: reviews of individual participant data meta-analyses find that requested data are frequently not obtained (Nevitt et al. 2017, pmid:28381561; Ahmed et al. 2012, pmid:22214758) and that funding support is associated with retrieval (Wu et al. 2021, doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011). Selective availability threatens transportability whenever inference links the IPD subset to the rest of the network, so a combined IPD and aggregate-data analysis needs explicit assumptions about that link plus sensitivity analysis for departures the observed data cannot identify. It is not a universal identification requirement: inference conditional on a fixed set of studies does not require a stochastic model of IPD availability.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Why it is open
Availability is determined by commercial and legal control, so it is informative about the trials themselves and cannot be assumed ignorable once the analysis generalizes beyond the IPD subset. Because withheld data are unavailable by definition, non-ignorable availability is not identified from observed data without restrictions or sensitivity parameters, and Ahmed et al. 2012 found that most IPD meta-analyses failing to obtain all requested data did not examine what that implied. Senior evidence-synthesis methodologists have asked in print why IPD are not routinely released to reimbursement authorities and guideline developers (Ades et al. 2024, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745), which locates the constraint in the access process. Separately, high-dimensional treatment-by-covariate interactions and within-study missing data remain hard even among the trials that do share, though these are estimation difficulties rather than proof that no IPD-NMA works.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Nevitt et al. 2017, BMJ
Systematic review of 760 IPD meta-analyses showing that only 25% retrieved 100% of eligible IPD and 43% retrieved 80% or more; documents that IPD availability is not a random subset.


Wu et al. 2021, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology
Cross-sectional study of 210 IPD meta-analyses tying data retrieval to trial number, funding support and intervention type; supplies the funding-related mechanism the entry asserted without a citation.


Ahmed et al. 2012, BMJ
Database survey naming data availability bias as a distinct threat in IPD meta-analysis and showing that most analysts who failed to obtain requested data did not examine or even mention the consequences.


Ades et al. 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Response to discussants of ‘NMA, the first 20 years’ asking in print why IPD are not routinely made available to reimbursement authorities and guideline developers; sources the framing of availability as an access process.


MOLGENIS Armadillo: a lightweight server for federated analysis using DataSHIELD, Bioinformatics 2024
Production federated-analysis infrastructure already used for one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts; shows federated analysis is deployed rather than speculative, while leaving sponsor-controlled participation untouched.


Phillippo et al. 2023, Medical Decision Making
Validates population-adjustment assumptions in multilevel network meta-regression by checking model predictions against observed aggregate study outcomes; partly realizes the external-validation idea without needing the withheld IPD.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Selection or pattern-mixture models of IPD availability, framed as sensitivity parameters rather than automatic correction, remain to be developed; the literature auditor searched for them and found none. Federated analysis should be treated as infrastructure to extend rather than to build, since DataSHIELD-based servers already run one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts (MOLGENIS Armadillo, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae726); what federation cannot do is compel a sponsor to join, so it broadens participation without removing selection. External validation is partly realized by comparing population-adjustment predictions against observed aggregate outcomes (Phillippo et al. 2023, doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162); completely withheld IPD cannot themselves serve as a validation set. Interaction terms need regularized or hierarchical structure rather than unrestricted high-dimensional models.

title: Selective IPD availability threatens transport across the network
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced. Reopened by the full-text reading: 3 findings from 3 papers survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed.
The source titled this. “IPD availability is sponsor-controlled and not ignorable” The title calls IPD availability not ignorable as a universal property, which the audit rejected since inference conditional on a fixed study set needs no availability model.
The source said. “Individual patient data are supplied for the sponsor’s own trials rather than for a random subset of the network, so the set of studies that can be population-adjusted or entered into an IPD network meta-analysis is systematically related to who paid for them. IPD-NMA identification requires an availability mechanism, and that mechanism is a data-access process rather than a statistical nuisance.”
What was wrong with it. The source made the availability mechanism a universal identification requirement for IPD-NMA and asserted that no configuration works straightforwardly once IPD are obtained; GPT-5.6 Sol judged both false, because inference conditional on a fixed study set needs no stochastic availability model. The empirical core carried no citation and is now sourced to Nevitt et al. 2017 (pmid:28381561), Wu et al. 2021 (doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011) and Ahmed et al. 2012 (pmid:22214758), the last of which names data availability bias directly.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied 2026-07-26 full-text reading of the consolidated library (687 papers).

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 3 surviving findings from: Comparative effectiveness of biological medicines in rheumat; Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis: A Handbook for He; Meta-Research: Methods and Protocols (Evangelou E, Veroniki . New citations: 10.1007/978-1-0716-1566-9, 10.1136/bmj.m2288

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, so there was no citation to check; I built the case independently. The empirical core is well established and the entry simply fails to cite it: Nevitt 2017 BMJ (760 IPD-MAs), Wu 2021 JCE (210 IPD-MAs) and Ahmed 2012 BMJ all quantify non-random IPD retrieval, and Wu identifies funding support as a predictor of retrieval. Ades 2024 RSM explicitly asks why IPD is not routinely released to reimbursement authorities. So claim 2 is supported and should be sourced. Claims 1 and 4 are defensible but I found no paper formalizing an IPD-availability mechanism as an identification requirement. Claim 5 (‘can be modeled explicitly’) is aspiration: I searched for selection/pattern-mixture models of IPD availability and found none. Claim 6 understates maturity: federated IPD analysis is deployed infrastructure (DataSHIELD/MOLGENIS Armadillo, EU Child Cohort Network), though not for trial NMA in HTA, and it does not solve sponsor withholding since joining the federation is still the sponsor’s choice. Claim 7 is partly realized by Phillippo 2023 MDM, which validates population-adjustment predictions against observed aggregate outcomes. Cites pmid:28381561: Supplies the missing empirical citation for claim 2 (IPD availability is not a random subset). Does not solve the problem; it documents it.. Cites doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2020.10.011: Directly ties IPD retrieval to funding/sponsorship, which is the specific mechanism the entry asserts without citation.. Cites pmid:22214758: Names ‘data availability bias’ as a distinct threat in IPD meta-analysis and shows analysts mostly do not address it. Supports the ‘cannot be checked from inside the analysis’ framing.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745: Senior evidence-synthesis methodologists state the access problem in print, which sources the entry’s ‘data-access process rather than a statistical nuisance’ framing.. Cites doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btae726: Partially deflates claim 6: federated IPD analysis is production infrastructure already used for one-stage IPD meta-analysis across cohorts, not a speculative response. It does not address sponsor-controlled participation.. Cites doi:10.1177/0272989X221117162: Partially realizes claim 7: population-adjustment assumptions are checked by comparing model predictions against the aggregate studies rather than against withheld IPD..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Selective IPD access is a genuine transportability and sensitivity-analysis problem, but the statement overgeneralizes. C1 is false as a universal identification claim: inference conditional on a fixed set of studies does not require a stochastic IPD-availability model. Such a model becomes relevant when generalizing from the IPD subset or correcting selection, and nonignorable availability is not identified from observed data without restrictions or sensitivity parameters. C3 and C4 are technically sound. C2 is an unsupported frequency claim. C5 is feasible as a selection or sensitivity model, not an automatically identified correction. C6 can reduce data-sharing barriers but cannot correct refusal to participate. C7 requires the withheld study to disclose suitable aggregate outcomes or participate in independent or federated validation; completely withheld IPD cannot themselves be a validation set. The assertion that there is no configuration in which IPD-NMA works straightforwardly is false.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted search treated availability bias and IPD-NMA identification as already solved. What exists documents the problem and gives partial workarounds, not a closed identification theory for sponsor-controlled IPD. Riley et al. (BMJ Evid Based Med 2022/2023) and the 2021 IPDMA handbook (Ch. 9.3) state that requested IPD are often unavailable and that availability bias must be examined, typically by comparing or combining IPD-based results with aggregate-data results from non-IPD trials. That is sensitivity to selective availability, not an explicit model of a commercial/legal availability mechanism inside IPD-NMA identification. Federated platforms (DataSHIELD and related 2022–2025 work) reduce the need to release IPD and are a real response to access barriers, but they do not identify effects when the set of contributing studies is non-ignorable by design, and they are not HTA-ITC-specific solutions for sponsor-owned IPD. Pattern-mixture work in meta-analysis targets missing outcomes within studies, not study-level IPD release. High-dimensional treatment-by-covariate interactions and within-study missing data remain widely acknowledged practical limits. Queries run: IPD-NMA availability mechanism/pattern mixture; availability bias Riley/Tierney/Ahmed; federated IPD meta-analysis/DataSHIELD; arXiv/medRxiv IPD-NMA selective availability; R packages multinma/maicplus/netmeta/crossnma for related PRs. Nothing retrieved closes the problem as stated.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

This problem is recurrent: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group’s framing.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Statement
Trials grouped under one outcome label may estimate non-equivalent quantities because they differ in follow-up, endpoint definition, analysis population or intercurrent-event handling; simulation of treatment switching in oncology shows that pooling estimates targeting different estimands yields a pooled estimator that targets no estimand of interest, even under a random-effects model (Metcalfe et al. 2025, doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10039). Estimand mapping is the response and it is no longer a proposal: it has been argued into the evidence-synthesis literature (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741), given a pragmatic framework with a worked NMA case study varying intercurrent-event strategies (arxiv:2510.15762), and codified as step 1 of a population-adjusted indirect comparison framework (doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1). What remains open is per-trial estimand mapping from published reports, where the needed detail is often not reported, and structured encoding of intercurrent-event handling and analysis population.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Why it is open
Indirect comparison arithmetic assumes the contrasts refer to a common estimand, but conformity is usually checked at the level of the outcome label rather than the outcome definition. Differences in intercurrent-event strategy and analysis population change the causal question each trial answers, and no covariate adjustment repairs that mismatch. Published reports frequently do not carry the detail needed to do the mapping trial by trial, and uptake of estimand-aware synthesis remains modest, particularly without IPD. An outcome taxonomy exists for classifying outcomes, but nothing machine-readable encodes intercurrent-event strategy or analysis population.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Metcalfe et al. 2025, Research Synthesis Methods
Simulation of treatment switching in oncology showing that pooling treatment-policy and hypothetical estimands produces a pooled estimator targeting no estimand of interest, and that this can mislead even under random effects.


Remiro-Azocar and Gorst-Rasmussen 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Position paper arguing that the language of estimands belongs in network meta-analysis and HTA, especially under the narrow treatment and target-population perspective HTA takes.


Remiro-Azocar et al., Incorporating estimands into meta-analyses of clinical trials (preprint)
Pragmatic framework for estimands in meta-analysis and NMA for HTA, applied to an NMA of semaglutide versus dulaglutide contrasting treatment-policy and hypothetical strategies for discontinuation and rescue.


Ishak et al. 2025, PharmacoEconomics
Six-element framework for reliable, transparent and reproducible population-adjusted indirect comparisons in which definition of the comparison as an estimand is element 1.


Ades et al. 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Names integration of the estimand framework with evidence synthesis as an explicit agenda item of the core NMA methods group.


Analysis of opinions from studies citing the COMET outcomes taxonomy, 2025
Shows an outcome taxonomy for evidence synthesis already exists and is widely cited, narrowing the gap to estimand-level, machine-readable detail rather than outcome classification as such.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Probable solution or research direction
The direction is to make the existing estimand frameworks routine rather than to invent them: apply the published meta-analysis and PAIC estimand frameworks to each contributing trial and report the mapping alongside the synthesis, so mismatches are visible before pooling rather than after. Extend outcome taxonomies such as COMET beyond outcome classification to encode intercurrent-event strategy and analysis population in structured form. Latent harmonization and multivariate endpoint models are appropriate only where a defensible linking model connects the endpoints and the available data identify its parameters; they cannot generally reconcile different treatment-policy questions, intercurrent-event strategies, populations or time points.

title: Trials combined under one outcome label are not one estimand
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Trials in the same comparison differ in follow-up duration, endpoint definitions, handling of intercurrent events, and analysis populations, so the quantities being combined are not the same estimand even before population adjustment.”
What was wrong with it. The source presented ICH E9(R1)-style estimand mapping and outcome ontologies as promising future directions; the literature auditor and Grok both found an active published programme already doing the mapping (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741, arxiv:2510.15762, doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) and a widely used outcome taxonomy already in routine use (COMET, pmid:40754038). GPT-5.6 Sol rejected the claim that endpoint definitions live in prose no tool can read: the obstacle is incomplete reporting and unreliable structured interpretation, not literal unreadability.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. prior_work is empty, yet an active published programme addresses exactly claim 2. Metcalfe et al. 2025 Res Synth Methods simulated pooling of treatment-policy and hypothetical estimands across oncology RCTs allowing treatment switching, and showed the pooled estimator targets nothing of interest; that converts the entry’s assertion from conjecture into a quantified result. Remiro-Azocar and Gorst-Rasmussen 2024 RSM argue the estimand language belongs in NMA and HTA; Ades et al. 2024 RSM call for integration of the estimand framework with evidence synthesis; Ishak et al. 2025 PharmacoEconomics already makes estimand definition element 1 of a six-element PAIC framework. Claim 1 is uncontroversial and is documented by the COMET outcome-heterogeneity literature. Claim 3 needs softening: the COMET outcome taxonomy exists and is in routine use for classifying trial outcomes, so an outcome classification standard is not absent, though I found nothing machine-readable that encodes intercurrent-event handling or analysis population. Claim 4 I could not verify with a retrieved source this session. Status is partially-solved: the diagnosis and the framework are published; per-trial estimand mapping from published reports is not. Cites doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10039: Quantifies the bias from combining trials whose estimands differ, which the entry states only qualitatively. Also confirms the gap is real.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741: Claim 2 is already a published position paper in the NMA/HTA literature, not a novel proposed direction.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1745: Establishes that estimand-framework integration is an explicitly stated agenda item of the core NMA methods group.. Cites doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1: Shows estimand-first definition is already codified as step 1 of a PAIC analysis framework, so the ITC-specific version of claim 2 is partly operationalized.. Cites pmid:40754038: Narrows claim 3: an outcome taxonomy for evidence synthesis already exists and is widely cited, so what is missing is estimand-level, machine-readable detail rather than outcome classification as such..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central estimand warning is correct and can be decision-critical. Differences in follow-up, outcome variable, analysis population, summary measure, or intercurrent-event strategy produce different estimands when they change the causal quantity being estimated; a common outcome label is insufficient. C2 is technically sound because structured estimand mapping exposes these differences before synthesis. C3 describes useful infrastructure, not a mathematical necessity for valid ITC. C4 holds only when a defensible measurement or linking model connects the endpoints and the available data identify its parameters. Latent or multivariate models cannot generally reconcile different treatment-policy questions, intercurrent-event strategies, populations, or time points. The assertion that no tool can read endpoint definitions in prose is false; the problem is incomplete reporting and unreliable structured interpretation, not literal unreadability.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. That trials sharing an outcome label often target different estimands (follow-up, endpoint definition, intercurrent events, analysis population) remains correct and is now a central theme in synthesis methodology rather than a neglected gap. Remiro-Azócar and Gorst-Rasmussen (2024) argue for estimand thinking as a parallel to narrow research questions in evidence synthesis. Remiro-Azócar et al. (arXiv:2510.15762, versions through 2026) propose a pragmatic framework for estimands in meta-analyses for HTA, apply it to an NMA of semaglutide versus dulaglutide, and contrast treatment-policy versus hypothetical strategies for discontinuation/rescue. EU HTA quantitative evidence-synthesis guidance (2024) also stresses that a common estimand should apply across studies in a synthesis. These works partially resolve C2: ICH E9(R1)-style mapping is no longer only a vague proposal; it is formalized for synthesis and illustrated. They do not close the problem: authors still note modest uptake, difficulty without IPD, and residual cross-trial misalignment. C3 (machine-readable outcome ontology standards for ITC evidence bases) and C4 (latent outcome harmonization models as deployed standards) were not found as solved; semantic-variability/LLM and specialized outcome ontologies exist outside routine ITC pipelines. Mismatched estimands therefore remain open as an operational constraint; the mapping response is partially developed. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1741: Places estimands at the center of evidence-synthesis question formulation; partially resolves the claim that estimand mapping is only aspirational (C2).. Cites arxiv:2510.15762: Provides a pragmatic estimand framework for meta-analysis/NMA in HTA and a worked NMA case study varying intercurrent-event strategies; partially operationalizes ICH E9(R1)-style mapping for synthesis (C2)..

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2) → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text: EVB-05 Unverifiable High priority Emerging

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Statement
Generic baseline-covariate reporting is already mandated: CONSORT 2025 item 25 requires a table of baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group, and CONSORT presents itself as a minimum set of items for a trial report (doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1004587). What no standard specifies is what population adjustment needs: which covariates, dispersion measures, any joint or correlation structure, and reporting on the analysis set that matches the reported effect estimate. In practice the adjustment set is therefore bounded by what the comparator publication happened to print; a review of 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment lists availability among the bases on which covariates were selected (Phillippo et al. 2019, doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333).

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Why it is open
The analyst does not control the comparator publication, so the moments needed for balancing are supplied or withheld by a third party with no stake in the later comparison. A CONSORT-style baseline table does not close the gap, because what is required varies with the estimand and the model, and marginal means and proportions can be insufficient when joint distributions, nonlinear terms or interactions matter. No journal, regulator or registry mandates that PAIC-specific increment, and how often it is missing has not been quantified, though reviews of PAIC practice report inconsistent and incomplete covariate reporting (Truong et al. 2023, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1653). The nearest thing to a PAIC reporting standard governs the analyst’s own reporting of the comparison rather than what the comparator publication must carry (Ishak et al. 2025, doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1).

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Phillippo et al. 2019, International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care
Review of 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment; reports that covariates were included on the basis of availability, expert opinion, effective sample size, statistical significance or cross-validation, sourcing the availability-bounded adjustment set.


CONSORT 2025 statement, PLOS Medicine
Trial reporting standard whose item 25 mandates a baseline demographic and clinical characteristics table per group; establishes that a mandated minimum baseline reporting set does exist, without specifying what population adjustment needs.


Harari et al. 2023, Research Synthesis Methods
Network meta-interpolation: adjusts for effect modification using subgroup analyses reported in aggregate publications, with standard errors, instead of treating the reported covariate set as a fixed constraint.


Truong et al. 2023, Research Synthesis Methods
Methodological review of PAIC practice documenting inconsistent reporting and incomplete covariate information; cited by the recency auditor as support that partial reporting is a live obstacle, without giving a prevalence estimate for the specific summaries PAIC needs.


Ishak et al. 2025, PharmacoEconomics
Framework for reliable, transparent and reproducible PAICs; the closest existing thing to a PAIC reporting standard, but it governs the analyst’s reporting rather than the comparator publication’s covariate summaries.

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define and benchmark the PAIC-specific increment over CONSORT, namely which covariates, which dispersions, any joint or correlation structure, and reporting on the analysis set matching the reported effect estimate, and pursue it as an addition to trial reporting guidance rather than as an analyst-side workaround. Quantify how often that increment is missing, which no auditor found measured, so the case for a standard rests on evidence rather than assertion. In the meantime, methods that build effect-modifier adjustment out of the subgroup information aggregate publications do report already exist and should be extended (network meta-interpolation, Harari et al. 2023, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1608); treating unreported summaries as missing data propagates uncertainty only once identifying assumptions, external information or priors are added, so partial identification and sensitivity analysis are the honest fallback.

title: No reporting standard covers what population adjustment needs
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source titled this. “No minimum covariate-reporting standard for aggregate-data trials” The title says no minimum covariate-reporting standard exists, but CONSORT 2025 item 25 already mandates a baseline characteristics table for each group.
The source said. “The covariate summaries that population adjustment needs are frequently absent from the comparator publication, or reported for a different analysis set, and no benchmarked minimum reporting set exists that would require them. Which covariates can be balanced is therefore decided by what a journal printed rather than by what causal reasoning requires.”
What was wrong with it. The claim was unattributed in the source and stated flatly that no benchmarked minimum reporting set exists; the literature auditor read CONSORT 2025 and found item 25 mandates baseline data (doi:10.1371/journal.pmed.1004587), so only the narrower PAIC-specific version survives, and it is now sourced to Phillippo et al. 2019 (doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333). GPT-5.6 Sol added that there is no universal finite set of summaries every PAIC requires, because the requirement depends on the estimand, the effect-modification basis, the link and outcome models and the weighting method.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): This entry is source_unsourced, so I judged it against the literature. I read the CONSORT 2025 full text. It does contain a mandated baseline-covariate reporting item, item 25 ‘Baseline data’, and the statement describes itself as ‘a minimum set of items to be included in a report of a randomised trial’, endorsed by ICMJE, WAME and CSE, with the same item present as CONSORT 2010 item 15. Claim 2 as written (‘No benchmarked minimum reporting set of baseline covariate summaries currently exists’) is therefore contradicted at face value. What CONSORT does not do is specify which covariates, require dispersion measures, require any joint or correlation structure, or require alignment with the analysis set used for the reported effect estimate; that narrower version survives and I found no PAIC-benchmarked standard. Claim 1 is supportable and I can source it: Phillippo et al. 2019 IJTAHC reviewed 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment and found availability was among the bases on which covariates were selected. Harari et al. 2023 network meta-interpolation exists precisely because full effect-modifier summaries are not uniformly reported. Claim 3 remains without a prevalence estimate.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. This entry is source_unsourced, so I judged it against the literature. I read the CONSORT 2025 full text. It does contain a mandated baseline-covariate reporting item, item 25 ‘Baseline data’, and the statement describes itself as ‘a minimum set of items to be included in a report of a randomised trial’, endorsed by ICMJE, WAME and CSE, with the same item present as CONSORT 2010 item 15. Claim 2 as written (‘No benchmarked minimum reporting set of baseline covariate summaries currently exists’) is therefore contradicted at face value. What CONSORT does not do is specify which covariates, require dispersion measures, require any joint or correlation structure, or require alignment with the analysis set used for the reported effect estimate; that narrower version survives and I found no PAIC-benchmarked standard. Claim 1 is supportable and I can source it: Phillippo et al. 2019 IJTAHC reviewed 18 NICE technology appraisals using population adjustment and found availability was among the bases on which covariates were selected. Harari et al. 2023 network meta-interpolation exists precisely because full effect-modifier summaries are not uniformly reported. Claim 3 remains without a prevalence estimate. Cites doi:10.1017/S0266462319000333: Supplies a real reference for claim 1, converting an unsourced assertion into a sourced one: in 18 NICE appraisals using population adjustment, availability was one of the reported bases for covariate selection.. Cites doi:10.1002/jrsm.1608: Existing partial response to the proposed direction: builds effect-modifier adjustment out of whatever subgroup information aggregate publications do report, with standard errors, rather than treating the reported set as a fixed constraint.. Cites doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1: Nearest existing thing to a PAIC reporting standard, but it governs the analyst’s own reporting of the comparison, not the covariate summaries the comparator publication must carry; so it does not close the gap the entry describes..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / unverifiable. The technical core of C2 is correct: absent or incompatible target-population summaries can prevent balancing of prespecified effect modifiers or make PAIC strongly assumption-dependent. C1 contains no substantive proposition. C3 is an uncited absence claim and C4 is an uncited frequency claim, so neither can be verified under the specified technical-only, no-literature lens. Moreover, there is no universal finite collection of summaries that every PAIC requires; requirements depend on the estimand, effect-modification basis, link and outcome models, and weighting method. Marginal means and proportions may be insufficient when joint distributions, nonlinear terms, or interactions matter. Treating unreported summaries as missing data propagates uncertainty only after adding identifying assumptions, external information, or priors; otherwise sensitivity analysis or partial identification is required. The reporting limitation remains open, but its alleged prevalence and the nonexistence of standards are not established here.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted search looked for a benchmarked minimum covariate-reporting set that would make aggregate-data publications PAIC-ready. Methodological reviews of PAIC practice document inconsistent reporting and incomplete covariate information as live obstacles (Serret-Larmande et al. 2023, J Clin Epidemiol; Truong et al. 2023, Res Synth Methods, doi:10.1002/jrsm.1653), supporting C2 and C4. CONSORT and trial reporting norms require baseline characteristic tables, but they do not mandate the full set of moments PAIC needs (means and SDs for continuous covariates on the analysis set of interest, consistent analysis populations, and joint/correlation structure). PRISMA-NMA update work (Veroniki et al. 2025 scoping/update papers) targets NMA reporting gaps (nodes, consistency, certainty of evidence) and is not a minimum AD covariate package for population adjustment. NICE DSU TSD 18 and EU HTA 2024 quantitative synthesis guidance describe what analysts need for MAIC/STC/ML-NMR but do not create a journal/registry mandate for publishers of comparator AD trials. No 2024–2026 standard was found that benchmarks a minimum reporting set and closes the reporting failure as a solved policy problem. C3 therefore still holds: the constraint remains what journals print. Treat incompletely reported AD as missing data with propagated uncertainty remains a proposed analyst-side response, not a solved standard.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text: EVB-07 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text:
Statement
Every standard network meta-analysis fits the arms a trial ran and says nothing about how the trial came to have those arms, which is a missing-data assumption on the design itself. The assumption differs by likelihood: a contrast-based model requires that design choice not depend on the unobserved contrasts given the observed ones, an arm-based model requires only that it not depend on the unobserved arm outcomes given the observed ones, and the two are not equivalent whenever the underlying risk that drives comparator choice also drives the size of the treatment effect, which is a transitivity violation. Where a sponsor or investigator selects the comparator with an eye to the expected control-arm event rate, network topology carries information about the parameters being estimated and neither assumption holds. No estimator both respects randomization and relaxes the requirement: the model valid under the arm-level assumption removed about half the missing-data bias in one constructed scenario and none in another, while introducing a second bias from compromising the within-trial randomized comparison. The arms a trial did not run are not modeled at all: their sizes, the allocation ratio, and the relation between the design decision and the underlying arm parameters appear in no published network likelihood.

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text:
Why it is open
The counterfactual arms were never run, so the assumption cannot be checked from the data, and the diagnostics a review reports are silent about it: model fit, heterogeneity and inconsistency statistics are unchanged whether design selection is informative or not. Existing missing-not-at-random selection models for meta-analysis are built the wrong way round for this case, since they condition on the sizes of the missing arms being known and posit dependence on the event fraction in the unobserved arm, which cannot be the mechanism because design precedes recruitment. The realistic mechanism connects a decision taken at protocol time to the underlying arm parameters through the investigator’s expectations, so identifying it needs external information about those expectations or a parametric link the network cannot test. The two candidate likelihoods also trade one bias for another: relaxing the missingness assumption by moving to an arm-based model imports between-trial comparisons into a within-trial contrast, so what is gained on selection is spent on confounding.

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




White et al. 2019, Statistics in Medicine
Separates the contrast-level and arm-level missing-at-random assumptions implicit in the two network likelihoods, shows they diverge when the reference-arm outcome is associated with both study design and the treatment contrast, and quantifies how much missing-data bias the arm-based model actually removes.


Rubin 1976, Biometrika
The missing-at-random framework that the assumption on trial design instantiates, and the source of the distinction between ignorable and non-ignorable selection.


Hong et al. 2016, Research Synthesis Methods
Casts arm-based network meta-analysis explicitly as a Bayesian missing-data problem in which unobserved arms are imputed, the framing under which a design-selection model would be written.


Zhang et al. 2014, Clinical Trials
Arm-based network model that reports absolute as well as relative summaries and treats arms absent from a trial as missing data to be recovered from the network.


Dias and Ades 2016, Research Synthesis Methods
Argues that arm-based synthesis breaks randomization and that the contrast-based likelihood is the one preserving it; states the cost side of relaxing the missingness assumption.


Senn et al. 2013, Statistical Methods in Medical Research
Sets out why treating arms as exchangeable across trials is a stronger and different assumption from treating within-trial contrasts as exchangeable, which is the trade governing any arm-based fix.


Piepho, Williams and Madden 2012, Biometrics
Gives the arm-based network model as a two-way linear mixed model, supplying the mixed-model machinery into which a selection component could be inserted.


Mavridis et al. 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Selection model for a full network meta-analysis; models the probability that a study is published rather than the probability that a comparison is designed, and shows what a network-level selection component looks like.


Copas and Shi 2000, Biostatistics
The sensitivity-analysis template for selection in meta-analysis, where a nonidentified selection parameter is varied across a range instead of being estimated; the pattern a design-selection analysis would follow.

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Model the protocol decision rather than the outcome: let the probability that a trial compares treatments j and k, with given arm sizes and allocation ratio, depend on the investigator’s expectation of the control-arm event rate and of the contrast, and write the network likelihood conditional on that design model. Because the mechanism is not identified from the network, treat its parameters as sensitivity parameters with elicited ranges and report each contrast as an interval over them, exactly as publication-bias selection models already do. Establish what is identified under weaker conditions: a network that already fits baseline-risk meta-regression absorbs part of the dependence between design and underlying risk, and the residual sensitivity should be quantified rather than assumed away. Simulate networks in which comparator choice is a function of the expected control-arm rate, crossing the strength of that dependence with network density and the number of trials per edge, and report bias, coverage and rank reversals for contrast-based, arm-based and selection-model fits. Add design provenance to reporting, since whether a comparator was mandated by a regulator, set by local standard of care, or chosen for expected performance is recorded nowhere and would sharply narrow the ranges an elicitation has to span.

title: NMA does not model informative trial-design selection
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single methodological comparison of arm-based and contrast-based network models, and the reviewer accepted it as distinct from analyst-side evidence-set assembly and from selective individual patient data availability. The result that ordinary network likelihoods can be biased under informative design selection is demonstrated in constructed scenarios rather than in an applied network, so the practical magnitude remains unmeasured.

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text: EVB-09 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text:
Statement
Maintenance and randomized-withdrawal trials randomize only patients who responded during an induction run-in, so each reports an effect conditional on its own responder population, defined by its own response criterion, its own assessment time and its own induction blinding. Pooling those arms in a network treats quantities conditioned on different populations as a single estimand, and the resulting comparison is driven by the enrichment rule as much as by the treatment: in one Crohn’s disease network the observed maintenance placebo response rates ran from 9 to 22 percent and remission rates from 10 to 44 percent, and higher placebo rates mechanically produced lower odds ratios. The dependence is systematic rather than incidental. Across 37 inflammatory bowel disease maintenance trials covering 12,075 patients, re-randomized designs gave remission in 41.9 percent on active drug against 20.3 percent on placebo, with a number needed to treat of 5, while treat-through designs gave 30.9 percent against 14.6 percent, with a number needed to treat of 7; the therapeutic gain itself is a function of the randomization structure. No standard method converts these arms to a common estimand from aggregate data. What is in use is an undocumented rescaling of re-randomized maintenance results to a treat-through equivalent through an induction response probability, appearing as one or two sentences in the methods sections of applied network meta-analyses with no derivation, no stated assumptions and no validation; the fuller version needs individual patient data from one trial to supply induction-to-maintenance transition probabilities stratified by depth of response, which are then assumed to transport unchanged to every other trial’s induction population.

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text:
Why it is open
The conditioning is a property of the design rather than of the reported numbers, so nothing published can undo it: converting a responder-randomized contrast to an all-randomized one requires the joint distribution of induction response and subsequent maintenance outcome, and trials publish only the marginal maintenance result within the enriched subgroup. The transition probabilities that would supply that joint distribution are estimable only from individual patient data, which in practice means only one trial’s sponsor can run the conversion, and once run they are assumed to transport to every other trial’s induction population with no way to check. Enrichment rules differ across trials in criterion, threshold and timing, so there is not one conversion but a family of them, each carrying its own untestable transport assumption. The canonical guidance is silent as well: the Cochrane Handbook chapter on variants of randomized trials covers cluster, cross-over, stepped-wedge and factorial designs and does not address randomized-withdrawal or responder-enriched designs, so a reviewer has no authoritative recommendation and pooling as though the conditioning did not exist remains the default.

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Varu et al. 2019, Current Medical Research and Opinion
Treatment sequence network meta-analysis in Crohn’s disease, presented as a methodological case study that is explicitly novel and unvalidated; its central input, maintenance placebo response conditional on remitter versus responder-non-remitter status at the end of induction, is estimable only from individual patient data.


Barberio et al. 2024, Digestive and Liver Disease
Meta-analysis of 37 inflammatory bowel disease maintenance trials showing that remission rates and therapeutic gain over placebo differ systematically between re-randomizing and treat-through designs; the empirical demonstration that the design and not just the drug drives the pooled contrast.


Barberio et al. 2025, Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics
Runs separate maintenance networks for re-randomizing and for treat-through trials rather than pooling them, and finds the rankings differ; the conservative alternative to conversion, at the cost of two answers to one question.


Jairath et al. 2016, Journal of Crohn’s and Colitis
Systematic review and meta-analysis of placebo rates in induction and maintenance trials of ulcerative colitis, quantifying how far the maintenance placebo rate depends on trial characteristics rather than on the disease.


Jairath et al. 2017, Alimentary Pharmacology and Therapeutics
The Crohn’s disease counterpart, establishing the same dependence of placebo rates on design and eligibility features across induction and maintenance phases.


Welty et al. 2020, Current Medical Research and Opinion
Applied network meta-analysis that recalculates maintenance data from re-randomized response designs to correspond to treat-through arms; the conversion appears as a methods-section statement with no derivation.


Disher et al. 2025, Advances in Therapy
Normalizes re-randomized trials to mimic a standard treat-through design inside an applied network, showing the same undocumented conversion is now routine in submissions.


Jairath et al. 2025, Journal of Comparative Effectiveness Research
Runs the conversion in the opposite direction, adjusting treat-through outcomes to align with responder re-randomized outcomes; the two directions have not been reconciled or compared.


Katz 2009, Clinical Journal of Pain
Reference treatment of enriched enrollment randomized withdrawal methodology and its interpretive limits, establishing that the estimand of such a trial is defined by the enrichment step.


Remiro-Azocar and Gorst-Rasmussen 2024, Research Synthesis Methods
Argues for importing estimand discipline into evidence synthesis; the framework in which a common target for enriched and parallel designs would have to be stated before any conversion is attempted.


ICH E9(R1) 2019, Addendum on Estimands and Sensitivity Analysis in Clinical Trials
Defines the population attribute of an estimand, which is precisely the attribute an enrichment rule changes; supplies the vocabulary but not the cross-trial reconstruction.

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Fix the target before the arithmetic: state whether the decision needs the effect among all patients starting induction or among induction responders, then express each trial’s reported contrast as a functional of the same underlying quantities so that any conversion is a derivation rather than a rescaling. Establish what is identified from aggregate data alone; with the induction response rate, maintenance arm sizes and maintenance rates published, the treat-through contrast is bounded by the range of possible dependence between induction response and maintenance outcome, and those bounds should be reported instead of a point estimate that silently assumes independence. Where individual data exist for one trial, estimate the transition probabilities from them and then test transport rather than assume it, by refitting with each candidate donor trial in turn and reporting the spread across donors. Simulate a network mixing treat-through and re-randomized trials whose enrichment rules differ in threshold and timing, and report bias, coverage and rank reversals for naive pooling, design-stratified networks and reconstruction. Standardize what a maintenance trial must report for any of this to be possible: the induction response definition, the assessment time, the induction response rate, and the maintenance outcome stratified by depth of induction response.

title: No common estimand or aggregate-data reconstruction for enriched and withdrawal trials
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from a single methodological case study whose approach is presented as novel and unvalidated, and the reviewer accepted it as more specific than the general estimand-mismatch entry EVB-03. Independent evidence beyond that paper supports it: a meta-analysis of 37 inflammatory bowel disease maintenance trials shows therapeutic gain differs by randomization structure, and the treat-through conversion now used in applied networks exists only as undocumented methods-section statements.

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text: EVB-11 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text:
Statement
Instruments for risk of bias due to missing evidence work by weighting per-comparison judgments about unreported and unpublished studies through the contribution each direct comparison makes to a network estimate. That machinery presupposes a connected network: contribution is defined by evidence flow along observed edges, and opposing biases can be argued to offset around a loop. Where the estimate of interest is a cross-gap contrast supplied by a bridge, there is no contribution path and no loop, so no existing tool assigns it a judgment; the one instrument built for networks states that it is not applicable when an intervention is disconnected and recommends appraising each subnetwork separately, which produces judgments for contrasts nobody needed and none for the contrast the analysis exists to produce. Nothing states how selective non-reporting inside a subnetwork propagates into a shared component effect, a shared baseline model, a class mean or a dose-response curve, nor in which direction it moves the bridged contrast. The propagation is not a routine extension of the connected case: a bridge parameter is estimated from the studies present in each subnetwork, so a subnetwork whose small unfavorable trials went unpublished contributes a biased bridge, and no second path exists through which the distortion could be detected or offset.

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text:
Why it is open
Contribution-based appraisal is defined on evidence flow through observed edges, and a disconnection is precisely the absence of such edges, so the weighting step has nothing to weight; a judgment for a bridged contrast has to be built on a different object, namely the bridge parameter, and nobody has defined the analogue of a contribution matrix on it. The direction of the distortion is bridge-specific rather than generic: unpublished small unfavorable trials shift a class mean, an additive component effect and a dose-response slope in different ways, so one general rule cannot be written and each family needs its own derivation. There is also no observable check, because the diagnostic that catches reporting bias in a connected network is the disagreement between two paths, and a disconnected network has one path by construction. And the appraisal instruments in use were designed around the study as the unit contributing to a synthesized comparison, so extending them requires changing what the unit of judgment is, not adding a signaling question.

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Chiocchia et al. 2021, BMC Medicine
ROB-MEN, the only tool giving per-comparison risk-of-bias judgments for missing evidence in a network; states explicitly that it is not applicable when an intervention of interest is disconnected and recommends evaluating each subnetwork separately.


Page et al. 2023, BMJ
ROB-ME, the pairwise instrument ROB-MEN adapts, framed around studies that are missing from a synthesis of a single comparison; it inherits the same assumption that the estimate of interest has contributing studies.


Nikolakopoulou et al. 2020, PLOS Medicine
CINeMA grades confidence in each network comparison across domains including reporting bias, using contributions from direct comparisons; it has no items for a bridge across a disconnection.


Papakonstantinou et al. 2018, F1000Research
Defines the contribution of each study and each direct comparison to a network estimate through paths, flows and streams; the machinery that has no value to assign when the contrast has no path.


Mavridis et al. 2014, Statistics in Medicine
Selection model for a full network meta-analysis that could in principle propagate selective publication into any shared parameter, but has been formulated and applied only for connected networks and ordinary treatment effects.


Goring et al. 2016, Research Synthesis Methods
Sets out the analytic options for treatment networks having no common comparator, defining the class of bridged analyses for which no missing-evidence appraisal exists.


Beliveau et al. 2017, Research Synthesis Methods
Evaluates random baseline treatment effects as a way of joining disconnected networks and shows how strongly the cross-gap contrast depends on the studies supplying the baseline model in each subnetwork.


Pedder et al. 2021, Medical Decision Making
Links disconnected networks through dose-response model-based network meta-analysis; a concrete bridge whose parameter is estimated from whichever dose arms happen to have been published in each subnetwork.


Page et al. 2021, Research Synthesis Methods
Review of publication and other reporting biases in meta-analysis, summarizing what detection and adjustment methods exist and how little is known about their behavior.

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Move the unit of judgment from the contrast to the bridge parameter: for each bridge family, state which studies in each subnetwork identify that parameter, then define the analogue of a contribution matrix on it so that per-study missing-evidence judgments can be weighted into a judgment about the bridge. Derive the sign of the distortion for the common families, since selective non-publication of small unfavorable trials moves a class mean, an additive component effect, a baseline model and a dose-response slope in directions that are predictable from the family’s algebra rather than arbitrary. Add bridge-specific signaling items to the existing instruments: whether the bridge parameter is identified in both subnetworks, how many studies in each supply it, and whether the two subnetworks differ in evidence completeness, since asymmetric completeness is what makes the distortion one-sided. Feed the resulting bias into the drift machinery already used for bridge uncertainty, so a reported interval carries reporting-bias-induced drift alongside structural drift rather than treating them as separate reports. Validate on connected networks analyzed as if disconnected, where the bridged and the observed contrasts can both be computed and the missing-evidence judgment can be scored against the discrepancy it was supposed to predict.

title: No missing-evidence appraisal for bridged cross-gap contrasts
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. One reader proposed this from the single instrument paper whose authors state that disconnected interventions were out of scope, and the reviewer accepted it on the grounds that appraising subnetworks separately does not appraise the bridged estimand. Resting on one instrument paper plus the disconnected-network literature, the gap is documented by explicit scope exclusion rather than by a demonstration that a bridge-level appraisal would be hard to build.

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text: EVB-13 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text:
Statement
A platform trial is a sequence of fixed designs, and only arms open for randomization in the same stage are concurrently randomized; a contrast assembled across stages is confounded with calendar time and with every design feature that changed between stages. Trials of this kind normally enter a systematic review or network meta-analysis as one trial-level effect per comparison, so a reviewer cannot tell which stages contributed or what share of the reported effect came from non-concurrent controls. Part of the necessary reporting already exists: item 14a of the Adaptive designs CONSORT Extension asks for the exact recruitment and follow-up dates of each treatment group and for a statement of whether all groups were recruited concurrently, with STAMPEDE as its worked exemplar. What no standard requires is the numbers, namely stage-specific treatment effects and their standard errors for each randomized comparison within each fixed design, which is what a reviewer needs to rebuild the within-trial network, reproduce the direct-evidence proportion, and test the trial’s own direct evidence against its own indirect evidence. No review-side standard requires concurrency to be recorded either: PRISMA-NMA adds items on network geometry but none on whether a contributing trial’s contrast was concurrently randomized. The stakes are measurable: in a network analysis of one STAMPEDE comparison the concurrent and non-concurrent evidence disagreed, with the test of inconsistency at p = 0.017, so a review that pooled them would have combined incompatible information without being able to notice.

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text:
Why it is open
The stage decomposition exists only inside the trial team’s own data, and the decision that destroys it is made at write-up, before any reviewer is involved and before any synthesis model is specified, so nothing fitted later can price what the report did not carry. Reporting guidance for adaptive trials is organized around making the adaptation transparent rather than around making the trial decomposable into concurrently randomized comparisons, which is why the recruitment dates are required and the stage-specific estimates are not. The analysis side moved first: network and time-adjustment methods for non-concurrent controls are published and implemented, so the obstacle is missing inputs rather than a missing model. Reconstructing individual data from published Kaplan-Meier plots recovers part of the information for time-to-event endpoints only, and it injects reconstruction error that then travels through the network unlabeled. Nobody has counted how many platform and multi-arm multi-stage trials now sit inside published networks, or how much of their contributed evidence is non-concurrent, so the size of the exposure is unmeasured and the case for a new item rests on a single demonstration.

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Marschner and Schou 2022, Clinical Trials
Embeds stratified and time-adjusted analyses of a platform trial in a common network framework, shows that unadjusted analysis is biased under time trends in risk, and applies it to a STAMPEDE comparison where direct randomized and indirect non-concurrent evidence conflict at p = 0.017; recommends that platform trials report stage-specific treatment effects for use in later reviews and re-analyses.


Dimairo et al. 2020, BMJ (Adaptive designs CONSORT Extension)
Reporting checklist for adaptive trials whose item 14a requires exact recruitment and follow-up dates for each treatment group and an explicit statement of whether all groups were recruited concurrently, illustrated with STAMPEDE; item 17c requires interim results used for adaptation decisions. This supplies the concurrency timeline but not stage-specific effect estimates per fixed design.


Lee and Wason 2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Quantifies the precision gained and the bias risked by including non-concurrent control patients in platform-trial analysis; establishes that concurrency is a quantitative property of a comparison rather than a formality.


Bofill Roig et al. 2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology
Model-based time-trend adjustments for platform trials with non-concurrent controls; shows the analysis machinery for using non-concurrent evidence exists, which is why the missing input rather than the missing method is the binding constraint.


Sydes et al. 2012, Trials
Describes the STAMPEDE multi-arm multi-stage design with arms stopped for lack of benefit and research arms added mid-trial; the concrete stage structure that a downstream network needs and that a single aggregate effect per comparison hides.


Hutton et al. 2015, Annals of Internal Medicine (PRISMA-NMA)
The review-side reporting standard for network meta-analysis, adding items on network geometry and on the summary of the network; carries no item asking whether a contributing trial’s contrast was concurrently randomized.


Thorlund, Druyts, Toor, Jansen and Mills 2014, Clinical Epidemiology
Converts a re-randomization trial into parallel-design form so it can populate a network, imputing the arm-level quantities the publication did not report; a worked instance of the general pattern in which non-standard designs enter networks only after reviewer-side reconstruction.

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write the missing item and attach it to the extension that already carries the concurrency dates rather than founding a new standard: a table of stage-specific treatment effects with standard errors for every randomized comparison within each fixed design, plus the stage membership and randomization probabilities of each arm, which is enough to rebuild the within-trial network and has already been illustrated in the platform-trial network literature. Add the mirror item on the review side, so that a network meta-analysis must state per contributing trial which contrasts were concurrently randomized and must report the network with and without the non-concurrent evidence. Quantify the exposure first, because it is the cheapest step and it decides how hard to push: audit published networks in oncology and critical care for platform and multi-arm multi-stage trials, and record how often the stage structure is recoverable from the trial report alone. Where it is not recoverable, compare the network built from digitized survival curves against the one built from the published aggregate effect, so that the error the missing item creates is measured rather than assumed.

title: Platform trials lack stage-level reporting for network synthesis
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. One reader proposed this and the reviewer accepted it as a within-platform reporting problem distinct from covariate reporting, estimand mismatch and external-control bridging, on the ground that it concerns the stage structure needed to classify direct evidence at all. It is partially addressed because the adaptive-design reporting extension already mandates per-group recruitment and follow-up dates and an explicit concurrency statement; what no standard requires, and what the single methods paper behind this entry recommends, is the stage-specific effect estimates, and no review-side standard requires concurrency to be recorded.

title: Selective non-publication of commissioned indirect comparisons is unmeasured
text: EVB-15 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Selective non-publication of commissioned indirect comparisons is unmeasured
text:
Statement
Publication bias in evidence synthesis is handled at the level of the primary trial, through funnel plots, comparison-adjusted funnel plots, selection models fitted inside a network and structured appraisal of missing evidence. Nothing operates at the level of the synthesis itself. A survey of the contracting firms that build indirect comparisons for industry found that 19 responding companies had conducted 476 network meta-analyses of which 102 were published, that sponsor refusal was the most common specified reason for having no plan to publish among the 129 unpublished analyses whose reasons were given, that 13 of those had been used in health technology assessment submissions rather than published, and that a protocol was publicly available for 11 of 162 published company-affiliated network meta-analyses. The denominator is therefore unobservable: nobody knows how many indirect comparisons were run on a given treatment, on which outcomes, or in which direction the withheld ones pointed. No registration requirement, agency disclosure rule or bounding method exists at this level, so an evidence map, a meta-research study or a decision that treats published network meta-analyses as an unbiased sample of the network meta-analyses performed cannot check that assumption or quantify its failure. The two conventional remedies both act on trials: funnel-plot asymmetry reads the studies inside a synthesis, and trial registries record trials rather than syntheses.

title: Selective non-publication of commissioned indirect comparisons is unmeasured
text:
Why it is open
The suppressed object is an analysis rather than a trial, so it leaves no trace in any register that exists: review registration is voluntary and, on the measured evidence, a publicly available protocol exists for only a small minority of published company-affiliated analyses, and no regulator or reimbursement agency publishes an inventory of the indirect comparisons submitted to it. Every trial-level detection method reads a pattern among the studies within one synthesis, so none can see a synthesis that was never written up; there is no analogue of small-study asymmetry at the level of a corpus of analyses. Whether the non-publication decision followed the results is unknown even in the one survey that measured the rate, because the firms responsible for two-thirds of the conducted analyses gave no reasons, so the selection mechanism cannot be characterized let alone modeled. A bound would need an assumption about how the withheld analyses differ from the published ones, and there is no dataset in which both are observed against which to calibrate that assumption. The parties who could make the denominator observable are the sponsors and the agencies, so the fix is a governance action rather than a statistical one, and no methods group has an incentive to own it.

title: Selective non-publication of commissioned indirect comparisons is unmeasured
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Schuit and Ioannidis 2016, Systematic Reviews
The only measurement of the phenomenon: 162 of 822 network meta-analysis papers had contracting-company authors, 93 firms were contacted and 37 responded, 19 disclosed 476 conducted analyses of which 102 were published, sponsor refusal was the leading specified reason for having no plan to publish, and a public protocol existed for 11 of 162 published company-affiliated analyses.


Lundh, Lexchin, Mintzes, Schroll and Bero 2017, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews
Establishes at trial level that industry sponsorship is associated with results and conclusions favoring the sponsor; supplies the direction of the mechanism that is assumed, but not shown, to operate one level up at the synthesis.


Page, Sterne, Higgins and Egger 2021, Research Synthesis Methods
Review of methods for investigating and dealing with publication and reporting biases in meta-analysis; maps the state of the art and shows that every method in it takes the studies within a synthesis as its unit.


Page, Sterne, Boutron et al. 2023, BMJ (ROB-ME)
Structured tool for judging risk of bias due to missing evidence in a meta-analysis; the closest existing instrument, again aimed at missing studies rather than missing syntheses.


Chaimani and Salanti 2012, Research Synthesis Methods
Comparison-adjusted funnel plot, the network-level detection tool; requires the studies inside the network and therefore cannot register a network that was never published.


Mavridis, Welton, Sutton and Salanti 2014, Statistics in Medicine
A selection model fitted inside a network; shows what the correction machinery looks like when the selection unit is the trial, and therefore what would have to be re-derived if the selection unit were the analysis.


Hutton et al. 2015, Annals of Internal Medicine (PRISMA-NMA)
Requires a published network meta-analysis to report its registration and protocol; the natural hook for a registration requirement, but it binds only analyses that reach publication and places no obligation on commissioned analyses that do not.

title: Selective non-publication of commissioned indirect comparisons is unmeasured
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Make the denominator observable before trying to model it. The cheapest route is agency-side, since reimbursement bodies already receive indirect comparisons in submissions: publishing the inventory of analyses submitted, including those withdrawn or superseded, would convert an unknown denominator into a measured one for exactly the decisions that matter most. The second route is a registration requirement for commissioned syntheses with the status trial registration has, recorded before the analysis is run and naming the treatments, outcomes and comparators. Failing both, derive a sensitivity bound: treat publication of the synthesis as a selection event, parameterize it by the probability that an analysis of a given direction and magnitude is published, and report how far the published corpus in a therapy area can be displaced across a plausible range of that parameter, calibrating the range against the one measured publication fraction rather than assuming it. A companion empirical study should compare estimates in published company-affiliated network meta-analyses against those in the corresponding health technology assessment submissions, which is the only setting where the same analysis is sometimes visible in both states.
