text: SFW-10 Partially addressed Very high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Statement
maicplus 0.1.2 still needs a joint sandwich estimator covering the outcome and weight-estimation equations (#111), parallel bootstrap (#148), explicit estimand metadata and ATT reporting (#142), alternative weight scaling (#178), reporting expansion (#154) and principled trimming or truncation that discloses the lost calibration and changed target (#141). Several disclosures the source asked for already exist in the release: the bootstrap re-estimates weights inside each IPD resample, the anchored path perturbs the published comparator effect by its standard error, scaled and unscaled weights are exposed, the survival effect is labeled as a hazard ratio, and the unanchored bootstrap documents that it assumes no uncertainty in the comparator trial population. The claim about propagating aggregate-data uncertainty in the bootstrap has no matching open issue, the nearest being #143 on pinning down the anchored bootstrap, although target covariate summaries do remain fixed. Treating estimated weights as fixed also does not invariably understate variance, and simple trimming changes calibration and the effective target without producing a clean ATT estimand.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Why it is open
MAIC weights are estimated, so a variance that ignores the weight-estimation step is wrong in a direction that depends on the design rather than always downward, and no released estimator stacks the outcome and weighting estimating equations even though the comparative evidence on which variance families behave well is published. Trimming or truncating weights changes the calibration and the population actually being estimated, and no agreed rule exists to implement, so an actively maintained package has nothing to adopt. Whether the published target summaries should carry uncertainty depends on the inferential framework, and the package conditions on them without saying that this is a choice. The remaining disclosure gaps are structural rather than technical: defaults produce valid-looking output, so an omitted estimand declaration is invisible downstream, which is how such errors reach submissions.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




maicplus 0.1.2 (CRAN, published 21 Feb 2025)
implements MAIC weighting, variance and reporting utilities whose open issues include weight-estimation-aware variance, trimming and estimand metadata; the report proposes it should evolve into a reference implementation


hta-pharma/maicplus (GitHub)
maintained open MAIC workflow repository, successor to older Roche MAIC tooling; open issues verified in the audit are #111 sandwich estimator for derived weights, #141 trimming and truncation, #142 ATT reporting, #148 parallel bootstrap, #178 alternative weight scaling, #154 reporting functions and #143 on pinning down the anchored bootstrap


maicplus 0.1.2 bootstrap and reporting implementation, hta-pharma/maicplus@aabcaf8
shows the bootstrap re-estimates weights within each IPD resample rather than treating them as fixed, the anchored path perturbs the published comparator effect by its standard error, scaled and unscaled weights are exposed, and the unanchored bootstrap documents its assumption of no uncertainty in the comparator trial population


Chandler and Proskorovsky 2024, Uncertain about uncertainty in matching-adjusted indirect comparisons? A simulation study to compare methods for variance estimation, Res Synth Methods 15(6):1094-1110
compares conventional raw-weight, ESS-rescaled, sandwich and bootstrap variance estimators across 108 scenarios and finds sandwich estimators downward-biased at small ESS with finite-sample adjustment markedly improving them; concrete guidance the variance work can be calibrated against


Remiro-Azocar 2022 (two-stage MAIC)
quantifies the trade-off from weight truncation, finding substantial precision and efficiency gains but considerable induced bias, and states that truncation shifts the target population or estimand definition; the evidence a trimming implementation should surface


Jiang et al. 2025 (the MAIC paradox)
shows with synthetic data that different entities can reach opposing conclusions from the same data when the target population is not clearly defined, sourcing the estimand-disclosure argument this entry makes


Ishak et al. 2025, A Framework for Reliable, Transparent, and Reproducible Population-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons, PharmacoEconomics
published PAIC reporting and risk-of-bias framework whose elements a reference MAIC workflow can implement structurally instead of designing disclosure requirements from scratch

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Implement the joint sandwich estimator over the outcome and weight-estimation equations, calibrated against the published comparison of variance families rather than derived in isolation, and add parallel bootstrap so the recommended sensitivity analyses fit submission timelines. Add trimming and truncation that report the calibration lost and the target actually estimated, using the published quantification of the bias and precision trade-off as the default warning. Attach explicit estimand metadata to the fitted object and expand reporting against the existing PAIC reporting framework (Ishak et al., doi:10.1007/s40273-025-01503-1) so the estimand, weight construction, variance method, any trimming-induced change of target and the survival effect measure are structurally disclosed. Decide separately whether target-summary uncertainty is propagated, and state which inferential framework the package assumes.

title: maicplus variance, trimming and estimand disclosure gaps
text:
Our study

Stacking the weighting step into the MAIC sandwich makes intervals narrower, not better
The question put to it. Does a stacked sandwich that accounts for weight estimation give better MAIC intervals than the fixed-weight sandwich or the ESS-based conventional variance, and what population does a trimmed MAIC actually estimate?
What it found. No. Stacking lowered the standard error in every untrimmed scenario (by up to 11%), because estimating calibration weights removes outcome variation the covariates explain; where MAIC intervals already undercover, at poor overlap, that made them worse (coverage down to 0.844). The fixed-weight sandwich was in band in 24 of 30 scenarios, the ESS-based variance in 18 and the stacked sandwich in 17, so current guidance stands. Trimming moved the estimand by up to 0.19 on the log odds ratio scale.
Results.

Stacked over fixed-weight SE: 0.887 to 0.993, below 1 beyond Monte Carlo error in all 30 untrimmed scenarios; DESIGN.md’s prediction of both signs fails.
Coverage: fixed-weight 0.893 to 0.960; ESS-based 0.885 to 0.980; stacked 0.844 to 0.953; stacked with n/(n-k) 0.847 to 0.953.
Every estimator loses coverage as ESS falls; the stacked sandwich fastest.
Trimming at the 95th percentile moved the estimand by up to 0.19; in 72% of trimmed scenarios the estimate was closer to the population the capped weights induce than to the declared target.

Design.

Estimand

Target-population marginal log odds ratio, A versus C; for trimmed analyses also the effect in the population the capped weights induce

Methods compared

fixed-weight sandwich, ESS-based conventional variance, stacked sandwich, stacked sandwich with n/(n-k)

Data-generating mechanism

Binary-outcome MAIC with three covariates, 90 scenarios crossing target shift, event risk, effect modification and its alignment, and weight trimming; four variance estimators; trimmed analyses scored against the declared target and the induced population.

Replicates

1000 per scenario, 90,000 in total


What this does not answer. No bootstrap and one sample size, so where stacking’s asymptotic advantage appears is not located. Binary outcome, three covariates, MAIC on means. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text: SFW-12 Confirmed open High priority Promising Implementation-specific

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Statement
outstandR reached CRAN as version 2.0.0 on 10 June 2026, titled Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data (Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar), implementing the parametric G-computation approach of Remiro-Azocar, Heath and Baio (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565). Its CRAN description is framed entirely around the two-trial limited-IPD problem with no mention of networks, so the pairwise focus holds, and no published validation covers its behavior in networks or across disconnected evidence. Dependence on the target covariate distribution is partly definitional rather than a defect, since standardization is defined relative to a declared target, and the package ships custom-copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes that acknowledge the sensitivity rather than hiding it. Dependence on the outcome model is a genuine robustness concern, and any disconnected-network use would additionally require structural bridge assumptions that standardization cannot identify.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Why it is open
Outcome standardization was developed for the two-trial indirect comparison, so extending it to a network requires deciding how standardized arm-level quantities from different studies combine while preserving within-study randomization, which is not a mechanical generalization. Reconstructing the target covariate distribution from limited published moments makes the result sensitive to the reconstruction, which the copula vignette exposes but cannot resolve. Nothing published characterizes the package’s behavior in networks or across disconnected evidence, and in the disconnected case standardization would need a bridge assumption it cannot identify from the data. The 2.0.0 separation of outcome model from balance model prepares the way for doubly robust variants that are not there yet.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation

What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




outstandR (project site)
computes compatible marginal effects by model-based standardization and covariate simulation as an alternative to conventional STC; documentation site including the custom-copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes


outstandR 2.0.0 (CRAN, published 10 Jun 2026; Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar)
released package titled Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data, framed around the two-trial limited-IPD problem; its 2.0.0 release notes separate outcome_model from balance_model to accommodate forthcoming doubly robust methods


Remiro-Azocar, Heath and Baio 2022, Parametric G-computation for compatible indirect treatment comparisons with limited individual patient data, Research Synthesis Methods
standardizes a GLM or Cox outcome model over the target covariate distribution to recover a marginal effect compatible with the aggregate-data trial; the method outstandR implements

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Characterize rather than rebuild: run outstandR against alternative reconstructions of the target distribution and alternative outcome models to map where the estimate moves, using the copula machinery the package already exposes. Extend the standardization from the pairwise case to networks by specifying how standardized arm-level quantities combine while preserving within-study randomization, and state explicitly which bridge assumption any disconnected-network extension would rely on. Use the 2.0.0 outcome-model and balance-model split as the hook for doubly robust variants, and publish the network validation that does not currently exist.

title: outstandR is pairwise only with no network or disconnected validation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “outstandR is pairwise only and sensitive to the simulated target” The title treats sensitivity to the target distribution as a defect, but the audit found it partly definitional and found shipped vignettes that acknowledge it.
The source said. “outstandR is an active outcome-standardization package producing compatible marginal effects through model-based standardization and covariate simulation, and a useful alternative to conventional STC, but it is focused on pairwise comparisons, is sensitive to the target distribution and outcome model, and needs broader network and disconnected-network validation.”
What was wrong with it. The source cited only the pkgdown site; the literature auditor found outstandR is now on CRAN at version 2.0.0 (10 June 2026) with the underlying method published (doi:10.1002/jrsm.1565), and that the package already ships copula and diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignettes addressing the target-distribution sensitivity the entry treats as unexamined. GPT-5.6 Sol added that sensitivity to the target distribution is partly definitional and that disconnected-network use would need bridge assumptions standardization cannot supply, making this a roadmap limitation rather than a defect in pairwise use.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The characterisation is accurate but the citation is stale. outstandR is no longer only a pkgdown site: version 2.0.0 is on CRAN, published 2026-06-10, titled ‘Model-Based Standardisation for Indirect Treatment Comparison with Limited Subject-Level Data’, authored by Green, Gao and Remiro-Azocar and built on the parametric G-computation paper (doi 10.1002/jrsm.1565). The CRAN description is framed entirely around the two-trial limited-IPD problem with no mention of networks, which supports ‘focused on pairwise comparisons’. Sensitivity to the reconstructed target is real enough that the package ships a custom-copula vignette and a diagnostics-and-uncertainty vignette, so the package acknowledges rather than hides it. The 2.0.0 NEWS separates outcome_model from balance_model explicitly to ‘future-proof the package for upcoming doubly-robust methods’. I found no published validation of outstandR in networks or disconnected evidence, so that claim stands, though absence of validation is not something I can positively verify.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Standardizing arm-specific outcome predictions over the same target joint covariate distribution yields compatible marginal effects and is technically preferable to conventional mean-covariate STC for nonlinear or non-collapsible models. Pairwise focus and broader network validation are reasonable open scope questions. Dependence on the target population is partly definitional rather than a defect, while dependence on the outcome model is a genuine robustness concern. Disconnected-network use would additionally require structural bridge assumptions that standardization cannot identify. This is a roadmap-level limitation for network use, not a critical defect for an explicitly pairwise analysis. No local outstandR source was available for code-level confirmation of package capabilities.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text: SFW-14 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Implementation-specific

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Statement
drMAIC 0.1.0 appeared on CRAN on 29 March 2026 as Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA, sole author Anupama Singh, implementing entropy balancing with augmented, doubly robust MAIC, diagnostics and bootstrap confidence intervals for binary and time-to-event outcomes, with one vignette and a single test file; its repository was created on 23 March 2026 and last pushed the next day. No accompanying methods publication and no independent evaluation were found, so treating it as a reference implementation is premature. What such an audit can settle needs separating from what it cannot: double robustness is an analytical property holding under identification, positivity, regularity and correct specification of at least one nuisance model, so simulation tests the implementation and its finite-sample behavior rather than the theorem. Augmented weighting for PAIC is also not new with drMAIC, since Gao, Heath and Baio (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10021) published G-MAIC, which combines outcome regression with weighting adjustment and was evaluated across 18 scenarios against MAIC and parametric G-computation.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Why it is open
A doubly robust weighting package makes a claim about behavior under misspecification that a user cannot check from their own data, so only review of the estimating equations plus finite-sample simulation can show whether the implementation delivers what the theory promises. Simulation evidence shipped with a method is generated under that method’s own assumptions, and here there is no shipped simulation and no methods paper at all, only one vignette and one test file. The field has no neutral benchmark suite, so a new package’s operating characteristics cannot be checked by anyone except its author. A CRAN release confers apparent legitimacy in HTA submissions faster than independent evaluation can be produced, so the validation gap widens with each new package.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




drMAIC 0.1.0 (CRAN, published 29 Mar 2026; Anupama Singh)
implements entropy balancing with standard and augmented, doubly robust MAIC, diagnostics, sensitivity tools and bootstrap confidence intervals for binary and time-to-event outcomes; one vignette, a single test file, and no accompanying methods publication found


Gao, Heath and Baio 2025, Regression augmented weighting adjustment for indirect comparisons in health decision modelling (G-MAIC)
combines outcome regression with weighting adjustment and uses a Bayesian bootstrap to propagate the uncertainty of population-adjusted estimates, evaluated against non-adjusted methods, MAIC and parametric G-computation across 18 scenarios; the published comparator any drMAIC benchmark should include

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Subject drMAIC to independent review of its code and estimating equations, then to finite-sample comparison under one nuisance model correct, both models wrong and weak overlap, reporting failed fits rather than only successful ones. Include the published comparators, G-MAIC and parametric G-computation, so the exercise places drMAIC against methods that already carry simulation evidence. Keep the claims separated in reporting: the double-robustness property needs a proof under stated identification and regularity conditions, while omitted-modifier scenarios test violation of exchangeability and belong in a sensitivity analysis. Component drift belongs only in a component-PAIC extension, not in this package’s benchmark.

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Our study

drMAIC 0.1.0 returns the MAIC estimate as its doubly robust estimate, with an interval six times too narrow
The question put to it. Does drMAIC 0.1.0 implement a doubly robust MAIC with valid intervals: is its augmented estimate robust to a wrong weighting model when the outcome model is right, and do its intervals cover?
What it found. No. drMAIC 0.1.0 averages the outcome model over the individual-data patients instead of the target population, so its doubly robust estimate equals its MAIC estimate in every replicate (difference below 2e-15) and keeps MAIC’s bias when the weights are wrong and the outcome model right (0.066 against 0.004 for correct augmentation). Its analytic SE divides by n twice and mixes probability and log odds scales: 0.028 against an empirical SD of 0.17 to 0.22, coverage 0.20 to 0.26. Its percentile bootstrap covers 0.78 to 0.79.
Results.

Defect 1: theta_stc = sum(w_norm * m_hat), so the augmented estimate reduces algebraically to the weighted mean of Y.
Defect 2 and 3: .dr_variance returns sum((w_norm*(Y-theta))^2)/n on the probability scale and it is reported as the SE of a log odds ratio.
Defect 4: bootstrap_ci() reweights on means only, refits the default outcome formula and holds the comparator fixed.
Wrong weights, right outcome model, target mean 0.5: drMAIC DR bias 0.066 (MCSE 0.007); correct augmentation 0.004; correct augmentation coverage 0.93 to 0.96 across cells.

Design.

Estimand

Target-population marginal log odds ratio, A versus B

Methods compared

drMAIC MAIC, drMAIC doubly robust with analytic interval, drMAIC percentile bootstrap, correctly augmented weighting with bootstrap SE

Data-generating mechanism

Unanchored binary-outcome transport in a 2 x 2 of correct or wrong weighting and outcome models at two overlap levels; drMAIC’s MAIC, DR estimate, analytic interval and bootstrap interval against a correctly augmented estimator. 8 cells, 600 replicates each, plus a bootstrap arm.

Replicates

600 per cell, 8 cells; package bootstrap 150 per cell in 2 cells


What this does not answer. One package version, binary outcome, one sample size; G-MAIC not run; the time-to-event path (a weighted median labeled a hazard ratio) read from code, not simulated. Peer review has not been done.
Peer review. Not yet done. The result stands on the study alone until it is.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument · Code and data: studies/SFW-14-testing-an-implementation-not-a-theorem · Protocol: registered before the run

title: drMAIC has no methods paper and no independent evaluation
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source titled this. “drMAIC’s doubly robust claims lack independent adversarial audit” The title demands an adversarial audit of the double-robustness claim, a standard the audit rejected since simulation tests the implementation rather than the theorem.
The source said. “drMAIC appeared on CRAN in March 2026 as an early implementation of standard and augmented, doubly robust MAIC with diagnostics and sensitivity tools. The report holds that its methodological and software claims require independent audit, adversarial simulation and head-to-head comparison with established transport estimators before it is treated as a reference implementation, because package availability is evidence of implementation and not of methodological superiority.”
What was wrong with it. GPT-5.6 Sol judged the proposed proof standard wrong: adversarial simulation checks implementation and operating characteristics but cannot establish or refute the double-robustness theorem, both nuisance models being wrong is an expected failure condition rather than a test of the property, an omitted modifier violates exchangeability rather than misspecifying a nuisance model, and component drift is irrelevant unless drMAIC is extended to component models. The literature auditor added that augmented weighting for PAIC already has a published comparator, G-MAIC (doi:10.1017/rsm.2025.10021), which any benchmark should include.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. CRAN confirms drMAIC 0.1.0 published 2026-03-29, ‘Doubly Robust Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison for HTA’, sole author Anupama Singh, entropy balancing plus augmented/DR MAIC with diagnostics, bootstrap CIs, binary and time-to-event outcomes, one vignette. Source line 1044 matches the entry’s wording verbatim. The repository corroborates the immaturity concern harder than the entry does: created 2026-03-23, last pushed 2026-03-24, two stars, and tests/testthat contains a single file, test_core.R. I found no accompanying methods publication and no independent evaluation, though per calibration an absence I found by searching is not proof. One correction of emphasis: augmented weighting for PAIC is not new with drMAIC. Gao, Heath and Baio (2025) published G-MAIC, combining outcome regression with weighting and evaluated over 18 scenarios against MAIC and parametric G-computation, so the benchmark the entry asks for has a published comparator to include.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Independent implementation audit and finite-sample benchmarking are prudent before treating drMAIC as a reference implementation. The report’s proof standard is nevertheless wrong: double robustness is an analytical property under identification, consistency, positivity, regularity, and correct specification of at least one nuisance model; simulation checks implementation and finite-sample behavior but cannot establish the theorem by itself. Both nuisance models being wrong is an expected failure condition, poor overlap targets positivity and numerical behavior, and an omitted modifier violates exchangeability rather than merely misspecifying a nuisance model. Component drift is not a relevant benchmark unless drMAIC is extended to component models. No local drMAIC source was available to verify C1-C3, while absence of prior audits and field-wide benchmarks are literature-status claims outside this lens.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-single-overstatement:codex

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text: SFW-16 Overstated Medium-high priority Established Implementation-specific

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Statement
MBNMAdose fits model-based dose-response network meta-analysis, and in a truly disconnected network the assumed dose-response form is not identified by the data being combined, so results can be highly sensitive when dose support is sparse or non-overlapping. That form is not beyond checking, however: randomized dose-level evidence still estimates the curve parameters and supports goodness-of-fit checks and comparison among curve families, and Pedder et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315) ran the deletion experiment, finding MBNMA estimates on disconnected networks consistent with NMA on augmented networks in 15 of 18 datasets, with the three failures needing a richer dose-response form. crossnma is also broader than the source described: its CRAN title is Cross-Design and Cross-Format Network Meta-Analysis and Regression and it handles individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both with meta-regression on up to three covariates, while its cross-design bias-adjustment parameter remains unidentified by the outcomes being combined. Neither package standardizes to an external target covariate distribution.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Why it is open
In a disconnected network the shared dose-response or class structure supplies the identification that randomization does not, so the comparison depends on a functional form the analyst chose, and a fitted curve returns a smooth plausible estimate at any dose without showing how much of the comparison the curve contributed. Deletion validation shows the assumption can hold in practice, but it was run on datasets where the connected answer was known, which is exactly what a genuinely disconnected application lacks. For crossnma, the parameter expressing how far nonrandomized evidence is down-weighted is not identified by the outcomes being combined, so residual confounding passes into the pooled estimate scaled by an assumed factor. Neither package carries a target covariate distribution, so combining doses or designs does not address who the estimate applies to.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




MBNMAdose (CRAN)
fits model-based dose-response network meta-analysis linking treatments and doses through a shared dose axis, which can connect otherwise disconnected networks under the assumed curve and class structure


crossnma (CRAN)
cross-design and cross-format network meta-analysis and regression for individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both using a three-level hierarchical model, with meta-regression on up to three covariates and explicit modeling of design bias; performs no standardization to an external target population


Pedder, Dias, Bennetts, Boucher and Welton 2021
deletes studies and treatments from a triptans network and compares MBNMA estimates on the resulting disconnected networks against NMA on augmented networks, agreeing in 15 of 18 datasets with the remaining 3 needing a more complex dose-response relationship; the validation evidence the entry omitted

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Probable solution or research direction
When dose-response models bridge disconnected evidence, report how much of the comparison is driven by the curve and class assumptions, and check them the way they can be checked: alternative curve families, goodness of fit against the dose-level randomized evidence, and deletion validation of the kind Pedder et al. performed. When designs are combined, treat cross-design exchangeability and residual confounding as explicit sensitivity parameters rather than fixed inputs, and exploit overlapping designs where they exist. In both cases obtain population adjustment and target transport from separate tooling rather than assuming the synthesis has supplied it.

title: MBNMAdose and crossnma bridges are unidentified across a disconnection
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. MBNMAdose can bridge otherwise disconnected treatments through an assumed dose-response form, and in a truly disconnected network that form is not identified by the data being combined, although Pedder et al. (2021) validated it by deletion in 15 of 18 semi-synthetic datasets; crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence and individual with aggregate data, and its cross-design bias-adjustment parameter is not identified by the data being combined. Neither package standardises to an external target covariate distribution.
The source titled this. “MBNMAdose and crossnma bridge on assumptions data cannot check” The title says the bridging assumptions cannot be checked, but randomized dose-level evidence supports fit and curve-family comparison and MBNMA was validated by deletion in 15 of 18 datasets.
The source said. “MBNMAdose is an active dose-response NMA ecosystem that connects treatments and doses mechanistically, and crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence with bias considerations. In both, the assumption that creates the link (the dose-response curve and class structure; cross-design exchangeability) can dominate the resulting comparison, and neither performs population adjustment or automatic target transport.”
What was wrong with it. Both auditors called the title claim too strong. The literature auditor supplied the paper the entry omitted, Pedder et al. (doi:10.1177/0272989X20983315), which validated MBNMA by deletion in 15 of 18 semi-synthetic datasets, and corrected the description of crossnma, which handles individual, aggregate and mixed-format data rather than only randomized plus nonrandomized evidence; GPT-5.6 Sol added that curve assumptions are partly checkable through fit and curve-family comparison and that mechanistic overstates what is model-based or semi-mechanistic dose-response modeling.

Literature and prior-art check

open / overstated. The title claim ‘assumptions data cannot check’ is too strong for MBNMAdose, and the entry omits the paper that shows why. Pedder, Dias, Bennetts, Boucher and Welton (2021) ran exactly the bridge-deletion experiment the agenda asks for elsewhere: they deleted studies and treatments from a triptans NMA and compared MBNMA estimates on the resulting disconnected networks against NMA on augmented networks, finding agreement in 15 of 18 datasets and identifying the three failures as needing a richer dose-response form. That paper sits in the catalog’s own documentation/refs folder yet SFW-16 cites only the CRAN page. Separately, crossnma is described too narrowly. Its CRAN title is ‘Cross-Design & Cross-Format Network Meta-Analysis and Regression’ and it handles individual participant data, aggregate data and mixtures of both with meta-regression on up to three covariates, so it is not merely an RCT-plus-observational combiner; the accurate residual claim is that it performs no standardisation to an external target population.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. C3, C4, and C6 are sound: MBNMAdose is not general population-adjustment software, crossnma combines randomized and nonrandomized evidence with bias modeling, and neither automatically standardizes to an external target population. C2 is sound only conditionally: in a disconnected comparison, shared curve or class structure can supply the otherwise missing identification. But randomized dose-level evidence still estimates the curve parameters and can support goodness-of-fit checks, comparisons among curve families, and bridge-deletion validation. The statements that the comparison is determined by functional form rather than randomized evidence and that the curve contribution cannot be seen are therefore too strong. C1 also uses ‘mechanistic’ too broadly for what is generally model-based or semi-mechanistic dose-response modeling. C5 is correct only as a causal-identification limitation: cross-design exchangeability and absence of residual confounding cannot be established from the combined outcomes alone, although crossnma can explicitly model design bias and exploit overlapping designs. The remaining transport and sensitivity-analysis gaps are open, but they are decision-critical only when disconnected or nonrandomized evidence is load-bearing; otherwise they are roadmap items.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2)
